Preface

TITLE 24 

A significant forward step in the legislation of the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico was made with the passage of the Rules and Regulations Act of 1958, Act June 30, 1957, No. 112, 3 L.P.R.A. §§ 1041 to 1059. 

Laws of Puerto Rico Annotated made available to the citizens of the Commonwealth the laws enacted by the Legislative Branch and the interpretation of those laws by the Judicial 

Branch. The Rules and Regulations Act performs the same service with respect to the regulations adopted by the Executive Branch for the execution of the laws. 

The regulatory system set up by this Act has two principal features: (1) All regulations which are within the scope of the Act must be filed in the office of the Secretary of State. Beginning three months after June 30, 1957, any such regulation which is not filed with the Secretary of State is void and ineffective. 

This provides an official record of the regulations. (2) For the information and guidance of the people, these regulations will be published by the Secretary of State. This publication will be in two stages: (a) The "Rules and Regulations of Puerto Rico", for which the citation "R.&R.P.R." has been adopted, will be a codification of all regulations originally filed. (b) The "Puerto Rico Register" will be published periodically and will contain new regulations and amendments to existing regulations, thus keeping R.&R.P.R. up to date. After publication of the Register begins, new regulations will not become effective until published therein, except in cases of emergency. 

Rules and Regulations of Puerto Rico. The regulations originally filed with the Secretary of State have been classified by subject matter. A system of arrangement and numbering has been adopted which greatly simplifies the search for the corresponding provisions of the laws and regulations. For this purpose, R.&R.P.R. will have the same title and chapter numbers as Laws of Puerto 

Rico Annotated (L.P.R.A.). Regulations interpreting and applying a law contained in a title and chapter of L.P.R.A. will be found in the same title and chapter of R.&R.P.R. In addition, the 

VII

section numbers of a regulation in R.&R.P.R. will correspond with the section number of L.P.R.A. which authorizes the adoption of that regulation. For example, regulations adopted under 

With this system a person reading a provision of the law can find the corresponding regulations and a person reading the regulations can find the corresponding law without an extensive search of indexes and tables.

Editorial features. The regulations have been arranged by titles. 

The text has been carefully edited and appropriate catchlines have been supplied. A source note under the first section of each regulation shows the agency which issued it, the approval date, the effective date if one is specified, the date of filing with the Secretary of State, and the File Number which it bears in the records of his office. The statutory authority for the adoption of the regulation is cited. Annotations of court decisions interpreting the regulations have been inserted. 

This set of R.&R.P.R. is published in both Spanish and English editions. Except in a few cases where the contrary clearly appears, the Spanish text has been treated as the official version. 

In some instances it has been necessary to change the English text as filed with the Secretary of State in order to correct apparent errors of translation.

Index and Tables. This volume contains a topical index of the titles which it covers. When the entire set is finished, the last volume will contain a complete and detailed index of all the titles. 

The Table of Agencies at the end of this volume, showing the regulations adopted by each agency which are included in these titles, will be replaced by a complete table at the end of the set showing all regulations of all agencies. 

Supplementation; Puerto Rico Register. R.&R.P.R. will be kept up to date by means of the Puerto Rico Register, which will be published periodically. This will be in the form of loose leaf pages, containing all changes and new provisions, which will be inserted in the original volumes of R.&R.P.R., replacing pages which have become obsolete. Thus, R.&R.P.R. will always be up to date with the latest issue of the Puerto Rico Register.

Printing and Binding. This volume has been produced in loose leaf form so that changes and new regulations can be incor- 

VIII

porated into R.&R.P.R. as quickly as possible after they become effective, and each section of the work will always be up to the minute.

This loose leaf ring binder has been chosen after exhaustive study of all available types of binders. Among its practical advantages are: (1) The pages lie absolutely flat no matter where you open it; (2) there are no hidden inner margins to force you to pry the pages apart in order to read them; and (3) pages can be inserted and removed with minimum time and effort. To insure durability under constant use, we have employed a quality paper throughout and strengthened the title tabs with reinforced holes.

In Appreciation. We acknowledge gratefully the advice, help, and constructive cooperation of all who made this set possible. 

Special appreciation is due the Secretary of State, Honorable 

Roberto Sánchez-Vilella, and Assistant Secretary of State, Honorable Nicolás Almiroty, for their effective cooperation and wise counsel in the planning and execution of this project, and to 

Honorable Hiram Torres Rigual, Executive Assistant to the

Governor, whose vision and tireless efforts assured the success of this undertaking.

As in Laws of Puerto Rico Annotated, the Spanish edition of this set was edited by Mr. Ignacio Rivera, Secretary of the 

Supreme Court of Puerto Rico. His great ability, wise judgment, and devotion to a high ideal deserve full credit for the excellence of this edition.

Conclusion. Equity Publishing Corporation, which performed the editorial work on Laws of Puerto Rico Annotated, is especially proud to have been chosen to edit and publish these Rules and 

Regulations of Puerto Rico, under a contract with the Secretary of State. We consider it a privilege to have this part in the progress and accomplishments of the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico.

General codification note. In order to obtain a more logical arrangement of the regulations of the Secretary of Health on the subject of food, drugs, and cosmetics, the general plan of classifying regulations in R.&R.P.R. under the corresponding chapter and section numbers of L.P.R.A. (see Preface of this volume) has been modified in this Part III of Title 24. 

The authority to adopt regulations on this subject is found in three different statutory sources: (1) the Food, Drug, and

Cosmetic Act of 1940, 24 L.P.R.A. §§ 711-732; (2) the statute authorizing Sanitary Regulations, 3 L.P.R.A. §§ 178, 179 

(Sanitary Regulations on other subjects are classified to 

24 L.P.R.A. § 350-1 et seq.); and (3) statutes on specific types of food and drugs in 24 L.P.R.A. chapter 53 et seq. 

General Regulations to enforce the Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act of 1940 were adopted on June 18, 1942. The sections of these Regulations correspond to the sections of the Act itself and are set out as subchapters 712, 713, 715, 719, 721, 724-728, and 731 of this chapter, with section numbers corresponding to the section numbers of 24 L.P.R.A. These 

General Regulations of 1942 incorporated by reference certain prior regulations which are set out in subchapter 730 and in chapters 55, 57, and 59 of this title. 

Subchapter 730 of this chapter contains supplementary and miscellaneous regulations adopted under statutory sources (1) or (2) above, which are general in nature or which relate to specific foods not covered by chapters 53 et seq. of this title and 24 L.P.R.A. 

Chapter 53 et seq. of this title contain regulations adopted under all three statutory sources above, relating to the specific foods and drugs covered by the corresponding chapters of 24 L.P.R.A. 

§ 712-2. Printed matter of original container of manufacturer (24 L.P.R.A. § 712(j)) 

Labeling includes all written, printed, or graphic matter accompanying an article at any time while such article is on sale in Puerto Rico or held for sale after shipment in interstate commerce. 

§ 712-3. Misleading (24 L.P.R.A. § 712(k)) 

The existence of a difference of opinion among experts qualified by scientific training and experience as to the truth of a representation made or suggested in the labeling is a fact (among other facts) the failure to reveal which may render the labeling misleading, if there is a material weight of opinion contrary to such representation.

T.24 712 Ch. 51 

 § 712-4. Newness of drug (24 L.P.R.A. § 712(n) (2)) 

Newness of a drug may arise by reason (among other reasons) of: (1) the newness for drug use of any substance which composes such drug, in whole or in part, whether it be an active substance or a menstruum, excipient, carrier, coating, or other component; (2) the newness for drug use of a combination of two or more substances, none of which is a new drug; (3) the newness for drug use of the proportion of a substance in a combination, even though such combination containing such substance in other proportion is not a new drug; (4) the newness of use of such drug in diagnosing, curing, mitigating, treating, or preventing a disease, or to affect a structure or function of the body, even though such drug is not a new drug when used for another disease or to affect another structure or function of the body; or (5) the newness of a dosage, or method of duration of administration or application, or other condition of use prescribed, recommended, or suggested in the labeling of such drug, even though such drug when used in other dosage, or other method or duration of administration or application, or different condition, is not a new drug.

Subchapter 713. Acts Prohibited SECTIONS 713-1. Giving of guaranty (24 L.P.R.A. § 713(g)) § 713-1. Giving of guaranty (24 L.P.R.A. § 713(g))

719-11. Definitions

In the construction and application of this Division the following definitions shall govern: 

(1) "Ice-cream industry". For the purposes of this Division, ice-cream industry shall be understood to be any industry or business whose industrial or other activity is related with the preparation or processing, labeling, handling, transportation, wholesale and/or retail in Puerto Rico of ice creams, ices, sherbets, water ices or any other similar frozen or semifrozen product, including novelties and specialties, such as bonbons or any similar product destined for sale for public consumption. (2) "Plain ice cream". Plain ice cream shall be understood to be any frozen or semifrozen milk product which has been churned during the process of freezing and includes any frozen milk product containing milk fat and nonfatty milk solids, the consistency of which simulates the texture or characteristics of frozen ice cream, and which contains 10 percent or more by weight of milk fat, regardless of the name under which it is manufactured and/or sold. Provided, that plain ice cream shall be prepared or processed from a pasteurized combination of one or more of the following ingredients: milk cream, whole milk with milk fat or milk butter added, nonfatty milk solids, with the addition of any one or more of the following ingredients: saccharose, dextrose, corn sirup, invert sugar, invert sugar sirup, dehydrated corn sirup, maple sugar sirup, bee's honey, water, salt, certified natural or artificial flavor, stabilizer, eggs or egg products, certified coloring, milk fat, fruits and/or fruit juices. Provided, further, that other ingredients may be used in the preparation or processing of ice creams with the previous approval of the Department of Health of Puerto Rico. The final product shall not contain more than 0.20 percent (1/5 of 1 percent) by weight of emulsifier, more than 0.5 percent by weight of stabilizer, nor more than 0.5 percent by weight of yolk solids. The weight per gallon of plain ice cream shall not be less than 4.5 pounds, and the weight per gallon of the total edible 1963 Vol. 2, No. 3 10.1

T.§ 719-11 

Ch. 51

solids shall not be less than 1.6 pounds. The final product, plain ice cream, shall contain not less than 10 percent by weight of milk fat, except when fruits, nuts, cocoa, chocolate and/or confitures are added for flavor, in which case, it shall contain not less than 8 percent of milk fat by weight. (3) "Ice cream (French ice cream, frozen custard, French custard ice cream)". Ice cream under this group shall be understood to be that product which, in addition to the ingredients and in the proportions of such ingredients already established for plain ice cream, contains not less than 14 percent by weight of milk fat and not less than 1.4 percent by weight of yolk solids. Provided, that when this product contains fruits, cocoa, chocolate, cake, nuts, confitures, etc., it shall contain not less than 12 percent by weight of milk fat and not less than 1.1 percent by weight of yolk solids, and the weight per gallon of the total edible solids shall not be less than 1.8 pounds. Provided, further, that this product shall be subject to all provisions of the preceding subdiv. (2) as are not in conflict with this one. (4) "Ice milk". Ice milk shall be understood to be any frozen or semifrozen milk product which has been churned during the freezing process and includes any frozen milk product containing milk fat and nonfatty milk solids, the consistency of which simulates the texture and characteristics of frozen milk, and which contains not less than 212 percent by weight of milk fat and not more than 4 percent by weight of milk fat, regardless of the name under which it is manufacured or sold. Provided, that ice milk shall be prepared or processed from a pasteurized combination of any or more of the following ingredients: milk cream, whole milk with milk fat or milk butter added, nonfatty milk solids, with the addition of one or more of the following ingredients: saccharose, dextrose, corn sirup, invert sugar, invert sugar sirup, dehydrated corn sirup, maple sugar sirup, bee's honey, water, salt, certified natural or artificial flavor, stabilizer, emulsifier, eggs or egg products, certified coloring, milk fat, fruits and/or fruit juices. Provided, further, that other ingredients may be used in the preparation or processing of ice milk with the previous ap proval of the Department of Health of Puerto Rico. The final prod uct shall not contain more than 0.20 percent (1/5 of 1 percent) by weight of emulsifier, more than 0.5 percent (1½ of 1 percent) by weight of stabilizer, nor more than 0.5 percent by weight of yolk solids. The weight per gallon of ice milk shall not be less than 4.5 1963 Vol. 2, No. 3 10.2

Ch. T.24 719-11 

pounds, and the weight per gallon of the total edible solids shall not be less than 1.5 pounds. Provided, further, that ice milk shall contain not less than 21½ percent and not more than 4 percent by weight of milk fat. (5) "Fruit ice cream or water ice". Fruit ice cream or water ice shall be understood to be any frozen or semifrozen product with a well-defined fruit flavor, the process of preparation or elaboration of which is similar to that for the preparation or elaboration of plain ice cream, regardless of the name under which it is manufactured or sold. Provided, that water ice shall be prepared or processed from a pasteurized mixture of any one or more of the following products: ripe fruit juices, fresh or frozen ripe fruits, canned chunk-crushed ripe fruits, with the addition of any one or more of the following ingredients: saccharose, dextrose, corn sirup, invert sugar, maple sugar sirup, bee's honey, water, salt, stabilizer, emulsifier and/or certified coloring. The weight per gallon of fruit ice cream or water ice shall not be less than 6 pounds. Provided, further, that the final product shall contain not less than 0.35 percent of edible organic acid, determined by volumetric analysis (titration), with a standard alkali, and calculated as lactic acid. This organic acid shall be wholly or partly derived from the fruits or fruit juices used in the preparation or processing of the fruit ice cream or water ice or shall be produced through the addition of citric, tartaric acid. Provided, further, that the final product shall contain not more than 0.5 percent (12 percent) by weight of stabilizer and not more than 0.20 percent (1/5 of 1 percent) by weight of emulsifier, both previously approved by the Department of Health of Puerto Rico. 

In case it is verified that the acidity specified in this Division for any fruit ice cream or water ice turns out to be substantially injurious to the natural and specific flavor of any fruit in particular from which it is prepared, the Secretary of Health of Puerto Rico shall specify the minimum acidity in such particular instance. In the preparation or processing of fruit ice cream or ice water other ingredients in addition to the ones herein specified may be used only upon the previous specific approval of the 

Secretary of Health of Puerto Rico. 

(6) "Sherbet". Sherbet shall be understood to be any frozen or semifrozen product, sweetened and prepared with fruits or fruit juices and milk solids. Fruits or fruit juices used in the elaboration of sherbet shall be fresh, adequately canned or preserved, 1963 10.3 Vol. 2, No. 3

T.§ 719-11 Ch. 51 

and shall contain not more than 5 percent by weight of total milk solids. Sherbet shall contain not less than 3 percent by weight nor more than 5 percent of total milk solids, with the exception of coconut or soursop sherbet. Provided, that when coconut or soursop sherbet is prepared or processed, the content by weight of total milk solids shall not be less than 5 percent and it does not have to contain milk fat. The process of elaboration of sherbet shall be similar to the process of elaboration of plain ice cream. 

Sherbet shall be prepared or processed from milk cream, whole milk or any form of milk solids, and one or more of the following ingredients: saccharose, dextrose, corn sirup, dehydrated corn sirup, invert sugar, maple sugar sirup, maple sugar, bee's honey, molasses, fruits or juices, water, salt, stabilizer and/or certified coloring. Provided, that the final product shall contain not more than 0.5 percent (1½ of 1 percent) by weight of stabilizer nor more than 0.20 percent (1/5 of 1 percent) by weight of emulsifier, both approved by the U. S. Department of Agriculture or by the Department of Health of Puerto Rico. Acidity in sherbet, except in the case of coconut or soursop sherbet, shall not be less than 0.35 percent of edible organic acid, as determined by volumetric analysis (titration), with a standard alkali, and calculated as lactic acid. 

The percentage of milk fat, except in the case of coconut or soursop sherbet, shall not be less than 1 percent nor more than 2 percent by weight. Acidity shall be derived wholly or partly from the fruits or fruit juices used in the preparation or processing of the sherbet or shall be produced through the addition of citric, tartaric or malic acid. Provided, that the weight per gallon of sherbet shall not be less than 6 pounds, and the weight per gallon of total edible solids shall not be less than 1.8 pounds. When coconut or soursop sherbet is prepared, its weight per gallon shall not be less than 4.5 pounds and the total edible solids per gallon shall not be less than 1.5 pounds. Provided, further, that when it is verified that the acidity specified in this Division for sherbet is injurious to the typical flavor of the fruit used in its preparation, the Secretary of Health shall stipulate the percentage of acidity in specific cases. Other ingredients in addition to those specified in this definition may be used only upon the previous approval of the Secretary of Health of Puerto Rico. When it is shown to the satisfaction of the Secretary of Health of Puerto Rico that the fat contents required for sherbets in this Division is injurious to the characteristic flavor of any fruit in particular, said Secretary of 1963 10.4 

Vol. 2, No. 3

Ch. 

T.24 § 719-11 

Health may reduce such fat percentage or may eliminate said ingredient in that specific case and for such particular fruit. (7) "Fat". The word "fat" as used in this Division shall be understood to mean the natural fat or butter of cow's milk. (8) "Mix". Mix is the unfrozen union and mixture of the ingredients to be used in the preparation or processing of products of the ice-cream industry. (9) "Stabilizer". The word stabilizer shall mean substances used to impart body, consistency and smoothness to the mix. (10) "Ice-cream plant". The term ice-cream plant shall mean any premise, building, house or dependency thereof, trucks or peddling structures, in which any product of the ice-cream industry is prepared, elaborated or processed. (11) "Average bacteriological computation". The term average bacteriological computation shall mean the logarithmic average of the computation of 4 consecutive samples. (12) "And/or". Wherever the conjunctions and/or are used, it shall be understood that the copulative "and" unites, and "or" shall be disjunctive where possible. (13) "Ice scrap". Ice scrap shall be understood to be, for the purposes of this Division, the product obtained by rasping, crushing, crumbling or chopping ice with an appropriate scraper or any other special device and to which sirup or any other liquid is added to sweeten and flavor it. (14) "Ice-scrap stand". Ice-scrap stand shall be understood to be any peddling cart, or any premise, establishment, or dependencies thereof in which ice scrap is prepared and/or served. (15) "Sirup". Sirup shall be understood to be any liquid used to sweeten and/or flavor ice scrap in the ice-cream industry. (16) "Other products of the ice-cream industry". It is the purpose of this Division that the People of Puerto Rico be not confused as to the exact nature of any product of the ice-cream industry; therefore, no product of the ice-cream industry in Puerto 

Rico other than those defined in this Division shall be prepared or processed, distributed, sold, given out, or otherwise offered to the public unless the Secretary of Health shall have previously specified the identity standards for such other products. Likewise, no such product shall be used in Puerto Rico even under a registered trade name or trademark, if said name directly or indirectly tends to confuse the public as to the nature of the product so designated. 1963 10.5 Vol. 2, No. 3

T.§ 719-11 Ch. 51 

For example, and independently of other cases, the word "cream”, specifically, or any other word of a similar sound may be used only to designate products the content of which fulfills the requirements established for plain ice cream. Provided, that when vegetable fat be used in any product of the ice-cream industry none of the names described in this Division may be used. In such case, the interested person or firm shall submit to the Secretary of Health a list of the ingredients to be used as well as the proportions thereof and the trade name with which the proposed product is intended to be labeled. The Secretary of Health shall accept or reject the name submitted. Provided, further, that the Secretary of Health shall accept for the labeling of products of the icecream industry only those using vegetable fat names which do not tend to deceive or confuse the consumer public. These names as well as the list of ingredients shall be in the Spanish language or in the Spanish and English languages. When both languages are used, the English shall at no time appear more prominently than the Spanish. 

(17) "Department of Health". By Department of Health shall be understood the Secretary of Health or his authorized representative or agent. (18) "Protection against flies". A premise whose doorway, window opening, skylight, or wall hole is protected against flies. shall be deemed adequately so protected only when the means of protection, whatever it may be, is operating effectively. A door with mesh wire or similar screen whose purpose is to prevent the entrance of flies and other insects shall not be considered to be protecting the premise adequately or operating effectively if it is out of order or if for any cause it stays open longer than the time necessary for a person to enter or leave. (19) "Direct communication". It shall be understood that there is direct communication between two premises, rooms, or dependencies: (A) If noncontiguous, when the opening of the door or window of either renders it likely for flies or any other winged insect to gain access to the other premise, room, or dependency not having adequate protection as defined in this Division. (B) When there is any opening or hole in the wall separating two contiguous enclosures. (C) When the partition walls between premises of dependencies do not cover or extend all the distance from floor to roof. 1963 Vol. 2, No. 3 10.6

Ch. T.24719-12 

(D) When the type or condition of the material of which any of the walls separating two premises, rooms, or dependencies is constructed allows flies or other insects to pass through. (E) Provided, that any ice-cream factory constructed on and after this Division takes effect shall have a hall or intermediate room between every enclosure, section, or dependency where one or more water closets, and/or urinals are installed and any other room or dependency where any food or its ingredients is handled, served, sold, prepared, frozen, pasteurized, homogenized, etc., and any other enclosure where utensils, equipment, containers and/or wrappers are washed, hygienized, deposited, or stored. The intermediate room or hall shall have a floor area of not less than 20 square feet and shall be constructed so as to render it impossible for a person to open the two doors at the same time. 

The installation of lavatories or any other cleansing facility other than water closets or urinals or devices for similar use shall be permitted. The use of bidets shall not be permitted in any of the premises of the ice-cream plant. (20) "Person". Person shall include both natural and artificial persons.

§ 719-12. Plans 

For the establishment of any ice cream, ice water and/or sherbet plant in Puerto Rico, it shall be necessary to submit beforehand to the Department of Health the plans of the structure therefor. Said plans shall include layout of the machinery, type thereof, and capacity of the equipment. Provided, that no ice cream, ice water and/or sherbet plant whatsoever shall be estab- 1963 10.7

Vol. 2, No. 3

T.24 719 Ch. 51 

lished in Puerto Rico without the previous approval by the Department of Health of the plans therefor, including layout and capacity of the equipment and machinery. 

§ 719-13. Licenses 

It shall be compulsory for any person who owns, manages, leases and/or otherwise has under his charge an ice-cream, ice-water and/or sherbet plant to comply with the provisions of this Division and to hold a license for the operation thereof. Said license shall be issued by the Department of Health on request of the interested party provided the requirements specified in this Division have been complied with. Said license shall be posted to the public in a conspicuous place of the plant or establishment. The licenses referred to in this section shall be prepared ad hoc by the Department of Health according to the model thereby accepted. 

§ 719-14. Sanitary conditions 

To obtain, hold and retain a license for ice-cream, ice-water and/or sherbet plants it shall be required that said establishments meet in all the dependencies thereof the sanitary conditions specified in the health regulations and laws in force for the purpose, and that they, in addition, fulfill the following further requirements, namely: (1) Equipment and utensils. All multiple-use utensils and the equipment used in the plant shall be made of a material approved by the Department of Health and so constructed as to facilitate its cleaning, and shall be kept scrupulously sterilized and in good repair. Any machinery to be used in the ice-cream industry shafl be previously submitted for acceptance and approval as satis factory by the Department of Health of Puerto Rico. 

(2) Floors. The floors of any premises of an ice-cream plant shall be of reinforced concrete or any other material of like impermeability, and so constructed as to be easy to clean. Its surfaces shall be maintained neat and clean and in good repair, and shall be level, flat and smooth. They shall also be graded properly so as to prevent water from ponding in the premises. 

The floors of rooms and premises of sanitary services where products or ingredients of the ice-cream industry are prepared, handled, or stored (except freezers), and where utensils are washed or hygienized, shall have adequate drain and shall be con- 1963 10.8 

Vol. 2, No. 3

Ch. T.24 § 719-14 

nected to a used-water disposal system accepted by the Department of Health. (3) Walls and ceilings. All walls and ceilings shall be constructed or revetted with reinforced concrete or any other water-tight material, with a level, flat and smooth surface easily washed and cleaned; shall be maintained acceptably clean, upkept and painted. 

The paint shall be of a light color and washable. Walls revetted with glazed tiles or similar material need not be painted. (4) Light level. All plant dependencies shall have a minimum floor-to-ceiling height of 10 feet and adequate natural and/or artificial lighting. In those buildings in which an air conditioning system of acceptable guarantee to the Department of Health is used, the floor-to-ceiling height or light level may be reduced to a minimum of 9 feet. By adequate lighting shall be understood that which at a height of 30 inches from the floor anywhere in the premises maintains an intensity of not less than 10 candles. These specifications shall not apply to refrigeration rooms or other dependencies where, due to the specific nature of the process, their application may be injurious. (5) Ventilation. Every room, dependency or premise of the plant shall be adequately ventilated. They shall be considered adequately ventilated when there are unobstructed doors, windows, skylights or other openings, equivalent in area to at least 10 percent of the total floor area. In the absence of the ventilation area above-mentioned, artificial or mechanical ventilation shall be considered adequate if it provides not less than one and a half (1½) air changes per hour, or 15 cubic feet per minute, per person. Of these two systems the one producing the higher volume of local ventilation may be used. These specifications shall not apply to refrigeration rooms nor to any other premises where, due to the specific nature of the process, their application may be injurious. (6) Doors and windows. The doors, windows, skylights, and other openings in any room or dependency where the final product or the mix or its ingredients is or are handled shall be adequately protected against entrance of flies and other insects by means of the use of 16-mesh wire (16 strands per lineal inch) or other net, system or device producing like effect and approved by the Department of Health. In every premise where protection against flies is required, the doors and windows shall swing outward, shall 1963 10.9

Vol. 2, No. 3

T.§ 719-14 Ch. 51 

be properly fitted to their frames, and shall be equipped with rapid-action automatic locks. It shall be indispensable to protect adequately against flies every premise where products of the icecream industry are being processed and the ingredients, the mix, or the final product are or is being handled, or are stored or deposited to be processed or handled, unless packed in flyproof containers. (7) Sanitary service. Every ice-cream plant shall be provided with the sanitary services required by the plumbing rules of the Planning Board. The sanitary service enclosure shall be adequately protected against flies and other insects and shall not have direct communication with the premise or premises where ice cream, ice water, sherbet, or the mix or ingredients therefor is or are handled, served, sold, processed, frozen, pasteurized, homogenized, etc., nor with the enclosures where utensils and/or equipment are washed, sterilized or deposited or stored. The doors of the sanitary service enclosures shall be properly fitted to their frames and shall be equipped with rapid-action automatic locks. (8) Washstands. Every ice-cream plant shall be provided with at least one washstand within the sanitary service enclosure for the use of the personnel and another in the processing room, and shall also provide soap, paper towels and an adequate receptacle for each washstand to deposit used towels. Washstands shall be kept clean and in good working order. Provided, that in addition to the washstands herein specified, hand-washing facilities shall be provided in every premise where the Department of Health deems it necessary for the protection of the public health. The use of common towels is hereby prohibited. No employee shall resume his work after using the sanitary service without first washing his hands. (9) Water supply. There shall be an abundant supply of running potable water in all rooms or dependencies where the mix is prepared, the product is processed, and the equipment and utensils are washed or sterilized; likewise, there shall be abundant running water in the sanitary service and washstands. Provided, that where there is a private water supply, this shall conform to the standards. 

promulgated by the Department of Health. 

(10) Sanitary piping. All piping and connections used for the conveyance of the ingredients or mix shall be made of metal or other material approved by the Department of Health of Puerto 1963 Vol. 2, No. 3 10.10

Ch. T.24 719-14 

Rico and shall be easily dismountable and noncorrosive; Provided, That after each use all piping shall be disassembled and washed, and afterward submitted to a bactericidal treatment by means of any system acceptable to the Department of Health. (11) Refuse disposal. The refuse from every ice-cream, ice-water and/or sherbet plant shall be rapidly disposed of. To this end. there shall be as many floor level sinks as may be necessary to drain any liquid refuse of the industry that may be spilled on the floor. In addition to the said sinks there shall be receptacles with tight fitting lids in places properly located to deposit all solid refuse. (12) Cleaning and treatments of utensils and other equipment.

All utensils and equipment used in the preparation, freezing or handling of the mix and its ingredients shall be properly washed immediately after use and not less than once a day. All utensils shall be sterilized after being washed, and the equipment used for the purposes specified above shall be sterilized after being washed and before re-use. Hygienization and sterilization shall be carried out by means of any system acceptable to the Department of Health. (13) Storage of multiple-use utensils. After a bactericidal treatment, multiple-use utensils shall be stored so as to be protected against all contamination by insects and dust. (14) Handling of equipment and utensils. Sterilized equipment and utensils shall be handled so as to prevent their contamination. (15) Storage and handling of single-service utensils and other material. Sanitary cups and spoons, novelties, cardboard containers, cones and other single-service utensils and materials shall be bought in sanitary containers and shall be stored in dry and clean places, vermin- and dust-proof. The same shall be properly handled to prevent pollution. (16) Refrigeration. Every product or ingredient liable to decomposition shall be kept at a temperature not higher than 50°F. (10° centigrade) in freezers that shall be cleaned as frequently as necessary. (17) Storage, display and dispatch of final products. The storage and display of final products, whether for wholesale or retail in the same premises, or for display or storage for wholesale to customers, branches, and/or peddling carts, shall be carried in 1963 10.11 Vol. 2, No. 3

T.§ 719-14 Ch. 51 

such fashion as to keep the products protected against dust, flies and other insects, and against any form of contamination. (18) Rats and other pests. Every building or premises devoted to an ice-cream plant shall be constructed ratproof. All persons directly or indirectly connected with the operation of an ice-cream, ice-water, or sherbet plant shall be bound to take all necessary precautions to maintain the building and its outbuildings and dependencies free of rats and other pests by means of effective measures for their extermination. In case of a rat and/or pest infestation the owner or manager of the plant shall be under obligation to exterminate same. (19) Personnel's cleanliness. Every employee shall wear clean clothing, shall maintain his body clean, specially his hands, while on duty. Every employee engaged in the processing of the final products or ingredients, in wrapping or packing, and handling the various products shall wear a white apron and cap, which shall be kept neat and clean, and shall not undertake any task of a different nature likely to contaminate his hands while working in the preparation of ice waters, ice creams, sherbets, etc. (20) Health certificate. All employees working in the processing as well as those in charge of handling the ingredients, the final products and the utensils and equipment, shall hold a health certificate issued by the Department of Health. (21) Miscellaneous. The dependencies and outbuildings of every plant of products of the ice-cream industry shall be kept clean and none of the operations related with the factory shall take place outside the proper boundaries of said plant. These plants shall have a room for the employees to change clothing in. This room shall be kept thoroughly clean at all times. The immediate surroundings shall be kept strictly clean. Garbage cans with tight fitting lids shall be provided for depositing refuse. Used and soiled caps and aprons shall be kept in adequate places outside the processing premises. Likewise, the preparation or elaboration processes shall be carried out in one or more premises fitted with glass windows or with fixed wire screens. The processing room or rooms shall be separated from any other premise where tasks other than those of preparation or elaboration are carried out, and shall communicate with other premises by means of doors fitted with rapid-action automatic locks. It is hereby postively 1963 10.12

Vol. 2, No. 3

Ch. 

T.24 § 719-16 prohibited to carry out any task whatsoever within said premises other than the task, proper, of preparation or elaboration, specially sale activities entailing the handling of money. Said premises shall be designed and constructed so as to preclude any chance of contamination of the products prepared therein by reason of dust, or of vermin that may penetrate into such premises thru holes leading to outside the building. No process of preparation or elaboration, or handling, may be carried out in any ice-cream, icewater and/or sherbet plant whatsoever, or their dependencies or outbuildings, when such processes are likely to contaminate or adulterate the final products or their ingredients. § 719-15. Branches and warehouses

All sanitary requisites related to the plants of the ice-cream industry products shall also apply to the branches, depots, and warehouses where, although these products are not elaborated, they are, however, stored for wholesale and/or retail. 

§ 719-16. Ambulatory stands. 

Every operator of a manual peddling cart for the sale of ice cream, ice water, sherbets and other products of the ice-cream industry shall hold a peddler's license according to the provisions of this Division, which license shall be issued thereto by the local public health unit corresponding to the town where the supplying plant, branches or deposit is located. Provided, that to obtain said license the following requisites shall be fulfilled: (1) The operator shall hold a health certificate issued by the local public health unit, which certificate shall be renewed annually or as frequently as the director of the public health unit may deem it necessary. (2) Said operator shall wear clean clothing and a white apron and cap. (3) The cart (stand) shall be kept in good repair and well painted. The same shall be constructed and revetted in its interior with watertight material and shall be equipped with a tight fitting lid, also constructed and revetted with watertight material. 

These carts (stands) shall display in clear legible letters the name of the product they sell. (4) The operator shall not cry out a product or trademark other than the very product or trademark of the products he carries in his cart. 1963 Vol. 2, No. 3 10.13

T.24 719 Ch. 51 

(5) The cooling system of these carts (stands) must be ap proved by the Department of Health of Puerto Rico. 

(6) Each cart (stand) shall be provided with an insect- and dust-proof compartment to store the sanitary spoons and other necessary material for the sale of these products. (7) The cups, lollypops [ice cream on sticks] (paletas) and other novelties shall be handled in the cart (stand) in a sanitary manner so as to prevent their contamination. 

§ 719-17. Transportation 

The conveyances for transporting products deriving from the ice-cream industry shall be kept in good repair, thoroughly clean and painted. The interior of the box where these products are deposited shall be kept dust- and insect-proof and scrupulously clean. The name of the manufacturer shall be clearly shown on the outside of the box in bold clear letters, legible at a distance of 30 feet. These conveyances shall be provided with a refrigeration system, whether thru the use of metalic sheets, thru the use of individual refrigeration units, or thru any other method, which shall be approved by the Department of Health of Puerto Rico and shall be exclusively used in the transportation of products deriving from the ice-cream industry. § 719-18. Cups, boxes, covers, wrappers, etc.

The cups or boxes for ice creams, ice waters, etc., shall be made of paraffined cardboard or paper or of any other material approved by the Department of Health of Puerto Rico. The covers thereof shall be made of the same material and shall close hermetically. 

The latter shall be properly handled so as to avoid contamination of the product. The lollypops [ice cream on sticks] and other novelties shall be wrapped in bags of special paraffined paper, duly labeled. These bags shall cover wholly all the edible part of the product; Provided, That under no circumstance shall there be expended to the public or stored such lollypops or novelties without the said wrapper. These novelties and other similar products shall be packed in cardboard boxes properly closed and labeled. 

Other products, such as ice-cream, ice-water or sherbet bonbons, that because of their nature can not be wrapped in individual bags, shall be packed in boxes, or shall be wrapped in bulk in bags such as the ones above described, when their nature and size so require. The foregoing does not apply to small cardboard boxes used 1963 

Vol. 2, No. 3 

10.14

Ch. 

 T.24 § 719-22 

for retail in soda fountains. Ice cream, ice water or sherbet to be sold at wholesale shall be packed in paraffined cardboard cylinders or other material or type of containers approved by the Department of Health of Puerto Rico. These containers shall be kept hermetically closed with a cover of the same material or of any other material approved by said Department of Health. § 719-19. Sale in ambulatory stands 

There is hereby strictly prohibited the sale on the street of ice creams, ice waters or any other product of the ice-cream industry in peddling carts when the product is retailed from bulk containers or cups or cones. Provided, that ice-cream industry products may be sold in peddling carts or vehicles only when said products are in the individual containers properly filled and covered in the plant. The carrying in the frozen compartment of these carts of products not appertaining to the ice-cream industry is likewise prohibited. § 719-20. Refreezing

The refreezing of any product of the ice-cream industry when, because of faulty preservation or any other cause, the same has unfrozen wholly or partially, or has started to unfreeze, is hereby strictly prohibited. 

§ 719-21. Labeling 

Every container of ice cream, ice water, sherbet, or any other ice-cream industry product, whether bulk or individual containers for sale at retail, including those for novelties, bonbons, ice cream cones, or any other product, shall include the following in its labeling: 

(1) Name of manufacturer, packer, or distributor. (2) Address. (3) Specific name of the product according to the Regulation, set out in this Division, to wit; French ice cream, plain ice cream, ice milk, fruit ice cream, sherbet, etc. (4) Fluid content (fluid ounces, pints, half gallons and gallons). 

(5) Name of flavor. 

§ 719-22. Elaboration of products of the ice-cream industry in soda fountains, hotels, refreshment stands, grocery stores, restaurants, etc. (a) The elaboration of products of the ice-cream industry in soda fountains, refreshment stands, grocery stores, restaurants, 1963 10.15

Vol. 2, No. 3

T.§ 719-22 Ch. 51 

hotels, trucks or ambulatory structures and other establishments engaged in other business activities shall also be carried out under the same sanitary conditions as apply to the plants engaged exclusively in this business. In said establishments such elaboration shall be carried out in a special dependency protected for the purpose against flies and dust and separated from the sale room. 

The requirements as to floors, height or light level, ventilation, water, etc., shall be the same prescribed for exclusive plants of ice cream and other similar products. (b) Besides the general requirements prescribed for every icecream plant, these establishments shall also meet the following: (1) They shall obtain a license from the Department of 

Health of Puerto Rico. 

(2) The ice-cream industry products shall be preserved in cabinets and other sanitary equipment protected against dust, insects, water and all forms of contamination. Said cabinets shall only contain ice-cream industry products of the same kind, brand and grade as are advertised in the establishment. (3) The cups, small cardboard boxes, and other wrappers shall be properly labeled. Provided, that cones need not be labeled provided the product served therein comes from a duly labeled sanitary container accessible to the purchaser in case he should wish to verify the kind of product served to him. If the cones or similar containers receive their contents otherwise, said cones or similar containers shall be labeled as hereinbefore prescribed, whether on the surface thereof or thru the use of a bag or wrapper which clearly fulfills the legal requisite and unmistakably establishes the actual or would-be identity of the product therein contained. Cardboard cylinders and other types of cardboard containers or containers of any other material approved by the 

Department of Health of Puerto Rico, and used to store or sell at wholesale any of the products of this industry, shall be properly labeled. (4) Cups, small cardboard boxes or cones shall be preserved in special sanitary equipment for the purpose, or shall otherwise be kept in the sanitary carton in which they are bought; Provided, That these cartons shall be opened at the lower end so that only this lower end of the cups, cones, and/or small boxes be exposed. (5) Cardboard or wooden spoons shall be kept in the original box duly closed, or shall otherwise be stored in a special pollutionproof compartment. 1963 Vol. 2, No. 3 10.16

Ch. T.24 719-24 

(6) Sirups shall be kept in an adequate sanitary equipment approved by the Department of Health of Puerto Rico. 

(7) There shall be maintained a sink or a receptacle with 3 tanks or compartments connected to the public sewer system. The first compartment or receptacle shall be full of clean water and shall be used to wash the ladle with which the ice cream is served as well as any other utensil which comes into contact with these products. In the second compartment the ladle or utensils shall be rinsed. In the third, which shall contain a chlorine solution at one hundred (100) ppm, these utensils shall be sterilized by maintaining them totally immersed for at least 5 minutes. (8) It is hereby positively prohibited to handle the cones directly with the hands. The lower exterior end of the cone shall be wrapped in a small sanitary napkin or sanitary paper so as to prevent the handler's hand from coming into contact with the cone. § 719-23. Sale of products of the ice-cream industry in soda fountains, grocery stores, motor vehicles, etc.

The preservation, handling and sale of products of the icecream industry in soda fountains, grocery stores, motor vehicles and other establishments shall be carried out under the same sanitary conditions as are prescribed by this Division for the plants or for those businesses engaged in other commercial activities which at the same time manufacture and sell the various products of the ice-cream industry. 

§ 719-24. Pasteurization 

The sale of products elaborated by the ice-cream industry without being pasteurized is hereby positively prohibited in Puerto Rico. Provided, that for the purposes of this Division, pasteurization shall mean the process by which part of the mix is submitted to a temperature of 150°F. and maintained at the temperature for not less than 30 minutes, immediately proceeding to cool said. mix rapidly at a temperature not higher than 40°F. and to store same at that temperature, using equipment duly approved by the Department of Health of Puerto Rico and operated in a proper and sanitary manner. Provided, that when the processor uses mixes previously pasteurized and only adds thereto potable water and/or fresh fruits, it shall not be compulsory to repasteurize the resulting mix. Provided, that nothing expressed in this definition shall be 1963 10.17

Vol. 2, No. 3

T.§ 719-24 

Ch. 51 construed as prohibiting any other pasteurization process whose efficacy is shown to be equal or higher than that of the process defined, provided it is previously accepted by the Department of 

Health of Puerto Rico. 

§ 719-25. Bacteriological computation 

For the purposes of this Division, the maximum bacteriological computation or recount permitted for the products of the ice-cream industry in Puerto Rico shall be the logarithmic average from a recount of bacteriological colonies, as may result from the culture of 4 consecutive samples. Provided, that said logarithmic average shall not be over 50,000 colonies per gram, except in the case of lollypops [ice cream on sticks] and novelties, when it shall not be over 100,000 colonies per gram. § 719-26. Coliform bacilli computation

The logarithmic count of coliform bacilli shall not exceed 10 colonies per gram; Provided, That the presence of coliform bacilli shall be permitted in isolated samples and never as a required minimum for each sample taken. Where the presence of coliform bacilli be continuous and persistent and in 3 ice cream samples taken consecutively, the sale of said product shall be suspended until the presence of the coliform organisms is controlled. § 719-27. Condition and age of water ices

The distribution and sale of old water ices which show shrinkage is hereby prohibited in Puerto Rico. The manner of determining same is by means of inspection, as old and shrunken water ice loses its creaminess and tends to pull away from the container. The distribution, donation and sale of products of the ice-cream industry in containers that have become deformed, or in any way damaged, is likewise prohibited. Products found in containers not perfectly in order and inadequate for display in supermarkets shall be immediately destroyed. 

§ 719-28. Responsibility 

The owner, manager, keeper, or employee of a water-ice plant or business, as the case may be, shall be duty bound to fulfill the requirements herein prescribed and to correct the deficiencies or violations of the regulations in force promulgated by the Department of Health. 1963 Vol. 2, No. 3 10.18

Ch. T.24 § 719-31 

§ 719-29. Revocation of license; closure

The Department of Health may revoke the sanitary license of any water-ice plant or establishment and may close said establishment if, after notice to the interested party giving him a reasonable term, he does not correct the sanitary deficiencies or violations of this Division of which he is notified by said department. Said license may be renewed after the requirements of this 

Division are fulfilled. § 719-30. Sanitary license for the sale of ice scraps

No natural or artificial person may sell, expose for sale, or offer for sale ice scraps in the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico without first providing himself or itself with the sanitary license issued by the proper health officer; Provided, That such products as are exposed for sale without the proper sanitary license shall be destroyed. § 719-31. Sanitary conditions of ambulatory ice-scrap carts or stands Peddling carts or stands devoted to the sale of ice scraps in Puerto Rico shall be sanitarily constructed and shall be maintained in sanitary condition. Provided, that said carts shall fulfill the following requisites: (1) Maintenance: They shall be maintained properly painted and in good repair. (2) Compartments: They shall be outfitted with one or more compartments to keep the bottles, vials or other sirup receptacles. 

Provided, that sirup bottles may be out of said compartments only at the time they are used. (3) Ice: Ice shall be kept in a watertight and nonabsorbent compartment. (4) Physical structure of the carts: Such part of the cart where the ice and sirups are found and where the scraping of ice is carried out shall be closed and shall be provided with a door in front through which the scraping shall be done. Said part shall be kept closed and shall only be opened at the moment of preparation of ice scraps or when any necessary operation of the business is carried out. Provided, that said carts shall be constructed in their upper part, where bottles and ice shall be kept and where the scraping is done, of wood, glass or other dust- and 1963 Vol. 2, No. 3 10.19

T.§ 719-31 

Ch. 51 insect-proof material accepted by the Department of Health of 

Puerto Rico. 

(5) Cleanliness: Ice-scrap peddling carts shall be kept scrupulously clean at all times. The surroundings where they are stationed, stopped, or located shall be completely clean. (6) Model construction: Every newly built ice-scrap peddling cart shall conform to a plan to be furnished by the Department of Health. Provided, that those carts already constructed at the time this Division takes effect shall be altered, following the recommendations of the health officer, to comply with the provisions of this Division. (7) Receptacles: Every ice-scrap peddling cart shall be provided with a receptacle with a tight fitting lid to deposit used cups and other refuse. (8) Water tank: Every ice-scrap cart shall be provided with a properly covered tank of adequate size full of chlorinated water two hundred (200 ppm) parts per million of active chlorine. The water in the tank shall be extracted thru a cock and shall be used for washing hands, the ice scraper, and other cleansing purposes. (9) Multiple-use utensils: The use of multiple-use utensils to serve ice scraps is hereby strictly prohibited. Sanitary cups shall be kept in their original boxes or cartons or in containers where they are protected against any contamination. 

(10) Sale of refreshments: The preparation of refreshments in ice-scrap peddling carts is hereby prohibited. (11) Origin of sirups: Every sirup or other product used to flavor or sweeten scraped ice shall be elaborated in a plant authorized by the Department of Health of Puerto Rico, and shall be used in its original container, provided, that the use of homemade sirups in the preparation of ice scraps is hereby prohibited. (12) Cloth for covering the ice: The use of fabric or woolen cloth or other similar absorbent material to cover the ice is hereby positively prohibited. (13) Peddlers: Ice-scrap cart peddlers shall wear clean clothing and a clean apron and shall keep themselves scrupulously clean, specially their hands. Their nails shall be kept well clipped and clean and they shall provide themselves with the proper health certificate by the Department of Health. 1963 Vol. 2, No. 3 10.20

Ch. T.24 719-35 

§ 719-32. Sanitary conditions of fixed ice-scrap stands 

Everything related to the origin of sirups, the handling of the final product, personal cleanliness, ice protection, prohibition of the use of glasses, etc., required in this Division in the case of icescrap peddling carts shall also apply to fixed stands of this product. 

In addition to ice scraps, fixed stands may sell refreshing drinks, provided the same are prepared, handled or served in a sanitary manner and in sanitary cups and that the sirups used are elaborated by a plant authorized by the Department of Health of Puerto Rico. § 719-33. Sirups, ice, etc.

Every sirup, ice or other product used in violation of the provisions of this Division shall be confiscated or denatured. § 719-34. Bacteriological count

The maximum bacteriological count permitted for ice scraps shall be the logarithmic average of the recount of bacterial colonies as resulting from the culture of 4 consecutive samples. 

Provided, that said logarithmic average shall not be over 150,000 colonies per milliliter. The requisites for the presence of colibacilli in ice scraps shall be the same as those required in this Division for the ice-cream industry products. 

§ 719-35. Sanitary facilities 

Every owner or manager of a fixed ice-scrap stand shall provide a place for the washing, rinsing and sterilization of containers and utensils used in the ice-scrap business and said place shall be provided with the following sanitary facilities: (1) The premises shall be constructed so as to be protected against entrance of rats, insects, and all other vermin. (2) They shall be provided with running, potable water and a 3-section sink with independent drainage into the sanitary sewer system or into any other adequate means for liquid refuse disposal. (3) There shall be adequate shelf or cabinet to keep the sterilized equipment. (4) Washing, rinsing and sterilizing operations shall be carried out as provided in this Division for such purposes. (5) The premises shall be kept thoroughly clean, painted and in good repair and shall be provided with the sanitary facilities prescribed by the Department of Health of Puerto Rico.

§ 719-36. Interpretation 

Words used in singular shall be understood to be also in plural where so justified; the masculine shall include the feminine and vice versa where necessary; where the term "and/or" is used, "and" shall be used where possible; otherwise "or" shall be used. 

§ 719-37. Penalties 

Any person who violates any of the provisions of this Division shall be guilty of a misdemeanor and upon conviction thereof shall be punished according to the provisions of the Puerto Rico Food, Drug and Cosmetic Act, Act No. 72 of 1940 [24 L.P.R.A. §§ 711 

to 732]. 

§ 719-38. Effectiveness 

This Division shall take effect 90 days after its approval. 

Approval date. Regulation File No. 821, set out in this 

Division, was approved by Secretary of Health Dec. 27, 1962.

Subchapter 721. Food Misbranding SECTIONS 721-1. False or misleading representation (24 L.P.R.A. § 721(a)) 721-2. Label on package (24 L.P.R.A. § 721(e)) 

721-3. 

Conspicuousness of printing (24 L.P.R.A. § 721(f)) 721-4. Name of ingredient (24 L.P.R.A. § 721 (i)) 

721-5. 

Flavoring; coloring; preservatives (24 L.P.R.A. § 721 (k)) 

§ 721-1. False or misleading representation (24 L.P.R.A. § 721(a)) 

(a) Among representations in the labeling of a food which render such food misbranded is a false or misleading representation with respect to another food or a drug, device, or cosmetic. (b) The labeling of a food which contains two or more ingredients may be misleading by reason (among others) of the designation of such food in such labeling by a name which includes or suggests the name of one or more but not all such ingredients, even though the names of all such ingredients are stated elsewhere in the labeling. 1963 Vol. 2, No. 3 10.22

Ch. T.24 § 721-2 

 § 721-2. Label on package (24 L.P.R.A. § 721(e)) 

(a) If a food is not manufactured by the person whose name appears on the label, the name shall be qualified by a phrase which reveals the connection such person has with such food, such as "Manufactured for and packed by ", "Distributed by or other similar phrase which expresses the facts. 

(b) The statement of the place of business shall include the street address, if any, of such place. (c) Where a person manufactures, packs, or distributes a food at a place other than his principal place of business, the label may state the principal place of business in lieu of the actual place where each package of such food was manufactured or packed or is to be distributed, if such statement is not misleading in any particular. (d) The requirement that the label shall contain the name and place of business and post-office address of the manufacturer, packer, or distributor shall not be considered to relieve any food from the requirement that its label shall not be misleading in any particular. (e) (1) The statement of the quantity of the contents shall reveal the quantity of food in the package, exclusive of wrappers and other material packed with such food. (2) The statement shall be expressed in the terms of weight, measure, numerical count, or a combination of numerical count and weight or measure, which are generally used by consumers to express quantity of such food and which give accurate information as to the quantity thereof. But if no general consumer usage in expressing accurate information as to the quantity of such foods exists, the statement shall be in terms of liquid measure if the food is liquid, or in terms of weight if the food is solid, semisolid, viscous, or a mixture of solid and liquid. (f) (1) A statement of weight shall be in terms of the avoirdupois pound and ounce. A statement of liquid measure shall be in terms of the United States gallon of 231 cubic inches and quart, pint, and fluid ounce subdivisions thereof, and, except in case of frozen food which is so consumed, shall express the volume at 68° 

Fahrenheit (20° Centigrade). A statement of dry measure shall be in terms of the United States bushel of 2150.42 cubic inches and peck, dry quart, and dry pint subdivisions thereof; or in terms of the United States standard barrel and its subdivisions of third, 11

T.§ 721-2 Ch. 51 

half, and three-quarters barrel. However, in the case of an export shipment, the statement may be in terms of a system of weight or measure in common use in the country to which such shipment is exported. (2) A statement of weight or measure in the terms specified in paragraph (1) of this subsection may be supplemented by a statement in terms of the metric system of weight or measure. (3) Unless an unqualified statement of numerical count gives accurate information as to the quantity of food in the package, it shall be supplemented by such statement of weight, measure, or size of the individual units of the food as will give such information. (g) Statements shall contain only such fractions as are generally used in expressing the quantity of the food. A common fraction shall be reduced to its lowest terms; a decimal fraction shall not be carried out to more than two places. (h) (1) If the quantity of food in the package equals or exceeds the smallest unit of weight or measure which is specified in subsec. (f) of this section, and which is applicable to such food under the provisions of paragraph (e) (2) of this section, the statement shall express (except as provided in paragraph (2) of this subsection) the number of the largest of such units contained in the package (for example, the statement on the label of a package which contains one quart of food shall be "1 quart", and not "2 pints" or "32 fluid ounces".) Where such number is a whole number and a fraction, there may be substituted for the fraction its equivalent in smaller units, if any smaller unit is specified in such paragraph (f) (for example, 14 quarts may be expressed as "1 quart 1½ pints" or "1 quart 1 pint 8 fluid ounces"; 11/4 pounds may be expressed as "1 pound 4 ounces"). The stated number of any unit which is smaller than the largest unit (specified in such paragraph (f)) contained in the package shall not equal or exceed the number of such smaller units in the next larger unit so specified (for example, instead of "1 quart 16 fluid ounces" the statement shall be "12 quarts" or 1 quart 1 pint"; instead of "24 ounces" the statement shall be "11/2 pounds" or "1 pound 

8 ounces"). (2) In the case of a food with respect to which there exists an established custom of stating the quantity of the contents as a fraction of a unit, which unit is larger than the quantity con- 12

Ch. 

T.24 § 721-2 tained in the package, or as units smaller than the largest unit contained therein, the statement may be made in accordance with such custom if it is informative to consumers. (i) The statement shall express the minimum quantity, or the average quantity, of the contents of the package. If the statement is not so qualified as to show definitely that the quantity expressed is the minimum quantity, the statement shall be considered to mean the average quantity. (j) Where the statement expresses the minimum quantity, no variation below the stated minimum shall be permitted except variations below the stated weight or measure caused by ordinary and customary exposure, after the food is received from interstate commerce or introduced into commerce, to conditions which normally occur in good distribution practice and which unavoidably result in decreased weight or measure. Variations above the stated minimum shall not be unreasonably large. (k) Where the statement does not express the minimum quantity: (1) variations from the stated weight or measure shall be permitted when caused by ordinary and customary exposure, after the food is introduced into commerce, to conditions which normally occur in good distribution practice and which unavoidably result in change of weight or measure; (2) variations from the stated weight, measure, or numerical count shall be permitted when caused by unavoidable deviations in weighing, measuring, or counting individual packages which occur in good packing practice.

But under paragraph (2) of this subsection variations shall not be permitted to such extent that the average of the quantities in the packages comprising a shipment or other delivery of the food is below the quantity stated, and no unreasonable shortage in any package shall be permitted, even though overages in other packages in the same shipment or delivery compensate for such shortage. (1) The extent of variations from the stated quantity of the content permissible under subsecs. (j) and (k) of this section in the case of each shipment or other delivery shall be determined by the facts in such case. (m) A food shall be exempt from compliance with the requirement of sec. 11, paragraph (e) of the Act [24 L.P.R.A. § 721(e)] if: 13

T.§ 721-2 Ch. 51 

(1) the quantity of the contents, as expressed in terms applicable to such food under the provisions of paragraph (e) (2) of this section is less than one-half ounce avoirdupois, or less than one-half fluid ounce, or (in case the units of the food can be easily counted without opening the package) less than six units; or (2) the statement of the quantity of the contents of the package, together with all other words, statements, and information required by or under authority of the Act to appear on the label, cannot, because of insufficient label space, be so placed on the label as to comply with the requirements of sec. 11, para graph (f) of the Act [24 L.P.R.A. § 721 (f)] and regulations promulgated thereunder. 

§ 721-3. Conspicuousness of printing (24 L.P.R.A. § 721(f)) 

(a) A word, statement, or other information required by or under authority of the Act [24 L.P.R.A. §§ 711-732] to appear on the label may lack that prominence and conspicuousness required by sec. 11, paragraph (f) of the Act [24 L.P.R.A. § 711 (f)] by reason (among other reasons) of: (1) the failure of such word, statement or information to appear on the part or panel of the label which is presented or displayed under customary conditions of purchase; (2) the failure of such word, statement, or information to appear on two or more parts or panels of the label, each of which has sufficient space therefor, and each of which is so designed as to render it likely to be, under customary conditions of purchase, the part or panel displayed; (3) the failure of the label to extend over the area of the container or package available for such extension, so as to provide sufficient label space for the prominent placing of such word, statement, or information; (4) insufficiency of label space (for the prominent placing of such word, statement, or information) resulting from the use of label space for any word, statement, design, or device which is not required by or under authority of the Act to appear on the label; (5) insufficiency of label space (for the prominent placing of such word, statement, or information) resulting from the use of label space to give materially greater conspicuousness to any other word, statement, or information or to any design or device; or (6) smallness or style of type in which such word, statement 14

Ch. T.24 § 721-4 

or information appears, insufficient background contrast, obscuring designs or vignettes, or crowding with other written, printed, or graphic matter. (b) No exemption depending on insufficiency of label space, as prescribed in secs. 721-2 or 721-3 of this subchapter, shall apply if such insufficiency is caused by: (1) the use of label space for any word, statement, design, or device which is not required by or under authority of the Act to appear on the label; (2) the use of label space to give greater conspicuousness to any word, statement, or other information than is required by sec. 11, paragraph (f) of the Act [24 L.P.R.A. § 721 (f)]; or (3) the use of label space for any representation in a foreign language. (c) (1) All words, statements, and other information required by or under authority of the Act to appear on the label or labeling shall appear thereon in the English or Spanish language. (2) If the label contains any representation in a foreign language, all words, statements, and other information required by or under authority of the Act to appear on the label shall appear thereon in that foreign language. (3) If the labeling contains any representation in a foreign language, all words, statements, and other information required by or under authority of the Act to appear on the label or labeling shall appear on the labeling in that foreign language. 

§ 721-4. Name of ingredient (24 L.P.R.A. § 721(i)) 

(a) The name of an ingredient (except a spice, flavoring, or coloring which is an ingredient of a food other than one sold as a spice, flavoring, or coloring), required by sec. 11 (i) (2) of the

Act [24 L.P.R.A. § 721 (i) (2)] to be borne on the label of a food, shall be a specific name and not a collective name. But if an ingredient (which contains two or more ingredients) conforms to a definition and standard of identity prescribed by regulations under sec. 9 of the Act [24 L.P.R.A. § 719], such ingredient may be designated on the label of such food by the name specified in the definition and standard, supplemented, in case such regulations require the naming of optional ingredients present in such ingredient, by a statement showing the optional ingredients which are present in such ingredient. (b) No ingredient shall be designated on the label as a spice, 15

T.§ 721-4 Tr 

Ch. 51 flavoring, or coloring unless it is a spice, flavoring, or coloring, as the case may be, within the meaning of such term as commonly understood by consumers. The term "coloring" shall not include any bleaching substance. or (c) An ingredient which is both a spice and a coloring, or both a flavoring and a coloring, shall be designated as spice and coloring, or flavoring and coloring, as the case may be, unless such ingredient is designated by its specific name. (d) A label may be misleading by reason (among others) of: (1) the order in which the names of ingredients appear thereon, or the relative prominence otherwise given such names; (2) its failure to reveal the proportion of, or other fact with respect to, an ingredient, when such proportion or other fact is material in the light of the representation that such ingredient was used in fabricating the food. (e) (1) A food shall be exempt from the requirements of sec. 11, paragraph (i), clause (2) of the Act [24 L.P.R.A. § 721 (i) (2)] 

if all words, statements, and other information required by or under authority of the Act to appear on the label of such food cannot, because of insufficient label space, be so placed on the label as to comply with the requirements of sec. 11, paragraph (f) of the Act [24 L.P.R.A. § 721 (f)] and regulations promulgated thereunder. But such exemption shall be on the condition that, if the omission from the label of the statement of the quantity of the contents affords sufficient space to state legibly thereon all the information required by such clause (2), such statement of the quantity of the contents shall be omitted as authorized by paragraph (2) under subsec. (m) of sec. 721-2 of this subchapter, and the information required by such clause (2) shall be so stated as prominently as practicable even though the statement is not of such conspicuousness as to render it likely to be read by the ordinary individual under customary conditions of purchase. (2) In the case of an assortment of different items of food, when variations in the items which make up different packages packed from such assortment normally occur in good packing practice, and when such variations result in variations in the ingredients in different packages, such food shall be exempt from compliance with requirements of clause (2) of sec. 11, paragraph (i) of the Act [24 L.P.R.A. § 721 (i) (2)] with respect to any ingredient which is not common to all packages. But such exemption 16

Ch. 

T.24 § 721-5 shall be on the condition that the label shall bear, in conjunction with the names of such ingredients as are common to all packages, a statement in terms which are as informative as practicable and which are not misleading, indicating that other ingredients may be present. 

§ 721-5. Flavoring; coloring; preservatives (24 L.P.R.A. § 721(k)) 

(a) (1) The term "artificial flavoring" means a flavoring containing any sapid or aromatic constituent, which constituent was manufactured by a process of synthesis or other similar artifice. (2) The term "artificial coloring" means a coloring containing any dye or pigment, which dye or pigment was manufactured by a process of synthesis or other similar artifice, or a coloring which was manufactured by extracting a natural dye or natural pigment from a plant or other material in which such dye or pigment was naturally produced. (3) The term "chemical preservative" means any chemical which, when added to food, tends to prevent or retard deterioration thereof; but does not include common salt, sugars, vinegars, spices or oils extracted from spices, or substances added to food by direct exposure thereof to wood smoke. (b) A food which is subject to the requirements of sec. 11, paragraph (k) of the Act [24 L.P.R.A. § 721(k)] shall bear label ing, even though such food is not in package form. (c) A statement of artificial flavoring, artificial coloring, or chemical preservative shall be placed on the food, or on its container or wrapper; or on any two or all of these, as may be necessary to render such statement likely to be read by the ordinary individual under customary conditions of purchase and use of such food. (d) A food shall be exempt from compliance with the requirements of sec. 11, paragraph (k) of the Act [24 L.P.R.A. § 721 (k)] if it is not in package form and the units thereof are so small that a statement of artificial flavoring, artificial coloring, or chemical preservative, as the case may be, cannot be placed on such units with such conspicuousness as to render it likely to be read by the ordinary individual under customary conditions of purchase and use.

 § 724-1. Drugs and devices (24 L.P.R.A. § 724(b)) 

(a) The name by which a drug is designated shall be clearly distinguishing and differentiating from any name recognized in an official compendium unless such drug complies in identity with the identity prescribed in an official compendium under such recognized name. (b) The term "drug defined in an official compendium" means a drug having the identity prescribed for a drug in an official compendium. (c) A statement that a drug defined in an official compendium differs in strength, quality, or purity from the standard of strength, quality, or purity set forth for such drug in an official compendium shall show all the respects in which such drug so differs, and the extent of each such difference.
