§ 725-1. False or misleading labeling (24 L.P.R.A. § 725(a)) 

(a) Among representations in the labeling of a drug or device which render such drug or device misbranded is a false or misleading representation with respect to another drug or device or a food or cosmetic. (b) The labeling of a drug which contains two or more ingredients may be misleading by reason (among others) of the designation of such drug in such labeling by a name which includes or suggests the name of one or more but not all such ingredients, even though the names of all such ingredients are stated elsewhere in the labeling. 

§ 725-2. Information required on label (24 L.P.R.A. § 725(b)) 

(a) If a drug or device is not manufactured by the person whose name appears on the label, the name shall be qualified by a phrase which reveals the connection such person has with such drug or device, such as "Manufactured for and packed by - ", "Retailed by "Distributed by or other similar word or phrase which expresses the facts. 99 99 $200 18

Ch. T.24 § 725-2 

(b) The statement of the place of business shall include the street address, if any, of such place. (c) Where a person manufactures, packs, or distributes a drug or device at a place other than his principal place of business, the label may state the principal place of business in lieu of the actual place where each package of such drug or device was manufactured or packed or is to be distributed, if such statement is not misleading in any particular. (d) The requirement that the label shall contain the name and place of business of the manufacturer, packer, or distributor shall not be considered to relieve any drug or device from the requirement that its label shall not be misleading in any particular. (e) (1) The statement of the quantity of the contents of a package of a drug shall reveal the quantity of such drug in the package, exclusive of wrappers and other material packed with such drug. (2) The statement shall be expressed in the terms of weight, measure, numerical count, or a combination of numerical count and weight or measure, which are generally used by consumers and users of such drug to express quantity thereof and which give accurate information as to such quantity. But if no general usage in expressing accurate information as to the quantity of such drug exists among consumers and users thereof, the statement of the quantity of a drug which is not in tablet, capsule, ampul, or other unit form shall be in terms of weight if the drug is solid, semisolid or viscous, or in terms of measure if the drug is liquid; the statement of the quantity of a drug which is in such unit form shall be in terms of the numerical count of such units, supplemented, when necessary to give accurate information as to the quantity of such drug in the package, by such statement (in such terms, manner, and form as are not misleading) of the weight or measure of such units, or of the quantity of each active ingredient in each such unit, as will give such information. (3) The statement of the quantity of a device shall be expressed in terms of numerical count. (f) A statement of weight shall be in terms of the avoirdupois pound, ounce, and grain, or of the kilogram, gram, and milligram.

A statement of liquid measure shall be in terms of the United States gallon of 231 cubic inches and quart, pint, fluid ounce, and fluid dram subdivisions thereof, or of the liter, milliliter, or cubic centi- 

WILL 

19

T.§ 725-2 Ch. 51 

meter, and shall express the volume at 68° Fahrenheit (20° Centigrade). (g) Statements of the quantity of a drug shall contain only such fractions as are generally used in expressing the quantity of such drug. A common fraction shall be reduced to its lowest terms; a decimal fraction shall not be carried out to more than three places, except in the case of a statement of the quantity of an active ingredient in a unit of a drug. (h) (1) Unless made in accordance with the provisions of paragraph (2) of this subsection, a statement of the quantity of a drug, in the terms of weight or measure applicable to such drug under the provisions of paragraph (e) (2) of this section, shall express the number of the largest unit specified in subsection (f) of this section which is contained in the package (for example, the statement on the label of a package which contains one pint of a drug shall be "1 pint", and not "16 fluid ounces"). Where such number is a whole number and a fraction, there may be substituted for the fraction its equivalent in smaller units, if any smaller unit is specified in such subsection (f) (for example, 14 pounds may be expressed as "1 pound 4 ounces"). The stated number of any unit which is smaller than the largest unit (specified in such subsection (f)) contained in the package shall not equal or exceed the number of such smaller units in the next larger unit so specified (for example, instead of "1 quart 16 fluid ounces" the statement shall be "112 quarts" or "1 quart 1 pint"). (2) In the case of a drug with respect to which there exists an established custom of stating the quantity of the contents as a fraction of a unit, which unit is larger than the quantity contained in the package, or as units smaller than the largest unit contained therein, the statement may be made in accordance with such custom if it is informative to consumers. (i) The statement of the quantity of a drug or device shall express the minimum quantity, or the average quantity, of the contents of the packages. If the statement is not so qualified as to show definitely that the quantity expressed is the minimum quantity, the statement, except in the case of ampuls, shall be considered to express the average quantity. The statement of the quantity of a drug in ampuls shall be considered to mean the minimum quantity. (j) Where the statement expresses the minimum quantity, no variation below the stated minimum shall be permitted except 20

Ch. T.24 § 725-2 

variations below the stated weight or measure of a drug caused by ordinary and customary exposure, after such drug is introduced into commerce, to conditions which normally occur in good distribution practice and which unavoidably result in decreased weight or measure. Variations above the stated minimum shall not be unreasonably large. In the case of a liquid drug in ampuls the variation above the stated measure shall comply with the excess volume prescribed by any official compendium for filling of ampuls. (k) Where the statement does not express the minimum quantity: (1) variations from the stated weight or measure of a drug shall be permitted when caused by ordinary and customary exposure, after such drug is introduced into commerce, to conditions which normally occur in good distribution practice and which unavoidably result in change of weight or measure; (2) variations from the stated weight, measure, or numerical count of a drug or device shall be permitted when caused by unavoidable deviations in weighing, measuring, or counting the contents of individual packages which occur in good packing practices. But under this paragraph variations shall not be permitted to such extent that the average of the quantities in the packages comprising a shipment or other delivery of the drug or device is below the quantity stated and no unreasonable shortage in any package shall be permitted, even though overages in other packages in the same shipment or delivery compensate for such shortage. (1) The extent of variations from the stated quantity of the contents permissible under subsecs. (j) and (k) of this section in the case of each shipment or other delivery shall be determined by the facts in such case. (m) A drug or device shall be exempt from compliance with the requirements of clause (2) of sec. 15, paragraph (b) of the Act 

[24 L.P.R.A. § 725 (b) (2)] if: 

(1) the statement of the quantity of the contents, as expressed in terms applicable to such drug or device under the provisions of paragraph (e) (2) of this section, together with all other words, statements, and information required by or under authority of the Act, to appear on the label of such drug or device, cannot because of insufficient label be so placed on the labels as to comply with the requirements of sec. 15, paragraph (c) of the Act [24 

L.P.R.A. § 725 (c)] and regulations promulgated thereunder; or 21

T.§ 725-2 

Ch. 51 (2) the quantity of the contents of the package, as expressed in terms of numerical count in compliance with paragraphs (e) (2) or (3) of this section, is less than six units, and such units can be easily counted without opening the package. 

§ 725-3. Conspicuousness (24 L.P.R.A. § 725(c)) 

(a) A word, statement, or other information required by or under authority of the Act to appear on the label may lack that prominence and conspicuousness required by sec. 15, paragraph (c) of the Act [24 L.P.R.A. § 725 (c)] by reason (among others) of: 

(1) the failure of such word, statement, or information to appear on two or more parts or panels of the label, each of which displayed under customary conditions of purchase; (2) the failure of such word, statement, or information to appear on two or more parts or panels of the label, each of which has sufficient space therefor, and each of which is so designed as to render it likely to be, under customary conditions of purchase, the part of panel displayed; (3) the failure of the label to extend over the area of the container or package available for such extension, so as to provide sufficient label space for the prominent placing of such word, statement, or information; (4) insufficiency of label space (for the prominent placing of such word, statement, or information) resulting from the use of label space for any word, statement, design, or device which is not required by or under authority of the Act to appear on the label; (5) insufficiency of label space (for the prominent placing of such word, statement, or information) resulting from the use of label space to give materially greater conspicuousness to any other word, statement, or information, or to any design or device; or (6) smallness or style of type in which such word, statement, or information appears, insufficient background contrast, obscuring designs or vignettes, or crowding with other written, printed, or graphic matter. (b) No exemption depending on insufficiency of label space, as prescribed in regulations promulgated under sec. 15, paragraphs (b) or (e) of the Act [24 L.P.R.A. § 725 (b), (e)], shall apply if such insufficiency is caused by: (1) the use of label space for any word, statement, design, or device which is not required by or under authority of the Act to appear on the label; 22

Ch. T.24 § 725-4 

(2) the use of label space to give greater conspicuousness to any word, statement, or other information than is required by sec. 15, paragraph (c) of the Act [24 L.P.R.A. § 725 (c)]; or 

(3) the use of label space for any representation in a foreign language. (c) (1) All words, statements, and other information required by or under authority of the Act to appear on the label or labeling shall appear thereon in the English or Spanish language. (2) If the label contains any representation in a foreign language, all words, statements, and other information required by or under authority of the Act to appear on the label shall appear thereon in that foreign language. (3) If the labeling contains any representation in a foreign language, all words, statements, and other information required by or under authority of the Act to appear on the label or labeling shall appear on the labeling in that foreign language. § 725-4. Habit-forming drugs (24 L.P.R.A. § 725(d)) (a) (1) The name of a substance or derivative required by or under authority of sec. 15, paragraph (d) of the Act [24 L.P.R.A. § 725 (d)] to be borne on the label of a drug shall be the name by which such substance is designated in such sec. 15, paragraph (d), or such derivative is designated in regulations promulgated thereunder. (2) A statement on the label of a drug of the name of a constituent, which constituent is a chemical derivative of a substance named in sec. 15, paragraph (d) of the Act, shall show the substance from which such constituent is derived and that such constituent is a derivative thereof. (b) (1) If the drug is in tablet, capsule, ampul, or other unit form, the statement of the quantity or proportion of such substance or derivative contained therein shall express the weight or measure of such substance or derivative in a specified unit of weight or measure of the drug. Such statement shall be in terms which are informative to the ordinary consumer and user of the drug. (2) The statement of the percentage of such substance or derivative contained in a drug shall express the percentage by weight; except that, if both the substance or derivative and the drug are liquid, the statement may express the percentage by volume at 68° Fahrenheit (20° Centigrade), but in such case the 23

T.§ 725-4 Ch. 51 

statement shall be so qualified as to show definitely that the percentage is expressed by volume. (c) The names, and quantities or proportions of all such substances and derivatives, and the statement "Warning May be habit forming", shall immediately precede or immediately follow (without intervening written, printed, or graphic matter) the name by which such drug is titled in the part or panel of the label thereof which is presented or displayed under customary conditions of purchase. 

(d) A drug shall not be considered to be misbranded under sec. 

15, paragraph (d) of the Act [24 L.P.R.A. § 725 (d)] by reason of failure of its label to bear the statement "Warning - May be habit forming", if such drug is not suitable for internal use and is distributed and sold exclusively for such external use as involves no possibility of habit formation. § 725-5. Drug not designated by recognized name (24 L.P.R.A. § 725(e)) (a) (1) The name of an ingredient, substance, derivative, or preparation required by clause (2) of sec. 15, paragraph (e) of the Act [24 L.P.R.A. § 725 (e)] to be borne on the label of a drug shall be the name thereof which is listed in such clause (2) of sec. 15, paragraph (e) of the Act, or, if not so listed, shall be a specific name and not a collective name. But if an ingredient is an article the name of which is recognized in an official compendium and such article complies with the specifications set forth therefor in such compendium, such ingredient may be designated on the label of such drug by the common or usual name under which such specifications are so set forth. (2) Where an ingredient contains a substance the quantity or proportion of which is required by sec. 15, paragraph (a), clause 2 of the Act to appear on the label, and such ingredient is not a derivative or preparation of such substance, as defined in subsec. (b)(1) of this section, the label shall bear, in conjunction with the name of the ingredient, a statement of the quantity or proportion of such substance in such drug. (3) An abbreviation or chemical formula shall not be considered to be a common or usual name. The name "acetophenetidin" shall be considered to be the same as the name "acetphenetidin”, "aminopyrine" the same as "amidopyrine". The name "alcohol", without qualification, means ethyl alcohol. 24

Ch. 

T.24 § 725-5 (b) (1) A derivative or preparation of a substance named in clause (2), sec. 15, paragraph (e) of the Act is an article which is derived or prepared from such substance by any method, including actual or theoretical chemical action. (2) A statement on the label of a drug of the name of an ingredient thereof, which ingredient is a derivative or preparation of a substance named in clause (2), sec. 15, paragraph (e) of the 

Act, shall show the substance from which such ingredient is derived or prepared and that such ingredient is a derivative or preparation thereof. (c) (1) If the drug is in tablet, capsule, ampul, or other unit form, the statement of the quantity or proportion of a substance, derivative, or preparation contained therein shall express the weight or measure of such substance, derivative, or preparation in each such unit. If the drug is not in such unit form the statement shall express the weight or measure of such substance, derivative, or preparation in a specified unit of a weight or measure of the drug, or the percentage of such substance, derivative, or preparation in such drug. Such statement shall be in terms which are informative to the ordinary consumer and user of the drug. (2) A statement of the percentage of alcohol shall express the percentage of absolute alcohol by volume at 60° Fahrenheit (15.56° 

Centigrade). A statement of the percentage of a substance, derivative, or preparation other than alcohol shall express the percentage by weight; except that, if both the substances, derivative, or preparation and the drug containing it are liquid, the statement may express the percentage by volume at 68° Fahrenheit (20° 

Centigrade), but in such case the statement shall be so qualified as to show definitely that the percentage is expressed by volume. (d) In case a statement of the quantity or proportion of a derivative or preparation in a drug is not as informative, to consumers or users of such drug, of the activity or consequences of use thereof as a statement of the quantity or proportion of the substance from which such derivative or preparation is derived or prepared, the quantity or proportion of such substance shall also be stated on the label of such drug. (e) A label of a drug may be misleading by reason (among others) of: (1) the order in which the names of ingredients, substances, derivatives, or preparations appear thereon, or the relative prominence otherwise given such names; or 25

T.§ 725-5 Ch. 51 

(2) its failure to reveal the proportion of, or other fact with respect to, an ingredient, substance, derivative, or preparation, when such proportion or other fact is material in the light of the representation that such ingredient, substance, derivative, or preparation is a constituent of such drug. (f) (1) A drug shall be exempt from the requirements of sec. 

15, paragraph (e), clause (2) of the Act if all words, statements, and other information required by or under authority of the Act to appear on the label of such drug cannot, because of insufficient label space, be so placed on the label as to comply with the requirements of sec. 15, paragraph (c) of the Act [24 L.P.R.A. § 725 (c)] and regulations promulgated thereunder. But such exemption shall be on the condition that, if the omission from the label of the statement of the quantity of the contents affords sufficient space to state legibly thereon all the information required by such clause (2), such statement of the quantity of the contents shall be omitted as authorized by subsec. (m) of sec. 725-2 of this title, and the information required by such clause (2) shall be so stated as prominently as practicable even though the statement is not of such conspicuousness as to render it likely to be read by the ordinary individual under customary conditions of purchase. (2) A drug shall be exempt from the requirements of clause (2), of sec. 15, paragraph (e) of the Act with respect to the alkaloids atropine, hyoscine or hyoscyamine contained in such drug, if such alkaloid is contained therein as a constituent of belladonna, hyoscyamus, scopola, stramonium, or other plant material, or any preparation thereof, which was used as an ingredient of such drug, and no practical and accurate method of analysis exists for the quantitative determination of each such alkaloid in such ingredient. But such exemption shall be on the condition that the label of such drug shall state the quantity or proportion of total alkaloids contained therein as constituents of such ingredient. 

§ 725-6. Directions for use, warnings (24 L.P.R.A. § 725(f)) 

(a) Directions for use shall include quantity of dose. Where it is deemed to be in the interest of the public health for the protection of the consumer, directions shall also include specification of: (1) directions for use in all conditions for which such drug or device is prescribed, recommended, or suggested in its labeling, 26

Ch. 

T.24 § 725-6 or in its advertising disseminated or sponsored by or on behalf of its manufacturer or packer, or in such other conditions, if any there be, for which such drug or device is commonly and effectively used; (If no specific claims are made for a drug, which would require complete directions with limitations for use under certain conditions, etc., a label covering the commonly accepted usage will be acceptable. Directions for use should be sufficiently adequate in all cases so as to reduce the necessity for special warning statements.) (2) quantity of dose (including quantities for persons of different ages and different physical conditions); (3) frequency and duration of administration or application; (4) time of administration or application (in relation to time of meals, time of onset of symptoms, or other time factors); (5) route or method of administration or application; or (6) preparation for use (shaking, dilution, adjustment of temperature, or other manipulation or process). (b) A shipment or other delivery of a drug or device shall be exempt from compliance with the requirements of clause (1), sec. 15, paragraph (f) of the Act [24 L.P.R.A. § 725 (f)]: 

(1) provided that the label of such drug or device bears the statement "Caution: To be used only by or on the prescription of a (the blank to be filled in by the word "Physician", "Dentist", or "Veterinarian"), and provided, further, that such drug or device is not a drug or device which is commonly sold or intended by the producer to be sold at retail direct to the consumer, and provided, further, that such drug or device is not sold except on the prescription of a physician, dentist or veterinarian. (2) if the label of such drug or device bears the statement "To be used only for manufacturing or compounding drugs or by or on the prescription of a physician, dentist or veterinarian, if sold as a drug". 

(The regulations exempt chemicals which are used both as drugs and for technical purposes from the drug labeling provisions if sold for technical purposes only, when such chemicals are labeled "For technical use not for medicinal use". The designation "For technical use" is not sufficient to exempt a product from the drug regulations. This statement should appear in company with the phrase "not for medicinal use".)

§ 726-3. Exemptions (24 L.P.R.A. § 726 (c)) 

A shipment or other delivery of a new drug shall be exempt from the operation of sec. 16, paragraph (a) of the Act [24 

L.P.R.A. § 726(a)] if: 

(1) the label of such drug bears the statement "For investigational use only"; (2) such shipment or delivery is made only to, and solely for investigational use by, an expert qualified by scientific training and experience to investigate the safety of drugs; and (3) The person who introduced such shipment or delivery into commerce holds a signed statement from such expert to the effect that he has adequate facilities for the investigation to be conducted by him, and that such drug will be used solely by him or under 28

Ch. T.24 § 728-2 

his direction for the investigation, unless and until an application under sec. 16, paragraph (b) of the Act [24 L.P.R.A. § 726 (b)] 

becomes effective with respect to such drug.

Subchapter 727. Cosmetic Adulteration SECTIONS 727-1. Adulteration (24 L.P.R.A. § 727(a)) § 727-1. Adulteration (24 L.P.R.A. § 727(a)) 

The term "coal-tar hair dye" includes all articles containing any coal-tar color or intermediate product which color or product alters the color of the hair when such articles are applied to the hair under the conditions of use prescribed in the labeling thereof; or under such conditions of use as are customary or usual. 

Subchapter 728. Cosmetic Misbranding SECTIONS 728-1. False or misleading representations (24 L.P.R.A. § 728(a)) 728-2. Label (24 L.P.R.A. § 728(b)) 728-3. Conspicuousness (24 L.P.R.A. § 728 (c)) § 728-1. False or misleading representations (24 L.P.R.A. § 

728(a)) (a) Among representations in the labeling of a cosmetic which render such cosmetic misbranded is a false or misleading representation with respect to another cosmetic or a food, drug, or device. (b) The labeling of a cosmetic which contains two or more ingredients may be misleading by reason (among others) of the designation of such cosmetic in such labeling by a name which includes or suggests the name of one or more but not all such ingredients, even though the names of all such ingredients are stated elsewhere in the labeling. 

§ 728-2. Label (24 L.P.R.A. § 728(b)) 

(a) If a cosmetic is not manufactured by the person whose name appears on the label, the name shall be qualified by a phrase which reveals the connection such person has with such cosmetic, such as "Manufactured for and packed by -", "Distributed by -", or other similar phrase which expresses the facts. (b) The statement of the place of business shall include the street address, if any, of such place. 29

T.§ 728-2 

Ch. 51

(c) Where a person manufactures, packs, or distributes a cosmetic at a place other than his principal place of business he shall indicate the place where such cosmetic was manufactured or packed or is to be distributed, if such indication is not misleading in any particular. (d) The requirement that the label shall contain the name and place of business and post-office address of the manufacturer, packer, or distributor shall not be considered to relieve any cosmetic from the requirement that its label shall not be misleading in any particular. (e) (1) The statement of the quantity of the contents shall reveal the quantity of cosmetic in the package, exclusive of wrappers and other material packed with such cosmetic. (2) The statement shall be expressed in terms of weight, measure, numerical count, or a combination of numerical count and weight or measure, which are generally used by consumers to express quantity of such cosmetic and which give accurate information as to the quantity thereof. But if no general consumer usage in expressing accurate information as to the quantity of such cosmetic exists, the statement shall be in terms of liquid measure if the cosmetic is liquid, or in terms of weight if the cosmetic is solid, semisolid, or viscous, or in such terms of numerical count, or numerical count and weight or measure, as will give accurate information as to the quantity of the cosmetic in the package. (f) (1) A statement of weight shall be in terms of the avoirdupois pound and ounce. A statement of liquid measure shall be in terms of the United States gallon of 231 cubic inches and quart, pint, and fluid ounce subdivisions thereof, and shall express the volume at 68° Fahrenheit (20° Centigrade). However, in the case of an export shipment, the statement may be in terms of a system of weight or measure in common use in the country to which such shipment is exported. (2) A statement of weight or measure in the terms specified in paragraph (1) of this subsection may be supplemented by a statement in terms of the metric system of weight or measure. (3) Unless an unqualified statement of numerical count gives accurate information as to the quantity of cosmetic in the package, it shall be supplemented by such statement of weight, measure, or size of the individual units of the cosmetic as will give such information. 30

Ch. T.24 § 728-2 

(g) Statements shall contain only such fractions as are generally used in expressing the quantity of the cosmetic. A common fraction shall be reduced to its lowest terms; a decimal fraction shall not be carried out to more than two places. (h) (1) If the quantity of cosmetic in the package equals or exceeds the smallest unit of weight or measure which is specified in subsec. (f) of this section, and which is applicable to such cosmetic under the provisions of paragraph (e) (2) of this section, the statement shall express the number of the largest of such units contained in the package (for example, the statement on the label of a package which contains one pint of cosmetic shall be "1 pint" and not "16 fluid ounces"), unless the statement is made in accordance with the provisions of paragraph (2) of this subsection. 

Where such number is a whole number and a fraction, there may be substituted for the fraction its equivalent in smaller units, if any smaller unit is specified in such subsec. (f) (for example, 1¾ quarts may be expressed as "1 quart 1½ pints" or "1 quart 1 pint 

8 fluid ounces"; 114 pounds may be expressed as "1 pound 4 ounces"). The stated number of any unit which is smaller than the largest unit (specified in such subsec. (f)) contained in the package shall not equal or exceed the number of such smaller units in the next larger unit so specified (for example, instead of "1 quart 16 fluid ounces" the statement shall be "112 quarts" or "1 quart 1 pint"; instead of "24 ounces" the statement shall be "11½ pounds" or "1 pound 8 ounces"). (2) In the case of a cosmetic with respect to which there exists an established custom of stating the quantity of the contents as a fraction of a unit, which unit is larger than the quantity contained in the package, or as units smaller than the largest unit contained therein, the statement may be made in accordance with such custom if it is informative to consumers. (i) The statement shall express the minimum quantity, or the average quantity, of the contents of the packages. If the statement is not so qualified as to show definitely that the quantity expressed is the minimum quantity, the statement shall be considered to mean the average quantity. (j) Where the statement expresses the minimum quantity, no variation below the stated minimum shall be permitted except variations below the stated weight or measure caused by ordinary and customary exposure, after the cosmetic is received from interstate commerce, or introduced into intrastate commerce, to conditions 31

T.§ 728-2 

(C 

Ch. 51 which normally occur in good distribution practice and which unavoidably result in decreased weight or measure. Variations above the stated minimum shall not be unreasonably large. (k) Where the statement does not express the minimum quantity: (1) variation from the stated weight or measure shall be permitted when caused by ordinary and customary exposure, after the cosmetic is received from interstate commerce, or introduced into intrastate commerce, to conditions which normally occur in good distribution practice and which unavoidably result in change of weight or measure; (2) variations from the stated weight, measure, or numerical count shall be permitted when caused by unavoidable deviations in weighing, measuring, or counting individual packages which occur in good packing practice. But under this paragraph, variations shall not be permitted to such extent that the average of the quantities in the packages comprising a shipment or other delivery of the cosmetic is below the quantity stated, and no unreasonable shortage in any package shall be permitted, even though overages in other packages in the same shipment or delivery compensate for such shortage. (1) The extent of variations from the stated quantity of the contents permissible under subsecs. § 728-3. Conspicuousness (24 L.P.R.A. § 728 (c)) 

(a) A word, statement, or other information required by or under authority of the Act to appear on the label may lack that prominence and conspicuousness required by sec. 18, paragraph 

(c) of the Act [24 L.P.R.A. § 728 (c)] by reason (among others) 

of: 32

Ch. 

T.24 § 728-3 (1) the failure of such word, statement, or information to appear on the part or panel of the label which is presented or displayed under customary conditions of purchase; (2) the failure of such word, statement, or information to appear on two or more parts or panels of the label, each of which has sufficient space therefor, and each of which is so designed as to render it likely to be, under customary conditions of purchase, the part or panel displayed; (3) the failure of the label to extend over the area of the container or package available for such extension, so as to provide sufficient label space for the prominent placing of such word, statement, or information; (4) insufficiency of label space (for the prominent placing of such word, statement, or information) resulting from the use of label space for any word, statement, design, or device which is not required by or under authority of the Act to appear on the label; (5) insufficiency of label space (for the prominent placing of such word, statement, or information) resulting from the use of label space to give materially greater conspicuousness to any other word, statement, or information, or to any design or device; or (6) smallness or style of type in which such word, statement, or information appears, insufficient background contrast, obscuring designs or vignettes, or crowding with other written, printed, or graphic matter. (b) (1) All words, statements, and other information required. by or under authority of the Act to appear on the label or labeling shall appear thereon in the English or Spanish language. (2) If the label contains any representation in a foreign language, all words, statements, and other information required by or under authority of the Act to appear on the label shall appear thereon in that foreign language. § 730-2. Taking and examination of samples 

To determine the degree of purity, the condition, the nature, or the correct labeling of any food or drug to be considered under this Division, samples shall be taken free of charge by the food and drug inspectors, or by the sanitation inspectors, or by any officer of the Department authorized by the 

Such samples shall be examined in the corresponding laboratory of the Department of Health. 

§ 730-3. Preparation of samples 

Unopened original containers from the manufacturer will be preferred, but in unusual cases an aliquot part representative of the average may be collected, and in either case such samples shall be packed or bottled and firmly closed and shall be sealed according to the following instructions:

They shall be corked, covered again with cloth and under this cloth the folded copy of the label on the flask shall be placed and the cloth shall be firmly fastened with string and over the latter shall be applied sealing wax and the two seals described further on. One of the ends of the cloth shall be pulled tight and fastened with sealing wax to the glass wall of the container and the inspector's seal shall be impressed on it. If the sample is solid or in the form of a powder or grease, the container shall be wrapped with paper, causing the ends of the wrapping paper to overlap one over the other, so the knot can be tied over this point; sealing wax shall be applied and the two seals mentioned further on shall be impressed on it. Each of the three units collected shall carry two labels or coupons: The first one folded four times and placed under the cloth cover or the wrapping paper, as the case may be; the second one glued to the exterior surface of the sample or container. $ 730-4. Printed forms

The printed forms sent with the samples shall be signed by the officer who has taken them. Three printed forms shall be filled out, an original and two copies. The original and one copy shall be sent with the package; the inspector shall keep the other copy. 35

T.§ 730-4 

Ch. 51

By package we mean the box or cover with which the samples that are to be shipped by express or mail are protected. case. § 730-5. Sealing sample without wax

It is understood that if for any reason the inspector cannot get the necessary materials to seal with wax a sample and affix his seal to it, he shall use the following procedure to seal the sample:

If the sample is in the liquid form, each flask or bottle shall be corked, it shall be covered again with cloth, and under this the folded copy of the label on the flask shall be placed and the cloth. shall be firmly fastened with string. The cloth covering shall be cut off around the edges leaving an edge of approximately onefourth inch. Over the cloth covering and part of the bottle neck shall be glued the strip of paper having impressed on it the seal of the Department of Health, giving the paper strip a light spirallike inclination so that it covers well a part of the glass surface of the neck and a part of the surface of the cloth. The sample serial number shall be written by hand with pen and ink on the edge of the paper strip, in such a way that the three initials are partially written on the cloth, that is, that half of each letter of the three initials shall be impressed on the paper strip and the cloth. The initials of the inspector shall appear on the lower part of the paper strip with the seal of the Department and they shall be written in the same way as the serial number, that is, part on the paper and part on the cloth. The inspector will ask the concerned person to write down his initials if he wishes to do so. The initial letters shall appear at the upper part and shall not be printed, but written the regular way, so that the initial letters shall guarantee the genuineness of the sample, and prevent the alteration or removal of the paper bond by another person and to prevent the contents of the sample from being substituted or changed.

If the sample is a solid or in the form of a powder or grease, the container will be wrapped in paper, causing the ends of the paper wrapping to overlap one over the other, so that over this point can be knotted the string that fastens the wrapping, and the printed paper band be glued. The rule in the preceding paragraph concerning the manner in which the serial numbers and the inspector's initials shall be written shall be strictly applied in this 36

Ch. T.24 § 730-10 

 § 730-6. Printed forms as evidence 

The printed forms filled out by the officers and their witnesses shall be part of the documentary proof to be presented before the courts of justice in the cases taken for their consideration. The inspectors shall abstain from appearing before the courts without such documentary proof. 

§ 730-7. Seals of business establishments, etc. 

The owners of dairy farms, milk depots, milk stalls, coffee grinding mills, business establishments, independent milk carriers, etc., shall provide themselves with distinctive seals, similar and not bigger than those used by the Department of Health; both shall be impressed by the government officer, one each side of the cloth covering the neck of the bottles or on the opposite sides of the packages. Such private seals shall be previously registered at the 

Department of Health. Any person, firm, or corporation who does not fulfill this requisite signifies that he renounces a right offered to him by law for the security and protection of his business. 

§ 730-8. Legibility of labels and names 

Labels shall be filled out with clear and legible writing. Proper names shall be printed. All proper names (including that of the inspector) that appear on the printed form shall include the complete Christian name and all surnames. The initials for the identification of the sample shall correspond exactly with the signature of the inspector. 

§ 730-9. Number of samples 

Official samples shall be taken at least in triplicate, a larger number being permitted if necessary, one of them being delivered to the person concerned and the others sent to the Department of 

Health for the pertinent investigation of the case. The informal samples called "investigation samples" are for the orientation of the laboratories concerned and shall consist of one unit, but shall be taken in triplicate if an order is given later on to take an official sample. 

§ 730-10. Notice of adulteration, etc. 

When from the examination, analysis, or investigation of a sample it occurs that, in the judgment of the Department, adulteration, contamination, or misbranding exist, or in some way the food 37

T.§ 730-10 Ch. 51 

or drug is not fit for public consumption, the person concerned shall be notified warning him that if he wants to verify the examination, analysis, or investigation of the official sample in his possession, it shall be done within the term specified in the warning and according to what is later provided for. 

§ 730-11. Term for verifying analysis 

In the case of milk adulteration, the verifying analysis, if so requested by the interested party, shall be performed within a term of 10 days from the time that the person, in whose name the sample of milk was collected, is duly notified of the adulteration; provided, that, in meritorious cases, and if good reasons are presented, this period can be extended for 5 additional days. Verifying analysis shall never be performed after 15 days of the notification of the adulteration or in the case that the milk is acid. 

The term for verifying analysis for nonperishable food products shall be 20 days from the time that the adulteration notification is presented to the interested person. But this term can be extended for 10 additional days provided the above-mentioned conditions prevail.

§ 730-12. Application for analysis of third sample 

Every person from whom a sample of food or drug has been taken which turned out to be adulterated and whose original analysis would not coincide with that of the duplicate sample. examined by his technician, in case he wants to ask for the verification examination on the third sample, must do it in writing and through his lawyer, his technician, or by himself, addressing it to the "Secretary of Health, San Juan, Puerto Rico." 

§ 730-13. Contents of application 

The concerned person shall state in his application that he is the person from whom the sample was taken or that it was taken. from his employee or representative, specifying the initials of the inspector, the serial number, the date on which the sample 38

Ch. 

T.24 § 730-16 was taken, and the name of the substance or material taken. Provided, that if such concerned person should delegate his representation to a lawyer or technician the application referred to shall be jointly signed by the petitioner and his representative; provided, further, that the technician to whom the representation is delegated shall be a technician authorized by the laws of Puerto Rico. 

§ 730-14. Causes for verification analysis 

No verification analysis shall be run without a reasonable cause, for which it is required that the petitioner shall base his petition on one of the following causes: (1) That it has been corroborated that the sample is within the official standard, and that it is only adulterated in appearance. (2) That the sample appears within the official standard and it is not adulterated. (3) That the sample is neither within the official standard, nor adulterated. (4) That the sample is not within the official standard and it is only adulterated in appearance. (5) That there is an analytical or technical error in the original investigation practiced. $ 730-15. Order for examination

In view of the claims made according to sec. 730-14, the Secretary of Health will order, if he thinks it is justified, the verification examination asked for, in which case the Director of the Bureau of Chemistry of the Department of Health shall appoint the date and hour for it to be performed and shall notify the petitioner or his representative in writing. § 730-16. Procedure; filing of original reports

The verification examinations on the samples shall be run in the presence of the director of the corresponding laboratory, or the officer delegated by him, the concerned person being allowed to be represented by a technician commissioned by him for that purpose. In such case it shall be a previous indispensable condition that the technician of the concerned person submit a copy of the report on the analysis practiced by him on the sample, which had been left in possession of such concerned person, which, with the analytical data, basis and conclusions of the technician, shall be presented by him before the said director or his delegate, in a 39

T.§ 730-16 

Ch. 51 closed envelope, sealed with wax, and stamped, which shall be filed by the latter. The said director or his delegate shall also file the result of the examination of the original sample with its basis and conclusions in a closed envelope, sealed with wax. § 730-17. Participation of technicians; memoranda

The technician of the petitioner shall witness the analysis practiced by the chemist of the Department during the administrative investigation to be carried out by the Bureau of Chemistry for verification purposes. The intervention of the said technician will be circumscribed: (1) to observing closely the process of analysis, of which he will take notes and may call the attention of the government chemist to any detail of interest to him and which he understands will affect the person he represents; (2) to raising any reasonable question or submitting any appropriate suggestion in relation to the investigation being practiced; (3) if he deems it convenient for his security, he may state his differences of opinion and observations in the sealed memorandum, which with an extra copy shall be filed in the laboratory, and such memorandum shall be prepared separately from the report of the verification analysis to be signed jointly by both technicians. The 

Director of the Bureau of Chemistry of the Department, or his delegate, will state his observations, if he wishes, in a separate memorandum which he shall close, seal with wax, and file, and shall supply a copy of to the petitioner or his representative. That which has been previously stated shall not prevent the chemists of both parties from preparing personal notations to refresh their memories when testifying as expert witnesses, and in this case it will not be compulsory to exchange the copies of the same. 

§ 730-18. Report on verification analysis 

The report on the verification analysis shall be signed jointly by both technicians noting separately any difference of opinion which may exist. This joint report of the concerned person and the Government, with the report of the technician for the concerned person and the technician for the Government, shall be part of the documental proof to be submitted to court. In the cases of adulteration, contamination or misbranding, in which no verifying analysis was practiced, the director of the corresponding laboratory, or his delegate, shall state his conclusions in a report 40

Ch. T.24 § 730-20 

which will be part of the proof of the people before the court. In this case, the analytical data shall be set aside to be submitted in open court, except in case of a judicial order to the contrary. 

§ 730-19. Official methods of analysis 

The official methods of analysis shall be: (1) those of the United States Pharmacopoeia in effect at the date of the investigation for the official medical preparations; 

(2) those of the Association of Official Agricultural Chemists of the United States, for foods and drugs when the latter are not official; (3) those of the United States Public Health Service; (4) otherwise, those from reference works of recognized authorities. 

§ 730-20. Warranties 

For the purposes of protection, the consumer may obtain, and it shall be valid, a warranty contained in the same invoice, duly subscribed by the manufacturer, agent, representative, distributor, importer, wholesaler, or retailer from whom the article has been obtained, stating that it is not adulterated, contaminated, or misbranded, such warranty expressing clearly the quantity of each part, the name of the article, the trademark and any other details which may serve for its identification. Warranties on labels shall not be valid. 

The following will be considered as a pattern for a warranty: "I/we, the subscriber (s), hereby guarantee that the items (food or drugs) enumerated in this invoice (if it is in a separate sheet, the articles should be stated in detail, as above explained) are not adulterated, contaminated, or misbranded according to the provi sions of the 'Food, Drug and Cosmetic Act of Puerto Rico'.

 § 730-21. Dangerous articles 

Adequate and honest labeling shall not exempt from responsibility the manufacturer or seller of an article, if, by the nature of the same, it is deleterious to health or human life, it being understood that the sale of any substance dangerous to health is absolutely prohibited. § 730-22. Preservative substance for food

If some food contains a preservative substance applied externally for its conservation which would not affect at all the nature of such food, it shall be labeled with clear and explicit instructions for its removal. § 730-23. Denaturalization or destruction of merchandise 

Denaturalization for industrial use shall be instituted or the merchandise shall be definitely destroyed when so ordered by the court concerned, or beforehand, if the concerned person consents to it; provided, nevertheless, that when an article is found in such a state of decomposition or putrefaction that its immediate destruction is necessary for the protection of the public health, it shall be done, collecting a written consent subscribed by the merchant or industrialist, or otherwise, a record of the proceedings shall be made in the presence of two witnesses of good reputation who will subscribe the act. § 730-24. Reports of poisoning or intoxication 

When any case of poisoning or intoxication occurs, it shall be investigated and the following shall be reported: (1) Number of intoxicated people. (2) Number of people who ingested the food. (3) Time elapsed before the first symptoms appeared. (4) Which were the most important symptoms. (5) Duration of the same, and time that the subsequent illness lasted. (6) If any death occurred, and if any autopsy was performed, the conclusions subscribed by the physician shall be submitted. (7) Grounds or observations on which are based the suspicion that the material sampled was the cause of the intoxication. (8) Any other detail that in the judgment of the officer will help to clarify the cause of the poisoning or intoxication. 42

All meat, fish, vegetables, fruits, and other prepared foodstuffs intended for human consumption shall be kept, stored, and transported at all times in flyproof and dustproof compartments or containers in such manner as to prevent contamination by dust, or by flies or other insects and to prevent handling by patrons or prospective purchasers. All such meat, fish, vegetables, fruits, and other prepared foodstuffs kept, sold, or offered for sale, shall be maintained in receptacles free from decayed matter of all kinds.

Ch. 51 § 730-102. Exposure for sale

When exposed for sale in the open air such meat, fish, vegetables, fruits, and other prepared foodstuffs shall be displayed on a shelf or platform at least 18 inches above the level of the ground. 

§ 730-103. Cleanliness 

All hotels, restaurants, eating places, candy factories, meat markets, bakeries, and the kitchens thereof, or any other place where foodstuffs are kept, prepared, cooked, or served to customers, shall be kept sanitary and clean; and the meats, fish, vegetables, candies, and other foodstuffs prepared to be cooked and served in said places shall be protected from dust, dirt, flies, and vermin by means of glass cases, wire screens, or other devices approved by the Department of Health. 

§ 730-104. Food handling 

No person shall handle meat, fish, vegetables, fruits, or other prepared foodstuffs intended for human consumption, except in original containers and packages, unless he has been supplied with a certificate of good health signed by the local health officer or by a physician approved by the Secretary of Health, and all such persons shall use all reasonable precautions to keep themselves clean. 

Codification. "Chief of sanitation" was changed to "health officer" pursuant to 3 L.P.R.A. § 188. 

§ 730-105. Storeroom as living quarters (a) The use of any storeroom as sleeping quarters is prohibited when the same is to be utilized for the sale, manufacture, handling, or storing of foodstuffs destined for public consumption. (b) The construction of living quarters will not be permitted, nor will any room already constructed be used as a bedroom, on the same floor of the building destined for the sale or storage of food substances, unless said rooms are absolutely independent from those containing merchandise. § 730-106. Morgues and autopsy rooms 

Morgues and autopsy rooms in hospitals, cemeteries, sanatoriums, etc., shall be made flyproof by screening all doors and windows. with wire netting.

 § 730-107. Breeding places for flies 

The existence of any collection or pile of garbage, manure, rubbish, dead animals or of any other animal or vegetable matter which may serve as a breeding place for flies, or to attract them, within the urban zone of any municipality, or near any inhabited place, shall be considered a public nuisance and the owner, tenant, or agent of the property upon which the said collection or pile of garbage, etc., exists shall be responsible therefor and shall be punished under the provisions of sec. 330 of the Penal Code [33 

L.P.R.A. § 1366]. 

§ 730-108. Condemnation; seizure

All meats, fish, vegetables, fruits, or other foodstuffs intended for human consumption found to be contaminated, adulterated, or unfit for human consumption for any reason may be retired from sale by a duly authorized officer of the Department of Health and its sale or use for human consumption may be prohibited or prevented by seizure or by any other means that may be necessary and such foodstuffs may be held until such time as the proper court may determine the disposition to be made thereof. 

§ 730-109. Penalties 

Any infraction of any of the provisions of this Division shall be punished in accordance with sec. 33 of a "Law to reorganize the 

Service of Sanitation," approved March 14, 1912 [3 L.P.R.A. § 

187].

§ 730-152. Kinds of stoppers or covers

It shall be the duty of every natural or artificial person engaged in the manufacture of carbonated beverages to put the beverages into bottles with the name of the manufacturer on the cover, label, or bottle. § 730-154. Approval of plans for bottling plants

No plant for the manufacture of carbonated beverages shall be established in Puerto Rico without first obtaining approval, by the Department of Health, of the plans for said installation. 

§ 730-155. Inspection of plants 

No plant of said kind shall be put in operation until the same has been duly inspected by the corresponding health officer so that he may verify if the installation of said plant is in accordance with the plans approved by the said Department of Health. 

§ 730-156. Freedom from deleterious substances 

The process of manufacture shall be such as will render the manufactured liquid free from pathogenic microbes and substances deleterious to health. 

§ 730-157. Cleaning of containers 

Before filling said containers with the manufactured liquid they shall be cleaned in appropriate machines approved by the Department of Health, the use of caustic soda and hot water being recommended. 46

§ 730-201. Definitions 

Vinegar 

The term "vinegar", when used without qualifying word, designates only the product secured by the alcoholic and subsequent acetic fermentation of apple juice. The terms "cider vinegar" and "apple vinegar" may be used also as equivalent to the term "vinegar."

§ 730-202. Fruit vinegar "Fruit vinegar" is the product obtained by the alcoholic and subsequent acetic fermentation of the juices obtained by pressing or maceration of two or more classes of fruits, provided, that if only one class of fruit juice is used, the product must be labeled as vinegar qualified by the name of the fruit used, as "banana vinegar," "orange vinegar," etc. When the label bears the name "fruit vinegar" the names of all the fruits and the proportion of each of the fruits used must appear in the label. 

§ 730-203. Wine vinegar or grape vinegar "Wine vinegar" or "grape vinegar” is the product made of the alcoholic and subsequent acetic fermentation of the juice of grapes. 

§ 730-204. Malt vinegar 

"Malt vinegar" is the product made of the alcoholic and subsequent acetic fermentation, without distillation, of an infusion of barley malt or cereals, whose starch has been converted by malt. 

§ 730-205. 

Sugar vinegar "Sugar vinegar" is the product made by the alcoholic and subsequent acetic fermentation of solutions of sugar, molasses, or syrup, refined or not. 

§ 730-206. Glucose vinegar "Glucose vinegar" is the product made of the alcoholic and subsequent acetic fermentation of starch sugar or glucose, which shall be dextrorotatory. 48

Ch. T.24 § 730-210 

FOOD; DRUG AND COSMETIC ACT 

§ 730-207. Spirit vinegar, distilled vinegar, grain vinegar "Spirit vinegar, distilled vinegar or grain vinegar" is the product made by the acetic fermentation of distilled and diluted alcohol. 

§ 730-208. Second pressing 

It is considered that the number of pressings used in preparing the juice is immaterial so long as the pomace is fresh and not decomposed. In the opinion of the Secretary of Health, the practice of allowing the pomace from the presses to stand in piles or vats for a number of days, during which time it becomes heated and decomposed, and then pressing, securing what is ordinarily called "second pressing," produces a product which consists in whole or in part of filthy and decomposed material and is therefore adulterated. § 730-209. Vinegar from dried apples or other dried fruits

Vinegar from dried apples or other dried fruits is the product made from dried apple skins, cores, and slices, or from other dried fruits or parts of them, by the process of soaking, with subsequent alcoholic and acetic fermentation, but the solution thus obtained is not entitled to be called vinegar without further designation, but must be plainly marked to show the material from which it is produced. The dried stock from which this product is prepared must be clean and come from sound fruit. § 730-210. Addition of water 

When natural vinegars made from cider, wine, or the juice of other fruits are diluted with water the label must plainly indicate this fact, as for example "diluted to ... per cent acid strength", provided, that the acidity of vinegar so diluted will not fall below 4 per cent acid strength. When water is added to the pomace in the process of manufacture, the fact that the product is diluted must be plainly shown on the label in a similar manner. Dilution of vinegar naturally reduces not only the acid strength, but the amount of other ingredients in proportion to the dilution, so that reduced vinegars will not comply with the analytical constants for undiluted products, but the relations or proportions existing between those various ingredients will remain the same. 

ANNOTATIONS 

1. Adulteration. Vinegar diluted with water which contained less than 4 percent acidity was adulterated under this section and § 730-216 of this title, and could not be sold as 49

T.§ 730-210 Ch. 51 

"imitation vinegar." People v. Asencio, 1945, 64 P.R.R. 502; 

People v. Ramos, 1936, 50 P.R.R. 74. 

§ 730-211. Mixture of vinegars 

As different kinds of vinegars differ in source, flavor, and chemical composition, mixtures thereof are compounds within the meaning of the Food and Drug Act, and, if they contain no poisonous or deleterious ingredients, they will not be held to be misbranded, if plainly labeled with the word compound, together with names and proportions of the various ingredients. § 730-212. Addition of boiled cider and coloring matter 

The addition of coloring matters, boiled cider, etc., to vinegar, wine vinegar, and the other types of vinegar, or mixtures thereof, conceals inferiority or produces an imitation product. In the first instance, the use of such products is an adulteration and therefore prohibited. Products artificially colored or flavored with harmless ingredients in imitation of some particular kind of vinegar will not be held to be misbranded if plainly labeled “imitation vinegar" in accordance with the provisions of the law. § 730-213. Mixture of distilled and sugar vinegars

The product prepared by submitting to acetic fermentation a mixture of dilute alcohol (obtained, for example, from molasses by alcoholic fermentation and subsequent distillation) and dilute molasses, which has undergone alcoholic fermentation, is not "molasses vinegar" but a "compound of distilled vinegar and molasses vinegar"; such mixtures, however, must contain a substantial amount of molasses vinegar and not a small amount for the purpose of coloring the distilled vinegar. The molasses used must be fit for food purposes and free from any added deleterious substances. 

§ 730-214. Diluted acetic acid 

The product made by diluting acetic acid is not vinegar and when intended for food purposes must be free from harmful impurities and sold under its own name. 

§ 730-215. Product obtained by distilling wood 

The impure product made by the destructive distillation of wood, known as "pyroligneous acid", is not vinegar nor is it suitable for food purposes. 50

Ch. T.24 § 731-1 

FOOD; DRUG AND COSMETIC ACT § 730-216. Acid strength 

All vinegars, diluted or not (and also diluted acetic acid), shall contain not less than 4 grams of acetic acid per 100 cubic centimeters.

§ 760-1. Construction and maintenance authorized 

The construction and maintenance of public and private slaughterhouses in Puerto Rico is authorized, subject to the provisions established by this subchapter.

§ 760-2. Municipal slaughterhouses required 

Every municipality of Puerto Rico shall have at least one public slaughterhouse, except where two municipalities are sufficiently close together to enable both to utilize the same slaughterhouse. 53 

---

T.§ 760-3 

Ch. 53 

§ 760-3. Permission for construction 

For the construction of a slaughterhouse in Puerto Rico it is indispensable to have permission from the Secretary of Health, after obtaining the favorable report of the local health officer, and the written approval of the plans by the sanitary engineer. 

§ 760-4. Departments of slaughterhouses 

Every newly constructed building to be used as a slaughterhouse shall have at least the following departments: (1) One for the slaughter of cattle. (2) One for the slaughter of swine, sheep, and goats. (3) One for the cleaning of tripe and intestines of animals slaughtered. (4) One with sanitary installations to supply abundant water, at ordinary temperature, and boiling water for the cleaning and scalding of swine. (5) One for the cleaning and bathing of employees. (6) One room for storing and weighing meat. (7) One office room. (8) Annexed to these departments there shall be a yard or sty protected from the inclemencies of the weather, divided into departments designed for the separation and selection of cattle and provided with a sanitary watering place and a dung pit properly located; provided, that where the financial resources of a municipality will not permit the construction of a slaughterhouse as prescribed in this section, the Secretary of Health is hereby authorized to approve constructions with a lesser number of departments. 

§ 760-5. Location 

No slaughterhouse shall be constructed, established, or maintained within the limits of a town or in the outskirts of same or at a distance of at least 100 meters from any house, building, or inhabited place, spring, brook, river, well, or current of water; provided, that the Secretary of Health may permit the construction, establishment, and maintenance of slaughterhouses within. a less distance from any house, building, or inhabited place, spring, brook, river, well, or current of water, if in his opinion the public health will be sufficiently protected thereby. 

§ 760-6. Details of construction 

All buildings to be used as slaughterhouses must be well venti- 54

Ch. T.24 § 760-10 MEAT lated and of a size proportionate to the number of cattle slaughtered. The height of the place designed for slaughter shall in no case be less than 5 meters, and the other departments shall be at least 4 meters in height. The rooms shall be watertight, so constructed as to be easily cleaned with water. 

The interior walls shall be of impervious material to a height of at least 212 meters from the floor. The floors shall be of cement or other impervious material and shall be ratproof. Said floors shall have sufficient inclination for drainage by means of a drain or pipe connected with a septic tank located at a distance of at least 10 meters from the building or connected with the open sea when this may be done without injury to public health. The offal or garbage from the patios shall be collected before the washing is done and shall not be permitted to flow into the tank. $ 760-7. Fixtures and utensils

The slaughterhouses shall be provided with the fixtures and utensils necessary for the handling of meat and for the handling and extraction of intestines, hides, offal, fats, etc. Said fixtures shall be of proper sanitary material and shall be kept strictly clean. 

§ 760-8. Cleaning 

The owners, lessees, agents, or persons in charge of slaughterhouses shall see that the walls, floors, and yards thereof are thoroughly and effectively washed at least once in every 24 hours, and shall distribute in the slaughtering and storing departments, at least twice a month, chloride of lime in a quantity proportional to the size of the same. The hooks and other apparatus for hanging meat shall be washed and cleaned daily. 

§ 760-9. Entrances; walks 

The entrance to slaughterhouses shall be accessible for carts in order that the meat may be easily taken from the storeroom for transportation, and the building shall be surrounded by a cement walk, sufficiently graded for drainage and from 75 centimeters to 1.50 meters in width, in accordance with the size of the building. § 760-10. Slaughtering outside slaughterhouses

The slaughtering of cattle in any other place than a slaughterhouse, authorized in accordance with the provisions of this sub- 55

T.§ 760-10 

Ch. 53

chapter, is prohibited; provided, that this restriction does not refer to the slaughtering of small animals (sucking pigs, kids, lambs, etc.) which may be killed in the yards or courtyards of the houses or farms when desired for family use and not made a daily practice. 

§ 760-11. Inspection of animals 

All cattle to be slaughtered shall be inspected by a veterinarian, health officer, or employee acting in his capacity, 24 hours before slaughtering, and these animals must be able to walk into the slaughterhouse, except in the case of hogs which by their extreme weight are unable to do so. All sick animals shall be rejected. 

After the animal is killed, the carcass and intestines shall be inspected, and destroyed if diseased, burning the same in presence of a health employee, using coal oil for such purpose; provided, however, that when an organ or any part of an animal is bruised or wounded, the part bruised or wounded shall not be offered for sale, but if the rest of the carcass is in good condition, it may be sold for public consumption. 

§ 760-12. Diseased or unfit animals 

No animal shall be slaughtered, or sold, for public consumption, affected by any of the following diseases: (1) Anomalies of the blood (anemia, leukemia, hemoglobinemia, icterus, uremia). (2) Animal parasitism (the parasite known to be directly or indirectly transmissible to man). (3) Putrid intoxication (sapremia). (4) Pyemia. (5) Septicemia, whether or not hemorrhagic. (6) Anthrax. (7) Rabies. (8) Glanders. 

(9) Tuberculosis. 

(10) Actinomycosis. (11) Carbuncle. (12) Malignant pustule. (13) Dysentery. (14) Hog cholera. (15) Swine plague. (16) Mycotic gastro-enteritis. 56

Ch. T.24 § 760-14 MEAT (17) Texas fever. 

(18) Tetanus. 

(19) Malignant fever. (20) Puerperal fever. (21) Emaciation. (22) Advanced pregnancy (the sale of fetus for human consumption is prohibited). (23) Recent parturition (at least 15 days must have elapsed). (24) Overheated, feverish animals. (25) Exhausted (fatigued animals should have 8 hours' rest before being slaughtered). (26) Fractures, bruises, contusions (when fever present). (27) Advanced stages of mange. (28) Advances stages of footrot. (29) Suppurative or gangrenous inflammation of the udder. (30) Wounds (when fever is present). (31) Any disease of the heart, lungs, liver, kidneys, spleen, peritoneum, pleura, or any organ which would render the meat unfit for human consumption. (32) Animals less than 30 days old (calves must dress at least 

45 pounds). § 760-13. Hours for slaughtering

The slaughtering for public consumption shall take place at the hours fixed by the health officer, in agreement with the municipal authorities and considering the necessities of the town; provided, that where the health officer and the municipal authorities are unable to agree as to the hour the Secretary of Health shall determine. § 760-14. Refuse; hides

Every slaughterhouse shall be provided with covered, watertight receptacles for the immediate collection of refuse. Said receptacles shall be removed, emptied, and cleaned immediately after slaughtering. 

The trimmings, fats, bones, organs, or refuse of animals shall not be boiled or prepared in the slaughterhouse nor within a radius of 100 meters in any direction. The hides shall not be cured within the building or surrounding area, but in a suitable place previously designated by the health officer. 57

T.24 760 Ch. 53 

§ 760-15. Trying out of fats, etc.

By authority of written permit given by the health officer, strictly subject to the provisions of this subchapter, the trying out of fats, bones, and other refuse of animals may take place in places properly arranged, furnished with all that is necessary to avoid offensive odors. § 760-16. Use of slaughterhouse and surrounding area

The use of slaughterhouses, though temporary, for any other purpose than for the slaughtering of animals, is strictly prohibited. 

The breeding of any kind of domestic animals shall not be allowed in the neighborhood of any slaughterhouse, nor the dwelling or lodging of any person, when not in accordance with the provisions of sec. 760-5 of this title. § 760-17. Health certificates and clothing of employees

The butchers, assistants, helpers, carriers, and all persons who directly have to do with the handling of the meat shall be provided with certificates of good health issued by the health officer, said certificate to be renewed every month. They shall wear clean clothing suitable to the work of slaughtering and handling meat, said clothing to be different from that ordinarily used. They shall be covered also with a white blouse, which shall always be kept clean. 

§ 760-18. Transportation of meat 

The meat shall be transported to the places designed for its sale with the greatest precautions in regard to neatness and cleanliness at all times, especially when loading or unloading the carts. 

The carts designed for the transportation of meat shall be covered, of size sufficient for this purpose, and exclusively used for said service. They shall be painted in oil on the outside and covered on the inside with tin, galvanized iron, or other smooth, polished material, with gratings or windows for ventilating purposes, the same to be screened in order to make them flyproof. The carts shall be provided with steel or nickel-plated hooks or nails on which to hang the meat. The transportation of meat in any other way shall in no case be permitted, nor shall the meat be placed on the floor of the cart, nor on any table, board, or other fixtures, but hung on hooks of nickel-plated or polished steel. 58

Ch. T.24 § 760-23 MEAT 

§ 760-19. Persons transporting meat 

The carriers of meat shall not transport same on the head or shoulders, without an impermeable and clean cloth to thus avoid all direct contact with the meat. They shall wear clean clothes and shoes, and their heads shall be covered. The driver of the cart shall in no case help in loading or unloading the meat. 

§ 760-20. Transportation of refuse 

The transportation or conveyance of the refuse from the slaughterhouse shall not be permitted through the streets of a town, without permission of the local health officer. There shall also be used suitable carts, which shall not stop on the way to their destination and shall be strictly subject to the provisions made in each case. § 760-21. Portable stalls for sale of meat

The installation of portable stalls for the sale of meat on the streets is absolutely prohibited.

Raw material (a) Only fresh milk, as defined in the requisites established for grade A milk by the Milk Ordinance and Code of the United States 

Public Health Service, 1939, may be subjected to freezing for human use. (b) Milk to be frozen must also have been pasteurized and homogenized; Provided, That by pasteurization shall be understood the process described in secs. 790-131 to 790-138 of this title, or improved in accordance with the most modern methods in this matter; and by homogenization shall be understood the process by which fat globules are broken up into smaller particles in such manner that: (1) after 48 hours of storage, the milk thus homogenized shall not show any visible separation of its fat; (2) after standing for 48 hours in a 2-pint vessel, there shall not be a difference of more than 10% between the fat content of the upper 100 milliliters of the milk and the fat content of the remaining 1971 

 62-88

Ch. 

MILK 

T.24 § 790-304 milk after being thoroughly mixed. Furthermore, before pasteurization and homogenization, the milk shall have been clarified and filtered according to the best industrial technique. § 790-303. Establishment, plant, equipment, or machinery

Every establishment, plant, equipment, or machinery for the freezing of milk shall be kept scrupulously clean; in general, all sanitary regulations which are applicable to similar establishments for pasteurization, bottling, etc., of fresh cow's milk shall apply to the establishments, plants, equipment, and machinery and to the personnel engaged in the freezing process. 

§ 790-304. Freezing and preservation 

(a) Freezing shall take place after the pasteurized, clarified, filtered, and homogenized milk has been poured by mechanical means into containers made of good quality waxed or paraffined paper or fiber, properly sealed and having a 1or 2-pint capacity; the container shall allow for the expansion caused by freezing, without breaking or cracking. (b) Freezing consists of bringing the milk to the solid state by action of reducing its temperature to -40° F. (-40° C.). This shall be done within 10 hours after pasteurization, the milk having been kept at a temperature not higher than 53.6° F. (12° C.), before that, previous to and following pasteurization, and up to the very minute of starting the freezing process. (c) The milk, once frozen, shall be continuously kept and maintained in the solid, frozen state at a maximum temperature of 14.0° F. (-10° C.) in refrigerating rooms in which no other article except milk or milk products, in their containers, may be stored or kept; provided, that upon changing, moving, loading, or carrying frozen milk from one refrigerating room to another, it shall not be kept outside the refrigerating room and at atmospheric temperature for more than 1 hour, unless the atmospheric temperature is below 14.0° F. (- 10° C.); and it being further provided, that in no case whatsoever shall the refreezing of milk be permitted after defreezing has started. (d) In no case and under no circumstances shall an adulterant be used in the milk as preservative or for any other purpose. 

Text references. In subsec. (b) the phrase "-40° F. (-40°

C.)" reads thus in the original of both English and Spanish texts. 89

 § 790-305. Product 

(a) The milk which has been previously frozen shall not appear after thawing flaky, or with ice particles, curdled or with sediment, or with its fat separated. And, furthermore, it shall taste and smell sweet and clean like fresh milk, without rancid or greasy odor or taste; or any other smell as of plants, fish, cheese, burning, or storage. (b) The finished product, both when frozen and after thawing, shall contain at least 3.25% fat by weight and not less than 8.0% of non-fat solids. Its bacterial content, in the usual plate counts, shall not be more than 30,000 per milliliter. Upon approval by the 

Secretary of Health, vitamins may be added. (c) Milk in the frozen state or which has been previously frozen shall not be distributed, offered in sale, sold, delivered, or given away to the consumer more than 2 weeks (14 days) after pasteurization; provided, that under very special conditions or circumstances, the Secretary of Health, if he deems necessary, may authorize the distribution, sale, and delivery to the consumer of milk in the frozen state or which has been previously frozen after said interval has elapsed from the time of its pasteurization, but never after 5 weeks (35 days) after pasteurization. $790-306. (b) All milk in the frozen state or which has been previously frozen shall be delivered to the consumer in its original and unopened container. In public establishments devoted to the sale of foods, the original container shall be opened in the presence of the consumer except when it is to be used for coffee, chocolate, or any other beverage or as an ingredient in the preparation of other foods. (c) The further use of the containers herein mentioned, after they have been opened, for any other purpose whatsoever is strictly prohibited.
