§ 790-310. Sanitary inspection and taking of samples for analysis (a) The Secretary of Health and his authorized representatives may inspect any plant, installation, machinery, equipment, boat, airship, vehicle, storeroom, refrigerating room, dock, refrigerator, establishment, milk depot, milk stand, etc., where frozen milk or milk which has been previously frozen is processed, stored, carried, kept, offered for sale, sold, or delivered, in relation to any phase of the sanitary control of the supply of frozen milk or of milk previously frozen and in relation to the provisions of this Division and of any law or sanitary regulation which may be applicable. 

(b) The Secretary of Health and his authorized representatives may proceed to the immediate seizure of any and all milk in the frozen state or which has previously been frozen and which is not kept or is not stored, conveyed, distributed, offered for sale, or sold, or delivered in the manner herein established; they may permit its use for industrial purposes which do not involve its consumption by humans, provided a surety bond is paid, which shall be double the value of the milk in the market. Said surety bond shall be forfeited in case the milk is used for purposes other than those authorized. Unless the milk is used for the authorized industrial purpose within 48 hours after authorization, or in case of failure to obtain the bond, the milk shall be destroyed without any compensation and the surety bond shall be returned. Any and all milk considered unfit for human use may be seized and its use may be authorized according to the above provisions or may be destroyed as the case may be. All seizure or destruction of milk shall be preceded by an order drawn up to this effect. (c) The Secretary of Health and his authorized representatives may take samples of frozen milk or of milk which has previously been frozen from any place where said milk may be found, without paying for them, for the psysiochemical or bacteriological examinations which they may deem necessary and as frequently as it is considered convenient and necessary. They shall always give the corresponding receipt or receipts stating the purpose for which the sample or samples are taken. (d) All taking of samples shall be ruled by the provisions of sec. 790-1 et seq. of this title. § 790-311. § 790-312. Penalties 

Aside from the suspension and cancellation of license for just cause, the violations of the provisions of this division shall be punished in accordance with the penalties fixed by the various laws which rule in this matter. Specifically, the adulteration of frozen milk or milk which has been previously frozen shall be subject to the penalties established by Law No. 77 of August 12, 1925

§ 790-313. Introduction of pasteurized frozen milk from sources in territorial United States of America

The introduction into Puerto Rico of pasteurized frozen milk from sources in territorial United States of America other than Puerto Rico shall be subject to the following conditions and requisites: (1) Raw material shall comply with the requisites established in sec. 790-302 of this title, through certification from the Department of Health of the state of origin as to the quality of the milk, confirmed by the United States Public Health Service, and shall also comply with the requisites established by the United States 

Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (52 Stat. 1040 et seq.; 21 U.S.C. 

301 et seq.) and its rules. (2) Establishment, plant, equipment, machinery, and personnel shall fulfill the requisites established under sec. 790-303 of this title as certified to by the Department of Health of the state of origin. (3) Freezing and preservation shall be carried out in accordance with sec. 790-304 of this title, subject to certification by the Department of Health of the state of origin to the effect that the natural or legal person whose product is being introduced into Puerto Rico has processed it as herein established and that the processing shall be periodically inspected so as to guarantee the quality of the product and compliance with these provisions; Provided, That in relation to any and all shipments received in Puerto Rico, the purser of the ship or plane in which it is conveyed shall certify that the freezing system was constantly kept at a temperature not higher than the maximum limit established in sec. 790-304 of this title; or, in case of any interruption or accident he shall state the temperatures, as taken every 15 minutes, which prevailed 1971 93

T.8790-313 

Ch. 55 in said system during the time which said disturbance lasted and until the temperature was brought back to the established maximum. This certificate shall be kept by the natural or legal person who is the consignee and shall be available for inspection by the 

Secretary of Health and his authorized representatives. 

(4) The product shall conform to the provisions of sec. 790-305 of this title. (5) The container shall be as prescribed in sec. 790-306 of this title. 

(6) Labeling shall be in accordance with the provisions of sec. 

790-307 of this title, in English or Spanish. (7) Distribution and delivery shall be made as established by sec. 790-308 of this title. (8) Licenses: All natural or legal persons who may desire to introduce into Puerto Rico, from the territory of the United States of America other than Puerto Rico, frozen pasteurized milk for trade and for human consumption in Puerto Rico, must obtain a license to be issued by the Secretary of Health of Puerto Rico, after having fulfilled all the requirements established herein. The license for introduction shall be for the specific product for which it is issued, certified in accordance with paragraphs (1)–(6) of this section. If the person who introduces the product is also responsible for its keeping and storage, distribution and delivery, he must also obtain licenses to those effects. (9) Sanitary inspection and taking of samples for analysis; techniques for tests of samples, penalties, etc.: Once in Puerto

Rico, all frozen milk or milk which has been previously frozen, as well as any milk of any type or condition which is introduced into Puerto Rico, shall be subject to the conditions, restrictions, and provisions established in this division or in any other set of regulations or in any law which may be applicable; likewise, in relation to any milk thus introduced, the penalties established by laws, regulations, and this division shall apply to the introducers, license holders or others, and their representatives.

790-521. Date of effectiveness § 790-501. Definitions and specifications 

For the interpretation or enforcement of this division, the following definitions and specifications shall be applied: 

(1) "Secretary". The Secretary of Health of the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico, or his authorized representative. 

(2) "Department". The Department of Health of the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico. 

(3) "Person". Natural or juridical person. (4) "Milk". When mentioned without qualification, it means the integral lacteal secretion, free of colostrum, that is obtained by the milking of one or more healthy cows. The milk for human consumption shall contain not less than 11.30 percent of total natural solids and not less than 3 percent milk fat. (5) "Goat milk". The natural lacteal secretion, free of colostrum, obtained by the milking of one or more goats. Goat milk for human consumption shall contain not less than 3.75 percent milk fat. For all purposes, goat milk shall be identified as goat milk, and shall be subject to all the requirements of this division. (6) "Milk products". Any food product composed partially or totally of milk as defined in this division. (7) "Milk fat, butter fat or lacteal fat". Is the natural fat of milk. 1971 

95

T.§ 790-501 

Ch. 55 (8) "Concentrated milk products, liquid or powdered". Concentrated milk products shall be understood to be those milk food products to which a great portion of water has been removed, and when the same is restituted in accordance with the instructions on the label on the container shall adjust to the standards established by this division for the corresponding products. (9) "Cream". Is that portion of the milk, mechanically separated, which contains not less than 18 percent of milk fat. (A) "Whipping cream, light whipping cream". Is cream which contains not less than 30 percent milk fat. (B) "Heavy cream or heavy whipping cream". Is cream which contains not less than 36 percent milk fat. (C) "Light cream, coffee cream or table cream". Is cream which contains not less than 18 percent milk fat. (D) "Sour cream or sour cream with culture". Is cream, the acidity of which is more than 0.20 of 1 percent expressed in terms of lactic acid, and obtained through the action of an added bacterial culture, which shall be previously approved by the Secretary of 

Health. 

(E) "Half and half". Is a product consisting of a mixture of milk and cream which contains not less than 10.5 percent milk fat. (F) "Half and half sour cream". Is half and half cream to which a bacterial culture has been added to make it sour, which has been previously approved by the Secretary and that contains not less than 0.20 of 1 percent acidity expressed as lactic acid. (G) "Whipped cream". Is a cream to which a harmless gas has been added in order to facilitate whipping of the product. It shall contain not less than 30 percent milk fat. It may also contain sugar or any other flavoring or stabilizer, which are harmless to health and previously approved by the Secretary, in an amount of not more than 0.5 of 1 percent. (10) "Concentrated or evaporated milk". Is unsterilized and unsweetened milk resulting from the removal of a considerable portion of its water. It shall contain not less than 7.9 percent of milk fat and not less than 25.9 percent of milk solids. The product shall be compatible, upon the addition of potable water, in the indicated proportion, with the milk definition on this division. (11) "Sweetened condensed milk". Is milk obtained through the evaporation of part of the water from whole milk, to which sucrose or a mixture of sucrose and dextrose in proportion of 18 pounds of sugar per 100 pounds of milk has been added. The product 1971 96

It shall contain an amount of milk fat not less than 26 percent per weight. (13) "Skim milk, fat free or defatted milk". Is milk whose milk fat content has been removed until reduced to 0.50 of 1 percent. (14) "Dehydrated skim milk solids or powdered skim milk”. Is skim milk from which at least 95 percent of the water content has been removed. (15) "Flavored milk". Is milk to which has been added a syrup or flavor made from wholesome ingredients, as previously approved by the Secretary of Health, and which shall contain not less than 

2.9 percent milk fat and not more than 0.5 of 1 percent of a harmless stabilizer. (16) "Flavored skim milk drink". Is a drink prepared with skim milk to which a flavor prepared with wholesome ingredients, previously approved by the Secretary, has been added. (17) "Cultured buttermilk". Is a product resulting from the treating of skim milk with lactic acid producing bacteria or similar culture, as approved by the Secretary. It shall contain a minimum of 8 percent solids, nonfat, and shall have an acidity of more than 0.20 of 1 percent expressed in terms of lactic acid. (18) "Cultured milk". Is a product resulting from the sourings and treating of pasteurized milk with lactic acid producing bacteria or similar culture, as approved by the Secretary. It shall contain not less than 11.30 percent of total milk solids, a minimum of 3 percent of milk fat, and shall have an acidity of more than a 0.20 of 

1 percent expressed in terms of lactic acid. (19) "Vitamin D milk". Is milk to which 400 units of Vitamin 

D per quart has been added. (20) "Native or country cheese". Shall be known by that name as cheese prepared in Puerto Rico. The milk and milk products to be used shall be pasteurized and subjected to equivalent thermal treatment which will result in the destruction of the phosphatase. 

The curdling will be affected by the addition of harmless lactic acid producing bacteria, or by means of enzymatic action or by means of any other method previously approved by the Secretary. 

Shall contain not less than 35 percent of solid fats and not more than 50 percent moisture. Once produced and packed, shall be THIEL 49 1971 97

Ch. 55 maintained at a temperature not higher than 45 degrees Fahrenheit until its delivery to the consumer. (21) "Butter". Is a product exclusively manufactured from pure milk or pure cream or both, with or without salt or added coloring, and shall contain not less than 80 percent of milk fat. The coloring shall be previously approved by the Secretary. (22) "Homogenized milk”. Is milk which has been submitted to a physical process so as to insure the breakup of the fat globules to such an extent that, after 48 hours of quiescent storage, at 45 degrees Fahrenheit, no visible cream separation occurs, and at the end of this period, the percentage of fat of the 100 milliliters in the upper part of a 1 quart bottle, still quiescent (or of proportional volume in containers of other sizes), does not differ by more than 10 percent in relation to the total percentage of remaining milk as determined after being thoroughly mixed. (23) "Reconstituted milk or milk products". Shall mean milk or milk products as defined in this division and resulting from the mixture of milk or milk product constituents and potable water. 

Shall conform to the definitions of milk and milk products of this division. (24) "Optional ingredients". Shall mean and include, dehydrated Grade A milk products, concentrated milk, concentrated milk products, flavors, sweeteners, stabilizers, emulsifiers, sourings, vitamins, minerals and similar ingredients. (25) "Eggnog flavored milk”. Shall mean a milk product, consisting of a mixture of milk fat, egg yolk solids, a sweetening and a flavoring agent. Shall contain not less than 3.25 percent of milk fat and not less than 0.5 percent of egg yolk solids. An emulsifier may be added, and a maximum of 0.5 percent of a stabilizer. (26) "Eggnog". Is a milk product, consisting of a mixture of milk and milk products containing not less than 6 percent of milk fat; not less than 1 percent of egg yolk solids; a sweetening and a flavoring agent. An emulsifier may be added and a maximum of 

0.5 percent of a stabilizer. (27) "Other products". For any other milk product not specifically defined in this division, the definition given in the last edition of "Grade A Pasteurized Milk Ordinance" recommended by the

Federal Public Health Service shall be accepted, or the definitions or standards or norms established by the General Foods and Drugs 

Administration, or as the Secretary of Health may determine. 1971 98

Ch. MILK T.24 795-501 (28) "Pasteurization". Pasteurization shall mean the process by which every particle of milk or milk product is subjected to a temperature of 145 degrees Fahrenheit or more for 30 minutes, being immediately cooled to a temperature of 45 degrees Fahrenheit or less. Pasteurization may be affected too by subjecting the milk or milk products to a temperature of 161 degrees Fahrenheit or more and holding it at such temperature for at least 15 seconds, followed by immediate cooling to a temperature of 45 degrees Fahrenheit or less. The pasteurized milk or milk products shall be poured or packed immediately into its final container. All these operations shall be performed in adequate equipment; Providing, nevertheless, That those milk products whose fat contents are more than the content of fat in milk or those which contain sweetening additives will be heated to a temperature of 150 degrees Fahrenheit or more and holding this temperature for a period of 

30 minutes or more; or at a temperature of 166 degrees Fahrenheit or more and holding this temperature for 15 seconds or more. Any substance added to the milk or milk products as authorized by this division shall be added before the process of pasteurization, except when the substance added is a harmless gas or a bacterial culture. 

It shall be understood that nothing included in this definition shall exclude any other process previously approved by the Secretary of 

Health. 

(29) "Dairy farm". Place where one or more healthy cows or goats are milked and whose milk as a whole or in part is sold or offered for sale for human consumption. (30) "Milk producer". Person who operates a dairy farm and provides, sells or offers for sale milk to pasteurization plants or processing centers. (31) "Pasteurized milk agent". Is that person who buys pasteurized milk and sells it under his own responsibility. (32) "Dairy plant or center for the pasteurization and/or processing of milk". Establishment, place or location where milk or milk products are pasteurized or processed. It being provided that, when the equipment of a pasteurization and/or processing plant is to be devoted or transferred to the production or elaboration of nonmilk products, the owner, manager, or person responsible for the establishment shall provide himself with a sanitary license issued by the Secretary authorizing him specifically for such purposes. 1971 

 99

T.§ 790-501 

Ch. 55 (33) "Milk shop". Establishment or business and their annexes or dependencies where pasteurized milk is stored for sale or is sold directly on a retail basis to the consumer. (34) “Urban zone". It shall be understood by "urban zone” or "city", any conglomeration of buildings, streets, squares, gardens, parks, etc., where the functions of collective life are carried on with such harmony, efficacy and convenience which characterizes individual life. Any "urban zone", whatever its extension, is constituted by 3 basic components: the "urban nucleus", or original center of the city; the "urban zone", peripheral part of the urban nucleus; and the "suburbs" which are extensions or expansions whether adjacent or not to the urban zone. (35) "Approved, accepted or authorized". Wherever in this division the above terms or their derivatives are used it shall be understood that it refers to the acceptance by the Secretary. (36) "Potable water". Pure water, from the hygenic point of view, whose bacteriological, chemical, physical and radioactive purity is of such a nature as to be considered fit for human consumption. (37) "Official laboratory". Is a laboratory (of the Department of Health) where biological, chemical and physical analyses are performed. (38) "Authorized laboratory". Is a laboratory which is not owned by the Health Department but is authorized by the Department to perform the tests of milk and milk product samples as required by this division.

Ch. T.24 § 790-502 

MILK § 790-502. Licenses 

(a) No person can produce, process, bottle, store, transport, sell, expose, offer for sale or donate milk for human consumption; or produce or process or bottle any milk product for human consumption unless it is provided with a license issued by the Secretary and previously complying with the requirements in this division. (b) The licenses shall be personal and not transferable and shall only authorize the business in the establishment for which it was issued. (c) Licenses issued in accordance with this division shall be valid for 2 years; Provided, That all licenses issued by the regulations repealed by this division (former §§ 790-1 to 790-174 of this title) shall be valid for a year upon the promulgation of this division. (d) The licenses shall be requested and issued in the form and model determined by the Secretary. They shall be fixed in a visible and conspicuous place in the establishment, being mandatory by the possessor to properly maintain it in good repair. In case of loss of any license, the interested person shall immediately notify the Secretary by written statement and apply for a duplicate. (e) The Department of Health shall retain the property right to any license. The possessor of licenses issued under this division shall be responsible for the violations even though such violations are performed by their agents or employees, except when such persons are surprised in flagrante delicto. (1) Types of licenses. In accordance with the provisions of this division, the following sanitary licenses shall be issued to those milk or milk products businesses: 

(A) For first class dairies. 

(B) For plants or center for pasteurization or processing of milk and milk products. (C) For pasteurized milk shops. (D) For pasteurized milk agents. (2) Refusal, suspension, cancellation and cancellation and revocation of licenses. The Secretary can refuse, suspend, cancel or revoke the licenses authorized by this division by the reasons indicated in the same and after complying with the established procedure. (A) Refusal of licenses. The Secretary can refuse to issue a license if and when the requirements of this division are not complied with. 1971 

 100.1

T.8790-502 

Ch. 55 (B) Cancellation of licenses. The licenses issued in accordance with this division can be cancelled by the Secretary for the following reasons: (i) At the end of commercial operations for which they were issued. (ii) When the business is sold, rented or granted to another person. (iii) By death of the person under whose name the license was issued. (iv) When the classification of the business changes. (C) Suspension of licenses. The Secretary can suspend any license for the following reasons: (i) When any violation to this division is determined. (ii) When an immediate problem is found which by its nature implies a serious public health hazard. (iii) When within the term of 2 years, 2 consecutive samples or 3 samples, although not consecutive, proceeding from the same establishment, turn out to be adulterated as determined by the Laboratory of Health and until the cases are resolved in the justice courts. (iv) When the standards for the maximum permissible bacteriological counts are violated as provided in sec. 790-505 of this title. (v) When by the use of violence or force or by any other means, the Secretary of Health or his authorized representative is not permitted to perform his corresponding official duties. (vi) When a duly authorized dairy farm incorporates milk from another authorized or clandestine dairy farm. The suspension can be for a term of no more than 90 days, provided that when the term of suspension has expired, a new license can be issued if it is so requested by the interested person after the correction of all deficiencies that caused such suspension. (D) Revocation of licenses. The Secretary can permanently revoke any license issued under this division for the following reasons: (i) When the Superior Court renders a final and firm sentence of guilt in cases of adulteration of milk in a relapsing case as provided for in sec. 790–502(2) (C) (iii) of this title. (ii) When the Superior Court renders a final and firm sentence of guilt in cases of obstruction to public justice as provided in sec. 790-504 (b) of this title. nyo 1971 

 100.2

Ch.

(E) Procedures for the revocation of licenses. The Secre tary shall notify the affected person the intention to revoke the license in accordance to the provisions of sec. 790-502 (2) (D) (i) and (2)(D)(ii) of this title. The person affected shall have the right to request a hearing in relation to the notified deficiencies within the next 10 days from the date of receipt of the notification of the intention to revoke the license. The Secretary shall hear the affected person in an administrative hearing and shall emit his final decision within the next 30 days. 

§ 790-503. General requirements 

Within the territorial limits of the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico, all activities related to the production, transportation, processing, sale and donation of milk and milk products shall be subjected to the following requirements: (1) Sale or use of milk and milk products in restaurants, groceries and similar establishments. Establishments such as groceries, cafes, restaurants and other similar places where milk and milk products are sold exclusively on a retail basis and/or use milk and milk products in the confection of foods, beverages, and for similar purposes, shall only obtain, store, utilize, sell and/or offer for sale milk or milk products coming from sources authorized by the Department of Health, providing that such establishments shall have adequate facilities to maintain the milk and milk products within the sanitary standards prescribed by this division. (2) Transferring of milk and milk products. Transferring of milk or milk products for commercial purposes from one container to another in the open air, public or private, or in any vehicle, business or place that is not authorized by the Secretary of Health is hereby prohibited. (3) Condition of equipment and utensils in dairy farms and plants or centers for pasteurization and/or processing. All the equipment, including machinery, milking pails, milk cans, strainers and any other utensil used in the handling, production, pasteurization, storage, bottling and packaging, transportation of milk or milk products, shall be in accordance with the "3A Sanitary Standards" or instead the Secretary of Health shall determine the standards to follow. They shall have smooth, nonabsorbent, noncorrosive surfaces, made of nontoxic material, and their construction and conservation shall be such as to permit their easy disassembling and efficient cleaning, hygienization and inspection. They shall be free 1971 100.3

T.§ 790-503 Ch. 55 

from dents, rust, cracks, defective soldering, dirt crusts, or any other undesirable condition. This is not applicable to disposable containers or single use. (A) Use. Any container, utensil or other equipment and its accessories, comprised in the above paragraph, which does not comply with its provisions, shall be taken out of use and removed from the dairy, plant or center for pasteurization and/or processing, etc., or else shall be seized. The presence or use of metallic sponges in the premises where the milk or milk products are produced or processed shall be prohibited. (B) Design and construction of the equipment and utensils at the dairy farms and plants or centers for pasteurizing and/or processing. In the future, any new container, receptacle, equipment or utensils to be used in dairies and plants or centers for pasteurization and/or processing, which may come in contact with milk and milk products as defined in sec. 790-501 of this title, shall comply with all the requirements of design, construction and operation established by the standards known as "3A Sanitary Standards" as promulgated jointly by the U.S. Public Health Service, International Association of Milk and Food Sanitarians, and the 

Dairy Industry Committee.

In those cases where there are no “3A 

Sanitary Standards" norms a specific authorization by the Secre tary of Health shall be required. (C) Installation, operation, maintenance and hygienization of the equipment and utensils in dairies and plants or centers for pasteurization and/or processing. The installation, operation, maintenance and hygienization of any containers, utensils or equipment comprised in the preceding paragraph shall be performed according to "3A Sanitary Standards" norms, and it is furthermore understood, that the Secretary of Health shall inspect and check such equipment, according to the established practice of said standards, or instead, those promulgated by the Secretary of 

Health. 

(D) Effectiveness of the standards and their amendments. 

The "3A Sanitary Standards" norms, and their amendments, shall prevail until the Secretary of Health determines otherwise. (4) Effectiveness of cleaning, hygienization, and bactericidal process. The effectiveness of any process of cleaning and hygienization and/or bactericidal treatment for all equipment or receptacle, which may come in contact with milk and its products, shall be determined periodically by bacteriological tests as may be deemed 1971 100.4

MILK 

T.24 790-504 Ch. 55 necessary. Articles or containers which are used only once shall be excluded from these provisions. (5) Health certificates. Any person whose work requires contact with the production, handling, bottling or packaging, storage or transport of milk or milk products; or with the utensils or with equipment related to milk and milk products shall be provided with a health certificate issued by the Department of Health. Said certificate shall be renewed each year from the date issued. The 

Secretary may require at any time a new medical examination of said persons, even if their health certificate is still valid. The Secretary may cancel any health certificate at any time, when there is justifiable cause. All health certificates shall be available at the place of work at all times for revision by Department of Health Officials and their mutilation and improper obtainment shall be illegal. It shall be the responsibility of the license holder, as required by this division, to request from each employee the corresponding health certificate before he starts working, and that the same be annually renewed. § 790-504. Inspections, sampling, examination of records, embargoes and seizures (a) Inspections. The Secretary shall inspect any business or establishment covered by this division, and shall do it as many times as necessary at any reasonable time, for the good of the service and the public health. Likewise shall inspect any establishment, site or place where milk or milk products are sold, offered for sale, stored, exhibited, utilized or processed, even in those cases that a license may not be required by this division. (b) Resistance or impediment. When a person by himself, his agents or employees commits or intends to commit any act of resistance or delay, obstruction, hindrance, aggression or attack by force or word, against the Secretary or his authorized representative, or denies free access to the farms, establishments with their annexes and surroundings, or vehicles related with the production, elaboration, storage, transportation, buying or selling of milk or milk products for inspection, sampling or any other activity related to the performance of his official duties, he may be accused for obstructing the course of public justice. The license shall be suspended without having to apply the procedure set forth in this division until said person allows free access to the business, so that the inspection, sampling, etc., may be carried out by the Department 100.5 

 1971

T.§ 790-504 

Ch. 55 of Health. If the owner of the establishment is accused and convicted of a felony, the license shall be revoked. (c) Records examination. When required by the Secretary, the license shall supply true data of the quantities of milk or milk products processed, transported, stored, bought or sold, as the case may be. He shall also be supplied with true data about the results of chemical, physical and bacteriological analyses, time temperature graphs of pasteurization and processing of milk and milk products, as well as any other information or data that the Secretary of Health may deem necessary for the fulfillment of his responsibilities. (d) Time and temperature graphs of milk and milk products pasteurization. The graphs of time and temperature of the pasteurization or processing of milk or milk products shall be made by each establishment for each day that the milk or milk products are processed and for each one of the pasteurization equipments in operation. Such time and temperature graphs shall be retained for at least 3 months from the day the graphs were made. They shall be well kept and available when requested by the sanitary authority. 

They shall contain the following information: (1) The date on which the graphic register was produced. (2) The signature of the supervisor in charge of production. (3) The quantity and type of the pasteurized product. (4) The initial temperatures at the beginning of the operation. (5) The temperature at the end of the operation. (6) The temperature of the indicator thermometer and the registering thermometer. (7) The duration of the process. (8) The temperatures and length of the rinsing, cleaning and hygienization of the equipment. (9) Any other information required by the Secretary of

Health. 

(e) Sampling. The Secretary is authorized to take all samples of milk and milk products, in any place or location as deemed necessary, for the fulfillment of his responsibilities, and when it is most convenient for the purpose of the service. In addition to the samples of milk and milk products deemed necessary, he shall also take samples of bactericidal agents, detergents, antibiotics, containers, equipment, etc., for the pertinent tests and examinations. (1) Raw milk. During each 6-month period a minimum of 1971 100.6

Ch. 

MILK 

T.24 $790-505 

4 samples of milk shall be taken from the dairy farms on different days for the bacteriological examinations. For the chemical analyses, as many samples of milk, as may be deemed necessary by the Secretary, shall be taken, establishing a minimum of 2 samples in 6 months for the determination of fat content, and a minimum of 1 monthly sample to determine the amount of added water or any other condition. (2) Pasteurized milk and milk products. The samples of raw milk, pasteurized milk and milk products shall be taken at the plants or centers for pasteurization and/or processing, at least 3 times a week for the corresponding chemical and bacteriological analyses. In addition, milk and milk product samples shall be taken in all establishments where milk and milk products are sold to the consumer and in any place or site, as frequently as the Secretary may deem necessary to determine the extent of compliance with this division. (f) Seizures and embargoes. When the Secretary finds or has reasonable motives to believe that a milk or milk product is adulterated or improper for human consumption or improperly labeled or dangerous to public health, he may embargo said article by fixing a label or appropriate mark giving advice that the product is supposedly adulterated or improper for consumption and that it has been detained or embargoed and advising that it cannot be disposed of in any way until the Secretary or a competent court gives permission for such purpose. Furthermore, in case that the product is proved to be adulterated or improper for human consumption he may require from the owner that the product be destroyed or denatured. If the owner does not agree to the denaturing or destruction of the product it shall be embargoed as indicated in this section until final results of the analysis or a 

Court order is obtained. § 790-505. Bacteriological classification of milk and milk products

It is hereby established and allowed for the following classifications of milk and milk products based on the bacteriological content, specified as follows: (1) First class raw milk for pasteurization. The total bacterial count for this milk shall not exceed 300,000 colonies per milliliter and not more than 30,000 colonies per milliliter in thermoduric counts. 

(2) Pasteurized milk-grade A. The first class raw milk after 

1971 100.7

T.24 790 

Ch. 55 being submitted to the process of pasteurization as defined in this division also shall meet the following conditions: (A) From each 4 samples taken consecutively on different days at least 3 of the samples shall have bacterial counts not higher than 30,000 colonies per milliliter, and total coliform counts not higher than 10 colonies per milliliter. (B) The efficiency of the process of pasteurization shall be determined by means of the test known as phosphatase test, which should be negative. It shall be the responsibility of all plants or centers for pasteurization and/or processing to perform a phosphatase test every day, at the end of the first pasteurization. The results shall be recorded and filed for a period of 3 months. In cases of positive phosphatase tests, the cause shall be determined and the deficiency shall be corrected immediately. No milk showing a positive result in the phosphatase test shall be sold to the public. (3) Pasteurized cream. Cream after having undergone the process of pasteurization as defined in this division, provided that the total bacteriological count for this cream does not exceed 30,000 colonies per milliliter. The total coliform count shall not exceed 10 colonies per milliliter. (4) Pasteurized milk products. The bacterial count in pasteurized milk products, except in cultured pasteurized products, shall not be higher than 30,000 colonies per milliliter and the coliform count shall not exceed 10 colonies per milliliter, including the cultured milk products. § 790-506. Procedures to determine the compliance of maximum bacterial counts allowed in raw milk (a) During each 6-month period the Secretary of Health shall collect from the dairy farms for bacteriological tests a minimum of 

4 samples on different days. (b) When one of the samples during the 6-month period shows a bacterial count exceeding the limit established by this division the person concerned shall be notified in writing about the abnormality found. At the same time that the person concerned is notified in writing, an additional sample shall be taken, which shall be called "additional sample". This additional sample shall be subjected to a bacteriological test, and the result of this test shall be accepted as the official bacteriological result of the sample in question. (c) If the count of the bacteriological test of the additional sample is higher than that established by this division, the person 1971 100.8

Ch. 

MILK 

T.24 790-507 concerned shall be notified in writing, that if one of the next samples taken within a 6-month period exceeds the bacteriological standard set by this division, his license shall be suspended. The license shall continue suspended until the analyses of 2 consecutive samples, taken on different days, show that the bacteriological counts are within the standards set by this division. 

§ 790-507. Labeling of milk and milk products 

(a) No milk or milk product shall be owned, stored, offered for sale, sold, donated or distributed in any form whatsoever, unless the container or bottle is properly labeled in accordance with the requirements of this division. Every label shall receive previous approval from the Secretary of Health by sending samples of the labels to be used. No labeling shall be used until it has finally been approved by the  (b) The labeling shall be placed on the container or the outer cap of the bottle and shall have a circular, rectangular or any other design, and its shortest dimension shall be no less than 1 5/16 inches. The label shall never be placed at the bottom of the container or bottle. The label shall be printed in a clear and legible form, and in contrast with any other printed matter, design or color. 

The milk and milk products bottled specially for sale or distribution in restaurants, bakeries, commercial establishments or institutions, in containers of several quarts may be labeled by using an adequate label approved by the Secretary of Health. The label shall be fixed to the container. The labeling shall contain the following information: (1) The word "Milk" or the name of the milk product. (2) The word "Pasteurized" (if it is so). (3) The word "Homogenized" (if it is so). (4) The name of the entity to whom the license has been issued and the license number. The name of any registered mark, trade mark, or any other similar identification. § 790-508. Conditions of the milk and milk products 

(a) Adulterated milk and milk products. (1) All milk shall be considered adulterated with added water when an examination reveals one of the following conditions: (A) Total solids of less than 11.30 percent. (B) Milk fat of less than 3 percent. (C) Acidity, expressed as lactic acid according to the method of "Milk Industry Foundation", of more than 0.17 of 1 percent. (D) Cryoscopic reading according to the method used by the 

Official Chemical Analysts Association, numerically lower than 0.530 degrees centigrade and with an acidity of not more than 

0.17 of 1 percent. (E) Mineral matter in acetic serum, less than 0.715 of 1 gram per 100 milliliters of milk. (F) Specific weight at 15 degrees centigrade, less than 1.029. (b) Other conditions. (1) Any milk or milk product shall be considered adulterated if it does not comply with the definitions in this division. (2) Any milk or milk products shall be considered adulterated if it contains any substance unauthorized by this division, or any poisonous or deleterious substance which might endanger public health. (c) Milk and milk products unfit for human consumption. (1) All raw milk, pasteurized milk or milk products, shall be considered unfit for human consumption, if any or several of the following conditions are found: 1971 

 100.10

Ch. 55

MILK 

T.24 $ 790-509 (A) Milk or milk products obtained from sick or extenuated animals and from animals fed with improper food. (B) Milk or milk products containing colostrum, blood, pus or excreta. (C) Milk or milk products containing pathogenic microorganisms. (D) Milk or milk products containing bactericides, preservatives, hormones foreign to the milk, pesticides or similar products. (E) Milk or milk products containing antibiotics. (F) Milk or milk products which contain dirt, foreign substances or any abnormality. (G) Milk or milk products which are stored, transported and bottled or packaged at higher temperatures than the refrigeration temperatures required by this division. (H) Milk or milk products not pasteurized in compliance with this division. (I) Milk or milk products which show bacterial counts higher than the limits established by this division. (J) Pasteurized milk or milk products which give positive results to the phosphatase test. (K) Milk or milk products which exhibit any other condition considered by the Secretary of Health as detrimental to public health. (L) Milk or milk products which show abnormal color, odor or taste. (M) Milk whose acidity is greater than 0.17 of 1 percent expressed as lactic acid according to the method of the "Milk 

Industry Foundation". § 790-509. Sanitary requirements for dairy farms

There shall be only one type of dairy farm for the production of milk: First class dairy farms. 

(1) Location. It shall be illegal to build, operate, or establish any dairy farm at a distance of less than 200 meters from the limits of an urban zone or from a place not approved by the Planning Board for such a purpose; it being provided that, in case the city, through its urban growth, reaches a distance of 200 meters or less from any dairy farm established and operating with a license granted by the Secretary of Health, he may revoke the license, if in his judgment, such an action is deemed convenient or necessary as a necessary measure for the protection of the public health. If the 1971 100.11

T.§ 790-509 Ch. 55 

building were to be located 200 meters or more from the urban zone as defined by this division, but in land zoned by the Planning Board of Puerto Rico, the plan shall be accompanied by the corresponding permit from said Planning Board. (2) Construction plans. The construction of dairy farms, milking barns and annexes shall not be allowed unless the construction plan, submitted in original and 2 copies, is approved by the  Said plans shall include the name of the owner, the town and ward where it is located, a site plan showing its location in relation to the nearest urban area, distance from roads, bodies of water, farms, stables, etc., including all annexes, location of equipment, sanitation systems, septic tank construction, plumbing and water disposal. The plan submitted shall be on a scale of 1/4 inch per foot, and shall include any other information which the 

Secretary of Health may require. (3) Walls, columns, ceilings and roofs. The walls and columns of the milking barns and their dependencies shall be constructed of cement or other approved impervious material. The walls and fences of the corrals in the dairy farms may be made of wood. The feeding stalls in the milking barns shall be made of cement or other approved impervious material. The surfaces of walls, columns, feeding stalls, stanchions, and ceilings shall be smooth, easy to clean, and shall be kept in good condition and clean. The milking barns and its premises, including the corrals and other buildings related to the dairy farm, and which are located less than 50 meters from said milking barns, shall be painted as often as necessary, inside and outside, with light-colored washable paint. The roofs shall be constructed of approved material, and in such a way as to prevent the passage of bat droppings, dust, insects or similar objects into the interior of the building. The stanchions, stalls, barns or other similar equipment or similar system used for keeping the cattle in the milking barns shall be constructed of tubing or other approved material; wood or other similar material shall not be considered acceptable. The roofs shall be of cement, galvanized iron or other approved material; roofing cardboard or other similar materials shall not be permitted. (4) Ventilation. The places utilized for the hygienization of equipment and utensils, the storage and cooling of milk, and those used for toilet facilities and for dressing rooms, and those used for storing feed in bags, shall be no less than 9 feet high (distance from floor to ceiling or false ceiling, interior measurements). 1971 100.12

Interior height shall be no less than 7 feet in the lowest part of the milking barns, cattle pens and corrals. The minimum ventilation area for any place or dependency shall be not less than 20 percent of its floor area, and shall be provided in such a manner that the best possible air circulation is allowed. Neither the door areas of any place nor the opening leading from one enclosed place to another shall be included as ventilation areas. (5) Artificial lighting. The dairy barns and its premises, when in use, shall be provided with enough natural or artificial light, adequately placed and distributed to the best advantage and in such a way that the workers will be able to see and carry out the processes of milking, cleaning and hygienization of the equipment and utensils, and the other operations of the business, by day as well as by night. The slope of the floor shall be of 1/4 inch per foot leading toward the drains, the drains shall be no more than 30 feet apart. 

No accumulation of water shall be permitted. Each drain shall be equipped with an adequate trap. The floors of the milking barns and other annexes shall be provided with drainage systems, placed and protected in accordance with the standards set by the Planning Board, and shall be well kept and clean. With the exception of the discharges from the sanitary facilities, the water discharges from the milking barns and its premises, including rain water coming from the roof may be used for pasture irrigation at a distance of not less than 50 meters from the dairy farms. The used water proceeding from the toilets and urinals shall be discharged into the sanitary sewerage system or into septic and filtering tanks or into equivalent systems constructed and maintained in compliance with the regulations of the Department of Health and the Planning Board. The dairy barns, its premises and surrounding areas shall be kept clean, in good repair, and free from objects foreign to the business. The manure shall be gathered daily and shall be dispersed on the field at a distance of not less than 50 meters from the milking barn and its annexes, and in such a manner as to prevent the breeding of flies; or it shall be disposed of by any other system previously approved by the Secretary of Health. The milking barns shall be free of manure and other wastes immediately after each milking. In corrals, mangers, and other places where cattle are kept, wastes shall be removed at least once a day. The necessary gutters and drainage systems shall be constructed. These shall have a minimum extension of 50 meters, or whatever the Secretary of Health may deem convenient for the proper disposal of the liquids and solids of the dairy farm and surrounding areas; and preventing that such liquids or solids contaminate, or add contamination to any body of water, or constitute a public nuisance. The ventilation areas of said places shall be provided with metallic screening or its equivalent of 16 threads per lineal inch. The windows and metallic screens, or their equivalent, shall be kept in good condition, clean, and installed in such a manner as to fulfill their purpose. No opening in these places shall lack protection against flies. The doors shall open to the outside, shall be provided with automatic closing devices, and conveniently fit their frames; both doors and frames shall be kept in good repair, clean and adequately painted. No door shall remain open for a longer period than is necessary for a person to pass through. (10) Hygienization area. Each dairy shall have a place for hygienization exclusively destined for the hygienization of containers, utensils and equipment related to the handling of milk, and for their storage after hygienization. When the water supply to be used in a dairy comes from a well, said well shall be located in such a way that the possibility of contamination does not exist, as determined by a sanitary inspection. The walls shall be constructed to meet the requirements established by the Secretary of Health, and shall not be put to use until it is determined that the water obtained from the well meets the requirements of drinking waters. (20) Hygienization of equipment and utensils. All the containers, equipment and other utensils used on the dairy farms or in connection with, for the handling, storage, cooling, transportation and conduction of milk, shall be subjected immediately after each use to an approved process of washing and hygienization. Said processes of washing and hygienization shall consist of the following essential steps: (A) Preliminary rinse. Rinse with clean clear water at a temperature between 90-110 degrees Fahrenheit until all milk residue and dirt is removed. (B) Washing. All milk residue and dirt shall be removed by using adequate detergents. Adequate brushes suitable for the utensils, equipment and its parts being washed shall be used. 1971 100.19

T.24790 Ch. 55 

Brushes shall be kept clean and shall be used in the proper manner. 

These brushes shall be replaced as often as deemed necessary. (C) Rinsing. The equipment and utensils already washed shall be rinsed with clear water until free of any milk residue, dirt and detergent. 

(D) Bactericidal Treatment. A bactericidal treatment shall be performed by one of the following methods: (i) Immersion of all utensils, equipment and accessories for at least 2 minutes in a chlorine solution at 100 parts per 1,000,000. (ii) When the bactericidal chlorine treatment is performed by contact and not by immersion, the minimum chlorine concentration permitted shall be not less than 200 parts per 1,000,000. (iii) Through the adequate utilization of iodine compounds, previously approved by the  (iv) By any other equivalent method approved by the 

Secretary of Health. 

(v) No utensil or equipment shall be subjected to a rinse or drying once it has undergone bactericidal treatment. It shall be handled and kept in such a way so as to prevent the contamination of any surface that comes in contact with milk. (21) Cleaning in place. Every dairy farm using a pipeline system for the conduction of milk shall have an automatic system for the hygienization of the same. The capacity of the hot water tanks in this system shall be adequate enough to permit the efficient operations involved in the hygienization in the area (cleaning in place) of the pipeline used for conducting milk and its accessories, and which allows the complete immersion of the vacuum discharger and the manual hygienization of those lengths of tubing for the conduction of milk and its accessories that cannot be cleaned in place; such as milk weighing jars, milking machines, milking pails, jars, etc. The cooling milk tanks shall be placed as close as possible to the vacuum discharger. The cleaning and hygienization in place of the pipeline conducting the milk shall be an indispensable requirement, and the process shall include the following steps: (A) Once the milking procedure is completed, a preliminary rinse shall be mandatory for the milk pipeline, by circulating potable water at a temperature between 90-110 degrees Fahrenheit, until the discharge is observed free of any milk residues. (B) Then, the washing shall proceed during not less than 20 minutes with an approved nonfoaming detergent solution which is properly circulated. This solution shall be at a temperature of not 1971 

 100.20

Ch.

T.24 790-509 less than 120 degrees Fahrenheit. The water used for the preliminary rinse shall not be used for the preparation of the washing solution. The use of a combination of bactericidal detergents shall not substitute the final bactericidal treatment. (C) The rinsing of the milk pipeline system shall be performed with clear potable water until the pipeline system is free of all residue of the detergent. (D) Shortly before the next milking the bactericidal treatment of all the installation shall be performed by the adequate circulation for at least 5 minutes of a chlorine solution maintaining not less than 200 parts per 1,000,000 until the end of the process. The operator may use any other bactericidal agent that has been previously approved by the Secretary of Health and under the conditions approved by him. (22) Hygienization of milking machines. When milking machines are used they shall be satisfactorily cleaned immediately after finishing each milking. They shall be dismantled and all parts properly scrubbed with appropriate brushes for each part and using an approved detergent solution, or any other acceptable substance. All the parts shall be rinsed with clear water until they are free of milk residues and detergents. The rubber parts whose surfaces come in contact with the milk, once rinsed, shall remain submerged in a caustic soda solution at a strength not less than 0.5 percent which shall be used only once. These parts shall be rinsed shortly before the next milking. After assembling all parts of the milking machine, they should be submerged in a solution of not less than 200 parts per 1,000,000 of chlorine solution, or it shall be circulated through them for at least 2 minutes or they shall be treated with any approved bactericidal solution in the way specified by the  In dairy farms with sanitary pipeline milking system, the milking machine shall be connected to the system during the processes of preliminary rinse, wash, and final rinse. All rubber parts shall be dismantled and shall be placed in contact with a caustic soda solution at 0.5 percent. Before the next milking they shall be rinsed in water and reassembled. They shall then be connected to the pipeline system for the hygienization of all the equipment. (23) Milking. The milking of cows shall be done in a sanitary way, and exclusively in the milking barns constructed for that purpose. The hind quarters and udders of milking cows shall be kept with clipped hair. Before the milking, the hind quarters, C7 1971 100.21

udders and teats shall be washed to remove all dirt and allowed to drain. Then the udders and teats shall be treated with a chlorine solution at a concentration not less than 200 parts per 1,000,000 or with any other acceptable bactericidal agent at the required concentration. The udders and teats shall be dry at the moment of milking. The milk, as it is being obtained from the milking shall be transferred immediately to the corresponding room for filtering, storage and cooling to a temperature not higher than 45 degrees Fahrenheit and shall be maintained at that temperature until the final delivery. (24) Processing and bottling or packaging of milk and milk products. No milk or milk product shall be processed at the dairy farms. No milk or milk product shall be handled or transferred in any form whatsoever at the dairies, with the exception of the milk obtained during the milking in that same dairy. (25) Personal hygiene. The milkers and other employees who handle the milk and containers, utensils or related equipment shall wear special caps, aprons and clean clothing during each operating period. The caps, aprons or uniforms shall be of light color, and when not in use, they shall be stored at the place reserved for them in the dressing rooms or toilets. No spitting or smoking shall be permitted in the milking barn, milking rooms or their dependencies. 

The milkers and employees shall also be responsible for practicing good habits of personal hygiene and shall maintain their bodies and especially their hands clean. Fingernails shall be trimmed and clean. 

(26) Health of the dairy cattle. 

(A) Brucelosis. Every request for a dairy farm license shall be accompanied by a certificate issued by the Department of Agriculture of Puerto Rico, certifying that the cattle are under the brucelosis eradication plan, in accordance with Law No. 181 of 1942, as amended [5 L.P.R.A. §§ 781 to 786]. The Secretary of Health may require additional certificates. (B) Bovine tuberculosis. Every request for a dairy farm license shall be accompanied by a certificate from the Department of Agriculture of Puerto Rico, certifying that the cattle have undergone the tuberculin test, in accordance with Law No. 181 of 1942, as amended [5 L.P.R.A. §§ 781 to 786]. All bovine cattle, whether intended for milk production or not, shall be submitted to the tuberculin test at least once every 2 years or whenever the Secretary

1971 100.22

Ch. 

MILK 

T.24 § 790-510 of Health may deem it necessary. No milk from cattle affected by brucelosis shall be either produced or sold. The certificates of the tuberculosis and brucelosis tests shall be kept at all times in the dairy farm files. (C) Mastitis. Any milking animal which, when submitted to a physical, chemical or bacteriological examination by authorized veterinarians or authorized technicians, produces milk with traces of blood, ropy milk, or abnormal milk in any other sense, even when complete hardening or inflammation of the udder is not evident, shall be excluded from the milking line and its milk shall be discarded for human consumption until a further examination shows that said animal has returned to a normal state of health. 

If the animal does not recuperate from the illness it shall be permanently excluded from the herd by order of an authorized veterinarian. 

(D) Animals treated with antibiotics. The milk from cows treated with antibiotics shall be considered unfit for human consumption during the period of treatment, and shall be discarded for such use until at least 72 hours have passed since the last treatment. 

The Secretary of Health shall indicate the minimum number of hours during which milk shall have to be discarded when specific antibiotics are used. 

(E) Other diseases. The Secretary of Health shall order the removal from a dairy herd of any animal which is suffering from a disease or condition which might be considered dangerous to the public health; and the owner or person in charge of said animal shall be responsible for disposing of it in accordance with the manner established by the applicable regulations, or, instead, as required by the  The Secretary of Health shall have the right to order an examination of any animal when a doubt exists about the state of its health; likewise he could exclude the animal from the herd. 

§ 790-510. Transportation of milk and milk products 

(a) Milk transports. Any vehicle used in the transportation of raw or pasteurized milk and milk products shall meet the "3A 

Sanitary Standards" requirements. They shall be of adequate sanitary construction and capable of keeping the product at the temperature required by this division. The milk transports shall be labeled in a clear and legible way to be seen at a distance of 50 feet and in a prominent place with the words "Milk Transport” and 1971 100.23

T.§ 790-510 Ch. 55 

clearly labeled with the name of the licensee, the license number, his address, and any other labeling required by the  The transportation of raw and pasteurized milk in the same vehicle at the same time is hereby forbidden. The milk trucks, which distribute milk to the consumer, shall be permitted to carry pasteurized milk and milk products only. The transportation of any other products except milk or milk products shall not be permitted. (b) Thermo tanks. The tanks used for the collection of milk or milk products in bulk shall meet "3A Sanitary Standards" requirements. Their construction shall be such as to prevent the contamination of the product; they shall be easy to clean and hygienize. 

They shall be kept clean and in good repair. Once the milk and milk products are delivered, the thermo tanks shall be cleaned and hygienized as stipulated in this division. The thermo tanks shall be equipped in such a way that the driver, upon collecting the milk at the dairy farm, may wash and disinfect the discharge valve of the cooling tank, the opening of said tank, and the connection of the connecting hose, before proceeding to connect to the thermo tank and collect the milk or milk product. (c) Milk collection at the dairy farm. (1) The collection of raw milk at the dairy farms shall not be permitted when the milk temperature is over 45 degrees Fahrenheit. (2) The collection of raw milk at the dairy farms shall not be permitted when, for any reason, the milk may be unfit for human consumption. (3) All spouts, discharge valves of the cooling tanks (farm tanks) of bulk milk, shall be disinfected in their interior with an approved bactericidal solution, as well as the spout or valve of the connecting hose to the bulk tank truck, immediately before the collection of milk. (4) It is mandatory to collect all the milk content of a cooling tank (farm tank). (5) Once the milk content is removed from the cooling tank (farm tank) of the dairy farm, the connecting hose between both tanks shall be disconnected and it shall be mandatory and the responsibility of the owner or the person in charge of the dairy to proceed to give a thorough rinsing with potable water to the cooling tank (farm tank) until every visible particle of milk or milk product is removed from the surface of the cooling tank (farm tank). (6) As soon as possible, the cooling tank (farm tank) shall 1971 100.24

Ch. 

MILK 

T.24 790-512 be washed with a detergent solution, using adequate brushes for this procedure. (7) The tank shall be rinsed immediately, until every particle of milk and detergent residue is removed. (8) Within the term of an hour before the next milking, the cooling tank shall be hygienized with a bactericidal solution approved by the  This solution shall be drained from the cooling tank and the same shall not be rinsed with any substance. (9) It is hereby prohibited to collect milk that is outside of the cooling tank, even though such milk meets the temperature requirements or is of normal visual characteristics. If this condition occurs, the collecting agent shall report it immediately to the nearest health authority who shall proceed to destroy said milk. (10) The milk at the dairy farms shall be collected at least once every 48 hours. § 790-511. (2) Other types of plants or centers for pasteurization and/or processing, as approved by the Secretary of Health. § 790-512. Requirements for plants or centers for the pasteurization and/or processing of milk or milk products Every plant or center for the pasteurization and/or processing of milk or milk products to be constructed or already constructed shall comply with the requirements established in this division. (1) Plans. The plans or sketches shall be submitted in triplicate at a scale of 1/4 of an inch per foot, and they shall have the following information:

(2) Milk source. All the milk obtained and used by a plant or center of pasteurization and/or processing shall come exclusively from authorized dairy farms. The different operations to take place in the plants or centers for the pasteurization and/or processing shall be performed in an adequate manner and in buildings constructed as required by the Secretary of Health and in such a way as to avoid contamination of milk and milk products and of the equipment and utensils. 

The ventilation of the buildings shall come directly from outside or through a ventilation system approved by the  The area occupied by the pasteurization and processing equipment shall not be larger than 25 percent of the floor space.

(ii) The floor shall be constructed of cement with sufficient length and width to permit the parking of the thermo tank with a slope of 1/4 inch per foot toward the drains.

All dry material, equipment, containers, detergents, bactericides, brushes, spare parts and other similar material shall be kept in the warehouse, away from the processing room, except the quantities that may be necessary for daily operations. (10) Light and ventilation. Every room shall be not less than 9 feet high at its lowest point (inside distance from floor to ceiling or roof), except the refrigeration area where the distance could be less. The minimum area of ventilation for each room shall be equivalent to 20 percent of the floor area, and shall be so provided as to facilitate the best possible circulation of air. The ventilation system shall be sufficiently effective as to prevent condensation on the walls, roofs or ceilings. Neither the areas nor those openings connecting one room with another shall be considered as a ventilation area. It shall be permissible to use mechanical means of ventilation, previously approved by the Secretary of Health, in any room or area. This mechanical ventilation shall be equivalent to the required natural ventilation. (11) Protection against flies, rodents and other vermin. All the establishment areas used for the processing, storage and refrigeration of milk and milk products shall be fly, rodent and vermin proof. 

The presence of flies, rodents and other animals shall not be permitted at any time inside the rooms. Every door and window shall open outwards only, shall fit properly to its frame, and shall be maintained in good repair and adequately painted. Every door shall be equipped with an adequate automatic closing device, and shall not remain open for any time longer than that needed for a person to pass. All ventilation areas shall be provided with metallic screenings or its equivalent of 16 threads per lineal inch. The screens or its equivalents shall be installed in such a way as to fulfill its purpose and shall be kept clean and in good repair. No opening shall lack protection against flies and rodents. (15) Time and temperature registers. In every pasteurization process, at least 2 thermometers of an approved type shall be provided. (16) Receiving of milk or milk product at plants or centers for pasteurization and/or processing. (A) When a plant or center for pasteurization and/or processing receives milk or milk products coming from a dairy farm, whether such receipt be in individual or collective form, it shall proceed to examine each shipment of milk or milk products. The examination shall include appearances, color, taste, odor, physical conditions, bacterial growth and temperature. The results shall be annotated in forms that are acceptable to the Secretary of Health, and shall be filed for a period of not less than one year. (B) Containers, tanks, thermo tank trucks, coolers, filters, separators, milk conduction lines and any equipment or utensil utilized in the transfer, storage, transportation of milk or milk products, that is found to be rusted, corroded, chipped or in any other way unfit to be used in the preparation of milk or milk products, shall be withdrawn from use until it is repaired and approved for further use. 1971

T.24 790-512 (17) Cleaning and hygienization of equipment and utensils in the plants or centers for pasteurization and/or processing. (A) All equipment and utensils used in the transfer, storage, transportation or processing of milk or milk products shall be thoroughly washed and hygienized in the following manner: (i) Immediately after each use, each piece of equipment and utensil shall be completely dismantled and shall be rinsed with clean water until every visible residue of milk or milk products is removed. (ii) After this initial rinsing the next step shall be a washing with hot water at a temperature between 90 and 110 degrees Fahrenheit, containing a cleaning agent in such a concentration as to remove visible dirt and grease. The washing chore shall be done by means of scrubbing with brushes, or through a spray of efficient pressure. (iii) Afterwards, a thorough rinsing with hot water shall be effected, until the object is clean and no cleaning agent remains. 

(iv) The hygienization shall consist of one of the following methods: (a) Hygienization of equipment and utensils through steam pressure for no less than 2 minutes. (b) Immersion of the equipment and utensils in water having a temperature of no less than 180 degrees Fahrenheit for a period of no less than 2 minutes. (c) Exposition of the equipment and utensils to a sanitizing solution of sufficient concentration and in such a way that the hygienization be effective. The type, form and concentration of the solution shall be approved previously by the 

(B) No reusable bottle or container for milk or milk products shall be utilized until it has been efficiently cleaned and hygienized by means of a method with time, temperature and alkali concentration factors that have been tested and approved by the Secretary of Health. 

(C) Concentration and time of exposition for the hygienization of thermo tanks. (i) For the thermo tanks, when the chlorine solution is applied through spraying, said solution shall be of a concentration not less than 250 parts per 1,000,000, and shall be applied for a period of no less than 5 minutes. 1971 

100.33

T.24 790 

Ch. 55 (ii) Any other equivalent method or hygienization agent whose effectiveness has been previously determined and approved by the Secretary of Health may be used. (D) The containers used in the preparation or storage of chlorine solutions shall not be made of wood, metal, or other substances that are rapidly affected by the solution. The chlorine solutions shall be prepared by dissolving or diluting in water enough liquid or powdered chlorine, sodium or calcium hypochlorite, or a similar chlorine compound, so that at all times the available amount of chlorine shall be that prescribed by this division, and shall be determined by the orthotolidine test or by the titration iodine content starch test. Each plant or center for pasteurization and/or processing shall have the equipment needed to carry out these tests, and said equipment shall be used regularly. A chlorine solution shall be used only once in the hygienization of equipment, utensils, containers, etc., used in the transfer, handling and processing of milk and milk products; except in those cases in which the chlorine concentration is maintained, in which case it may be used for the treatment of floors, walls, and other structural parts. 

(E) Cleaning and hygienization of the storage tank for milk products and of thermo tank. Also said card shall have the signature of the person who performed said job. Every tank or receptacle of any kind that is used for milk or any milk product shall be protected and shall be covered so that the desirable protection against possible contamination of the product is provided. (20) Refrigeration of the milk. Milk received in plants or centers for pasteurization and/or processing shall be kept at a temperature of 45 degrees Fahrenheit or less, except during the time when subjected to the process requiring heat. The product resulting from such process shall be kept, until the moment of its final delivery, at a temperature of 50 degrees Fahrenheit or less, but above freezing. (21) Disposal of liquid wastes. In cases where liquid wastes from the plants or centers for pasteurization and/or processing need special treatment before their final disposal, detailed information shall be submitted to the Secretary of Health, who shall determine if said treatment is acceptable. The liquid wastes shall in no manner create public nuisances. § 790-513. Milk shops and second class dairy farms (a) Raw milk shops and second class dairy farms. From the date when this division goes into effect the operation of new raw milk shops and second class dairy farms shall not be permitted, nor shall new licenses be issued for said shops or second class dairy farms. The existing licenses for these milk shops and second class dairy farms shall be cancelled 18 months after the effective date of this division. (b) Pasteurized milk shops. The pasteurized milk shops shall be used exclusively for the sale of pasteurized milk which has been. bottled of packaged in the plants or centers for pasteurization and/ or processing. The milk in these shops shall not be sold nor served except in the bottle or container in which it originally left the plant or center. 

§ 790-514. Requirements for milk shops 

(a) Required area. Every milk shop shall be installed in a place large enough to perform all operations of storage, hygienization, refrigeration and sale of milk. The place shall have not less than 

TITLE 25 

1971 100.35

T.24 790 

Ch. 55 

100 square feet of floor area, and its narrowest side shall be not less than 6 feet wide. The location shall be permanent, and shall have to be approved by the Secretary of Health and the Planning Board. 

(b) Maintenance. Every milk shop, annexes, dependencies and surroundings shall always be kept clean and free from garbage, wastes, stagnant waters and objects unrelated to the nature of the business. The shop shall be free from and acceptably protected against flies, other insects, rodents or other animals. These establishments shall not communicate with nor ventilate directly into dwellings, toilet facilities, latrines or other places where industries operate or work is done that may in some way contaminate the milk. (c) Ventilation and ceiling height. The ventilation area shall be equivalent to not less than 20 percent of the floor area. It shall be provided with metallic screening or its equivalent of 16 threads per lineal inch. The ceiling shall be not less than 9 feet high (from floor to ceiling). (d) Potable water. The milk shops shall have potable hot and cold running water for general cleaning. (e) Walls, floors, ceilings, etc. The walls, columns, floors, ceilings, roofs and other structures, the furniture, equipment and utensils shall be kept in a good state of cleanliness and preservation, and painted with washable light-colored paint. The floors, columns and walls shall be made of concrete or other approved material to a height of not less than 5 feet from the floor. (f) Activities not allowed. In the milk shops, no business other than the sale of pasteurized milk for which the license was granted shall be permitted. (g) Personal hygiene facilities. Milk shops shall have acceptable facilities for the employees to wash their hands. The wash basins shall be kept clean, in good repair, and operating. Soap, paper towels for hand drying and approved receptacles for the used paper towels shall be available. (h) Entrance to the interior of shops. No person shall be allowed to enter the interior of the shop unless he is an employee of said shop. 

(i) Equipment and utensils. Equipment and utensils for handling milk in milk shops shall be subjected to the same provisions enumerated in this division for equipment and utensils for handling milk in the dairy farms and plants or centers for pasteurization and/or processing.
