The building used as a factory for cheese, butter, evaporated milk, condensed milk, dehydrated or powdered milk, cream elaboration, other modified milk elaboration or elaboration of other products derived from milk shall fulfill the same conditions of construction and room distribution as those required of plants or centers for pasteurization and/or processing, and all the requirements of this division shall be applicable to said building. § 790-516. Specific prohibitions (a) It is specifically prohibited to receive, store, reconstitute, homogenize, pasteurize, package, or in any other manner handle powdered milk or powdered skim milk, in any processing plant or place where fresh milk is received, homogenized or otherwise handled; except in those processing plants where: (1) Fresh milk is converted into powdered milk or powdered skim milk. (2) The Secretary of Health has granted authorization to use dehydrated solids of skim milk in the preparation of dairy products. This authorization by the Secretary of Health shall be granted when the interested party requests it; as long as said interested party can show the Secretary of Health that he has a plant in which fresh milk is received, homogenized or otherwise handled, and that in this plant dairy products are prepared, for which preparation dehydrated solids of skim milk are needed. 1971 100.37

T.24 790 Ch. 55 

(b) Reconstituted milk, whole or skim milk, and reconstituted whole or skim milk drinks shall not be offered for sale to the public except in original containers for the retail market, properly labeled and unopened. In bulk containers, they may be sold to institutions which have individual licenses to receive said products. (c) It is specifically prohibited to sell, grant, give or in any way deliver powdered milk or powdered skim milk in bulk containers to any person who does not possess an individual license to receive said containers. (d) The transportation of empty milk bottles containing residues of milk or any other substance in trucks or vehicles belonging to processing plants for milk or milk products is hereby prohibited. § 790-517. Milk and milk products originating in places outside the borders of the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico 

From this date on, the distribution, handling, pasteurization, sale or donation of milk or milk products coming from sources out side the jurisdiction of the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico shall be prohibited unless said products are produced or processed under conditions and standards that are essentially the equivalent of the provisions of this division and this equivalency is so determined by the Secretary of Health through investigation and sanitary evaluation. § 790-518. Terms employed

Any word used in the singular shall be understood to be in the plural when justified by its use. The masculine shall include the feminine and vice versa, when necessary. 

§ 790-519. Penalties 

Any violation of this division shall be punished in accordance with the provisions of the applicable laws. § 790-520. Saving clause

If any article, paragraph, section or part of this division were declared null or unconstitutional by a Court possessing effective jurisdiction, said ruling shall not affect, act in detriment of, or invalidate the remainder of the division; rather, its effect shall be limited to the article, paragraph, section, or part of the present division that has been declared null or unconstitutional. 1971

§ 801-1. Definitions 

The following definitions shall apply in the interpretation and enforcement of this subchapter: (1) "Powdered skimmed milk" means fresh cow's milk from which the milk fat has been removed so that its milk fat content is less than 3 percent and from which its water has been removed later, by the spray process, until reduced to the condition of a powder, containing no more than 5 percent of water. (2) "Reconstituted whole milk" means powdered skimmed milk to which has been added cream from cow's milk and vitamins, 1971 100.39

T.$ 801-1 

Ch. 55 besides pure water, so that the final product has the same composition as fresh cow's milk, that is, 88 percent water by weight as a maximum, 3.25 percent milk fat as a minimum and not less than 

12 percent milk solids. (3) "Reconstituted skimmed milk" means dry skimmed milk to which has been added pure water, so that the final product contains less than 3.25 percent milk fat. (4) "Reconstituted whole milk beverage" means whole reconstituted milk to which has been added additional taste, color, or any nutritive substance whether natural or artificial and always subject to the laws and regulations in force for food and drugs. (5) "Reconstituted skimmed milk beverage" means reconstituted skimmed milk to which has been added additional taste, color, or any nutritive substance whether natural or artificial and always subject to the laws and regulations in force for foods and drugs. (6) "Mechanical dairy" means any machine or set of machines or equipment of any kind used for the reconstruction of milk in relation to the definitions (1) to (5) of this section, as well as the place, site, or establishment, with all its annexes and dependencies and personnel, where milk or milk products, in direct or indirect relation with those same definitions, are produced, homogenized, pasteurized, bottled, or handled in some form whether for institutional use or sale. (7) "Pure water" means drinking water from the sanitary standpoint, whose grade or purity bacteriologically has been and is periodically checked by the Health Department, of an acceptable chemical composition for the purpose of reconstituting milk and whose source has been approved by the

(a) Any person, firm, or corporation that wishes to engage in the following activities shall obtain an individual license, through application to the Secretary of Health, to: 1971

The production of reconstituted whole milk, reconstituted skimmed milk, reconstituted whole milk beverages and reconstituted skimmed milk beverages shall be done only in mechanical dairies, as defined, and subject to this subchapter; (3) store, package, sell, or offer for wholesale dry skimmed milk, whether in bulk containers or in containers for retail, as said containers are herein prescribed; provided, that wholesale shall be understood as being all sales in excess of 20 packages for retail; and provided, also, that it shall not be necessary to obtain an individual license for the retail of dry skimmed milk in containers for retail in quantities not considered as wholesale, the license for the retail being subject to subsecs. § 801-3. Containers 

(a) Powdered skimmed milk may be introduced into Puerto Rico only in bulk containers and containers for retail, as described below, and may be stored and transported only in them, namely: (1) "Bulk container" is any adequate container approved by us which contains 90 pounds of powdered skimmed milk as a minimum. (2) "Container for retail" is any adequate container, either of metal, glass, or any other material approved by us and having a capacity of 6 pounds as a maximum. These may in turn be contained in cartons, boxes, or packages of convenient sizes used for wholesale or retail; provided, that these provisions shall not apply to the powdered skimmed milk that is or may be sent to Puerto Rico by the Federal Government or its agents, and used exclusively in the feeding programs of the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico; provided, furthermore, that special permits may be issued for the use of other containers, with weights different from those prescribed above, when in the opinion of the Secretary of Health, a problem of health will not be created and there exists no real possibility of creating such problem by the use of such special containers. (b) Reconstituted whole milk and reconstituted skimmed milk beverages may be transported, sold or offered for sale only in bulk containers and in containers for retail as herein described. (1) "Bulk container" is a container or metal jug or any other impervious substance, approved by the Secretary of Health, duly labeled as prescribed in this subchapter, covered and sealed, and of 20-quart (40-pint) or 40-quart (80-pint) capacity for sale and delivery to institutions exclusively. (2) "Container for retail" is a container of glass or any other impervious material, which is approved by the Secretary of Health, original, duly labeled as prescribed in this subchapter, covered and recapped, and whose capacity may be one-half pint, 1 pint, or 1 quart (2 pints).

(b) All containers for retail that contain powdered skimmed milk shall be labeled in the same manner as prescribed for bulk container in subsection (a) of this section, except that in paragraph (4), description of contents shall be in the Spanish language, and shall consist of two parts, one that shall say "Powdered Milk Without Fat" in letters of a size that make it really prominent, and in addition, underneath and in parenthesis, in smaller letters, "Leche en Polvo Descremada". § 801-6. General provisions 

(a) The requirements for mechanical dairies, their installation and operation, shall be the same as those in force for pasteurization plants or plants for bottling fresh milk according to sec. 

790-1 et seq. of this title. (b) Any installation used to pack or repack powdered skimmed milk shall be subject to approval and inspection by the Secretary of Health or his representatives. (c) The transportation, distribution, and delivery of reconstituted whole milk, reconstituted skimmed milk, reconstituted whole milk beverages and reconstituted skimmed milk beverages shall be subject to the regulations for fresh cow's milk, according to sec. 790-1 et seq. of this title. (d) The collection of samples for analysis, both of powdered 106

(f) All reconstituted whole milk or reconstituted whole milk. beverages shall be homogenized and pasteurized and all reconstituted skimmed milk or reconstituted skimmed milk beverages shall be pasteurized during or immediately after its reconstitution according to regulations in force. (g) All reconstituted milk, whole or skimmed, or reconstituted milk beverages, whole or skimmed, that is to be served to customers in restaurants, hotels, inns, soda fountains, etc., must be served in its original container and opened in the presence of the customer. (h) Reconstituted milk and its products shall not be offered for sale after 36 hours of being reconstituted and pasteurized. (k) Powdered skimmed milk in containers for retail shall only be sold or offered for sale to the consumer in stores, markets, and other establishments of any kind devoted to retail business, as well as in schools and other public institutions as determined by the Secretary of Health, in the original containers and only in the following maximum amounts to each client: Two containers of 2 pounds, or 214 pounds, or twenty containers of 100 grams; provided, that all sales to a retailer shall be accompanied by a copy of the above provisions; and provided further, that, in the case of the retail distribution agencies specified in this section, including the schools and public institutions which the Secretary of Health designates or may designate in the future, are hereby issued the corresponding licenses subject to cancellation as provided in subsec. § 801-7. Specific prohibitions 

(a) It is specifically prohibited to store, reconstitute, homogenize, pasteurize, pack, or in any way handle powdered skimmed milk on any premises, plant, or place where fresh cow's milk is received, homogenized, pasteurized, or in any way handled. (b) Reconstituted milk, whole or skimmed, and reconstituted beverages, whole or skimmed, shall not be offered for sale to the public unless in original and unopened retail containers; such products may be sold in bulk containers to institutions with individual licenses to receive them. (c) It is specifically prohibited to sell, grant, donate, or in any form deliver powdered skimmed milk in bulk containers to any person, natural or legal, not having the individual license to receive and use it. 

§ 801-8. Amendments, repeals 

(a) All provisions of any other regulation in conflict with any provision of this subchapter are hereby amended or repealed. 

(b) Specifically, the provisions of Division 1 of subchapter 790 

of this title, insofar as they relate to this subject, are amended in compliance with the provisions of sec. 790-151 of this title. 

§ 801-9. Penalties 

In addition to the cancellation, temporary or permanent, of any license, the penalties for violations of the provisions of this subchapter shall be those established by Act No. 38 of April 25, 1929

§ 820-1. Harmless coloring material 

The addition of harmless coloring materials of vegetable or synthetic origin shall be permitted if they are certified according to the law, but in every case the original packages shall state for the information of the purchaser the use of such coloring materials.

Effectiveness. Sec. 5 of Regulation No. 4 provided: 

"These rules and regulations shall take effect thirty (30) days after its approval. "Approved today, April 28, 1934.”

Explanatory matter. Regulation No. 4, set out in this sub chapter, contained the following explanatory matter: "It is customary in the coffee grinding mills of Puerto Rico to color this grain with Prussian Blue. There is the belief that although Prussian Blue is poisonous, the presence of traces of it in foods is not dangerous. This office wants to inform that the presence of this colorant is illegal under any circumstance. "For the information of the manufacturers who process coffee in the grain in Puerto Rico with the addition of harmless coloring materials of vegetable or synthetic origin, but certified according to the law, notice is given that their addition is not prohibited if the original packages state clearly this fact for the information of the purchaser but the use of poisonous or deleterious coloring materials are absolutely prohibited, and in consequence, the use of Prussian Blue shall not be permitted under any concept. "The Department also wants it to be known that if the grain of coffee is colored, covered, or stained in such a form that its inferiority is cloaked or hidden, even if the coloring material were harmless or certified, this shall be considered an adulteration, the proceeding illegal, and the merchandise will be subject to confiscation." 111 [T.24]

T.§ 820-2 

Ch. 57 § 820-2. Prussian blue

The use of Prussian blue shall not be permitted under any circumstances. 

§ 820-3. Coloring to hide inferiority 

Coffee in the grain shall never be colored in such a form that it will cloak or hide its inferiority, and if this is done, it shall be considered an adulteration, any lot of coffee found in such condition becoming for that reason subject to condemnation or confiscation. 

§ 820-4. Violations 

Violation of this subchapter shall be punished according to the provisions of sec. 4 of the Act to Prohibit the Sale, Storage, and 

Transportation of Adulterated, Misbranded, Poisonous, or Deleterious Foods and Drugs, or Medicines, and for other purposes, approved on April 28, 1931.

§ 850-2. Permit 

(a) No natural or artificial person shall offer for sale, sell, or manufacture bread or other food products prepared with edible flour, without a permit issued by the proper health official; provided, that this permit may be revoked by the Secretary of Health whenever the sanitary provisions in force are not complied with, and the permit shall be revoked whenever a bakery remains without baking for a continuous period of 2 months or more. (b) It shall be the duty of owners of bakeries, when ceasing to operate, to notify the proper local health officer, informing him of the exact date when work was suspended. (c) When a permit has been cancelled it shall not be renewed unless all the conditions required by this Division for new bakeries have been duly complied with. (d) Exception is made to the provisions of this Division, as regards the above-mentioned period of 2 months, in the case of suspension of work because of force majeure, such as hurricanes, earthquakes, fires, floods, strikes, and other analogous causes, in which case the period shall begin to be counted when, in the opinion of the Secretary of Health, the foregoing abnormal conditions have ceased. (e) The Secretary of Health shall revoke the permit of every bakery in which laborers are employed without the corresponding certificate of health. (f) It shall be considered that any bakery operating without the permit required by this Division is producing an article without the required public health guarantees and that the same is unfit for human consumption and should be seized and its use shall be prohibited and it shall be ordered to be denatured.

Ch. T.24 § 850-4 BREAD Regulation No. 98 also provided for penalties for violations in accordance with 3 L.P.R.A. § 187 and repeal of conflicting provisions. $ 850-3. Location

Every building or premises used as a bakery and for the manufacture of the other foodstuffs referred to in the preceding section shall be erected in the locality providing the best sanitary conditions and separated from other buildings or premises used for industries producing offensive odors or other harmful effects which may affect the good quality of the bread and other products already mentioned. $ 850-4. Departments of bakery

The building or premises used as a bakery shall contain the following departments: 

(1) Kneading and baking. The oven shall be fireproof, with the specific requirements that the floor shall be of terra cotta or other refractory material. Said oven shall have two openings, one for the baking of bread, and the other, which must be on the outside of the building, for the introduction of fuel and the cleaning of the oven. The kneading shall be done by machinery when, in the opinion of the Secretary of Health, the quantity of bread baked justifies the expenditure. The dough shall be kept in a receptacle lined with a smooth, nonabsorbent material. (2) Warehouse for storage of flour and other ingredients connected with the industry. (3) Premises for the sale of bread. These premises shall contain a place for the storage and preservation of the bread in good condition. (4) Department for cleansing all utensils used in the work, in which department there shall be installed one or more porcelainlined sinks with an abundant supply of water. (5) Room for employees, provided with shower baths, porcelain washbowls, sanitary towels and an abundant supply of water. (6) A toilet or latrine as the case may be. The toilet room shall not be in direct communication with any department of the bakery. 

The latrine shall be constructed outside of the building and never at less than 3 meters from any part thereof. This department shall be maintained flyproof.

TITLE 25 

115

T.§ 850-5 Ch. 59 

 § 850-5. Walls 

The interior and exterior walls of the bakery shall be of concrete, metal work covered with cement, or brick. 

§ 850-6. Light and air 

All departments shall receive light and air directly from the street, from an alley 2 meters wide, or from a courtyard of not less than 3 by 5 meters, and in each department the area of the doors or windows opening into these spaces shall not be less than one-fifth of the area of its floor; provided, that when the greatest length of a department shall be more than twice the height from the floor to the ceiling, the Secretary of Health may require the installation, in the ceiling of said department, of a mechanical apparatus for air circulation and the construction of a glasscovered skylight. The courtyard and alley mentioned in this section shall be the property of the proprietor of the building and said openings shall be roofless. $ 850-7. Motor

The motor used in a bakery shall be placed outside of the site used for kneading and baking, unless it is an electric motor. 

§ 850-8. Floors 

The floors of all departments shall be at least 12 inches above the ground, constructed of cement, asphalt, or tiles, and shall be scrubbed daily. Said floors shall have the necessary drainage and shall be ratproof. 

§ 850-9. Interior walls, ceilings 

All departments shall be at least 12 feet high, the walls shall be plastered, cemented, polished, or wainscoated, the ceiling shall be plastered or covered with boards or metal, and shall be whitewashed at least twice a year. $ 850-10. Bathrooms and toilets

In the bathrooms and toilets the floors and the walls to a height of 1.50 meters shall be of a white, nonabsorbent material and shall form a solid body with the cement. 

§ 850-11. Furniture and utensils 

All furniture and utensils shall be so placed as to be easily moved, and the space between them and the floor shall be kept clean and (t 116

T.24 § 850-17 

in such condition that it will not harbor rats. No rubbish or any other objects which may become breeding places for insects or rats shall be kept in bakeries; provided, that all vessels, utensils, and other objects that are or may come into immediate contact with the bread after kneading and in the necessary handling process of making it shall be kept scrupulously clean. 

§ 850-12. Wood for fuel 

Wood for fuel shall be stored in an appropriate place outside of the building, and shall be piled on frames constructed in such manner that the distance between the lowest crossbeam of the same and the ground shall not be less than 2 feet; provided, that if the yard is of concrete no frame is necessary. § 850-13. Rats, flies, animals; nearness to other establishments; sweeping; sleeping in 

Bakeries shall be maintained rat-, fly- and insect-proof and free from all domestic animals, and shall be removed from cigar factories, stables, and barns. Neither shall these last-named establishments be installed within such distance as to be harmful to an existing bakery. Dry sweeping which may disseminate dust is prohibited. No person shall sleep in any department of a bakery. 

§ 850-14. Spitting 

Bakeries shall be provided with cuspidors, containing a sufficient quantity of disinfectant which shall be changed daily. Spitting on the floor is prohibited. 

§ 850-15. Health of personnel 

No person shall be employed in any bakery who is suffering from tuberculosis, scrofuloderm, venereal diseases, syphilitic ulcerations, or simple or contagious dermatosis. No person shall be employed unless previously provided with the corresponding health certificate by the proper officer of the Department of Health. 

§ 850-16. Cleanliness of personnel 

The manager, or person in charge of the bakery, as well as his assistants, shall always be clean while preparing, handling, manufacturing, or selling bread and flour products. $ 850-17. Flour standards

For the purposes of this Division, wheat flour or superfine wheat flour shall be understood to be that which being clean and sound 117

T.§ 850-17 Ch. 59 

conforms to the official standards of the Pure Food and Drug Law approved by the United States Congress on June 30, 1906, as applied to Puerto Rico. If different from this standard, it shall be considered abnormal and cannot be used in the manufacture of bread, except in accordance with the provisions of the following section. 

Codification. "Insular possessions" was changed to "Puerto 

Rico" pursuant to the Constitution.

Text references. The Pure Food and Drug Law of 1906 was repealed and superseded by the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act of June 25, 1938, ch. 675, 52 Stat. 1040; 21 U.S.C. 

§§ 301-392. 

§ 850-18. Mixture with inferior flour

The manufacture of bread containing a mixture of wheat flour and other flours of quality inferior to the standard fixed in the preceding section is not prohibited; provided, that when selling the product this condition is specified; and provided, further, that in the mixture, the maximum of inferior flour used shall be 50 percent. 

Cross references. Enriched flour, see § 855-1 et seq. of this title. $ 850-19. Wheat bread (a) For the purposes of this Division wheat bread shall be understood to be the product prepared with wheat flour, kneaded and fermented under good hygienic conditions by sanitary mechanical processes and placed in the oven until completely baked. (b) This bread shall be light and spongy, with a nutty smell and sui generis taste; filtered water or pure milk, eggs or lard shall be used in its preparation, and the salt and yeast used shall be of best quality and in good hygienic condition. § 850-20. Yeast

Only such yeasts shall be used as combine the following characteristics: Uniform creamy-white color, firm, uniform texture, damp but not soapy in appearance, with a characteristic odor of apples. No yeasts shall be used, the smell of which indicates incipient or advanced decomposition or which show dark or colored stripes. § 850-21. Quality of food sold

No product shall be sold or offered for sale in Puerto Rico if made from sour or unwholesome flour, or if mixed with mineral 118

Ch. T.24 § 850-25 BREAD salts or other ingredients, or if its condition is such that when used for food it may be injurious or seriously affect health. § 850-22. Wrapping; transportation

Every loaf of bread, of whatever kind, size or weight, as soon as it is baked, shall be carefully wrapped in paper and thus kept until distributed to the public; provided, that when a bakery has a regular order to deliver a certain quantity of bread every day at retail to a certain person, or in case of a large amount of loaves previously ordered, the loaves may be delivered wrapped in one bundle. This shall be done as soon as the bread is baked. Bread shall be kept and transported in vehicles which are insectproof and dustproof. 

§ 850-23. Fuel for ovens 

Boards or other substances which have been painted or subjected to any chemical preparation or which may be impregnated by injurious substances are prohibited for use as fuel in the ovens of bakeries. § 850-24. Addition of ingredients; unusual processes

The addition to wheat flours of any substances tending to increase their natural weight or volume is prohibited as well as the employment of processes extraneous to the natural and known processes of bread making which have been proven by experience; provided, that in any bread, the dough of which is not composed exclusively of wheat flour, yeast, common salt and well-filtered water, its composition shall be clearly expressed at time of sale; and provided, further, that nothing contained in this Division shall be understood to be opposed to the making of bread if its manufacture be in accordance with the general sanitary conditions required by this Division as to the making of wheat bread. 

§ 850-25. Compliance 

This Division shall be applicable to newly constructed bakeries; provided, that the Secretary of Health is authorized to omit any of its requirements when, in his opinion, the quantity of bread baked does not justify the expense and such omission will not be injurious to public health; provided, further, that bakeries now existing shall be altered and made to conform, as far as possible, to the provisions of this Division, within a reasonable time, as may be ordered by the Secretary of Health from time to time.

 § 850-26. Penalties 

Any person violating any provision of this Division shall be punished by a fine of not less than $1 nor more than $100, or by imprisonment of from 1 to 30 days, or both, in the discretion of the court.

Bread of normal acidity is desirable because it contributes to the digestion of this food and affords a pleasing taste during its mastication and deglutition.

§ 850-102. Conforming to standards

It shall be the duty of every manufacturer of bread prepared from wheat flour in the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico to conform strictly to the standards established in this industry, and to control the factors which determine a higher or lower acidity of the dough during the panification, that is: The cleanliness, the quantity of common salt, and the quantity and quality of the fresh and active ferment being used. § 850-103. Acidity

Wheat bread shall never exceed a normal acidity of 6 degrees, a degree of acidity being the number of cubic centimeters of a normal solution of caustic soda consumed in the titration of each 

100 grams of the bread dough. § 850-104. Effectiveness

This Division shall take effect from this date. Approved today, June 7, 1934.

§ 855-2. Definitions 

For the purposes of the enforcement and application of the provisions of this Subchapter, the following definitions shall govern: (1) "Federal regulations" means the regulations promulgated under the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act, as they appear in the Code of Federal Regulations, as heretofore or hereafter amended. (2) "Flour" means flour of any kind or description made from the wheat kernel and conforming to the definitions and standards contained in the Federal Regulations, but shall exclude whole wheat flour made from the entire kernel, and containing the same in full, without removal of the natural components. (3) "Enriched flour" means flour to which vitamins and other nutritional ingredients, essential to good nourishment, have been added, in conformity with the definitions and identity standards 121

§ 855-3. Use of enriched flour 

Any food product which is offered for sale in the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico, made in whole or in part with flour, shall be manufactured with enriched flour; provided, that other than enriched flour may be used in any imported food product, in the manufacture of which the flour used is 10% or less of its dry weight and when that portion of flour is not an essential in the nutritive content of that product and when used only with the purpose of providing consistency to the final product. 

§ 855-4. Conformance to law 

Any flour used, possessed, manufactured, given, presented, sold, stored, or anywise conveyed for industrial or commercial purposes shall meet the requirements established by Act No. 183 of May 12, 1948 [24 L.P.R.A. §§ 851-858].

§ 855-5. Nonconforming flour 

Any flour that is introduced or processed in the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico for agricultural, industrial, or for uses other than for human consumption shall be denaturalized prior to its entrance into Puerto Rico or immediately after being processed if processed in Puerto Rico. 

§ 855-6. Labeling 

Any flour or wheat flour product produced in whole or in part with wheat flour, that is offered for sale, stored, or given in the 

Commonwealth of Puerto Rico shall be labeled in conformity with

§ 712-1 et seq. of this title. 

§ 855-7. Suspension of provisions 

In the event that the Secretary of Health of the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico has indubitable proof that a shortage of enriched flour is imminent, he shall suspend the provisions hereof insofar as they refer to the use of enriched flour; provided, that the Secretary of Health may, as soon as circumstances permit, enforce this 

Subchapter in full again. § 855-8. Samples; investigation

For the purposes of strict enforcement of this Subchapter, the Secretary of Health and his legal representatives are hereby authorized to take samples to be used in examinations and investigations. His agents and officers shall have authority to enter at reasonable hours into any factory, establishment, store, or dock where flour may be stored or into any factory, establishment, or store where white bread or any other product made in whole or in part of flour is produced, handled, packed, sold, or stored for human consumption or into any vehicle in use for the transportation of the above. Such agents and officers shall be authorized to inspect any or all the places or vehicles aforesaid, and such flour or flour products, as well as such materials, containers, labels, and other equipment as may be found therein and to take the necessary samples for analysis.

Chapter 63. Drugs Generally Subchapter 910. Medicines and Other Products DIVISION 1. BIOLOGICAL PRODUCTS; CARE AND PRESERVATION SECTIONS

910-9. Penalties § 910-1. License for sale of biological products

No person, firm, syndicate, corporation, proprietor, or administrator of a pharmacy or drugstore in Puerto Rico shall offer for sale any biological product without having previously obtained a license from the Department of Health.

§ 910-2. Refrigeration 

All biological products kept for public sale by any person, firm, syndicate, corporation, proprietor, or administrator of a pharmacy or drugstore in Puerto Rico shall be stored in refrigerators, the temperature of which shall not be greater than 12.5° C. or 55° F; provided, that all biological products that are kept outside of the refrigerator shall be seized according to the provisions of Regulation No. 53. 

Text references. Sanitary Regulation No. 53, referred to in text, was not filed with the Secretary of State. For regulation relating to sampling and seizure of foods and drugs, see 

§ 730-1 et seq. of this title. 

129 [T.24]

T.§ 910-3 Ch. 63 

 § 910-3. Inspection of refrigerators 

Refrigerators designed for the storing of these biological products shall be open to inspection, for investigation purposes, by any inspector of the Department of Health from 6 a.m. to 10 p.m. 

§ 910-4. Thermometer 

The Department of Health shall provide each inspector engaged in this work with a certified thermometer, the mercurial column of which shall be visible and the degree of temperature marked, easy to read; and said inspector shall be duly instructed in the use of it. 

§ 910-5. Confiscation 

If the sanitary inspector should find, at any moment and during the investigation, that the refrigerator used for the keeping of biological products has a temperature greater than 12.5° C. or 

55° F., this would be sufficient reason for the said inspector to proceed to the confiscation, as provided sec. 910-2 of this title, of all the biological products found, at that moment, in the refrigerator. 

§ 910-6. License suspension 

The Department of Health shall revoke all licenses granted pursuant to this Division to any person, firm, syndicate, corporation, proprietor, or administrator of a pharmacy or drugstore incurring a second offense; and this person, firm, syndicate, corporation, proprietor, or administrator of a pharmacy or drugstore shall not offer for sale any biological product for a period of not less than 6 months. 

§ 910-7. License revocation 

The Department of Health shall revoke definitely the license of any person, firm, syndicate, corporation, proprietor, or administrator of a pharmacy or drugstore violating this Division for a third time; and shall direct a communication to all physicians of 

Puerto Rico notifying them that such person, firm, syndicate, corporation, proprietor, or administrator of a pharmacy or drugstore is prohibited from offering or exhibiting for sale any biological product. 

§ 910-8. Posting of license 

The license issued by the Department of Health authorizing the sale of biological products shall be so conspicuously placed over the refrigerator used for the storing of these products that it may be readily seen at all times. 130

§ 910-51. Registration of formulas 

(a) It is the obligation of each person, firm, syndicate, corporation, owner, or manager of a pharmacy or drugstore, business, industry, or factory that prepares or compounds original medicinal formulas, or patent medicines for internal or external pharmacological use, before placing such preparations on public sale in a drugstore, pharmacy, or any other business concern, or distributing in homes or giving them as free samples, in Puerto Rico, to submit for filing and registration the formulas of such preparations and to obtain a certificate of registration from the Department of Health of Puerto Rico. 

(b) It is the obligation, too, of any salesman or agent of patent and proprietary medicines to register his name and address in the office of the Head of the Inspectors of Food and Drugs in the 

Department of Health. 

(c) The provisions of this section will not be applied to any drug or medicinal preparation prepared according to a medical prescription written and signed by a physician legally authorized to practice medicine in Puerto Rico, provided this prescription has been given specifically for a particular person and not for general use, and that this drug or medicinal preparation has been sold or given for the exclusive use of the person for whom it was prescribed and prepared. 131

§ 910-52. Medicines covered 

The medicinal formulas or patent medicines to be considered under this Division are all those preparations or medicinal compounds manufactured or prepared for internal or external use and whose name, composition, or definition is not included under any formula or preparation registered in the U. S. Pharmacopeia or the National Formulary. 

§ 910-53. Application for registration 

(a) For the filing and registration, the petitioner shall submit to the Secretary of Health an application made under oath with the following information: 

(1) Name of the preparation.

(2) Name of the petitioner (indicating if he is owner, importer, or agent). (3) Place or address where the preparation is manufactured or compounded. (4) Consistency or form of preparation (indicating whether it is solid, liquid, in form of pills, etc.). (5) Complete formula of the preparation. (6) Uses and therapeutic action of the preparation. (7) Exact text of advertisements, posters, labels or literature that are attached to or included with the containers, being in form of circulars or pamphlets; and also should include: (A) If it is a corporation: (i) Complete name of the corporation. (ii) When and where incorporated. (iii) Board of directors of the corporation. (iv) Address of the business offices. (ii) Name of persons who do business under that trademark. (b) No person, firm, syndicate, or corporation, by itself or through its agents shall write, publish, distribute, or cause to circulate or shall post in any public place, or help directly or indirectly to write, publish, distribute, or post in a public place, or print in newspapers or publications of any kind, any propaganda concerning any patent or proprietary medicine whose labels, advertisements, or literature included with the containers contain assertions, statements, or other matter that may be misleading, false, or deceitful.

The labels, advertisements, printed material, pamphlets, etc., of a registered formula shall not be changed without previous consent of the  § 910-55. Confidential nature of formula

The Department of Health will not furnish information related to the components of any formula on file unless an order is issued by a court of justice. 133

T.§ 910-56 Ch. 63 

 § 910-56. Filing 

The documents of each registered formula will be filed in the Office of the Secretary of Health in an appropriate place under correlative numbers. 

§ 910-57. Certificate 

The Secretary of Health will give the applicant a certificate of the formula on file with its corresponding serial number. This certificate will indicate the name of each preparation as registered by any person, firm, or corporation, and also the name of the person who applies for the registry and the date. The Department of Health will publish every month in its official bulletin or in daily newspapers, a complete list of all the patent and proprietary medicines that have been registered in accordance with this Division. § 910-58. Department responsibility as to therapeutic properties, advertising In no label or advertisement whatsoever will a reference be made to the effect that the Department of Health accepts any responsibility as to the therapeutic properties of such preparations. $ 910-59. Refusal to file (a) The Secretary of Health will not file any medicinal formula under the following conditions: (1) If the alcohol content is in excess of the amount necessary as a solvent or preservative, or if the medicinal content is not of sufficient, quantity to make it useless as an intoxicating beverage. (2) If it is advertised or used directly or indirectly to cause abortion or for any immoral or illegal purpose. (3) If it is claimed by advertisements or recommendations that such preparation is specifically for the cure of any disease, or physical condition or deformity. (4) If it is to be used for infants of less than 1 year of age and if it contains any substance that is considered dangerous for such children. (5) If it is not in accordance with the provisions of subsec. (b) of sec. 910-53 of this title. (6) If it contains opium or any of its derivatives and it is not indicated on the label in letters no less than half inch in size. (7) If it contains cocaine (alkaloid) or its salts; alpha or beta eucaine, or its salts, or any mixture, compound, or product of eucaine or its salts.

Ch. T.24 § 910-62 

DRUGS GENERALLY 

(b) The Secretary of Health will give his approval for filing of any medicinal formula that has been investigated and accepted by the Council of Chemistry and Pharmacy of the American Medical Association, on the presentation by the petitioner of written proof to indicate that the medicinal preparation is in conformity with the conditions established by this section. 

§ 910-60. Inspection 

The inspector will collect from time to time, as ordered by the Secretary of Health, samples of the preparations with formulas that have been registered with the Department of Health, in accordance with the standard method for the taking of official samples as described by Regulation No. 53 of the Board of Health, that regulates the preparation of foods and drugs; however, it is to be understood that if the chemical analysis indicates that the composition of the preparation is different from the registered formula, or if the label or literature which accompanies the containers has been altered without being authorized by the Department, the Secretary of Health will cancel the registration of this preparation and will notify the person who sells it and the agent or authorized representative for the sale of the medicinal product. 

Text references. Regulation No. 53, referred to in text, was not filed with the Secretary of State. For provisions relating to sampling of drugs, see § 730-1 et seq. of this title. 

§ 910-61. Enforcement 

Whenever the Secretary of Health finds that the provisions of the preceding section; of subsec. (b) of sec. 910-53; or of sec. 

910-54 are violated, or, in general, that any medicine or patent formula is sold or distributed in homes, or given as free samples, in Puerto Rico, in violation of the general provisions of this division, he will order the corresponding criminal action to be followed and hence will ask the Secretary of Justice to establish the necessary civil procedure, so that the sale and distribution of such preparation will be stopped. The Secretary of Health is authorized to annul any certificate of registration given when the verdict of the court is established. 

§ 910-62. Penalties 

The breach of any of the provisions of this division will be punished according to sec. 33 of the "Act to Reorganize the Health 

Service," approved March 14, 1912 [3 L.P.R.A. § 187].

§ 946-1. Definitions 

In connection with this division, the following words and phrases shall have the meanings expressed hereunder: (1) "Practitioner". The professional authorized by law to practice as a physician, dentist or veterinarian in Puerto Rico. (2) "Pharmacy (Drugstore)". When not otherwise limited in this division, pharmacy shall mean an establishment registered and authorized by the Department of Health, in which chemical products, drugs, pharmaceutic products, pharmaceutical or proprietary specialties, prescriptions, medicine, and poisons are prepared, preserved, sold at retail, and placed in containers, and which may also deal in such other articles of lawful commerce, as may be customarily sold in the pharmacies of Puerto Rico. (3) "Medical or practitioner's formula or prescription". A written order by a physician, dentist, or veterinarian in order that certain medicine be prepared by a registered pharmacist, or by a pharmacy aide under the immediate supervision of a pharmacist, at a registered pharmacy or drugstore.

§ 946-2. Prescriptions - How issued 

All prescriptions for barbiturates, dangerous drugs or antibiotics must be issued exclusively by a physician, dentist or veterinarian, who shall be responsible for the correct prescription of barbiturates or dangerous drugs. § 946-3. Practitioner's orders or prescription requirements (a) All prescriptions for barbiturates, dangerous drugs or antibiotics must have the following information: (1) Date issued and practitioner's signature (must be signed at the moment issued). (2) Patient's name in full, and age. (3) Patient's complete address (including street and number, kilometer and barrio, as the case may be). (4) Directions for the use of the drug. (5) Name, address (street and number) of the practitioner. (b) These prescriptions must be written in ink or indelible pencil, or typewritten. 

§ 946-4. Filling prescriptions 

(a) Prescriptions for barbiturates, dangerous drugs and antibiotics shall be filled or prepared excusively by a pharmacist or a pharmacy aide under the immediate supervision of the pharmacist. (b) The pharmacist shall not fill any prescription which has been erased or altered in any manner, and which does not comply with the prescription requirements set forth in sec. 946-3 of this title. 

(c) It is permitted to fill partially a prescription containing barbiturates, dangerous drugs and antibiotics, only when there is not at hand a sufficient quantity of the dangerous drugs, barbiturates or antibiotics, or if the patient does not have enough funds to purchase the quantity prescribed, in which case the pharmacist must write on the front of the prescription the quantity issued and on the back of the prescription the reason for not dispensing the 

Nov. 30, 1963 

Vol. 2, No. 7 136A1

T.§ 946-4 Ch. 63 

quantity prescribed; providing, that if the balance of the amount prescribed is obtained from the same drugstore a new prescription will not be required. 

§ 946-5. Filling and copies of prescriptions 

The repetition of a medical or practitioner's order or prescription for barbiturates, antibiotics and other dangerous drugs is hereby prohibited, except when the prescription includes the written and signed order of a person empowered in this division to issue the same authorizing its repetition and also stating the number of times it may be refilled, in which case a notation of the date in which the repetition takes place must be made on the prescription. 

§ 946-6. Inventories - Pharmacies 

Every pharmaceutical establishment shall maintain for a period of not less than 2 years from the date thereof, an inventory of the barbiturates and dangerous drugs in its possession, prepared in accordance with sec. 9 of the "Barbiturates and Other Dangerous 

Drugs Law" [24 L.P.R.A. § 938]. 

§ 946-7. Manufacturers, wholesale druggists, or distributors

All manufacturers, wholesale druggists, or distributors of barbiturates and dangerous drugs, shall: (1) Maintain, for a minimum of 2 years from the date in which it was prepared, an inventory of the barbiturates and dangerous drugs in his possession, prepared in accordance with sec. 10 of the "Barbiturates and Other Dangerous Drugs Law" [24 L.P.R.A. 

§ 939]. (2) Issue to every person, establishment or institution to whom delivery of barbiturates and/or dangerous drugs is made, 2 copies of each invoice or voucher of delivery. (3) Inform the Secretary of Health concerning any new barbiturate product, dangerous drug or antibiotic to be distributed or introduced by them in Puerto Rico. (4) Label any barbiturate, dangerous drug and antibiotic covered by the provisions of this division, not subject to the provisions of sec. 503, clause (b) (4) of the Federal Foods, Drugs and

Cosmetic Act, on its container, in legible form, the following in scription: Act No. 126 (1960) [24 L.P.R.A. sec. 933] prohibits dispensing without practitioner's prescription".

§ 946-8. Telephone orders 

Notwithstanding the provisions of sec. 946-2 of this title, the pharmacist may fill an order for barbiturates, dangerous drugs or antibiotics received by telephone from a duly identified practitioner, who guarantees a state of emergency. The practitioner in turn shall reduce the verbal order (prescription) to writing and send it to the pharmacy for filing. § 946-9. Possession and protection of barbiturates and other dangerous drugs (a) The barbiturates and other dangerous drugs referred to in this division must not be accessible to the public and should be adequately protected. Said barbiturates and other dangerous drugs shall be always accessible during service hours for the inspection of the drugs and pharmacy inspectors and officials authorized by the Department of Health. 

(b) The barbiturates and other dangerous drugs must be kept in their containers properly labeled. (c) Care should be taken to avoid having more than one open bottle of the same drug and dosage. As soon as a bottle is emptied it should be eliminated from the place where it is kept. § 946-10. Losses (a) In case of the loss of barbiturates, dangerous drugs or antibiotics due to breakage, accident or theft, the owner, as soon as the breakage, accident, or theft is discovered, shall notify the

Secretary of Health immediately, by means of a sworn statement in duplicate.

 § 976j-3. Definitions 

For the purposes of this Division the following words and terms shall have the meanings expressed below, unless otherwise expressly stated in the text hereof: (1) "Person": Any natural or artificial person, including partnerships and corporations. 

(2) "Department": Department of the Treasury of Puerto Rico. 

(3) "Secretary": Secretary of the Treasury of Puerto Rico. 

(4) "Agent": Any official or employee of the Department designated by the Secretary to intervene in the application of the 

Narcotics Act of Puerto Rico and its Regulations, or any other person designated by the Secretary for this same purpose.

(5) "Narcotics Act": Act No. 48 of June 18, 1959, known as the Narcotics Act of Puerto Rico [24 L.P.R.A. §§ 973 to 976m]. 

(6) "Convict": Any person convicted in any court of Puerto Rico, of the United States, of any state or territory of the United States, or of any foreign country, for any violation or infringement of any law relative to the control of narcotic drugs. (7) "Nonresident convict": Any convict residing outside of 

Puerto Rico who enters the jurisdiction of Puerto Rico for the purpose of staying for more than 48 hours. (8) "Resident convict": Any convict residing in Puerto Rico. (9) "Narcotic drug": Includes coca leaves, opium, marihuana, isonipecaine, any substance neither physically nor chemically distinguishable from these, and any other substance that the Secretary, after a public hearing and upon expert opinion, may declare a narcotic drug.

(a) Every person registered under the provisions of this Division shall be bound to carry with him at all times the registration certificate which shall be issued to him upon registration. (b) The certificate of registration shall be in the form of an identification card and, even though it will bear the official title of the Narcotics Act, it shall contain only the information corresponding to the person registered that may be necessary for his positive identification.

§ 976j-12. Travelling permit 

(a) Any person bound to register under the provisions of sec.

49 

of the Narcotics Act [24 L.P.R.A. § 976a] and of this Division, shall report his intent, if any, of travelling abroad, or to the United States, its territories and possessions, at least 24 hours in advance of the trip. (b) Every registered person who intends to travel abroad, or to the United States, its territories and possessions, shall report under oath the purpose or motive of the trip, place and location where he is going, time he will be outside of Puerto Rico, as well as any other information which the Secretary or his agent may deem pertinent. (c) The Secretary or his agent shall issue a travelling permit to any person who shall comply with the provisions of this section, and the person to whom such travelling permit is issued shall be bound to return same to the Secretary or his agent within 24 hours after his return to Puerto Rico. 

§ 976j-13. Penal provisions 

Any person bound to register under the provisions of sec.

49 of the Narcotics Act [24 L.P.R.A. § 976a] and of this Division who fails or refuses to appear in person for such purpose, or who furnishes falsely or incompletely the information required by the Narcotics Act and this Division, or who refuses to be fingerprinted or photographed or to submit a sample of his handwriting or to notify any change of address, or who refuses to apply for a permit to travel abroad, or who refuses to return the travelling permit after his return to Puerto Rico, shall be guilty of a misdemeanor and shall be sentenced to a fine of not more than 1,000 dollars nor less than 200 dollars, or to imprisonment for not more than 2 years nor less than 3 months, or both, in the discretion of the court, pursuant to secs. 49 and 50 of the Narcotics Act [24 L.P.R.A. 

§§ 976a and 976b].

 § 976j-14. Administrative provisions 

(a) Returns, statements, records or any other document issued pursuant to the provisions of secs. 49 and 50 of the Narcotics Act 

[24 L.P.R.A. §§ 976a and 976b] shall be public documents, but shall be accessible to inspection only by those commonwealth or federal agencies whose functions are related to the work of public order, criminal, quasi-criminal, and fiscal investigation, public health, public service, supervision of persons on probation and other types of parole or conditional pardon, as well as to all other agencies whose officials are related to these functions and duties. (b) No officer or employee of the Department shall divulge, or make known under any circumstance, except pursuant to the Narcotics Act and as provided by this Division, the information contained in the returns, statements, records or other documents inspected by or furnished to the Secretary, or permit the examination or inspection thereof by persons not lawfully authorized. 

(c) Pursuant to sec. 28 of the Narcotics Act [24 L.P.R.A. 

§ 974y] any official or employee of the Department violating the preceding provision shall be guilty of a felony, as provided in sec. 48 of the Narcotics Act [24 L.P.R.A. § 976]. 

§ 976j-15. Narcotic-drugs destruction supervising committee

Every narcotic or narcotic drug confiscated and forfeited under the Narcotics Act [24 L.P.R.A. §§ 973 to 976m], if susceptible of being used for medical or scientific purposes, shall be delivered by the Secretary to the Secretary of Health or to a nonprofit charitable institution, upon request. If there is no request to that effect from the Department of Health or any such institution, or if such narcotic drugs are not susceptible of being used for medical or scientific purposes, the same shall be destroyed by the Secretary or his agent in the presence of a committee composed by the head of the Internal Surveillance Division of the Department and the person in charge of the Narcotics Administrative Transactions Section of the Special Investigations Office of the Department, and said committee shall draw up minutes of the act wherein shall be set forth the quantity and origin of the drugs destroyed and the date when destroyed.

Narcotics Act of Puerto Rico and its Regulations, or any other person designated by the Secretary for this same purpose.

(5) "Narcotics Act": Act No. 48 of June 19, 1959, known as "Narcotics Act of Puerto Rico" [24 L.P.R.A. §§ 973 to 976m]. 

(6) "Importer, manufacturer, producer, or compounder': Any person who imports, manufactures, compounds, or otherwise produces for sale or distributes any of the narcotics and other drugs regulated by the Narcotics Act; but the term does not include the persons who, under the provisions of said Act, are authorized to manufacture, compound or produce such narcotic drugs for sale or distribution on medical order or prescription. (7) "Collector": Collector of internal revenue of each municipality. (8) "Narcotic drug": Includes coca leaves, opium, marihuana, isonipecaine, any substance neither physically nor chemically distinguishable from these, and any other substance that the Secretary, after a public hearing and upon expert opinion, may declare a narcotic drug. 

(9) "Federal Narcotic Laws": The United States laws relating to opium, coca leaves, marihuana, and all other narcotic drugs.

§ 976j-54. Stamps and/or identification marks (a) Every importer, producer, manufacturer, compounder or wholesale dealer authorized to purchase, sell, distribute or in any manner dispose of narcotics or narcotic drugs shall do so in stamped containers or packages, duly identified by the stamp or identifica tion mark provided under the Narcotics Act [24 L.P.R.A. §§ 973 

to 976m] and/or the federal narcotic laws.

(b) Any such person who shall repack any narcotic drugs covered by the Narcotics Act shall be bound to affix to each new container a stamp, herein below described, on a conspicuous part of the new container and so that when the container is opened the stamp is destroyed and part thereof remains adhered to the container. 

§ 976j-55. Stamp described 

The stamp to be used on each new container, as stated in the preceding section, shall be rectangular in form, approximately 3 inches long by 1 inch wide, on paper of any color, containing at the upper front end the following legend in black ink: "Commonwealth of Puerto Rico, Department of the Treasury, Office of the 

Secretary" and at the center, in red ink: "Narcotic", and at the lower end, in black ink: "Repacked according to law". § 976j-56. Printing and safekeeping of stamps

The Bureau of the Treasury shall be responsible for the printing and safekeeping of the stamps to be used on each new container of narcotics. This Bureau shall adopt the necessary measures to have said stamp available for sale at all times after the original issue has been obtained. 

§ 976j-57. Sale of stamps 

The collectors shall sell the stamps to be used on the new containers of narcotics to every importer, manufacturer, producer or compounder repacking any narcotic drugs covered by the Narcotic 

Act [24 L.P.R.A. §§ 973 to 976m]. The collectors shall make their requisitions for the said stamps directly to the Bureau of the Treasury on the forms prepared for that purpose by the Collection Bureau. The Bureau of the Treasury shall send the stamps requested by the collectors directly to them and shall at the same time process the necessary documents for the accounting of the delivery of these stamps. § 976j-58. Stamp fee payable

The collectors shall sell the aforesaid stamps at the rate of one cent each to any importer, manufacturer, producer repacking any narcotic drugs covered by the Narcotics Act [24 L.P.R.A. §§ 973 to 

976m] and having his license in good standing, as verified by the collector in each case. Each such person shall be bound to affix 1962

§ 976j-59. Penal provisions 

(a) As soon as this Division takes effect and the collectors shall have put on sale the afore-mentioned stamps, the absence of such stamps on any container holding narcotic drugs shall constitute prima facie evidence that the same constitutes contraband. 

(b) As provided in sec. 34 of the Narcotics Act [24 L.P.R.A. 

§§ 974ee], every container or package of narcotic drugs so found shall be confiscated and forfeited; and there shall likewise be confiscated and forfeited every container or package of narcotic drugs which, although bearing such stamps, is found in the possession of persons not authorized by said act to possess them. (c) Every person possessing, safekeeping, selling, purchasing, transporting, concealing or in any manner acquiring or disposing of any of the narcotic drugs covered by the Narcotics Act whose wrappers or containers lack the distinctive marks, adopted in this Division for identification purposes, shall be guilty of a felony, and shall, upon conviction, be punished as prescribed in sec. 37 of the 

Narcotics Act [24 L.P.R.A. § 975a]. 

§ 976j-60. Druggists 

(a) Druggists and pharmacy aides duly authorized by law, the latter under the supervision of the druggist, may dispense narcotic drugs to any person on a written order or prescription duly issued by a physician, dentist or veterinarian authorized to prescribe narcotics, provided such order or prescription states the date on which issued, the complete name and exact address of the patient, the signature of the physician, dentist or veterinarian, and the registry number of the license entitling him to prescribe narcotics. 

No prescription for narcotic drugs shall be filled after the lapse of 2 days from its issuance. (b) Upon filling the prescription, the druggist or his pharmacy aide shall sign his name in ink or indelible pencil on the back of the prescription, expressing the date on which filled. The person filling the prescription shall label the container holding the dispensed drug. Said label shall express: (1) date on which filled: 1962

(2) name of the drugstore and license number; (3) complete name and exact address of the patient; (4) name of the practitioner. 

§ 976j-61. Cancellation or nonrenewal of licenses As provided in sec. 8 of the Narcotics Act [24 L.P.R.A. § 974e], the Secretary may, for good cause shown, cancel or not renew any license issued under the provisions of said Act to any person who shall at any time fail to comply with the provisions of said Act. 

The Secretary shall exercise the aforesaid power, in his discretion, in those cases in which he receives a report recommending such action from a master, who shall preside over a hearing, as provided hereinbelow. 

§ 976j-62. Summonses to hearings 

(a) When the Secretary or, in his behalf, the Director of Fiscal Investigations, has reason to believe that a given licensee under the Narcotics Act has failed to comply with the provisions thereof, he shall summon such person to appear before a master and show cause why any license issued to him under the provisions of the Narcotics Act should not be cancelled or not renewed. (b) Every summons to the aforesaid hearing shall be served and returned at least 5 days in advance of the day on which the hearing is to be held; and, as provided in subsec. (e) of sec. 57 of the 

Narcotics Act [24 L.P.R.A. § 976i (5)], the Secretary or his representative may direct any person so summoned to present documents, books, papers, cards or any other tangible property containing evidence which, in the judgment of the Secretary or his representative, is relevant. 

(c) Pursuant to subsec. (f) of sec. 57 of the Narcotics Act 

[24 L.P.R.A. § 976i (6)], in case of any refusal to comply with a summons or order issued by the Secretary under the powers granted him by said Act, the Secretary may resort to the Superior Court of Puerto Rico and pray the court a subpoena to compel obedience to said summons or order. § 976j-63. Holding of hearings (a) The hearing shall be presided over by a master, who shall be designated by the Secretary or his representative and shall be a public officer conversant with administrative law, preferably, a lawyer. The master shall decide on any question of fact and issues 1962 Vol. 1, No. 4 136.12

of law that may arise, as well as on the admission of evidence. (b) Every person summoned to appear shall do so personally, but shall be entitled to legal counsel and may present oral and/or expert testimony of such persons as he may deem pertinent, as well as documents, books, papers, cards or any tangible property containing relevant evidence. (c) The Secretary shall be represented by any officer or employee of the Department designated for the purpose, and may in turn present oral and/or expert testimony of such persons as he may deem pertinent, as well as documents, books, papers, cards or any tangible property containing relevant evidence. The proceedings of such hearing shall be taken in shorthand by a stenographic reporter. § 976j-64. Master's report

Immediately after the hearing the master shall render his report to the Secretary. Said report shall consist of a summary of the hearing, including an excerpt of each oral testimony given, as well as a description of any tangible evidence offered and accepted as such at the hearing. The master shall also set forth in said report the findings of fact and conclusions of law, with such recommendation as he may care to make. The master shall submit with his report a copy of the transcription of the stenographic record. § 976j-65. Secretary's decision

After receiving the report from the master who presided over the hearing, the Secretary shall make a decision on exoneration, cancellation, or nonrenewal of any license issued under the pro visions of the Narcotics Act [24 L.P.R.A. §§ 973 to 976m].

§ 1005-1. Definitions 

(a) "Poison" means any toxic substance that when applied externally to the body or introduced into the body through the mouth, rectum, vagina, skin, or lungs is able by its inherent properties to alter or detain some or all vital functions necessary to maintain life (Brundage Toxicology Manual). Poisons shall mean also all substances or chemical products whose composition includes arsenic, copper, mercury, lead, phosphorus, antimony, corrosive acids or alkaline bases or their derivatives and other substances of vegetable origin as alkaloids and glucosides, bland extracts or in powders, fluid extracts, tinctures and other substances of animal origin. (b) "Industrial poisons" means all substances, chemical products or any other type of products for technical, industrial, or agricultural use, such as insecticides, ovicides, fungicides, rodenticides, herbicides and industrial solvents. (c) "Inspector of Drugs and Pharmacies" means a pharmacist duly authorized to exercise his profession in Puerto Rico, who is an employee of the Government as determined by the Law of 

Pharmacy (Act 282 of 1945 [20 L.P.R.A. §§ 381-404]) with duties established by the Office of Personnel; providing, also, that such employee (the Inspector of Drugs and Pharmacies) shall be attached to the Bureau of Public Health Laboratories and shall possess good professional experience and shall enforce all present laws or others that may be enacted in the future to govern the practice of pharmacy or related activities, such as the manufacture, distribution and sale of medicines.

§ 1005-2. Registry of poisons The Inspector of Drugs and Pharmacies shall investigate the registry of poisons in all establishments that sell them at present or in the future. If a correction is made, no erasure shall be made but the notation shall be crossed out in red ink and the correct notation made at the margin. § 1005-3. § 1071-1. Births, marriages, and Deaths The following shall be registered in the General Registry of Vital Statistics of Puerto Rico and in local registries: 

(1) Births occurring in the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico. 

(2) Marriages performed in Puerto Rico. 

(3) Deaths occurring in Puerto Rico.

§ 1071-2. Events on high seas

On petition of an interested party the following may be registered: (1) Births occurring at sea if both parents or one of them is a resident of this Commonwealth. (2) Marriages celebrated at sea if the contracting parties or one of them is a known resident of this Commonwealth or has obtained a marriage license from any of the registries of Puerto Rico. 

§ 1071-3. Other matters to be recorded 

The following shall also be recorded not only in the General 

Registry but also in local registries: (1) Emancipations, recognitions and legitimations that affect or refer to any person whose birth is registered in any of said registries. (2) Adoptions. (3) Divorce decrees and decrees annulling a marriage.

§ 1071-4. Registration procedure 

To effectuate the notations referred to in the preceding section, the following rules shall be observed: (1) The documents pertaining to the decrees of emancipation, recognition, legitimation, adoption and in general to any judicial act which affects the civil status or the social condition of the registered person, shall be delivered or forwarded by the interested party to the Chief of the Bureau of Vital Statistics of the 

Department of Health of Puerto Rico, in charge of the General Registry of Vital Statistics of Puerto Rico, who shall issue a receipt on presentation of said document or documents; upon careful examination of said documents shall proceed to their final filing and shall make the corresponding notation on both the documents and the certificates, and shall instruct the corresponding local registrar to make an identical notation on the margin of the duplicate of the involved certificate which shall remain under his custody as a local record. (2) When a document presented or received for notations lacks required information for its validity or authenticity, the keeper of the general registry shall abstain from making the notation, and shall return it to the forwarding or delivering party, stating the defect or defects, for correction in the prescribed form. (3) In case of doubt regarding the origin or legality of the requested notation or if the interested or forwarding party does not recognize the need for correcting the defect referred to in the preceding rule, the Secretary of Health shall consult in writing with the Attorney General of Puerto Rico and shall resolve the doubt according to the determination of said Attorney General, without prejudice to the rights of the interested party, in any action in due form before a court. (4) When the birth of a person, to whom any of the notations that must be made refer, is not registered, the first step to be taken is to register said birth in accordance with the provisions of the Vital Statistics Act [24 L.P.R.A. §§ 1041-1302] and this Division. 

(5) When by virtue of a decree from a court it is necessary to alter any certificate filed in the General Registry of Vital Statistics, 141

T.§ 1071-4 

Ch. 83 a new certificate shall be made in accordance with the provisions of said decree, making on the previously filed certificate as well as on the corrected one notations of cross reference, in which there shall be stated the court which dictates the decree, date of the decree, and date of presentation to the Registry for its registration. 

§ 1071-5. Notations in books of old Civil Registry 

The same procedure as that established in sec. 1071-4 of this title shall be followed in regard to the notations which should be made in the books of the old Civil Registry of Puerto Rico, except that the documents pertaining to the act to which reference is made. in said section shall be presented or forwarded to the corresponding municipal secretary, who shall act in the form prescribed, noting in the margin of the books under his custody as well as on the duplicate filed in the court, the entries, corrections, additions, or amendments requested. 

§ 1071-6. Certificates of entries in Civil Registry 

The municipal secretaries in charge of the books of the old Civil 

Registry of Puerto Rico shall be authorized to issue certificates of the acts and entries contained in said books, or negatives if these do not exist, through payment of fees fixed by law, except when the copies requested are for legal or official use of any office of the Government of Puerto Rico or of the United States in which case these shall be issued free of charge. The same rule shall apply for the issuance of certified copies of the documents registered in the General Registry of Vital Statistics.

§ 1071-8. Age of children 

Municipal secretaries shall furnish information to an interested party with respect to the age of children registered in the books of the Civil Registry for the purpose of enrollment in public schools or for obtaining an employment permit. When said information is issued without certification no fee shall be collected. 

§ 1071-9. Relatives of registrars 

The registrars of vital statistics shall not register acts pertaining to themselves, or their relatives in direct line or by affinity or their collaterals to the second decree of consanguinity. For these registrations they shall be replaced by the alternate registrar designated to act as a substitute for them in the discharge of their duties. 

§ 1071-10. Registrations in old Civil Registry 

Registrars appointed by virtue of Act No. 24 of April 22, 1931 

[24 L.P.R.A. §§ 1041-1302], shall not make any registration in the books of the old Civil Registry. 

§ 1071-11. Alternate registrars 

In cases of absence, sickness, or any other legitimate disability of the registrar, the alternate registrar shall take charge. The appointment of alternate registrars shall be reported by the mayors to the Secretary of Health, giving the name of the designated person, date of appointment, and official and home address of the appointee so that the Department may communicate with them whenever circumstances demand. Compensation fixed by sec. 37 

of the Vital Statistics Registry Act [24 L.P.R.A. § 1236 note] 

belongs to the alternate registrar when he substitutes for the registrar. When the substitution is for less than one month, the 

Department will certify all payments to the registrar with whom the alternate registrar shall deal. 143
