Ch. 83

 § 1071-12. Examination of certificates 

The registrar shall examine the certificates on presentation and before accepting them for registration and before issuing a certificate of registration in case of births or burial or removal permit in case of deaths. 

§ 1071-13. Persons unable to write name 

When the interested or declaring party intervening in any registration does not know how to sign, it shall be necessary that another person, of legal age, sign in his stead as witness of the mark. 

§ 1071-14. Certificate unacceptable for registration 

If any certificate, received by mail, shall appear incomplete or with manifest errors, the registrar shall inform the sender that said certificate cannot be accepted for registration under said condition. No certificate having erasures, additions, or amendments or lacking information which could have been easily obtained, shall be accepted for registration. If all the required information cannot be obtained prior to presentation of the document for registration, the word "unknown" shall be written on the pertinent spaces. § 1071-15. Registration pending investigation

The prosecuting attorney or authorized officers in charge of the investigation of violent deaths or where a criminal act is suspected shall not delay in the remittance of the certificates on account of the investigation not being completed, but they shall certify the case as "pending investigation" and furnish the missing information on completion of the investigation. In said cases, the medical certification shall remain in blank until the investigation is complete and the cause of death determined. § 1071-16. Writing; required information

Certificates shall be written legibly, with indelible black ink, or typed, and no registration shall be considered complete if it lacks obtainable required information. § 1071-17. Place of registration of births and deaths; address

Births as well as deaths shall be registered in the place of occurrence, regardless of the place of residence of the newborn or of the deceased. The registrar shall see to it that all certificates contain the exact address, including street and house number or 144

Ch. 

T.24 § 1071-22 name of the barriada if in the urban area and name of barrio if in rural area. 

§ 1071-18. Signing of certificate 

All certificates shall be signed by the keeper of the register or the person officially substituting for him stating the date of registration. 

§ 1071-19. Corrections after registration 

After a certificate has been accepted by the registrar, neither it nor its transcription on the record books shall be subjected to erasures, additions, or amendments, without following appropriate legal procedure. Errors appearing on a certificate at presentation for registration or after registration, consisting of the misspelling or omission of any name, nickname, word or phrase, can be corrected, by rewriting in red ink, the word or words erroneously written or by inserting the omitted word or words. Necessary crossouts shall be made in such a way that the crossed-out word is legible. The registrar shall require evidence necessary to make said corrections according to each case. § 1071-20. Punctuality in making report 

No registrar who remits the monthly report after the fifth day of each month shall be entitled to the $2 compensation for punctuality in sending the report. A monthly report sent on the fifth day of a month, as indicated by the postmark, shall be considered as punctually remitted. § 1071-21. Completeness of monthly report 

The monthly report shall be accompanied by all certificates registered during the preceding month, or said report shall not be considered complete and the $2 compensation for punctual and complete remittance of the monthly report shall not be credited to the registrar's pay. § 1071-22. Date of presentation; retention of original certificate

The date of presentation of a certificate shall be the date on which it is received for registration at the registry. The registrar shall never return the original certificate to the declarants. In case of errors or omissions, the pertinent information shall be obtained by means other than returning the original certificate. 145

T.§ 1071-23 

Ch. 83 § 1071-23. Responsibility for registrations within district; fees

The registrars are held responsible for the exact registration of all births, marriages, and deaths occurring within their respective districts. However, no fees shall be paid for the registration of certificates of events occurring outside their districts. These shall be credited to the registrar of the corresponding district even though the latter has not registered them. § 1071-24. Unintelligible certificates; handwritten medical certifications

When the person filling out a certificate does it so badly that it is unintelligible, the registrar may demand of the said person that it be duly filled out. In any case where the certificate contains a medical certification, it must always be handwritten by the doctor authorizing said medical certification. § 1071-25. Certificates remitted only in monthly reports 

After the monthly report has been submitted, the registrar shall not remit any certificate to the Department until the following month, unless it is for the issuance of a certified copy or unless requested by the Department. § 1071-26. Requests for certified copies

When a person urgently needs a certified copy of any certificate, the registrar shall send the original certificate to the Department, even without a previous request by the Department, provided it comes accompanied by a request from the applicant and the fee for the issuance of certified copies in a certified check or postal money order payable to Official Bursar, Bureau of Vital Statistics.

The applicants shall state clearly their name and the address to which the certified copy is to be sent. § 1071-27. Subregistries; payment of deputy registrar

In the districts where one or more subregistries are established, the vital statistics monthly report corresponding to said subregistries shall be signed by the deputy registrar, with the initials of the local registrar, after the data has been checked. The fees shall be paid by the municipality in favor of the local registrar, with whom the deputy registrars shall deal directly for that part of the fees that belongs to them. 146

Ch. T.24 § 1071-34 

 § 1071-28. Index 

To facilitate the search for certificates in their registries, the registrars shall keep an alphabetical index of all registrations, separately, by type of certificate. § 1071-29. Register of physicians, midwives, embalmers, and undertakers A register of physicians, midwives, embalmers, and undertakers who reside and have open offices in the locality shall be kept in all registries. Sellers of coffins shall not be registered as undertakers, unless they are also in charge of interments. § 1071-30. Birth certificates; name of physician, midwife

On the birth certificates, medical attendance or its absence shall be specified. The name of the physician, midwife, or auxiliary midwife attending the delivery shall be stated. 

§ 1071-31. Certificates of registration of birth 

There shall be no charge for the issuance of the certificate of registration of birth provided for in sec. 34 of the Act [24 L.P.R.A. § 1234]. The registrar shall not issue said certificate in cases of stillbirths. § 1071-32. Multiple births

In cases of multiple birth, a certificate shall be issued for each child. § 1071-33. Information on certificate of birth registration

The registrar shall copy on said certificate of registration the information as it appears on the original certificate, so that the parents will be informed of the date of registration, name at registration, etc., for the purpose of reporting the existence of any error. 

The registrar shall see that it is corrected, inserting the necessary corrections or additions in red ink in the appropriate places of said certificate, according to the specifications of sec. 1071-19 of this title. 

§ 1071-34. One-year period of grace

Persons older than 10 days may be registered without penal sanction, during a year starting July 21, 1931. After this term has expired, if they present themselves voluntarily, they shall be registered by means of the cancellation, on the birth certificate, 147

T.1071-34 Ch. 83 

of a one-dollar internal-revenue stamp that the person concerned will furnish for each registration made. When the registration is desired of the birth of a person older than ten days, whose parents are absent or deceased, due to the fact that said birth has never been registered before, any close relative, or the physician or midwife who attended the birth may present and sign the birth certificate, in accordance with the regulations hereafter prescribed. § 1071-35. Registration of persons over 10 days old

In order to register a person over 10 days of age during and after the 1-year period of grace granted by law, the following rules shall be observed: (1) If the person whose registration is requested is a year old or under, has been born in the district where he is to be registered, and the registrar is certain that his birth has not been previously registered or is able to determine it by the written questionnaire to which he subjects the declarant or other persons, or by the examination of the books under his custody at the registry or those in the Civil Registry under the municipal secretary's custody, the registration shall be effectuated without other requisites than the presentation of the birth certificate and, if said registration is effectuated after the year of grace has expired, the cancellation of a $1 internal-revenue stamp in each case. (2) If the registrar can in no way determine that the birth has not been previously registered and doubts the validity of the declaration to that effect made by the interested party, he shall require the presentation of a sworn statement, according to the form prepared for that purpose by the  (3) The presentation of the sworn statement shall be required in every case of registration of a person over a year of age. (4) In case of a natural child the parent who attends to verify the registration shall sign the sworn statement and no mention. shall be made of the absent parent. (5) In the case of an acknowledged child both parents shall attend the registration, both signing the birth certificate and the sworn statement if the acknowledgment is made by both simultaneously; but, if the acknowledgment is made by only one parent, the said parent shall make the registration and the sworn statement. (6) In case of a legitimate or legitimized child, the fact that the marriage has been celebrated and the place and date of celebration shall be stated and in cases when it is necessary, if the registrar 148

Ch. 

T.24 § 1071-40 is not certain of the veracity of said circumstance, he may require the presentation of a certified copy of the marriage certificate. (7) When two or more children of the same parents are registered, said children may be included in one sworn statement, if necessary according to the above-mentioned rules. However, separate birth certificates shall be made for each child. § 1071-36. Sworn statements

The sworn statements referred to in the preceding section can be made before the registrar of vital statistics performing the registration. 

§ 1071-37. Statements contradicting legitimacy 

If a child has been born from an accepted marriage, or at a time in which he can be considered as born within wedlock, no statement contradicting its legitimacy can be expressed in the registration unless ordered there by a competent court after final decree. § 1071-38. Relation of person making birth declaration; death before registration (a) In the registration of a birth, the relation of the person making the declaration to the person whose birth is being registered shall be stated on the certificate. (b) If a child dies before his birth is registered, said birth shall be registered simultaneously with his death. § 1071-39. Burial, removal permit; issuance

The registrar shall not issue any burial or removal permit unless the corresponding death certificate contains a medical certification with the necessary data, if obtainable. 

§ 1071-40. Burial permit procedure 

With the burial permits, the following procedure shall be observed: (1) They shall be filed in the districts, in order of issuance, except removal permits, which shall be forwarded as they are received by the registrar issuing the burial permit, to the Bureau of Vital Statistics of the Department of Health, to be used as verifiers when payment is made to the corresponding registrar. (2) They shall be numbered, starting with number one at the beginning of each calendar year. 149

T.1071-40 

Ch. 83

(3) They shall carry the number of the death certificate to which they correspond and the number of the registry of origin. (4) They shall be delivered with the corresponding stub to the person in charge of the burial. (5) When the body is to be removed to another district for burial, the person in charge of the removal shall obtain from the health officer the due authorization, without which the removal shall not take place. The person in charge of the burial shall deliver the permit to the registrar of the district where the burial is to take place, who, in turn, shall issue a burial permit to the person in charge of the interment, retaining the transfer permit, which shall be forwarded to the Department of Health, endorsed with a note verifying that the decedent was buried according to permit

No. ............ (state appropriate number) of the district where interred. (6) The person in charge of the cemetery shall sign and give the date and time of burial on the back of the permit, and return it to the registrar, retaining the stub. 

§ 1071-41. Exhumation permits 

The registrars of vital statistics shall not issue permits for the exhumation of human remains, this being reserved to the corresponding local health office. 

§ 1071-42. Register 

(a) The municipal governments shall supply to cemetery keepers the register provided for in secs. 16 and 39 of the Act [24 L.P.R.A. 

§§ 1110, 1271], which shall contain the following information: 

(1) Date of burial. 

(2) Name of the decedent. (3) Place of death. (4) Cause of death. (5) Name and address of the undertaker. (6) Number of the grave. 

(b) The Secretary of Health shall prepare a model register for all municipalities. 

§ 1071-43. Violent death registration 

In case of violent death, when the death registration is made by virtue of an order of the judge or prosecuting attorney in charge of the case, the registrar shall request from said officer the neces- 150

Ch. T.24 § 1071-48 

sary information for the registration, including the medical certificate, which shall be provided in accordance with the provisions of sec. 13 of the Act [24 L.P.R.A. § 1107]. 

§ 1071-44. Death of unknown person 

In case of the death of an unknown person or the discovery of a body whose identification is not immediately possible, the death certificate shall contain the following: (1) Place of death or discovery of body. (2) Sex; race; apparent age; signs (marks) or physical defects that may serve for identification. (3) Approximate time of death. (4) Condition of body. (5) Dress, papers, or objects on the body or found near it that may afterwards serve for purposes of identification. 

§ 1071-45. Identification of body 

As soon as identification is made, a new registration shall be made expressing the circumstances required by sec. 9 of the Act [24 L.P.R.A. § 1103], which may have been obtained, making the corresponding notation in both registrations, for which the legal authority in charge of the case should submit to the registrar a testimony of his findings. § 1071-46. Body of unknown person in uninhabited place 

When the body of an unknown person is discovered in an uninhabited place, the registrar shall request from the judicial officer who made the investigation the necessary information to make the registration. 

§ 1071-47. Marriage license record 

Registrars of vital statistics shall keep a record of marriage licenses issued and in it shall state the license number, name of applicant, name of person whom applicant is to marry, and date of issuance. 

§ 1071-48. Duplicate marriage license 

If the original of a marriage license is lost, a duplicate may be issued, making the necessary notation at the foot of same, expressing said circumstance, without it being necessary to cancel a new internal-revenue stamp. 151

T.§ 1071-49 

Ch. 83 

§ 1071-49. Certificate from place of marriage 

When the contracting parties obtain a marriage license in one district and the ceremony is performed in another, the registrar where the marriage takes place shall receive the related documents and shall make the marriage certificate. 

§ 1071-50. Certificate of marriage to parties 

In all cases where the registrar of vital statistics registers a marriage, he shall be obliged to give or send to the contracting parties within 5 days after receiving the documents announcing the celebration, a certificate of said marriage in a special form that the Secretary of Health shall furnish. § 1071-51. Regular hours of registries

The registrars of vital statistics shall determine by common consent, with their respective mayors, the regular hours to be dedicated to the matters related to their positions; provided, that registrars shall be available to the public at any hour of the day or night, for the processing of deaths and removal permits of bodies of urgent character. 

§ 1071-52. Posting of registrars' names, addresses 

Registrars shall fix in a visible place in the building where their offices are housed, their name and home address, also of the alternate registrar, for the information of those persons who in compliance with the law should need their services out of regular working hours. 

§ 1071-53. Violations 

All violations of this Division shall be punished in accordance with provisions of sec. 42 of the Vital Statistics Act, approved by the Legislative Assembly of Puerto Rico on April 22, 1931 [24 L.P.R.A. § 1301]. 

$ 1071-54. Effectiveness

This Division shall take effect upon its approval by the Executive Council and promulgation by the Governor of Puerto Rico in accordance with provisions of sec. 3 of Act No. 24 of April 22, 1931 [24 L.P.R.A. § 1071]. 

Effective date. Vital Statistics Regulation No. 1, set out in this Division, became effective Feb. 16, 1932.

§ 1071-104. Office hours 

The office hours of the registry of vital statistics, wherever the office may be located, shall be the same as governs employees of the Public Health Unit. 

§ 1071-105. Absence from duty 

The registrar shall attend to rendering his daily services during the hours indicated in the above rule; and shall not leave his office temporarily unless expressly authorized to do so by the chief of the Public Health Unit. In case his absence should extend for a period of time considered by the chief of the Unit to be sufficiently long to affect the service, the registrar shall not leave the service without having first installed the deputy registrar as a substitute for him during his absence. This rule shall not apply when the registrar is rendering his service in the registry of vital statistics office during the morning or in the old Civil Registry office in the afternoon, in those places where the registry of vital statistics office and the old Civil Registry office are not located in the same place. 

§ 1071-106. Compliance by registrar The registrar shall observe the provisions of the Vital Statistics Registry Act [24 L.P.R.A. §§ 1041-1302] and of the rules and regulations promulgated by the Secretary of Health in the registration of births, marriages, and deaths occurring or performed within his registration district; but under no circumstances shall he register any document which does not pertain to his district. 

§ 1071-107. Local documents 

The registrar of vital statistics shall maintain all the local documents so that they may be examined and investigated by the registry inspector or by an official duly authorized for such work. 154

Ch. T.24 1071-113 

 § 1071-108. Procedure for registration 

Immediately after having accepted a birth, death, stillbirth, or marriage certificate, the local registrar shall proceed to sign it, number it, and transcribe it in the corresponding book as a local document. He shall see to it that these documents are filled in with permanent black ink or with a typewriter whose ribbon is in good condition. 

§ 1071-109. Completion of certificate form 

The registrar of vital statistics shall not accept for registration any birth, death, or marriage certificate not completed according to the Vital Statistics Registry Act [24 L.P.R.A. §§ 1041-1302]. 

§ 1071-110. Assistance to persons visiting office 

It shall be the duty of the registrar to help those persons visiting his office to request information about the registration of births, deaths, and marriages and shall provide all the necessary facilities so that the interested party is able to fulfill the purpose that led him to visit the registry office; all this without violations of the 

Law and of the regulations in force. § 1071-111. Certifications of birth, death, and marriage records

The registrar of vital statistics shall issue certifications of the birth, death, and marriage records in the old books of the Civil Registry under his custody or care, upon written application of the interested party, accompanied by a 50-cent special vital statistics internal-revenue stamp, canceling half of the stamp in the copy issued and the other half on the application. He should issue certifications without the aforesaid internal-revenue stamp to agencies of the Commonwealth Government or Federal Govern ment and to the chapter of the American Red Cross.

§ 1071-112. Maintenance of registry book, applications 

The registrar of vital statistics shall maintain up-to-date his registry book of certifications issued and shall file all the applications issued in order of date of issuance, duly numbered so that they may be easily investigated by the registry inspector or any other official of the Department of Health duly authorized for such work. 

§ 1071-113. Return of burial permits 

The registrar of vital statistics shall request from the person.

155

T.§ 1071-113 

Ch. 83 officially in charge of the cemetery to return within the period of time expressed by Law the burial permits that he may have received and on the basis of which he permitted the burial of each body in the cemetery under his custody. 

§ 1071-114. Examination of returned burial permits 

Immediately after receiving burial permits mentioned in the above rule, the registrar shall proceed to check them with the death certificates registered so as to verify their exactness and to detect any violation of the Law with respect to this matter. 

§ 1071-115. Violations 

The registrar of vital statistics shall report violations of the 

Vital Statistics Registry Act [24 L.P.R.A. §§ 1041-1302] and regulations to the Secretary of Health only, but through the mediation of the chief of the Bureau of Vital Statistics. § 1071-116. Duties outside office hours

The registrar of vital statistics shall not be obliged to render any service to the public outside his office hours unless in the case of applications for the transfer of bodies in which case he shall be ready to issue the corresponding permit even outside the regular office hours. 156

§ 135-1. Office of civil defense 

(a) In compliance with the provisions of the law, an Office of Civil Defense for the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico has been established and organized as follows: (1) General divisions 

(A) Information and Public Relations. 

(B) Inspection and Supervision. (C) Planning, Operation, and Training. 

(D) Administration. 

(E) Personnel and Recruiting. (F) Legal. (2) Special divisions (A) Auxiliary Fire Services. (B) Auxiliary Police Services. (C) Warden Services. (D) Engineering Services, including rescue, protection of 161

water reservoirs, power lines, telephone services, and restoration of public services, etc. (E) Auxiliary Medical Services, including nurses, hospitals, first aid, funeral services, public welfare, protection against special weapons and against radiological, biological, and chemical warfare. 

(F) Communications Services. 

(G) Alarm against enemy aerial or submarine attacks. 

(H) Transportation. 

(I) Evacuation. 

(J) Investigation of sabotage, black market, and illegal raising of prices.

"On 12 January 1951, the 81st. Congress of the United

States approved Act No. 920 [50 U.S.C. App. § 2251 et seq.] 

authorizing a Program of Federal Civil Defense, through which the responsibility for the establishment of Civil Defense was designated for the states, territories and other political subdivisions. Ch. T.25 § 135-2 

CIVIL DEFENSE 

"The above-named law requires that all necessary arrangements be made to protect the population against possible attack in the event of war, including atomic, bacteriological, chemical and radiological attack, etc. It further requires that protection be established against the consequences of direct and indirect sabotage of enemy agents; through illegal raising of prices, hoarding of articles of prime necessity, and against the consequences of natural disasters such as floods, hurricanes, earthquakes, fires, and, in general, provides for the common defense, the preservation of order, for the financial welfare and public security and for the preservation of life and property in Puerto Rico. "The law authorizes the establishment of an Office of 

Civil Defense for the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico and authorizes a Civil Defense Organization in the capital city of San Juan, and in the rest of the municipalities. "By virtue of the above-named law, a plan and a general program will be prepared for the Civil Defense of Puerto Rico that will coordinate the organization, planning, and programs of the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico with those of the city of San Juan, the municipalities of the Island, and with the plans of the Federal Government." 

§ 135-2. Organization of the civil defense volunteer corps 

(a) Due to our geographical status as an island, we cannot enjoy the benefits of mutual aid, today's basic concept of National Civil 

Defense. 

(b) Any help we would receive from the Continent in the event of an enemy attack or a disaster caused by nature, would be delayed by the distance which separates the Island from the United States, not to mention the enemy action which could delay its arrival. 

Furthermore, we should bear in mind the strategic importance which Puerto Rico has in connection with Civil Defense of the continental United States, as well as its overall importance as a target. 

(c) The Commonwealth of Puerto Rico must organize a full quota component of Civil Defense, well-trained and well-disciplined, with equipment and material sufficient to face by itself, for a reasonable period of time, any emergency which might arise, without depending on immediate help from outside. 

(d) A Corps of Volunteers of Civil Defense shall be organized in proportion to the general population of the Commonwealth, not less than 15% of the total population; provided that, unless war has been declared or until so directed by the Governor, the Civil Defense Organization shall be organized on the basis of approximately 10% of the total population, distributed among the following services: 163

§ 135-3. Civilian Defense personnel 

(a) Any member of the Corps of Volunteers of Civil Defense who, in the performance of his official duties in cases of emergency caused by natural disasters, enemy attack, or while performing duly authorized training exercises is hurt or wounded, without negligence on his part, shall have the right to be hospitalized in the government hospitals (or in any municipal hospital near the place of the accident) until he has fully recovered and as long as medical treatment is necessary. While he is hospitalized he shall receive, in accordance with the position held at the time of the accident, subsistence allowance which shall be determined by the Director of Civil Defense and the Director of the Bureau of the Budget with the approval of the Governor of Puerto Rico. (b) Until special legislation in regard to this matter is approved, all expenses incurred shall be paid and charged to the emergency fund of the Governor of Puerto Rico. (c) In the event a member of the Corps of Volunteers of Civil Defense of Puerto Rico dies while in performance of his official duties in cases of emergency caused by natural disasters, enemy attacks, or while performing duly authorized training exercises, his dependents shall receive an amount which shall be determined by the President of the Industrial Commission and approved by the Governor of Puerto Rico, to be charged to the emergency fund, until special legislation in regard to this matter is approved. 164

Ch. 

CIVIL DEFENSE T.25 § 135-6 

(d) If the volunteer or employee did not have any relative dependent upon him for subsistence, the disbursement shall be limited to the payment of funeral expenses and shall not exceed $100, in addition to all other costs of medical treatment, hospitalization, and medicines which have been incurred, in accordance with the aforementioned provisions. 

§ 135-4. 

Accidents for which exception has been made Accidents occurring under the following circumstances are not compensable and consequently shall not entitle the volunteer, employee, or his beneficiaries to the aforesaid rights: (1) When the volunteer or employee attempts to commit a crime, or intentionally self-inflicts an injury. (2) If the volunteer or employee is intoxicated and this intoxication is the cause of the accident. (3) When negligence of the volunteer or employee has been the sole reason for the injury. (4) If the volunteer is not engaged in the performance of official duties with the Civil Defense Organization or is not undergoing authorized training exercises. 

§ 135-5. Local civil defense offices The municipalities shall organize a local Civil Defense Office following rules enacted by law and shall conform to the special and general divisions established in the organization chart of Civil Defense, so that each existing division in the Office of Civil Defense of the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico shall coordinate their services with the corresponding division in the local organization, or in order that the people of the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico will receive the benefits of these services. 

§ 135-6. Municipal Civil Defense Corps 

The municipalities shall recruit volunteers and all necessary personnel for the organization and establishment of their Civil Defense Corps within quotas corresponding to their respective populations, thus giving an approximate total to each municipality (as shown in Exhibit "B"), and shall cooperate in the training of other Civil Defense personnel under the supervision and with the assistance of the corresponding agencies and institutions of the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico.

INTERNAL SECURITY § 135-7. Uniformity of municipal civil defense 

(a) For the sake of uniformity and to insure their function as part of the Civil Defense of Puerto Rico a uniform organization should be established for the different units in the municipalities. 

The charts of organization, marked Exhibit "C", include: (1) Auxiliary police. (2) Auxiliary firemen. (3) Mobile unit. 

(4) First aid — Department of Health. 

(5) Lunchroom and kitchen unit. (6) Shelter unit. (7) Personnel identification and registration unit. (8) Wardens. (b) The wardens shall be organized in the metropolitan areas at the rate of 1 per 100 persons, and 1 Assistant Chief of Wardens per 5 wardens. In the rural zones there shall be 3 wardens per 500 persons.

Text references. Exhibit "C", referred to in text, is not included in this compilation. 

§ 135-8. Reception, Aid, and Shelter Centers 

(a) All the municipalities of the Commonwealth, including Vieques and Culebra, shall prepare Reception, Aid, and Shelter Centers, where all those persons who have lost their homes as a result of an enemy attack shall receive assistance and shelter. (b) These centers shall offer shelter, food, medical assistance, and clothing if needed, and as long as is required by the emergency. 

(c) The direct supervision of the Reception, Aid, and Shelter 

Centers of the Civil Defense shall be a responsibility of the Division of Public Welfare of the Department of Health of the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico. 

(d) The basic organization for the Reception Centers is as follows: 

(1) A leader. (2) An assistant leader. (3) Administrative division - records, information, reception, social services, religious services, etc. (4) Food supplies division. (5) Division in charge of lunchroom services. (6) Clothing distribution division. (7) Medical division. (8) Police division. (9) Fire division. 166

Ch. T.24 § 135-8 

CIVIL DEFENSE 

(10) Shelter division. (11) General supplies division. (e) The Reception Centers shall be divided into three classes, according to their capacity: (1) Class A: Capacity to receive and provide for not less than 

10,000 persons. (2) Class B: Capacity to receive and provide for not less than 

5,000 persons. (3) Class C: Capacity to provide for from 1,000 to 5,000 persons. (f) The leaders of the reception centers shall be authorized to appoint and utilize whatever personnel may be necessary for the performance of satisfactory emergency services as indicated herewith by the Director of the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico, and may also strengthen the services of these centers by dispatching units from the various services of the Corps of Volunteers of Civil Defense and appointing additional personnel. (g) The leaders of the Reception, Aid, and Shelter Centers in the various municipalities shall be appointed by the local director and the personnel necessary for their operation shall be appointed from their corresponding quota, subject to the command of the local director and the Mayor of the municipality. (h) The Reception Centers shall be organized taking into consideration existing public buildings, warehouses, etc., with water and sewerage service, electricity, approach to highways and roads, and sanitary facilities. The possibility of establishing provisional camps using house tents or other housing means for these purposes should also be considered. Land having natural drainage should be preferred for establishing these camps. (i) In case of an emergency as contemplated here, the Civil 

Defense of Puerto Rico, with the approval of the Governor, shall have the authority to take possession of, and utilize any building, land, farm, or property which shall be necessary for these purposes. (j) The planning for the operation and organization of the Municipal Reception Centers shall be submitted by the municipal authorities for the consideration of the Director through the Public Welfare Division, within 60 days after the director of the Center has been appointed. List of municipalities and reception centers is included herein.

§ 135-9.

Departments, agencies, and institutions of the Common wealth of Puerto Rico 

All the departments, agencies, and institutions of the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico shall render their services, assistance, and cooperation to the Civil Defense Organization and shall be in charge of training and supervising the instruction of the auxiliary Civil 

Defense Units. 

§ 135-10. Police 

(a) The Police of Puerto Rico, whose duties in peacetime include the preservation of law and order, protection of lives and homes, and, among other things, the control and management of traffic, shall also render these duties in wartime but under much more difficult and complicated conditions. (b) The Police of Puerto Rico must insure the efficiency, discipline, and preparation of the auxiliary personnel furnished by the 

Civil Defense of Puerto Rico. The Police shall take charge of super vising the training and instruction of the Civil Defense Auxiliary Police. 

§ 135-11. Fire department 

Puerto Rico has an efficient Fire Service under a centralized command. In time of war, the duty of the Fire Service will be more difficult and complicated, and they shall have the aid and cooperation of an Auxiliary Firemen's Corps, which shall be trained, disciplined, and organized under the supervision and guidance of the 

Fire Service in order to insure the highest efficiency. 

§ 135-12. Department of Health 

(a) Puerto Rico has the advantage of having a Department of Health under State control. This Department includes medical services, hospital services, nurses, first-aid services, and in addition a Public Welfare Division and a Bureau of Vital Statistics. 

(b) For the reasons above-mentioned regarding the convenience and necessity of having the auxiliary services organized and trained under the direction of the corresponding government services, the personnel of the Auxiliary Medical Services should be organized and trained under the supervision of the Department of Health, including the Division of Public Welfare and the Bureau of Vital 

Statistics.

§ 135-13. Department of Education (a) The Department of Education of the Commonwealth of 

Puerto Rico, through its School Lunchroom Division and its Division of Community Education, can and should cooperate with Civil Defense in its educational program. The personnel of this Department, because of their specialized training, are properly qualified to render their services in the Reception, Aid, and Shelter Centers after the disaster. (b) In addition, the Department of Education shall cooperate through its staff of professors and students in a general campaign of public instruction in accordance with the principles accepted by the Federal Civil Defense Administration. 

(c) The school lunchrooms will be of great assistance in the preparation of the general program, in case of enemy attack or emergency caused by nature. 

§ 135-14. Department of Public Works The Secretary of Public Works shall organize under his super vision all engineering and rescue services, the restoration of public services, and the protection of industries, plants, and public service installations, utilizing all the official personnel that he deems necessary according to the nature of the functions to be executed. The organizations of the Auxiliary Civil Defense Services shall be in charge of the corresponding branch of the Department of Public Works, and the training and supervision shall be carried out under the rules and regulations approved by the Secretary of Public 

Works. The chiefs of the Auxiliary Civil Defense Services corre sponding to the services stated above, shall, in case of disaster, function in accordance with the plans approved by the Civil Defense under the authority of the Secretary of Public Works. 

§ 135-15. Ports Authority 

The Ports Authority with the cooperation of the Office of Transportation of the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico, shall be in charge of the organization of transportation of the Civil Defense of Puerto Rico, using all available means, and shall coordinate the transportation of the different municipalities, all this with the approval of the Director.

CIVIL DEFENSE § 135-16. Communications Authority The Communications Authority shall prepare and organize the communications system of the Civil Defense of Puerto Rico, and shall organize Command and Control Centers, as indicated by the Director of Civil Defense. 

§ 135-17. American Red Cross 

(a) It is the responsibility of the Red Cross to provide for the rehabilitation and care of families that are victims of disasters caused by nature, such as hurricanes, fires, floods, earthquakes, and so forth, in accordance with regulations established by the national organization. Should a disaster occur, the Red Cross shall go into action immediately and cooperate with the government authorities in the rescue, evacuation, and care of the wounded, making all necessary arrangements for sheltering, feeding, and clothing of those victims in need of this assistance. (b) The Red Cross has also agreed to cooperate to the maximum in the training of Civil Defense volunteers in first aid and home nursing and as auxiliary nurses. (c) As soon as a natural disaster occurs, the Red Cross shall immediately contact the Governor of Puerto Rico, the Mayors, and other governmental agencies so as to avoid duplicity of effort, and to accelerate rescue and rehabilitation activities. (d) In case of disaster by enemy action, the Red Cross shall place under the authority of the Civil Defense its entire organization including its resources and personnel for participation in the 

Civil Defense activities.

(f) The Transportation Services shall operate under the supervision of the Director of the Ports Authority, who shall, in turn, receive orders from the Governor of Puerto Rico or on his behalf from the Director of Civil Defense. 

(g) When a municipality has been attacked and turned into a disaster area, the command and control of all Civil Defense personnel within the municipality shall be a responsibility of the Mayor of said municipality or, on his behalf of the local director of Civil Defense, unless the Governor deems it proper to personally assume command of said municipality or delegates a representative to assume responsibility. SECTIONS § 135-21. Control and command in peacetime 

In peacetime control and command of the auxiliary groups of local defense will be exercised by the Mayor of each municipality, or by the local director, subject to the authority of the Governor.

§ 135-101. General instructions 

In cases of disaster caused by nature, Civil Defense is by law charged with the carrying out, during an emergency, of all functions of government having to do with the protection of the health, lives, and property of the civilian population in the devastated area. Under this authority everything necessary to fulfill these purposes will be done, including evacuation of areas or buildings 174

Ch. 

CIVIL DEFENSE 

T.25 § 135-102 likely to endanger the lives of their occupants, whether in cases of hurricanes, fires, floods, earthquakes, etc., and both before the disaster, as a preventive measure, and thereafter.

§ 135-102. Red Cross 

In cases of this nature, the Red Cross has the responsibility of providing food, clothing, shelter, and rehabilitation to all persons stricken by the disaster. These activities are the exclusive function of the Red Cross, in time of peace, and all of the personnel of Civil Defense shall assist and cooperate in the activities to the end that the Red Cross's work may be carried out with the speed and efficiency requisite in these cases.

There should be a prearranged coordination between Civil Defense and the Red Cross in the preparation of their plans and organization so as to eliminate any possible gaps between the plans of Civil Defense and those of the Red Cross. Civil Defense in each community shall designate a liaison officer to work with the Red Cross. This officer will be one of the members of the local Civil 

Defense and will keep the local director informed as to the Red Cross requirements for the faithful accomplishment of its mission. 

Immediately after a disaster has occurred, the Red Cross will need the personnel of the Civil Defense to take care of the property that the Red Cross will use for giving assistance to the persons stricken by the disaster. It will also need the personnel of the 

Communications Section to send messages, as well as the personnel of the Auxiliary Police to maintain order in the designated shelters and surroundings. According to the foregoing, each local director shall select carefully a group of Civil Defense volunteers, to whom these duties will be specifically assigned. These volunteers will render their services under the control of the liaison officer of Civil Defense and according to the requirements of the Red 175

T.25 135 Ch. 7

Assistant zone director (a) The Director of Civil Defense shall designate for each zone an assistant director who will act as his representative in case of emergency. The assistant director will have in a zone all the powers conferred by law on the Commonwealth director. The assisant director of Civil Defense in charge of each zone shall work out a 178

T.25 § 135-106 

CIVIL DEFENSE 

plan of mobilization and operation of Civil Defense in said zone and coordinate it with the local plans of the municipalities comprising the zone. These plans should cover disasters caused by nature as well as those brought about by war. In addition, he shall coordinate the operation of the various services within Civil 

Defense. 

(b) The zone plans shall be adjusted to these general considerations and to the plans of the Director of Civil Defense, and will have as a general practice the offering of all the aid required by the disaster area in the shortest possible time. (c) The heads of the departments, offices, and agencies of the government with Commonwealth services that carry out functions of Civil Defense, such as police, fire, medical services, public welfare, school lunchrooms, price stabilization, etc., shall designate a zone chief for each service. This zone chief shall prepare the plan of operation of his service within the zone and will be the official who in case of disaster shall take charge of directing and coordinating, within the general plans that the assistant director in charge of the zone designates, all activities appertaining to the units of Civil Defense belonging to the service under his orders. 

For example, the zone chief of the fire service shall coordinate and direct all of the activities of the municipal units of firemen within this zone. The zone chief of medical services will do the same with all medical units belonging to that zone, and the zone chief of police will carry out the same functions with respect to the police units. 

§ 135-106. Zone Board 

All of these officials, together with a representative of the Red Cross, shall, upon appointment issued by the Director and by the heads of each service, constitute the Zone Board. The Zone Board will coordinate all activities of Civil Defense of the municipalities within its jurisdiction, in accordance with the general provisions of Civil Defense of Puerto Rico. The Civil Defense plans prepared by the assistant director in charge of a zone, with the cooperation of the Zone Board, shall be submitted to the Director of Civil 

Defense of Puerto Rico for his approval. 

In case of disaster, the Board of each zone, under the chairmanship of the assistant director of Civil Defense, shall appear personally in the disaster area, shall put into execution such plans as may 179

be appropriate, and shall make all such other arrangements as the situation may call for. Each Zone Board shall set up quarters in a place previously designated by the Director of Civil Defense of 

Puerto Rico, establishing a provisional control center in such place.

§ 135-109. Federal aid; civil departments (a) Legal arrangements. Act No. 875 of the 81st Congress, approved September 30, 1950 [42 U.S.C. § 1855 et seq.], has as its objective the providing of aid from the Federal Government to the state and local governments in the carrying out of their work of assistance in cases arising as a consequence of grave disasters, and, in addition, the restoring of necessary public services, and the cooperation with state and local governments in the development of their disaster plans.

Said law defines grave disasters as including any disaster caused by nature, or arising as a consequence of an act of war. 

The law requires that upon the occurrence of a disaster, or in case of an impending disaster, the Governor shall certify the necessity of receiving federal aid as provided for by law, ascertaining that a reasonable amount of funds from the Government of the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico or from its municipalities or other agencies will be used for aid in such a disaster. 

Upon receipt of such a certification, the President of the United States will decide whether or not to authorize federal aid for the disaster in question. (b) Putting the law into effect. The afore-mentioned law has been put into effect by Executive Order Number 10,427, of January 16, 1953, which provides: (1) that the federal agencies shall provide assistance to any state that suffers the consequences of a disaster; (2) that in providing such aid, the activities of said federal agencies be coordinated, and the personnel, equipment, material, and all available means be utilized in accordance with the authority granted by law; (3) that the plans and preparations of the federal agencies made in anticipation of the occurrence of the disaster be coordinated; and (4) that the aid and other activities of the federal agencies be coordinated and carried out within the established practices and legal authority of said agencies. (c) Federal aid. Federal aid may be authorized in the following manner: (1) By utilizing or lending to the Government of Puerto Rico, or to the municipal governments, equipment, goods, facilities, personnel, and other means available to the federal agencies. This may be with or without compensation. 181

T.§ 135-109 Ch. 7 

INTERNAL SECURITY 

(2) By distributing medicines, food, and other staple articles through the American Red Cross. (3) By donating to the Commonwealth and municipal governments equipment and material which, in accordance with existing law, may be considered as surplus with respect to the needs and responsibilities of the Federal Government. 

(4) By carrying out, on public or private lands, such construction works as are essential for the protection of life and property; by removing debris, by making emergency repairs and temporary substitutions of local public services damaged or destroyed in the disaster, and by contributions to the Commonwealth and municipal governments for the purposes specified in this clause. 

In view of the foregoing, it is absolutely necessary that the plans of the federal agencies and departments be properly coordinated with the plans of Civil Defense of Puerto Rico and those of the municipalities. (d) Other federal agencies. In Puerto Rico there are numerous representatives of departments and agencies of the Federal Government, whose activities will be of great importance for Civil Defense if need be. In order to coordinate the operation of these representatives of the federal departments and agencies with the plans of Civil Defense of Puerto Rico, the Honorable Harley A. Miller, now Prosecuting Attorney of the U. S. District Court for Puerto

Puerto Rico, in charge of these functions.

Federal aid; Armed Forces (a) General instructions. The Armed Forces will, as far as their resources permit, cooperate in the orientation of key officials of the Commonwealth and municipal governments in those phases of Civil Defense and related subjects in which the Armed Forces have special preparation and technical knowledge, including the formulation of plans for Civil Defense. Military leaders will encourage and assist the civilian population in their plans for organizing their own defense.

The Armed Forces on the domestic front must be free of complications which may weaken their combat potential before the enemy. 

The installations belonging to the Armed Forces, such as camps, forts, training centers, naval or air bases, etc., are not included in the field of operation of Civil Defense of Puerto Rico, and Civil 183

T.§ 135-110 

INTERNAL SECURITY 

Ch. 7

Defense activities will not be extended to any of these centers except at the express request of the commanding officer of such an installation or his superior in the Armed Forces in Puerto Rico. (b) In peace time. Under the provisions of Act No. 875 of the 

Federal Congress, approved September 30, 1950 [42 U.S.C. § 1855 

et seq.], and in accord with Executive Order Number 10,427 of

January 16, 1953, the Armed Forces of the United States may extend aid to the civilian population of Puerto Rico in cases of disasters caused by nature, such as hurricanes, earthquakes, floods, fires, etc. (c) Request for aid from the Armed Forces. A request for aid, submitted to the Armed Forces, shall contain the following information: (1) Nature and extent of the disaster. (2) Area or places affected. (3) Number of persons seriously affected by the disaster, and the needs of these persons as to food, clothing, shelter, hospitalization, or evacuation. (4) Measures taken by local and Commonwealth authorities and by the Red Cross.

Each request for aid for the civilian population of Puerto Rico, made to the representatives of the Armed Forces, shall first be submitted to the Director of Civil Defense for his approval and presentation to the proper authorities. A local director may send such a request directly to the military authorities only in default of all possible means of communication between the local director and the Director of Civil Defense of Puerto Rico, or when the aid asked for is of such an urgent character that it does not admit the delay which the routing of the request through official channels necessarily entails. (d) Fires. In cases of fire, the groups of firemen for the installations, posts, bases, or camps of the Armed Forces may, on request of the Fire Service of Puerto Rico, help extinguish fires that develop in any village, town, or city of Puerto Rico. (e) Floods. In cases of floods that may cause grave danger to the lives of the civilian population in a given sector of Puerto Rico, the Armed Forces of the United States may extend aid to the civilian population, in the way of the use of troops, equipment, and material. 184

T.25 § 135-111 (f) Hurricanes. In cases of hurricanes, the Armed Forces may extend aid to the civil authorities, municipal or Commonwealth, by providing food, medicine, and clothing or shelter to that part of the civilian population that could not be or has not been taken care of by the civil authorities or by the Red Cross. (g) In war time. All plans of Civil Defense for wartime operations should be coordinated with the plans of the Armed Forces. 

A general plan coordinating the activities within the Army, Navy, and Air Force will be prepared for the disposal of explosives, including guided missiles and bombs. 

Any citizen having knowledge of the existence of any of these artifacts should immediately notify the nearest police station. 

In case of emergency caused by acts of war, the Armed Forces may extend aid to the civilian population provided it may be done with a minimum depletion of the Armed Forces resources and supplies, and keeping in mind that the military needs must have precedence at all times.

In case of an atomic attack the Armed Forces should not be relied on to provide military protection to the disaster area unless it is necessary for national defense. (h) The Air Force. The Air Force will be responsible for notifying Civil Defense of the presence or proximity of enemy aircraft. 

Civil Defense, in turn, will relay the alarm to the civilian population. (i) National Guard of Puerto Rico. In case of war the National 

Guard of the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico will form part of the Armed Forces of the United States, and will consequently be subject to all of the afore-mentioned concerning the Armed Forces. 

In case of disaster caused by nature, occurring in time of peace, the National Guard may extend aid and render services of the utmost importance. It will be called upon to do so, if necessary, on the express order of the Governor of the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico. § 135-111. Civil Defense of Puerto Rico, with the exception of the wardens corps.

According to law, in cases of emergency brought about by an act of war or by a disaster caused by nature, the Government Secretaries and the heads of the authorities, agencies, and instrumentalities of the Government, as well as the mayors, may utilize all or any part of the personnel of their departments, offices, agencies, or instrumentalities, in conformity with the norms established by the Civil Defense, in order to render to the civil population the services and activities required for the safeguarding of lives, property, and health. 

(b) Commonwealth Government. Clause 5 of sec. 6 of the Civil Defense Act of Puerto Rico of 1951 [25 L.P.R.A. § 135] authorizes the Governor of the Commonwealth or the Director to utilize all available services and facilities of the offices and agencies of the Government of Puerto Rico and its municipalities, and make compulsory the rendering of these services by the departments, agencies, offices, and instrumentalities. 

Section 20 of the said law [25 L.P.R.A. § 145] provides that all auxiliary and volunteer Civil Defense services shall, as soon as they are organized, be incorporated into the corresponding units of the Government of Puerto Rico, in cases of emergency or whenever the Governor deems it advisable. Said law, likewise, provides that volunteer Civil Defense services shall be organized in cooperation with the heads and directors of the corresponding Commonwealth services, with the cooperation of the Civil Defense directors. 

Our system of government has the following services: Fire; police; health, including hospitals, medical, nursing, and welfare services; engineering; communications; transportation; and other services, all of which operate under Island-wide system and organizations, according to methods and norms of recognized efficacy. 

These same systems shall continue to be utilized and operated in cases of emergency caused by war or by natural disaster, each service taking over its respective duties and obligations to the people and the community and increasing its personnel with volunteer and auxiliary Civil Defense Corps, which will thus join their effort to those of the regular staff of the departments, offices, agencies, and instrumentalities of the Government of Puerto Rico. § 135-112. Civil Air Patrol 

In case of emergency the Civil Air Patrol of Puerto Rico, with all of its units, both air and ground, shall function within the plans prepared by Civil Defense of Puerto Rico, and its local units will incorporate their functions within the plans of Civil Defense in the municipality where they are located. 

The following responsibilities are assigned to the Civil Air Patrol: 

(1) In case of disaster it shall be the task of the Civil Air Patrol to carry out reconnaissance of the disaster area and to inform the Director of Civil Defense of the magnitude and nature of the disaster with an approximate indication of the size of the area, nature of the destruction, and an estimate of the losses sustained in lives and property. 

(2) The Civil Air Patrol shall also provide Civil Defense with all

The officer in charge of the Civil Air Patrol in Puerto Rico at present is Colonel Orlando Antonsanti. 

§ 135-113. Hurricanes Generally 

The period of hurricanes in the Caribbean begins on June 1 and ends on November 1, approximately 6 months. Over a period of about 50 years, Puerto Rico has suffered the effects of 5 hurricanes, namely, San Ciriaco, August 8, 1899; San Felipe, September 13, 1928; San Nicolás, September 10, 1931; San Ciprián, September 26, 1932; and San Mateo, September 21, 1949.

The losses caused by these five hurricanes aggregate about $162,000,000. In round figures, casualties amounted to 4,000; injured, 10,000; total houses destroyed, 250,000. It is estimated that these hurricanes left approximately 1,000,000 persons homeless. 

The San Ciprián hurricane in 1932, which was not one of the most violent, seriously affected 46 municipalities, by destroying totally or partially 893 classrooms, 42,000 houses and buildings, and damaging some 32,446 houses. The San Felipe hurricane destroyed about 250,000 houses and damaged in part some 200,000. 

Its total damages were conservatively estimated at $85,000,000, and around half a million persons were rendered homeless. This storm affected almost all of the municipalities of the Island, with varied intensity. § 135-114. Distinctive characteristics (a) Generally we have warnings of the whereabouts of a hurricane and the approximate hour and date of its arrival, and estimates as to its intensity, general direction, and trajectory. (b) A hurricane may cause damage over an area equal or almost equal to all of Puerto Rico, and may last eight or more hours. (c) The nature of the damages and their importance may vary according to the distance from the center of the hurricane, and depending also on the velocity of the wind. (d) Damages such as the following may be occasioned by winds that at times have exceeded 160 miles per hour, and also be brought about by the heavy rains that generally accompany a hurricane, and the consequent floods that follow. 188

Ch. T.25 § 135-114 

CIVIL DEFENSE 

(1) Destruction of great numbers of houses of fragile construction, and deroofing and other damages to numerous buildings. (2) Breaking of the water pipelines and interruption of services. (3) Knocking down of poles and destruction of telephone and telegraph lines and interruption of these services. (4) Land or rock slides, and knocking down of trees and poles across highways, streets, and roads, thus interrupting means of transportation and pedestrian traffic, and causing damages to bridges. (e) In the affected area of the hurricane there will very likely be a large number of persons whose homes have been destroyed or damaged in such a way that for the time being they cannot continue living in them, and they will need shelter, clothing, and food. (f) Large numbers of persons will also be affected by the economic upheaval caused by the hurricane's destruction or damaging of buildings in which there are industries, factories, or businesses. (g) In order to meet the problems outlined above and others that will undoubtedly arise, Civil Defense should give preferent attention to: (1) restoring communications (highways, roads, telephone and telegraph lines) by giving to the Department of Public Works all the aid and cooperation that the engineering, communications, and transportation services can offer; (2) cooperating through auxiliary policemen and firemen in the maintenance of order and the prevention of fires which, in case of suspended water services, may assume dangerous proportions; and (3) giving immediate attention to all injured and helpless persons through the auxiliary medical services of Civil Defense. (h) As soon as the hurricane is over, the Red Cross will undertake its function of aiding all those persons who are destitute or homeless as a consequence of the hurricane, and Civil Defense will give all of the cooperation that the Red Cross may request. (i) Contrary to what happens in case of an atomic explosion, in which the disaster area covers several miles of an intense destruction and a great volume of losses is centralized in that area, in the case of a hurricane, the disaster area may be of such an extent as to cover the whole Island, as has already happened in the past, with the interruption of communications, which make it indis- 189

T.§ 135-114 

Ch. 7 INTERNAL SECURITY 

pensable for each municipality or community to have its Civil Defense so well organized and trained that it may be able to carry on by itself and be self-sufficient to take over and attend to the local needs in such municipality or community. __________ 

§ 135-115. Reconnaissance after hurricane 

Immediately after the occurrence of a hurricane, the Civil Air 

Patrol and the Police of Puerto Rico shall, without need of express orders, carry out a rapid preliminary reconnaissance of the disaster area, and shall submit to the Governor and to the Civil Defense 

Control and Command Center a report containing the following data: (1) Municipality or municipalities affected, and extent of the disaster area. 

(A) Homeless. 

(B) Injured. (2) Approximate number of buildings destroyed or damaged. 

(3) Estimated number of persons: 

(4) Highways obstructed. (5) Estimated damages to: 

(A) Plantations. 

(B) Crops.

This information on plantations and crops shall be obtained by the Civil Air Patrol from the air, and included in their report. 

Said information will be forthwith referred to the Department of Agriculture for its evaluation and remarks, with a view to determining the estimates of the damages and to starting the necessary measure for resumption of cultivation in such area. (C) Factories, shops, and houses.

This information will be obtained and submitted by the Police of Puerto Rico. 

(6) The Police shall use vehicles equipped with radiotelephone to carry out their reconnaissance, and transmit the information the same way, also advising the local Civil Defense director of all the information available relative to his municipality.
