§ 135-117. 

Warnings 

Hurricane warnings will be given to each municipality in compliance with the system already established by the Weather Bureau of the Federal Government. The Weather Bureau will be responsible for the warnings to the civilian population while the Army and the Navy will have the same responsibility in respect to their bases and installations.

The Weather Bureau will issue warnings directly to the Office of the Governor of the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico and to the Chief of Police, who shall in turn transmit the warnings to all police stations in the area that may be affected by the hurricane.

Upon receipt of the hurricane warnings at any police station, the officer in charge shall send a copy thereof to the local director of Civil Defense and shall forthwith cause to be hoisted the following warning signal for the civilian population: 

(1) YELLOW FLAG, indicating that a tropical storm is ap proaching and that the speed of the wind is not expected to exceed 

55 to 63 miles per hour. (2) GREEN FLAG, indicating that a tropical storm is approaching and that the speed of the approaching wind is expected to exceed 55 to 63 miles per hour. (3) Storm warnings for small watercraft will be placed in conspicuous places at the warning stations of the Weather Bureau, as said Bureau may determine. 

§ 135-118. Local director The principal duties of local directors of Civil Defense in these cases are the following: 

191

T.§ 135-118 Ch. 7 

INTERNAL SECURITY (1) Mobilization: Upon receipt of notification of the approach of a hurricane likely to affect his municipality, the local director shall proceed to mobilize all volunteer groups of Civil Defense whose services are required. 

(2) Warning to the public: The local director of Civil Defense will be responsible for bringing to the attention of the civilian population of his municipality the contents of the warning of the threat of a hurricane, and will utilize for this purpose such personnel of Civil Defense as he may need. This obligation applies both to the urban and rural zones. In order to accomplish this, it is recommended that for disseminating these warnings there be used all public warnings systems of the community, as well as any other appropriate means, such as motorized patrols that go through the different parts of the community. Extensive use should be made of the radio.

We must emphasize the importance of alerting the civilian population and that they be given warning of the threat of a hurricane so they may take the necessary steps for protection. 

These warnings must especially be received in all those zones and places which, because of their topographical location, are exposed to the greatest danger, such as areas near rivers, streams, lakes, dams, or the sea; areas of fragilely constructed houses that may be washed out by flood or by the sea; areas of weak and flimsy constructions; industrial plants and shops where there are groups of workers; and schools. 

§ 135-119. Shelters 

In accordance with the proclamation given by the Governor of Puerto Rico on June 9, 1952, in all the municipalities of the Island shelters have already been selected to provide housing in cases of a disaster of this type for all persons who live in fragile houses, near rivers, streams, lakes, dams, or the sea, and may therefore be exposed to the danger of floods or of the violence of the surf. 

The local directors of Civil Defense shall provide themselves with lists of these shelters and shall inspect them in cooperation with the local officials of the Departments of Public Works and Education, of the Police of Puerto Rico, and of the local Red Cross. Any shelter or shelters that in their judgment do not meet the necessary requirements, either because of their location or by the nature of their structure, may be eliminated from said list. 

The urban and rural zones shall be divided into sectors and the 192

Ch. 

CIVIL DEFENSE 

T.25 § 135-120 selected shelters will be assigned to the different sectors according to the number of inhabitants of each sector who may need shelter for the protection of their lives.

The local director of Civil Defense will request the Chief of 

Police and the Chief of the Fire Service to provide police and fire protection in each building selected for use as a shelter, in order to guarantee order and avoid fires while they are occupied. To this end, the regular personnel of these groups, as well as personnel belonging to the volunteer groups of Civil Defense, may be used. 

The Red Cross will take charge of the operation and administration of these shelters in all other respects, and its personnel shall be extended all help and cooperation requested or required of Civil 

Defense. 

The local director of Civil Defense shall prepare a list of all things required in regard to shelter, and shall furnish a copy of it to the following persons: Chief of Police of the locality, Chief of the Fire Service, representative of the Department of Public Works, Superintendent of Schools, local Chief of the Department of Health, and the local representative of the Red Cross.

§ 135-120. 

Evacuations Sec. 6 of the Civil Defense Act of Puerto Rico of 1951 [25 

L.P.R.A. § 135], in clause (f) of subd. (3), authorizes the Governor of Puerto Rico to provide for the evacuation of the civilian population of certain areas and for their lodging in previously selected locations. This authority has been delegated to the Director of Civil 

Defense of Puerto Rico, in accordance with subd. (7) of sec. 6 of the same law, which provides: "To delegate to the Commonwealth Director any authority vested in him under sections 130-146 of this title, and to provide for the subdelegation of such authority in the name and on behalf of the Government of Puerto Rico." 

By virtue of the provisions of this section, the Director of Civil Defense of Puerto Rico authorizes the local directors to exercise this authority in his behalf in necessary cases. This authority carries with it the highest and most delicate function of government, and should be exercised only when the civilian population is in great danger and the protection of their lives requires it. 

It will be the responsibility of the local director, in cases of hurricane, to decide what areas should be evacuated, what shelters the evacuated persons should occupy, and when to begin the evacu- 193

T.25 135 Ch. 7 

INTERNAL SECURITY 

ation, which he himself will order. Even when the responsibility and authority to order evacuation belongs to the local director, we advise that he coordinate these activities with the Police, Fire Service, Public Works, Superintendent of Schools, and the representative of the Red Cross.

The local director will be responsible for seeing that all measures taken for the moving of civilian population to shelters in cases of evacuations be carried out in an orderly fashion and under his direction, and before the fury of the hurricane and the presence of its danger are so immediate as to cause loss of lives or accidents. 

In cases of warnings of immediate danger under threat of a hurricane the evacuation of the civilian population to the shelters should be terminated at least two hours before the time indicated by the 

Weather Bureau for the possible arrival of the hurricane.

The evacuated areas should be guarded and protected by the police (which has incorporated the auxiliary police of Civil Defense) in order to avoid thefts and losses of property.

Local directors will prepare an evacuation plan fulfilling the above instructions and designating responsible persons for the execution of these measures. This plan shall include the route to be used in effectuating the transfer of the persons to be evacuated from the designated area to the proper shelters.

The local director of Civil Defense shall designate a person to take charge of everything related to shelters in the community and, as soon as the hurricane season begins, to inspect the shelters and make sure that they are available for use in case of necessity. The local director of Civil Defense is advised to utilize in his locality the services of the Division of Public Welfare in order to have a proportionate number of evacuated persons from each zone assigned to each shelter. ________ 

§ 135-121. Rescue 

In cases of hurricane, the heavy rains that accompany them constitute an additional danger for those persons who live in ravines and low places that are exposed to flooding. In certain areas near the sea there is also the danger of being beaten and flooded by the heavy tides.

Special care must also be taken with those people living on the banks of streams or rivers and who may be swept away by the floods.

All rescue units of Civil Defense shall be mobilized and provided 194

Ch. 

CIVIL DEFENSE 

T.25 § 135-124 with the necessary equipment, such as ropes, boats, life jackets, rafts, etc., that may be utilized for purposes of rescue. A system of observation of these potential disaster areas shall also be established, in order to be ready to offer the necessary aid. 

§ 135-122. - Sick and injured 

In cases of emergency of this nature the medical services of Civil Defense shall be mobilized in order that they may be ready to take charge of any injured or sick requiring immediate attention. The injured or sick will be taken to the nearest available medical center. 

§ 135-123. 

Social aid, food, clothing, and shelter The social aid that includes food, clothing, shelter, and rehabilitation in cases of disaster caused by nature, and the need for which arises after a disaster has occurred, is an exclusive function of the 

Red Cross. 

Civil Defense will lend to the Red Cross, in the accomplishment of its mission, all cooperation and assistance this institution may request, and will place at its disposal all available means of Civil Defense that can be useful to the Red Cross, as the latter may determine. This cooperation of Civil Defense should be offered with rapidity and as circumstances may demand. 

§ 135-124. Functions of mayor 

Upon occurrence of a disaster of this nature, Civil Defense shall forthwith make a survey and obtain data as regards the number of homeless persons in the municipality who are in immediate need of help with food, shelter, and clothing, and shall submit such information to the mayor of the municipality in writing, without delay. 

Once this information has been received, the mayor shall notify the local representative of the Red Cross of the number of needy persons and the nature of the need required. If the Red Cross does not have the means or organization available in said community, the mayor shall remit such information by the fastest means to the Director of Civil Defense of Puerto Rico, reporting the outcome of his contact with the Red Cross. He will also inform the Governor of the situation.

If, as a result of lack of facilities for establishing contact between the mayor and the Director of Civil Defense, no means exist for transmitting the information and the outcome of such contact, then 195

T.§ 135-124 

INTERNAL SECURITY 

Ch. 7 the mayor is authorized to formulate his request for immediate aid to the nearest authorities of the Armed Forces, including the 

National Guard of Puerto Rico. 

§ 135-125. - Recommendations for civilian population 

The active collaboration of the civilian population in cases of hurricanes is clearly specified in the plans and programs of Civil 

Defense. Passive collaboration, none the less effective, may be offered by observing the following instructions, aside from such other means that common sense may dictate in unforeseen circumstances: (1) After the hurricane has started in a town, no one should go outdoors. This is to avoid being hit by zinc roofing, a sudden cave-in or any object producing contusion which may cause death or serious injury. (2) In the course of a storm, a period of calm ensues which gives the impression that the hurricane has passed. No one should be deceived. At such moment what is commonly called virazón (change of wind) takes place and a few minutes later the winds will return with equal or greater impetus. For this reason it is recommended that everyone remain indoors or in the shelters during this period of calm. (3) Insofar as possible the use of alcoholic drinks should be avoided, so that everyone has complete control of his faculties and may face with calmness whatever unforeseen situation may arise. (4) Families with children should provide themselves with canned milk to meet the requirements of the home for not less than three days, since the storm may obstruct the means of communication, depriving the civilian population of milk deliveries for several days. (5) All families using electric service should provide themselves with kerosene lamps, flashlights, or candles, since this service may be interrupted for several days on account of the storm. (6) The residences using electric or gas stoves for cooking should provide themselves with kerosene stoves or charcoal burners. (7) All families should provide themselves with sufficient water to meet their most pressing needs for a period of not less than three days, since the water service may be interrupted or the water may become contaminated as a result of the storm. (8) For the best protection of life and property it is recom- 196

Ch. T.25 § 135-126 

CIVIL DEFENSE 

mended that the civilian population take the following precautions at the beginning of the hurricane season: (A) Make a careful inspection of the houses in order to determine the doors, windows, walls, and parts of the roof that are not secure and in a condition to resist the force of a hurricane. (B) That with reasonable anticipation, at the beginning of the hurricane season, the necessary arrangements be made to secure such parts of the house as are not sufficiently strong. (C) That adequate provision be made for nails, hammers, lumber, and other materials to be used in safeguarding their residences in the face of a threatened hurricane, in order to avoid the difficulty of acquiring these materials when the hurricane approaches, either because of scarcity on the market or for lack of the means or time to do it. 

§ 135-126. Floods 

(a) Generally. Due to the heavy intensity of rainfall and the steep slopes of river beds in Puerto Rico, floods may occur unexpectedly.

All the measures herein enumerated as necessary to be taken in cases of hurricane, also apply in cases of flood.

During the year 1952, Puerto Rico suffered two serious floods on different occasions. The first occurred in Fajardo in the month of May. The second was more extensive and occurred in the zones of Ponce, Santa Isabel, Gurabo, San Lorenzo, and Isabela in the month of September. Both occurred suddenly, one in the evening, and the other early in the morning. The alert system put into effect by Civil Defense avoided great losses of life to the civilian population in both cases.

In these floods the losses were calculated at approximately a million dollars, and more than 500 homes were damaged and 63 totally destroyed. More than 2,000 persons needed social assistance as a result of this emergency. (b) Warnings. It is imperative that warning of the proximity of a flood and of the areas in danger be carried out to the population affected within the shortest possible time, and also that mobilization of Civil Defense be effected with like rapidity. Radio stations should be used for this, if they exist in the locality, also warning sirens, loud speakers, and all other means the local director may make available. Emphasis is placed on the importance of having a number of motor vehicles organized and prepared beforehand for this purpose. 197

T.§ 135-126 Ch. 7 

INTERNAL SECURITY 

(c) Evacuations. Evacuations in case of flood must begin rapidly. As soon as danger for certain areas becomes apparent, the 

Director of Civil Defense should order evacuation of those areas, following the instructions relative to hurricanes. (d) Rescue. It is equally important that the rescue units of the municipalities give special attention to the inhabited areas in the vicinity of the sea or the banks of rivers or streams or in ravines, which are susceptible to being flooded or beaten by the surf, as the case may be; and in each one of these places there should be organized personnel of Civil Defense who are residents of the area affected and who can immediately take charge of initiating the rescue activities of Civil Defense, with equipment to facilitate their work, such as ropes, boats, drag hooks, etc. 

§ 135-127. Earthquakes 

(a) General instructions. Needless to say, earthquakes occur suddenly and without warning, frequently with disastrous consequences. The city of Mayagüez, Puerto Rico, has suffered severely from earthquakes.

In cases of earthquakes causing grave damage to any community the Director of Civil Defense shall immediately mobilize all of the personnel and begin without delay the work of rescue and street cleaning and the reestablishment of communication. Not infrequently earthquakes bring with them great tidal waves and it is advised that appropriate measures be taken for such emergencies. Also, fires occur as a result of short circuits or by the upsetting of kerosene stoves. (b) Warning. Civil Defense shall give immedate warning to the public about any building or construction that, as a result of the earthquake, has been left in a condition dangerous to its occupants, to passers-by, or to the community in general, in order that the necessary measures be taken to avoid unfortunate accidents. (c) Shelters. All arrangements made with respect to shelters in cases of hurricanes also apply in cases of earthquakes. 

(d) Evacuation. When the director of Civil Defense in the local ity is convinced, through advice of officials of the Department of Public Works, that the occupation of a given building, construction, area, or site may constitute immediate danger to its occupant or to the neighborhood, he shall without delay order evacuation of 198

Ch. T.25 135-129 

CIVIL DEFENSE 

said building, construction, site, or area, following the instructions established for evacuation in cases of hurricanes. (e) Sick and injured. In cases of this nature, if circumstances so require, the medical services of Civil Defense shall be mobilized in order that they may be in a position to take charge of any injured or sick requiring immediate attention. The injured or sick will be taken to the nearest medical center available. (f) Social aid, food, clothing, shelter. The task of offering social assistance to those injured by the effects of an earthquake is the exclusive task of the Red Cross, and Civil Defense, as previously stated, will offer all cooperation that may be requested. 

§ 135-128. Fires 

Civil Defense should not be mobilized in cases of isolated or limited-range fires. Civil Defense will be called in cases of fire when in the judgment of the local director the fire, by its violence or extent, assumes the proportion of a conflagration or endangers the security of a considerable proportion of the community, or when the fire chief of the community requests from the local director the services of the auxiliary fire service group of Civil Defense. 

These auxiliary firemen who voluntarily respond to the extinguishing of a fire and whose participation in said fire fighting is known and accepted by the local fire chief will be considered in all legal aspects as carrying out their official duties as members of Civil Defense of Puerto Rico and will have the right to enjoy all of the attendant privileges.

All that has been stated herein about warnings to the public, shelters, evacuations, rescue, sick and injured, social aid, food, clothing, and shelter in cases of hurricanes, floods and earthquakes, applies also in cases of a disaster caused by fire. 

§ 135-129. General provisions The local directors of Civil Defense shall utilize all available means of the community to accomplish the work entrusted to them and shall keep the Director of Civil Defense of Puerto Rico in formed of the extent of their efforts. Should a local director reach the conclusion that the means available in the community are insufficient, or if, in his judgment, such means are not enough to meet a given emergency, he shall forthwith inform the Director of Civil Defense.

§ 135-201. Declaration of emergency 

When a disaster of major proportions has occurred and a state of emergency is declared by the Governor of Puerto Rico, the following measures shall be taken: 

(1) The orders issued by the Governor of Puerto Rico shall be put into effect. (2) All departments, authorities, agencies, offices, and instrumentalities of the Government of the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico and of the municipalities affected shall put into effect the emergency plans previously prepared and coordinated with the 

Civil Defense of Puerto Rico. 

200

Ch. 

CIVIL DEFENSE 

T.25 § 135-201 (3) All departments, authorities, agencies, offices, and instrumentalities of the Government of the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico and of the municipalities affected by the disaster shall submit the reports requested in the pertinent section of this Division. (4) The assistant directors of Civil Defense in charge of each zone affected by the disaster, and the corresponding zone boards, shall take charge of the coordination on the scene of all activities of their respective departments, authorities, agencies, and offices, and of the Red Cross and the Civil Defense in the zones under their jurisdiction. (5) The departments, bureaus, agencies, and instrumentalities of the Government of the United States located in Puerto Rico shall put into effect their emergency plans according to the instructions of the Federal Administration of Civil Defense and in coordination with the plans of the departments and agencies of the Government and of the Civil Defense of Puerto Rico.

Introduction: Regulation File No. 425, set out in this Divi sion, contained the following introduction: "On May 20, 1953, the Governor of the Commonwealth of

Puerto Rico approved the FIRST PHASE of the Operational Plan of Civil Defense for Cases of Disaster Caused by Nature. 

"The primary purpose of said FIRST PHASE OF THE 

PLAN is to see to the adoption of all emergency measures indispensable to the safeguarding of lives and the personal safety of the civilian population, inasmuch as 'in case of disaster caused by nature, Civil Defense is by law charged with the carrying out during an emergency of all functions of government having to do with the protection of the health, lives, and property of the civilian population.' "This SECOND PHASE of our plan deals with the organization, preparation, coordination, and direction of the effort which our Government will have to engage in so as to carry out the reconstruction, restoration, and rehabilitation of the disaster area. This effort on the part of the Government of the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico will be coordinated with and accompanied by such supplementary aid as the federal government may be able to render and such additional measures as the municipalities and the Red Cross may adopt. "To eliminate any possible gaps between their plans and to prevent overlapping of effort, there should be a prearranged coordination between Civil Defense and the Red Cross with regard to preparation of plans and organization of their effort, so that each entity may devote itself to the activities devolving upon it. "The worst disasters that can be caused by the implements of war invented by man, including the atomic bomb, some- 201

T.§ 135-201 Ch. 7 

INTERNAL SECURITY 

times pale to insignificance before the destructive potentialities loosed by the uncontrollable force of cyclones, earthquakes, floods, fires, and tidal waves, and in order that the best use may, in cases of disaster, be made of the personnel, resources, and facilities provided by the departments, agencies, authorities, bureaus, and offices of the Government of the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico, the said entities shall take the following steps: "1. They shall work out beforehand an organization which provides for rendering, with a minimum of personnel, means, and facilities, all indispensable services devolving upon them. "2. As soon as the foregoing provision is complied with, they shall work out plans and make the necessary preparations for utilizing all the personnel, resources, and facilities available to them in the work of rehabilitation, reconstruction, and relief of the community. 

"3. The Director of Civil Defense shall coordinate with the plans of Civil Defense the plans and preparation of each department, authority, agency, bureau, or office of the Government of the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico in cases of disaster, and then the plans of Civil Defense with those of the Red 

Cross. 

"4. For the general task of reconstruction, the department, agencies, and bureaus of the federal government shall also prepare emergency aid and relief plans under the provisions of Executive Order No. 10427 of January 16, 1953, issued by the President of the United States, and as the Civil Defense 

Administration of the United States may direct, which plans shall be coordinated with those of Civil Defense of Puerto Rico." 

§ 135-202. Mobilization of Civil Defense 

(a) Once the Governor of Puerto Rico has declared a state of emergency, all directors of Civil Defense of the municipalities comprised within the area of the disaster shall mobilize the groups of volunteers of Civil Defense. All these units of Civil Defense, except the wardens, shall form a part of the regular services of the Government of the Commonwealth and shall act according to the plans outlined for the purpose. (b) When a municipality becomes a disaster area, the coordination of all functions of Civil Defense and of the services of the Commonwealth groups within the said municipality shall be the concern of the mayor, or of the local Civil Defense director as his representative. The function of coordination shall be exercised by the mayor or by the local director according to the plans and directives of the assistant director of Civil Defense in charge of that zone and in harmony with the plans of Civil Defense of Puerto Rico. (c) Civil Defense shall not be mobilized in those municipalities not included within the disaster area specified by the Governor, 202

Ch. T.25 § 135-204 

CIVIL DEFENSE unless the Director of Civil Defense of Puerto Rico issues an order to that effect.

§ 135-205. General instructions concerning reports 

These reports shall be brief and concise. They shall be submitted as soon as possible, not later than 72 hours after the disaster has occurred, using the speediest means available. If the telegraph and telephone service is interrupted, sending it by radiotelephone is authorized, using the following radiotelephonic systems: 

1. Police of Puerto Rico. 

2. Water Resources Authority. 

3. Aqueduct Service. 

4. Amateur radio operators. 

§ 135-206. Federal aid 

(a) The responsibility and obligation of organizing and directing the work of reconstruction and rehabilitation and of ministering relief to a community upon the community's undergoing a major catastrophe or disaster caused by nature, fall entirely upon the Government of the Commonwealth and of its municipalities, and so it has been acknowledged by Congress through Public Law No. 206

Ch. T.25 § 135-207 

CIVIL DEFENSE 

875 which fixes the obligation and responsibility of organizing, directing, and preparing the means for rehabilitation and relief upon the governments of the states and the municipalities, to which governments it will render supplementary aid as soon as it has ascertained, from the Governor's report, that the state and the local government and other entities are using all the means reasonably available to them for carrying out the said work. (b) Should the Governor decide that a disaster or catastrophe due to natural causes is of major proportions and that, as such, federal aid is needed in order that the Government of Puerto Rico and its municipalities and other entities may be able effectively to alleviate the human suffering and carry out the requisite reconstruction and rehabilitation work, this aid shall, under the said 

Federal Law No. 875, be directly requested from the President of the United States by the Governor of Puerto Rico. 

(c) Upon such action being taken by the Governor, the Director of Civil Defense of Puerto Rico shall, with the authorization of the Governor, submit to the Regional Administrator of the Federal 

Civil Defense, through the Regional Director of the Federal Civil 

Defense, all available information relating to the disaster and covering the following points: (1) Nature and extent of the disaster. (2) Kind and type of federal aid required. (3) Estimate of federal funds required. (4) Any other federal aid required. (d) Upon the granting of federal aid to Puerto Rico, such aid shall be rendered through a written agreement stipulating that the funds and aid extended by the federal government shall be used in conformity with the terms of the agreement, which shall be signed by the Governor of Puerto Rico. § 135-207. Federal aid in cases of lesser disasters (a) In the case of a disaster caused by nature and not of an extent justifying its being classified as a major disaster, that is to say, of a limited scope, federal aid may also be requested by the Governor of Puerto Rico, but such request shall be made to the Regional Director of the Federal Civil Defense, who shall process it before the federal authorities within the norms already established by the Administration for such cases. (b) Just as in cases of major disasters, the Director of Civil 

Defense of Puerto Rico shall, through the authorization of the 

207

T.§ 135-207 Ch. 7 INTERNAL SECURITY 

Governor of Puerto Rico, submit all pertinent information and data to the Federal Administration at Washington. 

§ 135-208. How federal aid shall be used 

(a) Any federal aid received for such purposes, whether in the form of supplies, food, or funds, shall be used for the purposes for which requested and in accordance with the instructions of the pertinent federal agencies and such special instructions as the 

Governor of Puerto Rico may issue. 

(b) Each department, agency, office, bureau, or instrumentality of the Government of Puerto Rico and of its municipalities shall use federal supplies, equipment, medicine, and funds specifically allotted to it for the purpose of reconstruction, rehabilitation, and aid according to the applicable federal instructions and to such directives as the Governor may prescribe. 

§ 135-209. Coordination of plans 

(a) The working out of the plans of the departments and other agencies of the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico for these purposes and their coordination with the plans of Civil Defense require a fixing of fundamental objectives and aims common to both groups and whereby they may, in the shortest time possible, be able to render the community the services required by the emergency. 

(b) A prearranged coordination with Civil Defense plans shall be established in order that Civil Defense personnel may be readily integrated into the regular government services whenever necessary and in order that the work performed by Civil Defense may be of the greatest practical usefulness within the activities of each department, agency, office, or instrumentality of the Government of Puerto Rico in its emergency plans. 

§ 135-210. Working out plans 

(a) Here in Puerto Rico we know that cyclones and hurricanes have repeatedly caused catastrophes of major proportions. Our plans, therefore, should be aimed at repairing the damage and destruction caused by these natural phenomena. See provisions relating to characteristics of hurricanes and cyclones, sec. 135-113 

et seq. of this title. 

(b) Each department, agency, office, or instrumentality of the Government of the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico and of its municipalities which has equipment, supplies, means, facilities, personnel, or other resources that can be used in cases of major disaster 208

Ch. T.25 135-214 

CIVIL DEFENSE 

caused by nature shall prepare a plan for taking part in the work of reconstruction, rehabilitation, aid, and relief to be carried out in accordance with the orders of the Governor of Puerto Rico. (c) The said plan shall provide for the department, agency, office, or instrumentality to continue rendering a minimum of the essential and indispensable service devolving upon it, and, as to the remainder of its means, resources, and personnel, it shall, in addition, prepare a plan for use in the reconstruction, rehabilitation, and relief work appertaining to it. § 135-211. Inventory of equipment and supplies; list of personnel 

It is of the utmost importance that inventories be prepared of all equipment available in the said department, agency, or instrumentality for use in cases of emergency. In these inventories there shall be set forth the location of the equipment, that is, the place where it is to be found. There shall also be prepared a list of the personnel available in case of emergency for reconstruction and rehabilitation tasks, independently of the personnel which is to continue working in the normal functions of the department, agency, or instrumentality. 

§ 135-212. Fixing responsibilities 

It is likewise important to fix clearly the responsibilities in the different fields of action within each department, agency, office, and instrumentality, so as to preclude conflicts over responsibilities with regard to functions and territory or jurisdiction. See provisions relating to territorial subdivisions and zone boards, sec. 

135-104 et seq. of this title. 

§ 135-213. Puerto Rico Police 

The Puerto Rico Police shall work out plans for using the Civil Defense Auxiliary Police in cases of disaster in each municipality, as circumstances may require. 

We suggest that in the event of cyclones the Auxiliary Police or such number thereof as may be necessary be called into service immediately after the occurrence of the disaster and for such time as circumstances may demand. 

§ 135-214. Fire Service 

Interruption of water services, together with interruption of traffic along our highways, both of which generally follow a cyclone, 209

T.§ 135-214 Ch. 7 

INTERNAL SECURITY 

are bound to create a particularly dangerous situation with regard to the possible consequences of a fire.

The Puerto Rico Fire Service shall use as many Civil Defense auxiliary firemen as it considers necessary, not only for the putting out of fires that may occur, but also for doing surveillance duty to prevent fires from starting. 

§ 135-215. Communications Authority Civil Defense personnel attached to the Communications Services should be used in addition to the personnel assigned from the Engineering Division - for rendering whatever services in this branch are most urgent, including the repair of telephone and telegraph lines. 

§ 135-216. Transportation Authority 

The Transportation Authority shall, in cooperation with the 

Office of Transportation of the Government of the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico, furnish whatever transportation is necessary for the activities of Civil Defense in its duties on the Commonwealth level.

Each municipality shall furnish whatever transportation is necessary for Civil Defense purposes within its jurisdiction.

Each department, agency, or instrumentality of the Government of Puerto Rico which uses Civil Defense personnel for the purposes of its emergency plans, whether within the municipality to which it appertains or outside the said municipality, shall furnish whatever transportation is necessary for the moving and conveyance of Civil Defense personnel. 

Furthermore, the Transportation Authority shall pay special attention to the necessary repairs and immediate restoration of service at the airports under its jurisdiction, and it shall, through the Director of Civil Defense, inform the Governor of Puerto Rico of its readiness for services. 

§ 135-217. Public Works (Including repairs by the Puerto Rico Water Resources, Aque duct, and Communications Authorities.)

All activities relating to the field of engineering will be in the charge and under the supervision of the Puerto Rico Department of Public Works. 

It is very important that preparation be made in advance to hold to a minimum the effects which the destruction or impair- 210

Ch. 

CIVIL DEFENSE 

T.25 § 135-218 ment of bridges and roads will entail with regard to all the repair work which it will be necessary to do in the various municipalities of the Island, especially insofar as aqueducts are concerned, and also insofar as concerns the services rendered by the Water 

Resources Authority. 

The Civil Defense engineering personnel of each municipality shall be proportionately assigned to the Aqueduct Service, the 

Water Resources Authority, the Communications Authority, and the Department of Public Works, as well as to any other additional service which in the judgment of the heads of Public Works may merit this allotment.

It is also suggested that stocks of material be provided in each municipality for the commonest emergency repairs in aqueduct services, so that these repairs may be made locally. 

Any interruption of vehicular traffic will retard the mobilization of Water Resources, Aqueduct, and Communications repair units, as well as those of the Department of Public Works itself, and for this reason all local repair services should be reinforced to the point where they can function even when isolated. 

It is especially recommended that the Department of Public 

Works organize Civil Defense Engineering Corps brigades in each municipality for the removal of debris and anything else blocking the streets and thoroughfares of each municipality. The basic idea behind this recommendation is that there are in each municipality Civil Defense Engineering Corps cadre which, simultaneously in each municipality, can, under the direction of Public Works officers, start the work of emergency repairs and restoration of services. § 135-218. Department of Health, including welfare

The floods caused by the torrential rain which accompanies cyclones cause the death of countless domestic animals, cattle, and horses, a situation which will gravely affect the purity of water if it is not attended to at once. Special Civil Defense cadres should be created for attending to this emergency.

The personnel of Civil Defense can be of great use in preventing the development of epidemics and the spread of contagious diseases by attending to the cleaning of brooks, rivers, and dams which supply the aqueducts. That same personnel can also carry out whatever other undertaking the Department of Health assigns it toward those ends.

211

T.§ 135-218 

INTERNAL SECURITY Ch. 7 

The personnel of Civil Defense can also be used in, among other things, the following activities: The rescue of injured and wounded people and their transportation to medical centers and hospitals, and the affording of additional personnel for reinforcing the emergency service at health centers and hospitals. 

The Welfare Division of Civil Defense shall be mobilized as soon as a state of emergency has been declared, and it shall become a part of the Bureau of Public Welfare and shall carry out all the work of investigation and welfare service required of it. 

It is highly important that the task to be carried out by Civil 

Defense personnel be facilitated, namely: 

(1) That the personnel for carrying out the necessary work be assigned. 

(2) That the heads of Civil Defense groups and of the Health personnel which is to be in charge of directing them, be appointed. (3) That the necessary coherence be established, after proper preparation and orientation. 

§ 135-219. Department of Agriculture and Commerce The Department of Agriculture and Commerce shall direct all agricultural rehabilitation work and its effort should be coordinated with that of all federal agricultural agencies located in Puerto 

Rico, as these agencies can be of great assistance.

Civil Defense has cadres established under the direction of responsible heads in each of the barrios of Puerto Rico, in addition to the personnel in the urban zones, and it can help the Department of Agriculture in the dissemination of information and the carrying out of plans prepared by the Department. 

§ 135-220. Department of Education 

School lunchrooms shall render service to the Red Cross pursuant to the conditions stipulated between them. 

With the cooperation of the Puerto Rico Housing Authority, the Department of Education shall prepare and direct all tallies made for determining the extent of the damages sustained by private dwellings and buildings.

As soon as a tally is made, the Department of Education shall send it to the Puerto Rico Housing Authority for study and evaluation, so that the said Authority may then forward it, with its report and conclusions, to the Governor of Puerto Rico, through the Director of Civil Defense.

CIVIL DEFENSE § 135-221. Department of the Treasury (supplies) 

The administrative procurement unit created under 3 L.P.R.A.

§§ 915-925 shall, within the provisions of the Civil Defense Act and as an emergency measure, handle the acquisition and procurement of all equipment, real estate, property, food, fuel, means of transportation and communication, facilities, including buildings and any other property which may be useful, necessary, or convenient for the relief of the civilian population and for the reconstruction or rehabilitation of property, all chargeable to the Emergency

Funds of the Governor of the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico or to such funds as the Governor may specifically determine. 

The administrative procurement unit shall set up the policy and procedure to be followed in order that the acquisition and procurement of the real estate, equipment, property, etc., referred to in the foregoing paragraph, may be carried out in a decentralized manner by all departments and agencies and in all the municipalities of the Government of Puerto Rico, in accordance with the requirements of the emergency. 

Codification. References to the "Service Office" were changed to the "administrative procurement unit created under 3 L.P.R.A. §§ 915-925" pursuant to 3 L.P.R.A. § 925. 

§ 135-222. Funds and expenditures

As soon as the Governor of Puerto Rico has allotted the funds and designated the amounts available for making the special expenditures and disbursements occasioned by the state of emergency declared, the Office of the Bureau of the Budget of the 

Government of Puerto Rico shall prepare a distribution of the said funds among the various departments, offices, agencies, bureaus, and instrumentalities of the Government and of the municipalities, which distribution shall be submitted to the Governor for approval through the Director of Civil Defense.

Federal agencies in Puerto Rico have different and varying functions, and the public's acquaintance with these activities may serve as guidance and be very useful to many persons who have suffered damages as a result of a disaster.

For such reasons we especially recommend that our departments, agencies, and instrumentalities make a careful survey of the means, facilities, and aid that said federal agencies may offer them. to improve the task of reconstruction and rehabilitation in the community. These agencies are listed in the following sections. 

§ 135-224. U. S. Department of Agriculture 

The U. S. Department of Agriculture has agencies whose activities are varied and cover the several aspects of the program for agricultural development. Note the following: (1) Agricultural Extension Service which may render services of orientation to the farmers on the following subjects: (A) General preventive sanitary measures, including utilization of water, disposal of rubbish, utilization of food, etc. (B) Measures for the care of animals and reconstruction of buildings damaged or destroyed. (C) Measures which must be taken in case of the suspension, stoppage, or interruption of lighting and electric power services. (D) Measures for storage of crops and for production. (2) Farm Credit Administration. The Bank makes loans-in-aid through the Production Credit Association and the National Farm 

Loan Association for rehabilitation of farms. Such loans are made as though they were bank loans and must be secured by first mortgages. These loans shall be made through the Federal Land Bank. (3) Farmers Home Administration makes loans-in-aid at 5% for a term of up to 10 years to farmers who need help for the purchase of cattle feed and equipment, for the repairing or reconstruction of buildings or sheds, and for the renovation of property on the farm. (4) Forest Service. This Service is authorized to operate in case of disaster in the neighborhood of the forests of the National 

Forest Reserve. 

(5) Production and Marketing Administration provides storage and, under certain conditions, distributes farm products. It has been very active in cases of disaster in the United States, has 214

T.25 § 135-225 supplied cattle feed in disaster areas, and has operated as coordinating agent of all the activities of the U. S. Department of 

Agriculture in said areas. (6) Soil Conservation Service provides technical assistance and equipment for the rehabilitation of farms affected by the disaster.

§ 135-225.-U. S. Department of Commerce 

(a) National Production Authority has regulations authorizing priority for materials and equipment necessary to carry out repairs in cases of restoration and rehabilitation following a disaster. It will cooperate and assist in locating material and equipment to be sent to the disaster areas. (b) Bureau of Public Roads. According to the federal laws, federal funds may be disposed of for the repairing or reconstruction of such roads or bridges as have been built with federal aid and which may be damaged or destroyed. 

(c) Civil Aeronautics Administration. This agency has an ex tensive network of communications. It may provide means of communication to local authorities when the commercial systems are not available and may help in determining the extent of the damages to airports, in the repairing of airports, and in the mobilization of local aircraft for emergency operations. (See Air Force, in First Phase of the Plan [§ 135-101 et seq. of this title].) 

(d) Federal Communications Commission provides priorities for emergency communications. (e) Federal Reserve Board. Federal Reserve Banks are authorized, in cases of major disasters, to adopt special measures liberalizing the system of loans for necessary repairs as a consequence of a disaster. (f) Food and Drug Administration may help in the organization of federal corps of the Commonwealth or of the local governments to investigate food and drugs that have been exposed to the effects of the disaster. (g) Public Health Service may give, in cooperation with the 

Department of Health of Puerto Rico, technical assistance in rela tion to sanitary methods and in all that may endanger the public health. 215

(h) Federal Housing Administration. This agency may guaran tee up to 100% of the loans for the reconstruction of homes destroyed by a disaster, and obviate the down payment requirement for repairs and rehabilitation in the disaster areas. 

§ 135-226. U. S. Department of Labor 

The U. S. Department of Labor may cooperate with the Department of Labor of Puerto Rico in everything related to the reemployment of workers who have been left unemployed as a result of the disaster. 

§ 135-227. U. S. Treasury Department 

(a) U. S. Coast Guard provides help to civil authorities in connection with communications, rescue, and evacuation. (b) Division of Disbursement distributes federal funds and is the Division in charge of making the payments to the agencies or departments and instrumentalities of the Commonwealth for purposes of federal aid in cases of disaster. (c) Reconstruction Finance Corporation has funds for cases of disaster, for the purpose of making loans at the rate of 3% for rehabilitating the damages caused by the disaster. These loans are available to individuals, commercial firms, churches, or nonprofit corporations which have sustained damages or losses as a result of the disaster. These loans are mostly made for a maximum term of 10 years. Some loans for construction may be extended up to a term of 20 years. The funds for these loans may be obtained through a declaration by the Reconstruction Finance Corporation of the existence of a disaster, without it being necessary that the President of the United States make the formal declaration of the existence of the disaster. Representatives of the Reconstruction

Finance Corporation may be contacted through any federal reserve bank. (d) Veterans' Administration. This agency has certain authority to liberalize the down payment requirements on homes which are to replace those destroyed or damaged by a disaster. Loans can be made up to the total value and with 30-year maturity. Loans of up to $500 for repairing and rehabilitation as a result of a disaster can be obtained for those dwellings on which the Veterans' 

Administration has a mortgage. 216

DIVISION 4. COORDINATION OF EXECUTIVE FUNCTIONS 135-301. Powers of Director of Civil Defense 

135-302. Use of agencies of Government 

§ 135-301. Powers of Director of Civil Defense The Director of Civil Defense in Puerto Rico shall have the following powers and shall prescribe the corresponding instructions and orders: (1) The powers and authority conferred upon the Governor by sec. 6 of the Act, subsec. (b), paragraph (2) [25 L.P.R.A. § 135 (b) (2)], for the preparation of a plan and general program for the Puerto Rico Civil Defense, integrating and coordinating the said plan and program, as far as possible and suitable, with the plans of the Civil Defense of the Federal Government and of the states of the Union; and coordinating the preparation of plans and programs for the Civil Defense in the municipalities and in the Capital of the Commonwealth, integrating and coordinating the said plans, as far as it is possible and suitable, with the plan and pro gram of the Puerto Rico Civil Defense. 

(2) The powers and authority conferred upon the Governor by sec. 6, subsec. (b), paragraph (3) [25 L.P.R.A. § 135(b) (3)], to carry on any practice of Civil Defense, including direction and control of the following: (A) Black-outs, air raid drills, mobilization of Civil Defense forces, and any other drills or exercises. (B) Notices and drills of attacks, and means to be used for carrying them out. (C) Putting into effect a plan which will guarantee the means to have all lights out or covered in the community. (D) Making sure all bypass valves of aqueducts, gas tanks, 217

T.§ 135-301 

INTERNAL SECURITY 

Ch. 7 and electric energy are off, and stopping all public services and utilities. (E) Regulating the conduct to be observed by the citizens, and the transit of pedestrians and motor vehicles, before, during, and immediately after the attack drill or in case of enemy attack. (F) Providing means for the evacuation of the civil population from certain areas and for their lodging in previously indicated places. (3) The powers and authority conferred upon the Governor by sec. 6, subsec. (b), paragraph (5) [25 L.P.R.A. § 135(b) (5)], to use the existing services and facilities of the offices and agencies of the Government of Puerto Rico, and of its political subdivisions. 

All these agencies and offices shall cooperate and shall render their services and facilities when so required by the Director of the 

Puerto Rico Civil Defense. 

(4) The Director of the Puerto Rico Civil Defense may delegate the powers specified in paragraph (2) of this section to the assistant directors of the Puerto Rico Civil Defense and on the local or municipal director of Civil Defense. 

(5) Shall have the power to exercise the authority conferred upon the Governor of Puerto Rico, according to sec. 6, subsec. (b), paragraph (9) [25 L.P.R.A. § 135(b) (9)], to obtain, through the Federal Civil Defense Administration, equipment, materials, services, and supplies to carry on the provisions of the aforementioned Act, in accordance with the regulations established for this purpose by the Secretary of the Treasury of Puerto Rico; also, to make and enter into pacts and agreements with the Federal Civil Defense Director in regard to the time, manner, and payment of these acquisitions.

CIVIL DEFENSE § 135-302. Use of agencies of Government 

In case of disaster the following provisions are to be observed in order to get the best use of the personnel, the means, and the facilities belonging to the departments, agencies, authorities, bureaus, and offices of the Government of the Commonwealth of 

Puerto Rico: 

SECTIONS 

Rico, the Honorable Luis Muñoz Marín, has issued the following Executive Order, whereby the Civil Defense is entrusted with the mission of coordinating the executive functions of the different Government departments and agencies during any kind of disaster." (1) There shall be an organization prepared beforehand to provide for the rendering of essential services with a minimum of personnel, means, and facilities. (2) Once the above provision has been fulfilled, plans and the necessary preparations shall be made to use all available personnel, means, and facilities in the rehabilitation, reconstruction, and help of the community. 

(3) The Director of Civil Defense shall coordinate the plans and preparations to govern in case of disaster of each department, authority, agency, bureau, or office of the Government of the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico with the plans of the Puerto Rico 

Civil Defense.

§ 135-402. Provisions for recruitment 

The recruitment of volunteers for the Civil Defense auxiliary services will be conducted in accordance with the provision of this 

Division. 

§ 135-403. Recruitment committees - Establishment 

A "recruitment committee" is established in all and every municipality of Puerto Rico, including the Municipality of San Juan, which will be composed by the following officials: 

(1) The mayor 

(2) Local civil defense director (3) School superintendent (4) Chief of police (district commander) (5) Health center medical director, or public health unit medical director (6) Chief, public welfare local unit (7) President, American Red Cross municipal committee (8) Two local civic leaders. 

The mayor will act as president of the recruitment committee. 

§ 135-404. 

Vice-president and members

At its first meeting for organization, the recruitment committee will designate a vice-president. The vice-president will assume the functions of the president during his absence. 1962 Vol. 1, No. 4 220

Ch. 

CIVIL DEFENSE 

T.25 135-408 

At this meeting the recruitment committee members, as established by sec. 135-403 of this title, will select the two civic leaders of the community who will be members of the committee. § 135-405. Secretary

The local civil defense director in each municipality will act as secretary of the recruitment committee, and will have as his duties to convoke committee meetings, reception and revision of applications for enrollment, submit the applications for enrollment to the recruitment committee, and to prepare the acts of the meetings. § 135-406. Regulations

The recruitment committee is empowered to promulgate the regulations governing the procedure to be followed in its meetings and decisions. 

§ 135-407. Applications for admission 

(a) The recruitment committee will meet semi-monthly, or as deemed necessary, to consider the applications for admission to the 

Civil Defense auxiliary services. The recruitment committee will consider the applications for admission received by the local civil defense director and will determine the auxiliary service to which the applicant shall be assigned. This decision will be based on educational background, knowledge, experience, and character of the applicant. (b) The applicant will be assigned to one of the following auxiliary services: (1) Administrative (2) Welfare (3) Fire (4) Communications (5) Black market (6) Engineering (7) Medical (8) Police (9) Rescue (10) Transportation (11) Wardens.

The recruitment committee will reject all applications for admission to the auxiliary services not accompanied by the Police certificate. 

§ 135-410. Loyalty oath 

After the application for enrollment in one of the auxiliary services is approved by the recruitment committee, the local civil defense director will inform the applicant requesting that he take the prescribed oath in accordance with the provisions of art. 14, Puerto Rico Civil Defense Act (Public Law No. 183, of 1951) 

[25 L.P.R.A. § 143]. This oath will be taken by a judge or an official authorized by law, and will be duty free. 

§ 135-411. Documents to State Office 

After the oath requirement is satisfied, the local civil defense director will forward the application for enrollment Form OCD-1 duly executed, two 2″ × 2″ photographs, and Form OCD-2 identification card to the State Civil Defense Office. The applicant will sign his name in the corresponding space of Form OCD-2 identification card, and the other information will be filled out by the State Civil 

Defense Office.

The State Office of Civil Defense will proceed to fill out any corresponding parts of Forms OCD-1 and OCD-2, "Personal In formation for Enrollment in the Civil Defense Auxiliary Services" 

and "Identification Card", respectively, and will assign an identification number to the applicant, which will be indicated in the identification card. § 135-413. Delivery and return of identification card

defense director for delivery to the corresponding volunteer. § 135-414. Requirements for admission 

(a) The members of the auxiliary services will meet among other requirements determined by the State Civil Defense Director, with the consent of the Governor, the following: (1) Citizenship. Be an American citizen. (2) Age. There is a minimum of 18 and a maximum of 45 years for enrollment in the Civil Defense auxiliary services. (3) Height and weight: (A) Height: A minimum height of 5′ 71½". (B) Weight: Weight shall be proportioned to the height of the applicant. 

(4) The State Civil Defense Director is authorized in his discretion to exempt from the prescribed requirements of age, weight, and height: 

(A) Women. 

(B) Volunteers having exceptional qualifications to perform the duties of the auxiliary services for which they are recruited. (C) Active members of organizations such as Boy Scouts, Girl Scouts, Police Athletic League, Civil Air Patrol, et cetera. 

(D) Pensioned or retired members of the Puerto Rico Police,

Puerto Rico Fire Service or any similar government or civilian organization. (5) Academic background. It is established that the applicant must have completed, at least, the ninth grade of elementary school for enrollment in the Civil Defense auxiliary services. 

(6) Physical condition. The members of the auxiliary services must be physically capable of performing their duties. Volunteers for the Police, Fire, and Nursing auxiliary services must undergo a physical examination. The physical examination certificate will be issued by the health center medical director or by the public 1962

The local civil defense director with the cooperation of the Puerto Rico Police and other government authorities will perform a thorough investigation of the moral character, reputation, habits, behavior in the community, ways of acting and other similar information of the applicants for enrollment in the auxiliary services.

The State Civil Defense Director is authorized to establish, with the consent of the Governor, requirements for enrollment higher or lower than the ones listed above, when according to this judgment the recruitment situations require so. 

§ 135-415. Powers of State Civil Defense Director 

The State Civil Defense Director is empowered to arrange for, organize, order and control the preparation of manuals for procedures and instructions to develop the administrative policy and any other matter necessary for the organization and functioning of the Civil Defense auxiliary services.

§ 221d-51. Organic structure 

The basic functional organization of the Police shall consist of units hereinafter mentioned which shall be administratively organized by the Superintendent pursuant to the needs which from time to time may arise in order to attain a better functioning and the most efficient coordination of the Police duties. 

(1) Office of the Superintendent: The Office of the Superintend ent shall adopt, prescribe and execute the general policy and standards for the operation and administration of the Police. (2) Bureaus: The Bureaus mentioned below shall operate under the direction of an Assistant Superintendent appointed by the 

Superintendent. The Assistant Superintendents designated from among the members of the Force shall maintain their ranks and shall continue to be members of the Police with all the duties, prerrogatives and rights inherent thereto. 

The Superintendent may, with the express authorization of the Governor, enlarge the number of these Bureaus and provide for their administrative organization, as well as to fix their duties. 

(A) Bureau of Field Operations: This Bureau shall be com posed of all the units comprised within the field operation structure, their main duties being the rendering of all those services for the protection and safety of the citizens, as well as to keep the public order. (B) Bureau of Administration: This Bureau shall be in charge of the administration of all the personnel system, the education and training of same, the legal phase of the Police, the budget and financial matters of the Organization, as well as the program of public relations and information between the Agency and the community. 

(C) Bureau of Inspection Services: This Bureau shall be in charge of the inspections of the Police, the investigations in connection with the conduct of the members of the Force and examination of the legality of the financial transactions of the Organization. 

(D) Bureau of Technical Services: This Bureau shall be in charge of the administration of the services in connection with transportation, communications, crime statistics and criminal identification of the Police. 

Aug. 31, 1968 

Vol. 7, No. 8 224

Ch. T.25 § 221d-56 

 § 221d-52. Command authority 

The supreme authority of the direction of the Police shall be vested in the Governor, but the administration, supervision and immediate direction of the Organization shall be under the control of the Superintendent. 

§ 221d-53. Organization of the Force The Force shall be composed of: Colonel, lieutenant colonels, majors, captains, first lieutenants, second lieutenants, sergeants, detectives, guardsmen and agents of the Criminal Investigation Corps. 

§ 221d-54. Appointments 

(a) The appointments of colonel, lieutenant colonels and majors shall be made by the Superintendent subject to the approval of the Governor. 

(b) All other members of the Force shall be appointed by the 

Superintendent. 

§ 221d-55. Probationary period 

(a) Except in the case of the colonel, the enlistment of every person as member of the Police shall be subject to a probation period of two years, during which period the member may be separated from the service at any time. (b) The members of the Police separated during the probationary period may appeal before the Police Commission when they allege their separation was due to political, religious or racial reasons. They may also appeal when a disciplinary action for a serious shortcoming is imposed carrying suspension from employment and pay for a period not in excess of 6 months. 

§ 221d-56. Enlistment requirements 

(a) With the exception of vacancies which might occur at the level of colonel, lieutenant colonels, majors and members of the Criminal Investigation Corps, all candidates for enlistment in the Police shall meet, among other requirements which the Superintendent may establish, the following: (1) Weight and height. (A) Height: A minimum of 5 feet 7 inches and a maximum of 6 feet 6 inches. 1970 

Vol. 9, No. 4 

225

T.§ 221d-56 

INTERNAL SECURITY 

Ch. 21 (B) Weight: The required weight shall be that which keeps proportion to the height of the candidate, according to the employment announcement.

At his discretion, the Superintendent may exempt from the former requirements of weight and height, women and other candidates who possess exceptional qualifications to discharge the duties as members of the Force. (2) Age. A minimum age of 19 years and a maximum of 35 years for enlistment in the Police is hereby fixed, except in direct entry cases and members of the Criminal Investigation Corps, whose minimum age for enlistment is fixed at 21 years, with the exception of the Director, whose minimum age shall be 25 years. 

(3) Academic requirements. 

(A) For enlistment as guardsman: High school graduate. (B) For direct entry as detective: University or college degree and considerable experience in police or similar work. (C) For direct entry as an officer: University or college degree and some experience in the direction and supervision of personnel. 

(D) For entry as member of the Criminal Investigation Corps: 

(i) A bachelor's degree from the University of Puerto

Rico or from any other accredited university, or its equivalent. (ii) Any other requirement which the Superintendent may deem necessary to fill the position referred to in the employment announcement. (4) Physical condition. All candidates, including the members of the Criminal Investigation Corps, shall undergo a comprehensive physical examination performed by the Police medical officer and any other examinations or tests which the Superintendent may determine. (5) Other requirements. All candidates for appointment to the Police and to the Criminal Investigation Corps must approve such capacitation, aptitude, and ability tests to which they may be subjected. (A) A thorough investigation of their character, reputation, habits, behavior in the community, manners, citizenship, and other details of similar nature. (b) The Superintendent is hereby authorized, with the consent of the Governor, to lower the requirements set forth in this sub- 1970 226

§ 221d-57. Promotion requirements 

The requirements for promotion to the different categories up to captain level, inclusive, shall be established by the Superintendent in the proper announcements for tests; Provided, however, That among the basic requirements the following shall be included: (1) Tests of capacity, aptitude or ability such as written examinations, personal interviews and other similar exercises. (2) Fair, equitable and reasonable requirements as to experience, behavior and other similar ones; Provided, however, That academic preparation may substitute the requirement of experience, as specified in the announcements for tests. § 221d-58. Reemployment requirements

The Superintendent may authorize the reemployment in the Force at the same level and with the same salary provided by law in these cases, of all former members of the Force who during their time of service observed good behavior and who were separated for reasons other than fault on their part and who at the time of such separation had no faults pending. The names of the former members whose applications for reemployment are approved will be entered in a reemployment list in the order in which the applications are received by the Superintendent. Before approving a reemployment, the Superintendent shall investigate applicant's conduct during the time he was out of the Force. § 221d-59. Roll of eligibles (a) Appointment list. This list shall include the names of those persons who have qualified through the approval of the Police entrance examinations. (b) Promotion list. This list shall include the names of those members of the Force who have qualified through the approval of promotional examination for higher ranks. (c) Reemployment list. (A) This list shall include the names of the former members whose reemployment applications have been approved. The date on which the applications are received by the Superintendent shall determine the order of appearance on the list. The candidates appearing in the reemployment list shall have priority over those who appear in the promotion list for the purpose of covering vacancies in their ranks. 

Aug. 31, 1968 

Vol. 7, No. 8 227

T.§ 221d-59 Ch. 21 

INTERNAL SECURITY 

(B) The requirements for appointments and promotions shall be established taking into consideration the written examination or together with such other factors as the Superintendent may deem necessary. The examination announcement shall determine the relative value of the written examination and/or of the other factors which form part of the examination. (C) Once promotion lists are established and published, they shall in no manner whatsoever be altered, unless this becomes necessary to correct a plain and noticeable error. These lists shall be in effect for a period of not less than 1 nor more than 2 years, from the date on which they are established. (D) Upon expiration of the established minimum duration period, the Superintendent may cancel the list or lists of eligibles. 

Promotions shall be made in strict order of precedence in the list of eligibles. This rule-strict order of precedence in promotionsshall not apply to a member of the Force who has lost his eligibility for promotion as hereinafter set forth. He shall be promoted when his turn is reached in the list of eligibles provided his ineligibility has ceased, but if, when ineligibility ceases, his turn has been passed over, he shall then be entitled to the first turn in such list. 

§ 221d-60. Ineligibility 

(a) Any candidate or member of the Force who at the time of taking an examination gives or receives any aid from a fellow member or from any other person, shall become ineligible and his examination shall be considered void. (b) All those members of the Police who have been punished for serious shortcomings shall be ineligible for promotion for a period of 1 year. All those members of the Police who have been punished for slight shortcomings shall also be ineligible for promotion for a period of 6 months. From the moment the punishment is decreed and during the period of ineligibility they shall not be entitled to promotion. Ineligibility for promotion shall start from the date of expiration of the last punishment. The Superintendent may lift the ineligibility in the promotion list of those members of the Force who, while in an ineligible status, distinguish themselves through acts of heroism or of such other nature that may reflect great merit upon their service record. 

§ 221d-61. Vacancies 

Vacancies for each of the categories shall be filled in the manner hereinafter indicated: 

Aug. 31, 1968 

Vol. 7, No. 8 228

Ch. T.25 § 221d-62 

 (1) Guardsmen. Guardsmen vacancies shall be filled through selection among the applicants who have passed the offered examinations and complied with the requirements established in sec. 

221d-56 of this title. (2) Sergeants. Sergeants vacancies shall be filled from the promotion list already established after the applicants have complied with the requirements established in sec. 221d-57 of this title. (3) Detectives. Detective vacancies shall be filled in 2 ways: (A) Through promotion, after the candidates have complied with the requirements established in sec. 221d-57 of this title; and (B) Through direct entry when the candidate possesses and complies with the requirements established in subsec. (3) of sec. 221d-56 of this title. (4) Officers. Officers vacancies, except those of colonel, lieutenant colonels and majors, shall be filled: (A) Through promotion according to the list and after having complied with the promotional requirements established in sec. 221d-57 of this title. (B) Vacancies in the Criminal Investigation Corps shall be filled by the Superintendent based on such requirements he may establish for such purposes. (C) Direct entry after having complied with the entrance requirements established in Sec. 221d-56 of this title. (5) Outstanding services. Whenever a member of the Police may distinguish himself for extraordinarily exceptional or outstanding services, the Superintendent may promote him to the immediate superior category without being subject to the promotion requirements herein before established. § 221d-62. Physical conditions that disqualify for police membership (a) It shall be a requisite that every candidate entering, reentering and advancing in the Force shall pass a physical examination by the Police medical officer pursuant to the physical requirements mentioned below. Likewise, it shall be the duty of every member of the Police in active service to undergo a physical examination at any time the Superintendent may deem it necessary, in order to determine if his physical condition meets the established standards.

(c) In exercising the discretion conferred upon him by the foregoing provision, the Superintendent shall consider: (1) The special and exceptional circumstances which may affect the public service; and (2) Whether the retention would accelerate or aggravate the physical condition of the agent. (d) The member of the Force who may have been retained in active service pursuant to the foregoing provision shall keep his right to participate in promotions. SUBDIVISION 5. SPECIAL GUARDSMEN AUTHORIZED BY THE GOVERNOR AND CONTRACTING OF SERVICE 

1971 

Vol. 10, No. 6 236.1

T.§ 221d-81 Ch. 21 

INTERNAL SECURITY § 221d-81. Special guardsmen authorized by the Governor 

The special guardsmen to increase the Force authorized by the Governor whenever he deems it necessary, shall be governed by the following provisions: 

(1) Selection and appointment: The selection and appointment of these special guardsmen shall be of the exclusive province of the Superintendent. 

(2) Entrance requirements: Entrance requirements shall be established by the Superintendent in accordance with the existing conditions and needs of the Service. 1971 

 236.2

Ch. T.25 § 221d-81 

(3) Promotions: These special guardsmen shall not be eligible to compete for promotions within the regular Force. 

(4) Duties and responsibilities: Special guardsmen shall have the same rights, duties and responsibilities as regular guardsmen. (5) Salary: Special guardsmen shall receive the same salary and allowances as regular guardsmen. 

(6) Direction and supervision: Special guardsmen shall be covered by the same provisions prescribed for the direction and supervision of the regular members of the Force, all of which is within the exclusive province of the Superintendent or of the Officer so designated by him. (7) Uniform, insignias, arms and equipment: The uniform, insignias, arms and equipment to be used by these special guardsmen shall be determined by the Superintendent, depending upon the duties assigned to them, but always guaranteeing the maximum of safety. (8) Working period: The working period of special guardsmen shall be the same as that established for the members of the 

Force, pursuant to sec. 16 of the Police Act [25 L.P.R.A. § 2210] 

and the provisions of this division in connection therewith. Besides, the same benefits established for the members of the Force in sec. 

17 of the Police Act [25 L.P.R.A. § 221p] shall be applicable hereto. 

(9) Removals: When in the judgment of the Superintendent the conduct, habits, responsibility or efficiency of a guardsman does not warrant his stay in the Force, he shall be immediately discharged. (10) Whenever a special guardsman is charged with the commitment of a serious shortcoming and the Superintendent determines he was in the legal performance of his duties, he shall be provided with counsel. (11) Whenever such a special guardsman is injured in the performance of his duties, he shall be covered by the same provisions applicable to the regular members of the Force in the performance of their duties, as provided in sec. 7 of the Act [25 

L.P.R.A. § 221f]. 

(12) In the absence of a specific provision to govern any matter not included in the foregoing provisions, the same shall be decided pursuant to the standards that the Superintendent may establish.
