SUBDIVISION 6. DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES OF THE MEMBERS OF THE FORCE SECTIONS 

221d-91. Duties and responsibilities 

§ 221d-91. Duties and responsibilities 

Within the scope of their prerrogatives, each member of the Force shall have, among others, the following duties and responsibilities: (1) To protect life and property, prevent crime and disorder. (2) To enforce the laws, regulations and municipal ordinances, with a high spirit of justice, without incurring in partiality or personal prejudice. (3) To observe and protect the civil rights of the citizen. (4) To observe excellent conduct at all times. (5) To take all precautions to guarantee the protection of persons detained or under arrest. (6) To treat politely the public and render the necessary help to those requesting it. (7) To give proper protection to those persons legally assembled for a lawful act, and maintain order at the place. (8) To perform his duties anywhere in the Commonwealth of

Puerto Rico without limitation of jurisdiction of any kind whatsoever, and to this effect he shall consider himself on duty at all times. (9) To obey the orders issued by his superior officers. (10) To be on time in his engagements and prompt in performing his duties. (11) To act in a just, calm and wise manner at all times. (12) To explain and advise the public as to the best compliance of the law, as well as to matters related to public safety. 

SECTIONS SUBDIVISION 7. DISCIPLINARY MEASURES 

221d-101. 

Serious shortcomings 

221d-102. Slight shortcomings § 221d-101. Serious shortcomings

The following shall constitute serious shortcomings, for which the Superintendent may decree the permanent removal, demotion 

Aug. 31, 1968 

Vol. 7, No. 8 238

Ch. 

T.25 § 221d-101 or suspension of any member of the Force for a period not in excess of 6 months:

Rule 1. Insubordination or disobedience to any written or oral order issued by the Superintendent, officers or by any member of the Force with authority to give orders, including his refusal to explain his acts in the course of an administrative investigation. 

Rule 2. To ridicule, criticise or censure, in writing or orally, in public or in private, the official actions, directives, findings or orders of the Superintendent, officers, members of the Police with sufficient authority to give orders, or any civil officer of the Police with sufficient authority to give orders, whether he be vested with such power by legal authority or by resolution of the Superintendent, and when such orders were issued as a result of and in connection with the official duties of such officers. 

Rule 3. To challenge without sound basis the honesty, integrity, and competence of any member of the Police or civil officer, or to make improper statements with the sole purpose of hurting his dignity. 

Rule 4. To assault, batter or make use of improper or offensive language against the Superintendent, officers, civil officer or any other member of the Police.

Rule 5. To commit a felony or a misdemeanor involving moral turpitude, or conviction for such offenses. 

Rule 6. To give false testimony before a judge, the Police Commission of Puerto Rico, or any administrative agency or investigating officer, or to swear to and subscribe any document changing or falsifying the facts.

Rule 7. To act in such a way as to imply cowardice. 

Rule 8. To show manifest incapacity, incompetence, neglect or carelessness in the performance of the duties, functions and responsibilities of the members of the Police mentioned in sec. 221d- 

91 of this title. To that effect, the members of the Police shall at all times and at any place be considered within the jurisdiction of the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico in off duty periods and shall keep their condition as such members. 

Rule 9. Improper use of firearms: (a) To threaten with or make use of a firearm in cases not authorized by law against any person, whether a member or not of the Force. 

Aug. 31, 1968 

Vol. 7, No. 8 239

T.§ 221d-101 

INTERNAL SECURITY 

Ch. 21 (b) To fail to take the necessary precautions with the official arms. (c) To leave firearms at the reach of persons who may make improper use of them or to permit other persons to use them. 

Rule 10. To give, receive or allow the giving or receiving of improper help during examinations for admission or promotion in the Police.

Rule 11. To enlist or reenlist in the Police through deceit or fraudulent means by concealing information which, if known, would be in conflict with the requirements adopted for enlistment and reenlistment; or to aid or advise any other person to enlist or reenlist by fraudulent means. 

Rule 12. Use of alcoholic beverages: (a) To make use of alcoholic beverages while on duty. (b) To make use of alcoholic beverages while in uniform, whether in a public or private place, even if he is not on duty. (c) To make excessive use of alcoholic beverages while off duty. (d) To refuse to have a sample of his blood, urine or breath taken in order to determine the percentage of alcohol in his blood, when so required by any member of the Police. (e) To drive or operate a motor vehicle under the effect of alcoholic beverages.

Rule 13. To forge a signature on an official or on any other document.

Rule 14. To allow the use of alcoholic beverages or drugs to persons under his custody or to persons under arrest, whether held for investigation or under suspicion in connection with the commitment of a public offense.

Rule 15. To be familiar or associate with persons of doubtful conduct or outlaws, except when complying with his duties. 

Rule 16. To be familiar or associate with convicted persons or who are under charges of any fault involving moral turpitude, except in those cases in which said persons are up to third-degree relatives either through consanguinity or affinity. 

Rule 17. To communicate or give away to any person information which might help violators to avoid being detected, arrested, punished or investigated. 

Aug. 31, 1968

Vol. 7, No. 8 

240

Ch. 

T.25 8221d-101 

Rule 18. To advise or incite any member of the Police to commit any of the faults enumerated in this section or to be an accomplice in the commitment of any of them. 

Rule 19. To inflict physical injury or use improper language towards any person, or to act against his civil rights. 

Rule 20. To sell, lend, use or in any manner whatsoever dispose of property which may have been entrusted to his custody for official use.

Rule 21. To sell, lend, use or in any manner whatsoever dispose of evidence obtained or property under the custody of the Police. 

Rule 22. To impute acts to any person which may give rise to an administrative investigation, or the filing of an information or complaint, knowing that the facts so imputed are false, or to alter, modify or fail to file an information or complaint without proper authorization. 

Rule 23. To give, offer, ask or accept any reward, gift, present or any other object of value which may influence, directly or indirectly, so as to please somebody in police matters, or which may adversely reflect on the Police.

Rule 24. To belong to or join any organization having the nature of a labor union. 

Rule 25. To abandon the service without proper authorization.

Among others, the following acts shall be considered abandonment of service: to fall asleep while on duty; to chat, to be idle, to read while on duty; to engage in private business; to go away from the area assigned to him without just cause, or to engage in acts which are not closely connected with the duties entrusted to him. 

Rule 26. To observe improper, immoral or disorderly conduct detrimental to the Police, including acts such as to procreate children out of wedlock; to have marital relations out of wedlock; to associate with prostitutes, homosexuals or persons who use or are engaged in the narcotic drugs business; to have any book, writing, drawing, engraving, painting, printed matter, images, poster, emblems, photos or any other material or objects which may primarily tend to attract or incite lascivious, morbos or obscene acts in nudism or sex; to recommend, help, advise or incite the practice of miscarriages; to visit brothels, or perform any other acts which may be against the dignity, honesty and mores of the society. 

When any of the acts hereinbefore mentioned were committed while in the discharge of official duties, the same shall not consti-

Rule 27. In the case of supervisors and officers, failure to file charges for serious shortcomings when he is acquainted with such offenses; and in the case of members of the Police, failure to reveal the commitment of serious shortcomings by fellow members of the Police.

Rule 28. It shall constitute a serious shortcoming every slight shortcoming committed by any member of the Force after he has been punished previously on 3 different occasions for slight shortcomings in the period of 5 years, effective from the commission of the first offense. § 221d-102. Slight shortcomings

Slight shortcomings shall be those for which the Superintendent and the senior officer in rank, as regards personnel under his command, may impose as punishment the suspension from employment and pay for a period not to exceed 15 days and/or a reprimand.

SECTIONS SUBDIVISION 8. PROCEDURE IN THE HANDLING OF CHARGES AND RESOLUTIONS 

221d-111. Serious shortcomings 

221d-112. Slight shortcomings § 221d-111. Serious shortcomings (a) Any member of the Police, who in the opinion of the Superintendent commits a serious shortcoming, may be permanently discharged, demoted or suspended from the Force without pay, for a period not to exceed 6 months.

All resolutions of the Superintendent permanently discharging, demoting or suspending from employment and pay any member of the Force for a period not longer than 6 months, must be in writing and notice given to the member or members so affected by said resolution in the manner hereinafter provided. The resolution shall state the grounds on which the Superintendent bases his action. (b) Whenever possible, notice of the resolution shall be served personally by the District Major of the locality where he resides or by a representative of said officer. 

Aug. 31, 1968

Vol. 7, No. 8 

242.2

Ch. 

 T.25 § 221d-112 

(c) If it is impossible to serve notice personally to the party aggrieved by the resolution of the Superintendent, said notice shall be executed by leaving a copy thereof at his home or usual residence, delivered to a person residing therein of sufficient age and discretion. The person making the delivery shall make a note as to date, hour and place where such delivery was made. He may also be notified through any other method including registered mail with return receipt requested, in which case the date of delivery appearing therein shall constitute the date of notice. As regards personal notice, the District Major or his representative shall send to the Superintendent, through official channels, a certificate stating the date, hour and place of notice.

Any party aggrieved by the resolution rendered by the Superintendent may appeal to the Commission within the term of 10 days to be counted from the date when officially notified of the resolution from which appeal is being taken. § 221d-112. Slight shortcomings (a) When a citizen complains of a slight shortcoming on the part of a member of the Police or when the Superintendent or any senior officer has knowledge of a slight shortcoming, said senior officer shall proceed to investigate the matter thoroughly and if as a result of said investigation it is established that a slight shortcoming was committed, charges shall be preferred. (b) The charge or charges shall be preferred in writing and signed by the senior officer who witnessed or has knowledge of the offense, using the printed forms which for said purpose shall be furnished by the Superintendent of the Police. (c) The charges shall indicate what provision of the Regulations has been violated, stating therein the specific facts imputed to the respondent. (d) A copy of the charges shall be delivered personally to the respondent, who shall answer them in writing within 5 days after the date of delivery. (e) Upon being served with copy of the charges, the respondent shall sign a copy thereof, thus indicating that he has been served with copy of said charges. (f) If the respondent refuses to receive the copy of the charges, the member of the Force who serves them shall so certify on the reverse side thereof. 

Aug. 31, 1968

Vol. 7, No. 8 

242.3

T.§ 221d-112 

INTERNAL SECURITY 

Ch. 21 (g) In both cases, if the respondent fails to answer the charges within 5 days after the date of notice thereof, the proceedings shall continue as if he had filed a full denial of the charges. (h) Within 5 days after the date on which the respondent should have answered the charges, the corresponding senior officer shall take the action which he may deem advisable pursuant to sec. 221d-102 of this title. The senior officer is hereby authorized to reach any of the following conclusions: (1) That the charges were not proved and, therefore, should be dismissed. (2) That the charges were proved and, therefore, he shall impose the punishment which he may deem proper and applicable, publishing same in a General Order. (i) The notice of the decision shall be made in writing and delivered personally to the respondent by the senior officer. (j) When the punishment imposed bears a suspension from employment and pay, it shall be revised by the Superintendent. (k) In all cases the member so authorized to impose the punishment shall furnish the Superintendent of the Police, within 5 days after the date of entry of the resolution in the case, the complete file of same. (1) Any party aggrieved by a resolution of the member so authorized to impose punishments may appeal to the Superintendent within a term of 10 days, and if the respondent fails to file a notice of appeal within this term, the punishment imposed shall become final and unappealable. (m) The appeal of a respondent before the Superintendent of the Police shall be considered duly filed by delivering a notice of appeal in the latter's office. (n) For appeal purposes, a notice of appeal shall be deemed to be filed on time if on the date on which it was received in the office of the Superintendent or deposited in the post office according to the postmark on the envelope, the term of 10 days since the notice of the punishment has not elapsed. The 10-day term for appeal from the resolution to which the respondent is entitled shall start on the date on which he was personally notified by the senior officer. (0) Within reasonable time from the receipt of the appeal in the office of the Superintendent, the latter may confirm, reduce or quash the punishment.

§ 221d-123. Arms and equipment 

(a) Revolver and ammunition. (1) All the members of the Police shall use, as the official arm, the revolver which the Superintendent may assign him. This revolver shall at all times be carried in its holster and duly fastened. (2) All the members of the Police on duty shall at least carry 

12 bullets. The use of a multiloader is hereby authorized.

The use of blackjacks is hereby authorized for all members of the Police. (c) Miscellaneous equipment. The members of the Police, other than officers, shall use as equipment, apart from the official revolver and ammunition, a whistle to give alarm and signals, a leather belt, a night stick, a cord and black shoulder belt, a small memo notebook and any other arm which the Superintendent may assign him. § 221d-124. General provisions as to uniform, insignia, arms and equipment. (a) Whenever the policeman is on duty, he shall use his whole uniform, except when a special duty is entrusted to him by his immediate supervisor, for the performance of which it should be necessary not to wear the uniform. (b) All the members of the Police are hereby prohibited, whenever they are on authorized leaves, to wear isolated pieces of the uniform. (c) Every member of the Police shall keep his uniform clean and well pressed. (d) All the members of the Police shall only use the official arm assigned to him by the Superintendent. The use of an arm other than the one assigned to him is hereby strictly prohibited. 

SECTIONS SUBDIVISION 10. WORKING PERIOD 

221d-131. Weekly working period 

221d-132. Duty to work in excess of the legal working period 

§ 221d-131. Weekly working period 

The legal working period for the members of the Police shall consist of 8 hours per day and not in excess of 48 hours per week. § 221d-132. Duty to work in excess of the legal working period (a) The members of the Police shall be bound to work in excess of the working period or legal workweek in the cases hereinafter provided: 

Aug. 31, 1968 

Vol. 7, No. 8 242.11

T.§ 221d-132 

INTERNAL SECURITY 

Ch. 21 (1) In the case of force majeure or emergency, such as earthquakes, fires, floods, hurricanes, elections, riots or strikes, and in any other case so declared by the Governor. (2) When the needs of the service as hereinafter mentioned demand so: (A) When, as prescribed by law, the members of the Force are to interfere with an offender, or to prevent the commitment of a crime or to fulfill a mission, even if their working period has been completed and they are off duty. 

(B) Capture of fugitives. 

(C) Police missions in which the continuity of the work being performed by the member or members of the Force is indispensable to carry out the mission. (b) In all cases in which a member of the Force has worked in excess of the established working period or legal workweek, he shall be entitled to compensatory leave at the rate of one day for each 8 extra hours worked. 

Compensatory leave shall be granted in the nearest possible date within the year following the accumulation of same, and if the service conditions permit so. However, compensatory leave shall in no case be granted in excess of 30 days during any calendar year. 

The officers shall take the necessary measures in order to avoid serving extra time that will result in the accumulation of compensatory leave in excess of 30 days. Besides, the necessary measures shall be taken in order that the members of the Force may be able to enjoy the compensatory leave within the year following the accumulation of such leave, inasmuch as compensatory leave cannot be accumulated for more than one year. (c) The members of the Force shall at all times keep their conditions as such, for all legal purposes and they are subject to all the provisions of law and of regulations, no matter where they may be during off duty periods, within the jurisdiction of the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico, with all the duties and prerrogatives which as such members of the Police they may have by law.

Effectiveness § 221d-141. Power to adopt manuals of procedure, instructions and administrative orders The Superintendent of the Police is hereby authorized to provide, organize, order, regulate and control the preparation of manuals of procedure, instructions and administrative orders, in order to develop the administrative policy as well as any other matter necessary for the best and efficient operation of the Police. § 221d-142. Joining or affiliating with labor organizations; scope of the prohibition

The joining and affiliation of the members of the Police of Puerto Rico to any organization of a labor union character is hereby prohibited; Provided, however, That this prohibition has not the scope to proscribe the affiliation or membership of the members of the Force in entities connected with their profession, organized for legal purposes, if such entities are not of a labor union nature. § 221d-143. Power to modify or amend this division 

The Superintendent of the Police, by virtue of the authority conferred upon him by law, hereby reserves his right to modify or amend in any sense this division as he deems it proper for the best interests of Puerto Rico and subject to the approval by the 

Governor of Puerto Rico. 

§ 221d-144. Separability clause 

The provisions of this division are separate. So, if any provision, clause, paragraph, article, rule, section or part of this division or its application to any person or circumstance were challenged or declared unconstitutional or null, such decision or nullity shall in no way affect the other provisions, but its effect shall be limited to the provision, clause, paragraph, article, section or part of this division so declared unconstitutional. 

§ 221d-145. Effectiveness 

This division shall take effect and shall have force of law immediately after its approval by the Governor and filing in the Office of the Secretary of State, pursuant to the provisions of Act

§ 221j-1. Terms and definitions 

The meaning of terms not defined in this subchapter shall be exactly the same as that of terms employed in Act No. 77, approved the 22nd of June, 1956 [25 L.P.R.A. §§ 221 to 221t]. 

"Law" means Act No. 77, approved the 22nd of June, 1956 [25

L.P.R.A. §§ 221 to 221t]. 

"Commission" means Police Commission. 

"Chairman" means Chairman of the Commission. 

"Superintendent" means Superintendent of the Police. "Member" means any member of the Commission. "Secretary" means Secretary to the Commission or that person duly authorized to act as such in his place. "Secretaryship" means the secretaryship of the Commission. "Appellant" means members of the Force who appear on appeal before the Commission. “Hearing” or “public hearing" means audience before the Commission or before any of its members for the purpose of acting upon appeals by members of the Force.

 § 221j-2. Organization of the Commission 

(a) The Commission's offices shall be located in the City of San Juan, Puerto Rico, but the Commission or any of its members designated by the Chairman may hold sessions any other place on the Island if it becomes necessary. (b) All correspondence for the Commission should be addressed to: Police Commission, San Juan, Puerto Rico. Attention of the Secretary. 

(c) The Commission, or any if its members designated by the Chairman, shall hold public hearings, hearings, or sessions as many times as may be necessary for performing those duties with which they are vested by the Law, at its offices in San Juan as well as any other place on the Island. 

§ 221j-3. Duties and attributes of the Chairman (a) The Chairman shall designate one of the Commissioners to fulfill the duties as Acting Chairman when the former shall be absent.

Ch. 

T.25 § 221j-4 (b) The Chairman shall be the executive officer of the Commission and as such shall supervise all work connected with matters before the same, and shall represent this entity during official activities, or may delegate such representation to any other of its members, as well as to the Secretary. (c) The Chairman, acting on his own initiative, and upon the request of any member of the Commission or interested party, may suspend any session of the Commission. (d) The Chairman of the Commission shall assign the necessary personnel to carry out the work of the Commission. (e) Any member of the Commission, having a complaint against any one or more of the employees thereof, may file said complaint with the Chairman, who shall be invested with the duty of convening the Commission in full for the purpose of hearing and acting on said charges, but the same may be examined and acted upon by a majority of the Commission which shall consist of three members present. 

§ 221j-4. Appeals 

(a) Any member of the Force affected by a decision of the Superintendent may appeal to the Commission within a period of 10 days from the day on which notice was served of an action subject to appeal. (b) An appeal shall be established through the filing with the 

Secretary of a written appeal by the injured party. An appeal shall be considered filed on time, if, on the date on which same is filed with the Secretary, or was deposited in the post office, according to the date of the postmark, there has not expired a 10-day period since the subject of the appeal was notified of the punishment or decision; provided, that the 10 days which the affected party has for appealing from the decision of the Superintendent shall be counted from the date on which he was notified by the Superintendent of the Police or by the district commander where he lives, either directly or through a duly authorized representative of either of these. (c) If it is not possible to notify the affected party personally of the decision of the Superintendent, the same shall be served by leaving a copy thereof at his home or usual place of residence, said notice being delivered to a person of sufficient age and discretion, residing thereat. The date, hour, and place of delivery shall be made a matter of record by the person delivering the notice. 243

T.§ 221j-4 Ch. 21 

INTERNAL SECURITY 

(d) For the purpose of compliance with the preceding provisions of this section, in all cases where a member of the Force is notified of the resolution of the Superintendent which may be the object of an appeal before the Commission, the Superintendent, or his duly authorized representative, shall furnish the Secretary of the Commission with a certificate, wherein there shall appear the date, hour, and place of delivery of the notice, as the case may be. (e) The Superintendent, within 10 days after being notified of an appeal by the Secretary of the Commission, shall submit the whole history of the case to the Commission. (f) The Superintendent may appear in person or designate any other officer to represent him at the hearing of cases before the Commission in the discretion of the Commission, unless his presence is strictly necessary. (g) All appellants shall furnish the Superintendent with a copy of the written appeal filed by him or his lawyer with the Commission. (h) The Secretary shall establish and maintain a registry of appeals wherein every case shall be entered in chronological order immediately upon the receipt of the written appeal. (i) The Secretary shall note on the written appeal the date and hour of receipt of same, and shall immediately proceed to register same in the registry of appeals. 

§ 221j-5. Date for public hearing 

(a) In setting dates for public hearings, the Commission shall follow the order in which the cases were filed, but cases may be called for hearing without necessarily following this restriction, when in the opinion of the Commission there are special circumstances which so justify. (b) If the appellant is interested in suspension of any hearing already set, he may file with the Secretary a request to that effect at least 48 hours before the date set for the hearing. The appellant shall appear before the Commission on the date and hour set for the holding of same, unless he shall have received advance notice from the Commission to the effect that suspension of the case has been granted. 

§ 221j-6. Citations 

(a) Citations to compel the appearance of witnesses shall be issued by the Secretary under the official seal of the Commission. 244

Ch. 

T.25 § 221j-7 (b) When one of the parties involved can satisfactorily justify before the Commission that the witnesses to be used by him in a case should be notified through the Commission, he shall submit a written request no less than 5 days prior to the date fixed for the hearing, specifying the exact name and address of each witness to be summoned, although their nonappearance would not be a reason for the suspension of the case set for hearing. (c) Parties concerned may present at any public hearing, at the opening of the case, all witnesses they please although they have not been summoned by the Commission. (d) The Commission may reject irrelevant testimonies or summon witnesses whose testimony it may consider pertinent, although these may not have been offered or requested by the parties involved in the case. It may also order or require the furnishing of any documents necessary to the case in question. (e) Citations may be expedited through the Superintendent of the Police, or through any other channels which the Commission may deem adequate. 

§ 221j-7. Public hearings 

(a) All hearings shall be public, together with testimony of all parties concerned, a stenographic record being taken of the full history of all cases considered. (b) When an appellant fails to appear in person, or through his attorney, at any hearing, and from the file of the case it appears that the appellant and his attorney were duly notified of the hearing, or that neither of them was located, the hearing may be held in their absence. In such a case the Superintendent or his representative may introduce evidence to uphold his decision appealed from. (c) In appeal cases referred to in paragraph (b) of sec. 6 of the Law [25 L.P.R.A. § 221e], that is to say, dismissals which it is alleged were the result of political, religious, or racial reasons, the same rules shall be applied, insofar as possible, as those established for appeals in general. (d) The Commission shall hold sessions and hearings in cases of appeal as often as it becomes necessary to hear cases on schedule, and these sessions or hearings shall be set by the Chairman, but on one day a week, ordinary sessions shall be held unless previously cancelled or suspended by the Chairman, for justifiable reasons. 245

T.§ 221j-7 Ch. 21 

INTERNAL SECURITY 

(e) Rules of evidence before courts of law shall not be enforced in any case whatsoever before the Commission. (f) For the observance of order and security during hearings before the Commission, all defendants as well as witnesses, members of the Force, shall bear no arms whatsoever. The Marshal shall see to it that this rule is complied with. 

§ 221j-8. Duties and attributes of the Secretary 

(a) The Secretary shall be the executive officer of the Commission, and as such shall be the legal custodian of all documents, records, and property relative to the Commission, and all resolutions, records of proceedings, and agreements shall be certified by him. (b) He shall prepare all schedules of cases before the Commission and shall notify dates of hearings in accord with the Chairman. (c) He shall issue citations to witnesses and see to it that they are served. (d) He shall certify as to the appearance of witnesses for the payment of per diems and mileage. (e) He shall report on all decisions and resolutions of the Commission; shall prepare a record of each and every hearing; and can also issue certificates regarding decisions and resolutions of the Commission. (f) He shall act as liaison officer between the Commission and the heads and employees of the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico, and between the Commission and the public in general. 

§ 221j-9. Amendments; separability 

Any section or paragraph of this subchapter may be amended or repealed and additional rules may be adopted following provisions set forth in sec. 11(b) of the Law [25 L.P.R.A. § 221j]; it being resolved that if any clause, paragraph, article, section, or part of this subchapter be declared unconstitutional by a court of competent jurisdiction, said decision shall in no way affect, hinder, or invalidate the rest of this subchapter, but its effect shall be limited only to the clause, paragraph, article, section, or part of this subchapter which has thereby been declared unconstitutional. § 221j-10. § 222b-1. Definitions 

When used with the context of this subchapter the terms listed below will mean the following: 

(1) "The Law"-Public Law No. 88 of May 31, 1967 [25 L.P.R.A. §§ 222 to 222c]. 

(2) "Secretary"-The Secretary of the Treasury of the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico. 

(3) "Superintendent"-The Superintendent of the Puerto Rico Police. 

(4) "Personal property”—All personal property which the Police may have taken possesion of as a result of their official functions, 

(A) Fire arms. 

(B) Stolen, robbed or swindled property connected with criminal actions pending in courts. (C) Property retained by reason of the investigation of the commission of an offense. (D) Personal property whose disposal has already been provided through another legislation. (5) "Center or centers-Localities or places where the personal property referred to in the Law is deposited for examination by the interested parties.

§ 222b-2. Center designation 

The Superintendent will establish deposit centers in those local police headquarters designated by him, wherein the property deposited will be available for examination by interested persons. Among other factors that should be considered to designate these centers are the following: amount of personal property to be deposited; the origin or place where the Police acquired possession of the property; existing physical and environmental facilities to insure that the largest number of persons may have access to the centers. 

§ 222b-3. Personal property registry 

In each center a registration book shall be kept with the following information: (1) Description of the property therein deposited. (2) Date in which the Police took possession of the property. (3) Place and circumstances under which the Police acquired possession of the property. (4) Any other information that in the Superintendent's judgement may be necessary to implement the Law. 

§ 222b-4. Operation of centers 

The Superintendent will determine the days and hours when these centers will be in operation, considering the public needs and the facilities in each center. 

§ 222b-5. Public information 

(a) The Superintendent will publish a public notice, once every 6 months, in 2 newspapers of general circulation in Puerto Rico, informing the public the location of the centers wherein personal property is deposited for public examination. (b) Likewise, the Superintendent, in coordination with the Municipal authorities shall post on the Bulletin Board of each municipality wherein a deposit center is located, a general list of the personal property under the custody of the Police. June 30, 1968 

Vol. 7, No. 6 

246.2

Ch. 

T.25 § 222b-8 

§ 222b-6. Procedure to claim personal property 

(a) All claims of personal property will be made directly to the Superintendent in a special form to be designed for that purpose. (b) This form shall be filled in by the person who claims to be the legitimate owner of the claimed property, or by his legally authorized representative. In the case of a deceased presumed owner, the application may be filled in by the administrator or the executor that may have been appointed. If either has not been appointed, the application may be filled in by the heirs of the deceased. (c) The information given in this form shall be duly sworn, and should include all documentary evidence or genuine proof which may credit the claimant as the legitimate owner of the claimed property. (d) Once the legitimate ownership of the personal property has been verified, the Superintendent shall deliver it to the claimant and shall demand a receipt. § 222b-7. Personal property delivered to a person who is not its legitimate owner

When the Superintendent knows of a person who has claimed and obtained personal property, not being its legitimate owner he will take all the necessary action towards the indictment of such person. 

§ 222b-8. Delivery of personal property to the secretary 

(a) After a lapse of one (1) year from the date the Police took possession of the personal property, and if no claim has been filed, the Superintendent will prepare a list of that personal property and will deliver it to the Secretary. (b) Personal property object of an administrative or judicial claim will remain under the custody of the Superintendent until the claim or litigation has been definitely resolved. (c) Perishable personal property of limited durability shall be delivered to the Secretary any moment after the Police acquired its possession and after the Superintendent has tried by all reasonable means to find its owners, with negative results. INTERNAL SECURITY § 2850-2. Authority and effectiveness 

The provisions of this subchapter are promulgated pursuant to secs. 4, 16, 23, 24, 28 and 32 of Act No. 108, of June 29, 1965 [25 

L.P.R.A. §§ 285c, 285o, 285v, 285w, 286 and 286d], and shall take legal effect after their approval by the Governor and their publication as provided by the "Regulations Act of Puerto Rico" [3 

L.P.R.A. § 1041 et seq.]. 

§ 2850-3. Applicability 

None of the provisions of this subchapter shall be applicable to private detectives nor to private detective agencies nor to safety agencies when they are rendering services for public purposes and for the benefit of the United States of America, the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico or any of the municipal governments of Puerto Rico, or of any political subdivision or public corporation thereof. 

None of the provisions of this subchapter shall be applicable to detectives or agents of the Puerto Rico Police, appointed under the law [25 L.P.R.A. § 221 et seq.], nor to any person employed by the 

Police of Puerto Rico while in the discharge of his official duties; nor to any magistrate or attorney in the practice of his profession; nor to any person engaged in furnishing information as to the business, financial condition and credit of natural or artificial persons; nor to any person who investigates by himself any matter in which said person is an interested party; nor to public insurance adjusters, watchmen or night watchmen who, in their individual capacity, are engaged in such trades or occupations in private enterprises or in public, industrial, commercial or agricultural establishments. § 2850-4. Compliance with statutory provisions

Since it appears that the practice of the profession of private detective and the services rendered by private detective agencies and safety agencies, when duly regulated as provided by Act No. 

108 [25 L.P.R.A. § 285 et seq.] and this subchapter, are a valuable contribution to promoting the general welfare, the peace and order in the Puerto Rican community, the Superintendent of Police shall discharge his responsibilities under Act No. 108 and this subchapter, overseeing the compliance with the provisions of law and of this subchapter, and harmonizing the public interest with the interests of private detectives, private detective agencies and safety agencies. Revocation and refusal to renew; review § 2850-21. Applications; requirements

All applications for licenses to practice the profession of private detective and to operate a private detective agency or a safety agency shall be filed with the Superintendent of Police, in writing, in the printed forms supplied to that effect by the Superintendent. 

Each application shall be accompanied by sufficient demonstrative proof that the applicant meets all the requirements established by Act No. 108 and this subchapter. Each application shall, furthermore, be subscribed and sworn to by the applicant. § 2850-22. Verification; denial

After the application for license has been filed, using the printed form prescribed by the preceding section, the Superintendent shall verify that the same complies with all the requirements established by Act No. 108 and this subchapter, and shall require, furthermore, compliance, to his satisfaction, with any condition subsequent to the filing of the petition as may be required by Act No. 108 and this subchapter, for the granting of the license being applied for. After verifying that the application complies with all the requirements and conditions prescribed by Act No. 108 and this subchapter, the 

Superintendent of Police shall issue the corresponding license to the petitioner. The Superintendent shall not deny an application for license without first granting the interested party the opportunity of a hearing where said party shall have the opportunity of appearing and presenting evidence, examining witnesses, and asserting his rights. In any case the Superintendent shall give notice to the interested party, in writing, of the grounds for his action or finding.

If the interested party has appeared at the above-mentioned hearing, and the Superintendent denies his petition for a license, said party may file a petition for review before the San Juan Part of the Superior Court of Puerto Rico, within the period established

§ 2850-23. Expiration and renewal 

All licenses issued shall expire on the 30th day of June of each year, and are renewable upon payment of a fee in the same amount as that paid for obtaining the original license. 

§ 2850-24. Identification card 

The Superintendent shall supply to every person to whom he grants a private detective license an identification card, renewable annually at the time the license is renewed, and its holder shall carry it with him at all times when acting as a private detective. 

Said identification card shall not be valid without the Superintendent's signature. 

§ 2850-25. Exhibition of license 

All private detectives and agencies shall keep their licenses in a visible place in their offices. § 2850-26. Revocation and refusal to renew; review

The Superintendent may revoke or refuse renewal of a license for any of the causes provided in sec. 17 of Act No. 108 [25 L.P.R.A. 

§ 285p]. The Superintendent's refusal to renew or his revocation of a license shall state the date on which the action is effective and shall be subject to the same procedure and opportunity for hearing, and appeal for review prescribed by sec. 2850-22 of this title on denial of an application for license. 

§ 2850-27. Applicable provisions 

Concerning applications for licenses from private detective schools, and all matters regarding said licenses, the provisions of secs. 22, 24, 25 and 26 of Act No. 108 [25 L.P.R.A. §§ 285u, 285w, 285x and 285y], shall be applicable.

§ 2850-41. Categories Pursuant to the provisions of sec. 2 of Act No. 108 [25 L.P.R.A. 

§ 285a], private detectives are classified in 3 different categories: (1) The private detective who conducts investigations or inquiries for the purpose of obtaining information on the various matters indicated in sec. 2(a) of Act No. 108. 

(2) The private detective who seeks or obtains evidence to be used in judicial or quasi-judicial proceedings, referred to in sec. 2(b) 

of Act No. 108. 

(3) The private detective who protects persons or property for the purpose of preventing the commission of the crimes mentioned in sec. 2(c) of Act No. 108. 

§ 2850-42. Requirements; proof of its compliance

Every person requesting a license as private detective, under any of the 3 aforementioned categories, shall prove, as provided in sec. 4 of Act No. 108 [25 L.P.R.A. § 285c], that he meets all of the 

(1) That he is of age. (2) That he is a citizen of the United States of America, and of the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico. The latter means having resided in Puerto Rico for at least one year immediately preceding his filing of an application.¹ (3) That he has not been convicted of a felony or misdemeanor involving moral turpitude. (4) That he is a person of excellent moral repute. No private detective license shall be granted to any person who is a habitual drunkard or mentally incompetent or a drug or narcotic addict, nor to any person who has been convicted of any offense related to drugs or narcotics. (5) That he has furnished the bond provided by sec. 7 of Act No. 

108 [25 L.P.R.A. § 285f]. 

(6) That he has paid the license fee provided by section 12 of 

Act No. 108 [25 L.P.R.A. § 285k]. 

(7) That he has filed his fingerprints with the Superintendent. (8) That he is not holding any public office or employment of any sort, with or without pay, in the Government of the Common-

§ 2850-43. Other requirements 

In addition to evidencing compliance with the requirements and conditions stated in the preceding section, private detectives, in order to obtain a license as such, shall: (1) Have successfully completed a course of study in a private detective school authorized by the Superintendent of Police. The course of study shall contain a minimum of 1,000 hours of study, and competent professional practice, in accordance with the following determinations: (A) In the case of private detectives mentioned in sec. 

2850-41(1) of this title, 500 hours of study and 500 hours of competent professional practice shall be required. (B) In the case of private detectives mentioned in sec. 

2850-41(2) of this title, 500 hours of study and 500 hours of competent professional practice shall be required. (C) In the case of private detectives mentioned in sec. 

2850-41 (3) of this title, 100 hours of study and 900 hours of competent professional practice shall be required. (2) To have passed a written examination prepared by the Superintendent, for the purpose of ascertaining the applicant's knowledge of those matters reasonably related to those functions he will have to fulfill. When preparing the examinations for each of the private detective categories, the Superintendent shall bear in mind that said functions to be fulfilled are different for each of such categories. (3) To have observed good behavior and reputation in the past, as evidenced by such investigations as, for said purpose, the Superintendent may carry out, pursuant to the provisions of subd. (4) of sec. 15 of Act No. 108 [25 L.P.R.A. § 285c]. To facilitate these investigations, every applicant shall, upon filing his petition, authorize the Superintendent of Police to make efforts, on behalf of the petitioner, for obtaining from any private institution, official agency of the Government of Puerto Rico and the Federal Government, including the Armed Forces, pertinent information about the applicant, comprising his work, medical and scholastic history, and any other information as may appear in the files of said agencies and institutions with reference to the applicant. The information thus obtained shall be used by the Superintendent solely for official purposes.

Ch. T.25 § 2850-61 

PRIVATE DETECTIVES 

§ 2850-44. Disclosure of information, prohibition

No person who is or has been a private detective, or an employee of a private detective, shall disclose privately or publicly any information obtained by him in the course of his employment, without the previous express written consent of the person who contracted for his services, excepting such information connected with the commission of public offenses and those other instances where he is required by law to do so. Every private detective, in his capacity as employer, shall strictly comply with the obligation imposed upon him by the second paragraph of sec. 18 of Act No. 108 [25 L.P.R.A. 

§ 285q]. 

SECTIONS 

§ 2850-45. Private detectives not residing in Puerto Rico

The Superintendent may authorize any private detective not residing in Puerto Rico, accredited as a private detective authorized to practice his profession anywhere in the United States of America, temporarily to engage in the practice of said profession in Puerto Rico, without the payment of any fee, for the sole purpose of discharging a specific mission.

DIVISION 4. AGENCIES 

2850-61. Classes 2850-62. Requirements 2850-63. Employees § 2850-61. Classes 

Pursuant to the provisions of Act No. 108 and of this subchapter, two classes of agencies are established: (1) The private detective agency, which refers to any person, natural or artificial, engaged in the practice of the profession of private detective and employing one or more persons for such purpose. (2) The Safety Agency for the protection of private enterprises, which refers to any person, natural or artificial, specially engaged in the rendering of custodial services or in the protection of private property in industrial, commercial or business establishments, or in those establishments connected with the development of agricultural enterprises, and employing one or more persons for such purposes. T.§ 2850-62 Ch. 27 

INTERNAL SECURITY § 2850-62. Requirements 

Every agency requesting a license under either of the hereinabove mentioned two categories shall comply with one or both of the 

(1) That one or more private detectives with licenses granted thereto by the Superintendent, under Act No. 108, request the agency. (2) That said license is requested by a corporation duly organized, according to its certificate of incorporation, to operate private detectives or safety agency, or both, provided its principal executive officer in Puerto Rico is a private detective with a license granted thereto by the Superintendent, under Act No. 108.

SECTIONS § 2850-63. Employees 

Every agency holding a license for any of the two categories indicated in sec. 2850-61 of this title, may employ such persons as are necessary for its operation. Any person so employed shall not have to hold a license as private detective but shall not, without said license, be authorized to act as private detective.

The Superintendent hereby establishes, pursuant to the provi sions of sec. 23 of Act No. 108 [25 L.P.R.A. § 285v] and of this subchapter, the following requirements and conditions for the operation of private detective schools: (1) To offer separate and distinct programs of study, one of them directed to the preparation of the private detectives in categories (1) and (2) of sec. 2850-41 of this title, and another to the preparation of private detectives according to category (3) of sec. 2850-41 of this title. T.25 § 2850-82 (3) The required subjects referred to by the prior subdivision will cover basic knowledge of the following matters: (A) Civil rights guaranteed by the various constitutional and legislative provisions in force in Puerto Rico. (B) Rules of Evidence, as concerns the Courts' nonadmission of evidence. (C) Criminal Law, particularly as concerns the constituent elements of the various public offenses in Puerto Rico. (D) Rules of Criminal Procedure, particularly as concerns those situations where a private person may perform an arrest in 

Puerto Rico. 

(E) Scope of the legal concept of self-defense and of the legal concept of the excessive use of force. (F) Situations where private detectives, or any private person, are required to advise the Police of Puerto Rico on any information they may obtain. (G) Methods to be followed so as to preserve all the evidence as may be useful in solving a crime. (H) Duty of every citizen, and very specially, of private detectives, to assist in the maintenance of public order and the proper administration of justice. (4) The program of study for private detectives in category (3) of sec. 2850-41 of this title shall be approved by the Superintendent and shall consist of at least 100 hours of study and 900 hours of competent professional practice and shall contain basic knowledge of the following matters: (A) The most efficient fire-control methods and what to do so that a fire will not spread unnecessarily. (B) Duty and way of notifying the proper authorities of any developing situation demanding the intervention of government entities (i.e., fires, thefts, acts of violence). (C) Scope of the legal concept of self-defense and of the legal concept of the excessive use of force. (D) Situations where a private person may perform an arrest in Puerto Rico. (E) Methods to be followed so as to preserve all the evidence as may be useful in solving a crime. § 2850-82. Accreditation of courses of other schools

The provisions governing private detective schools contained in Act No. 108 and in this subchapter shall not apply to public or private schools accredited by the Department of Education that offer in their curriculum courses for teaching and training private detectives.

PART III. FIRE PROTECTION Chapter 31. Puerto Rico Fire Service Subchapter 314. Fire Prevention; Safety Regulations DIVISION 1. THEATRES SECTIONS 314 1. Definitions

General rules 

§ 314-1. Definitions 

Unless otherwise specified in this subchapter, the following words herein contained shall be understood to mean as follows: (1) "Theatre" means any building or part of any building used regularly or frequently as a place of assembly for the purpose of presenting shows, dramatic performances, opera, moving pictures, vaudeville shows, lectures, or any other performances, exhibitions, or shows, be they free or by paid admission. (2) "Orchestra" comprises the area of the main floor of the theatre containing orchestra seats, except the portion of the floor containing box seats. (3) "Balcony" includes the rows of seats located over the main floor and which are not part of the rear balcony. (4) "Boxes" are separate compartments with railing, located around the orchestra or balcony. (5) "Rear balcony" is the top of the theatre and includes all rows of seats located behind or at the sides of the balcony. (6) "Stage" means the part of the theatre adequately built and provided for the purpose of placing the scenery and curtains thereon and for enacting or presenting dramas or any other kind of theatrical works. (7) "Main floor" means the first or main rows of the auditorium. (8) "Lounge" comprises the space between the lobby and the corridor, when such a space has been provided, or between the lobby and the main floor. 249 [T.25]

T.§ 314-1 Ch. 31 

INTERNAL SECURITY 

(9) "Lobby" means an enclosed vestibule directly accessible from the main entrance. (10) "Corridor" means the space between the lounge and the rear seats of the main floor, or the space behind the last row of the rear balcony. (11) "Section" consists of one or more rows of seats, said section being located one above the other like the main floor, the mezzanine, the balcony and gallery. (12) "Exit doorways" includes all doors leading from any floor of the building to the outside, either to a street or an open courtyard. (13) "Courtyard” means an open space, vacant, and completely open to the air, which forms and is used as a part of the theatre, and which has free and rapid access to the outside. (14) "Exit" means any means of egress from any theatre floor to the street. The width of an exit shall be the minimum width of any door, opening, stair, or corridor at its narrowest point, free from obstruction. (15) "Owner", for all legal purposes, shall be understood to be the person who as proprietor owns a building or part of same used as a theatre, likewise including the lessee, producer, administrator, or whoever may act as representative. (16) "Aisle" comprises the space between sections of rows of seats or between these and the walls, and are used to make different places accessible to the occupants.

Insular Fire Chief, have been adopted in accordance with_the provisions of Law No. 158, approved May 9, 1942 [25 L.P.R.A. 

§ 311 et seq.], and as amended and approved by the Honorable Governor of Puerto Rico, Rexford G. Tugwell, May 10, 1946, are hereby promulgated for the knowledge of all concerned. "Among the powers conferred on the Insular Fire Chief of

"Complying with said authority conferred by law, the undersigned Insular Fire Chief has redacted the following regulations, keeping in mind uppermost the urgent necessity to reduce to a minimum the fires which have brought so much ruin and desolation to Puerto Rico. "These regulations are the result of a careful study of those safety measures recommended and adopted by private organizations and governmental institutions in the United States of America, adapted to the convenience and needs of our Island. The result of their application will serve as a guide for future modifications. "With the cooperation of the owners of these establishments, or the persons managing them, as well as with the cooperation of the general public in the observance of these regulations, it will be possible to attain a high degree of safety throughout the Island. These are our hopes and expectations."

§ 314-2. Entrances 

The space for the entrances to the theatres shall have a width of not less than 20 inches for every 100 persons to be accommodated. 

Moreover, one foot shall be added for easy access. If the theatre has only one entrance door, this shall be not less than 6 feet wide and shall open in an outward direction. 

§ 314-3. Seats 

(a) The seats shall be located not less than 2 feet 6 inches from back to back measured in a horizontal direction. (b) The minimum width of the seats shall be not less than 18 inches measured from the center of the armrests. If benches are used, the seating capacity shall be determined in the proportion of one seat for every 18 inches of length. (c) All seats, chairs, or benches, except the box seats, shall be firmly fixed to the floor. (d) No seat shall have more than six seats intervening between it and the nearest aisle. 251

T.§ 314-4 Ch. 31 

INTERNAL SECURITY § 314-4. Aisles 

(a) The aisles shall have a width of not less than 1 foot 8 inches for every 100 persons using them, plus an additional foot for easy passage through same, but no aisle shall have a width of less than 

2 feet 6 inches. (b) The aisles shall be kept unobstructed and no person shall be allowed to place a seat or any other obstruction, nor stand, in said aisles during a performance. 

§ 314-5. Stairs 

(a) Stairways shall be provided on the basis of 22 inches of stairway width for every 100 persons accommodated. (b) The tread of the stair steps shall be not more than 10 inches and the riser not more than 8 inches. (c) All staircases shall have a handrail not less than 30 inches high. (d) Circular staircases of triangle-shaped steps are not permitted. (e) Outside fire escapes shall be constructed of forged iron, steel, reenforced concrete, or any other fireproof material. Frame buildings may have outside stairs of the same material. 

§ 314-6. Exit doorways 

(a) Exit doorways shall open in an outward direction and shall be located in such a way that the required width for exit corridors will not be reduced. (b) Revolving doors are prohibited. (c) No doorway (window or any other opening) on any floor to be used by the public may be obstructed by metal bars, chains, iron grates, or screens. 

§ 314-7. Exits 

(a) In the main floor and balcony there shall be at least 2 exit doors, each 44 inches wide, for a capacity of 200 or less. Additional exits shall be on the basis of 22 inches of width for every 100 persons. (b) The exit doors shall open outwards and shall be equipped with automatic-release bolts which will open the doors in the same outward direction when a 15-pound pressure is applied. These devices may consist of bars or panes extending not less than twothirds of the door's width and should be placed at a convenient 252

Ch. 

T.25 § 314-8 height, usually not less than 30 nor more than 40 inches about floor level. (c) The use of latches, bars, bolts, or any other kind of lock on exit doors, during performances, is absolutely prohibited. (d) All exit doors shall have an electric sign installed in a circuit independently of the general circuit, with the word "EXIT” in letters not less than 6 inches high, and these shall be illuminated by red bulbs during the performance. 

§ 314-8. Projection rooms 

(a) The projection room, including the floor, shall be constructed of a fireproof material. (b) The projection room's doors shall open outwards. (c) The projection windows shall be equipped with a device which closes automatically in case of a firebreak, thereby preventing the public from becoming aware of said firebreak. (d) No articles of combustible materials shall be allowed in the projection room with the exception of the films being projected. (e) The films which are not in use shall be kept in an approved fireproof lidded box. (f) Smoking inside the projection room is absolutely prohibited and a sign reading "SMOKING PROHIBITED” shall be conspicuously placed. (g) A fireproof container shall be provided for pieces of film and other rubbish, and these shall be kept at all times in the container until they are removed from the building. 

(h) The dimensions of the projection room shall be as follows: 

(1) With only 1 projector, the room shall be at least 6 feet long by 6 feet wide and 7 feet high. (2) With 2 projectors, the room shall be at least 9 feet long by 9 feet wide and 7 feet high. (3) With 3 projectors, the room shall be at least 12 feet long by 12 feet wide and 7 feet high. (i) The projection room shall be provided with ventilators having an exhaust capacity of not less than 15 cubic feet nor more than 50 cubic feet per minute for each lamp plus 200 cubic feet per minute for the room itself. The ventilators shall be installed directly above the projector or projectors and in direct contact with fresh air and shall be made of fireproof material. Besides these ventilators, the projection room shall also have other means of ventilation. 253

T.§ 314-8 Ch. 31 

INTERNAL SECURITY 

The projection room door shall be self-closing. (j) Two fire extinguishers of a type approved by the Fire Chief shall be installed in accessible and visible places and where they can be easily reached by the operator. They shall be kept in good working condition and recharged at least once a year and shall have a card attached indicating when and by whom they were recharged. (k) A flue to carry the hot air outside the building shall be installed over each projector. (1) A separate fireproof room, directly connected with the projection room by doors, shall be constructed to be used for winding and unwinding films. This room shall lead to the corridors or to the outside of the building. 

§ 314-9. Stage 

(a) The theatre's stages, except those used exclusively for moving pictures, shall have two exit doors separated by a certain distance. (b) On each side of the stage and in accessible places, a 212gallon extinguisher of an approved type shall be placed and shall be kept in good working condition and recharged at least once a year and shall have a card attached indicating when and by whom they were recharged. 

§ 314-10. Electric installations (a) Installation. The wiring method shall be metal conduit or other approved metal raceway system. The number of conductors permitted in any conduit or electrical metallic tubing, for border or stage pocket circuits, shall not exceed that permitted by the National Electric Code. Portable cables or flexible cords may be used on the stage or elsewhere whenever fixed wiring methods are impracticable. (b) Stage switchboard. (1) Dead front. Stage switchboards shall be of the dead-front type. (2) Guarding. Stage switchboards having exposed live parts on the back of such boards shall be enclosed by the building walls, wire mesh grills, or by other approved methods. The entrance to this enclosure shall be by means of a self-closing door. (3) Control and overcurrent protection of receptacle circuits. 

Means shall be provided at the stage switchboard for the control 254

Ch. 

T.25 § 314-10 and individual overcurrent protection of branch circuits to stage and gallery receptacles. (4) Metal hood. The stage switchboard shall be provided with a metal hood extending the full length of the board to protect all equipment on the board from falling objects. (5) Dimmers. Dimmers shall conform to the following: (A) A dimmer shall be disconnected from all ungrounded supply conductors when the switch or circuit breaker, controlling the supply, is open. (B) Resistance or series reactor type dimmers may be placed in either leg of the circuit. If designed to open either the supply circuit to the dimmer or the circuit controlled by it, the dimmer shall then comply with the requirements of the National 

Electric Code. 

It is recommended that resistance or reactor type dimmers be placed in the grounded neutral conductor of the circuit provided they do not open the circuit. (C) An auto-transformer type dimmer shall be energized by a circuit operating at not more than 150 volts between conductors, and one conductor shall be connected to the required identified grounded conductor of the wiring system. (c) Stage equipment; fixed. (1) Circuit loads. Footlights, border lights, and proscenium side lights shall be so arranged that no branch circuit supplying such equipment will carry a load exceeding 15 amperes; provided, that where heavy-duty lampholders only are used for border lights, such circuits may conform to the provisions of the National Electric Code for circuits supplying heavy-duty lampholders. (2) Footlights. If the metal trough construction is not used, footlights shall consist of individual outlets with lampholders, wired with rigid or flexible metal conduit. The circuit conductors shall be soldered to the lampholder terminals. Disappearing footlights shall be so arranged that the current supply shall be automatically disconnected when the footlights are replaced in the recess designed therefor. (3) Cables for border lights. Cables for border lights shall be

Type K or Type S flexible cord. The cables shall be suitably sup ported. Such cables shall be employed only where flexible conductors are necessary. (4) Receptacles. Receptacles intended for the connection of arc lamps shall have not less than 35 amperes capacity and shall 255

T.§ 314-10 

INTERNAL SECURITY 

Ch. 31 be supplied by conductors not smaller than No. 6. Receptacles intended for the connection of incandescent lamps shall have not less than 15 amperes capacity and shall be supplied by conductors not smaller than No. 12. Plugs for arc and incandescent receptacles shall not be interchangeable. (5) Lamps in scene docks. Lamps installed in scene docks shall be so located and guarded as to be free from mechanical injury and so as to provide an air space of not less than 2 inches between such lamps and any combustible material. (6) Flue-damper control. If stage flue dampers are released by an electrical device, the circuit operating the latter shall be normally closed and shall be controlled by at least 2 single-pole switches enclosed in iron boxes having self-closing doors without locks or latches, one switch being placed at the electrician's station and the other where designated by the inspection authority. The device shall be designed for the full voltage of the circuit to which it is connected, no resistance being inserted. It shall be located in the loft above the scenery and shall be enclosed in a suitable iron box having a tight, self-closing door. (d) Stage equipment; portable. (1) Arc lamps. Arc-lamp frames and standards shall be so installed and guarded as to prevent their becoming grounded. A qualified operator shall be employed for each lamp, or for each 2 lamps not more than 10 feet apart and so placed that one operator can properly watch and care for both. (2) Lights on scenery. Brackets on scenery shall be wired internally and the fixture stem shall be carried through to the back of the scenery where a bushing shall be placed on the end of the stem, except that externally wired brackets or other fixtures may be used when wired with Type P or other cords designed for hard usage which shall extend without joint or splice through the scenery, and terminate in an approved type stage connector located within 1 inch of the fixture. Fixtures shall be securely fastened in place. (3) Festoons. Joints in festoon wiring shall be staggered where practicable. Lamps enclosed in lanterns or similar devices of combustible material shall be equipped with approved guards. 

(4) Special effects. Electrical devices used for simulating lightning, waterfalls, and the like, shall be so constructed and located that flames, sparks, or hot particles cannot come in contact with combustible material. 256

Ch. 

T.25 § 314-10 (5) Connectors for flexible conductors. Connectors for flexible conductors shall be so constructed that tension on the cord or cable will not be transmitted to the connections. The female half of the connector shall be attached to the live end of the cord or cable. (6) Conductors for portables. Flexible conductors used to sup ply portable stage equipment shall be Type K or Type S cord, except that reinforced cord may be used to supply stand lamps if the cord is not exposed to severe mechanical injury and is protected by a fuse of not over 15 amperes. (e) Dressing rooms. (1) Hanging lamps. Hanging lamps shall not be installed in dressing rooms. (2) Lamp guards. All incandescent lamps in dressing rooms, if less than 8 feet from the floor, shall be equipped with open-end guards riveted to the outlet box or otherwise sealed or locked in place. (f) Grounding. All metal raceways shall be grounded. The metal frames and enclosures of equipment including border lights shall be grounded, except the frames and enclosures of portable equipment on grounded circuits operating at not over 150 volts to ground or on ungrounded circuits not exposed to any voltage higher than 150 volts to ground. Grounding, if employed, shall be done in the manner specified in the National Electric Code. 

(g) Construction. 

(1) Footlights. If metal trough construction is employed for footlights, the trough containing the circuit conductors shall be made of sheet metal not lighter than No. 20 USS sheet metal gauge (.0359 inch in thickness) treated to prevent oxidation. Lampholder terminals shall be kept at least one-half inch from the metal of the trough. The circuit conductors shall be soldered to the lampholder terminals. (2) Borders and proscenium sidelights. Borders and proscenium sidelights shall be constructed as prescribed in the above paragraph, shall be suitably stayed and supported, and shall be so designed that the flanges of the reflectors or other adequate guards will protect the lamps from mechanical injury and from accidental contact with scenery or other combustible material. Borders shall be wired with asbestos-covered (type A), asbestos varnished- 257

cambric (types AVA, AVB), or, if the temperature does not exceed 

90° C. (194° F.), slow burning (type SB) conductors. (3) Pockets. Receptacles intended for the connection of portable lighting equipment shall be mounted in suitable pockets or enclosures. (4) Arc lamps. Arc lamps shall comply with the following: (A) Portable arc lamps shall be substantially constructed entirely of metal not less than No. 20 USS sheet metal gauge (.0359 inch), except where approved insulating material is necessary. The design shall be such as to provide proper ventilation while retaining sparks, and to prevent carbons or other live parts of lamps from making contact with metal of hood. (B) Hoods for other lens lamps shall have the front opening equipped with a self-closing hinged doorframe having either wire gauze or glass. Hoods for lens lamps may have a stationary front and solid door on either back or side. (C) Mica shall be used for the insulation of the lamp frame. (D) The switch on the standard shall be of such a design that accidental contact with any live part will be impossible. (E) Rheostats shall be enclosed in a substantial, properly ventilated metal case affording a clearance of at least 1 inch between case and resistance element. If the rheostat is mounted on the standard, a clearance of 3 inches above the floor shall be maintained. (F) If stranded conductors are used, they shall be connected to lamp, rheostat, and switch terminals by means of approved lugs or connectors; provided, that approved pressure connectors shall be used at arc lamp terminals. (5) Portable strips. Portable strips shall be constructed in accordance with the requirements for border lights and proscenium side lights in subsec. (g) (2) of this section. The supply cable shall be protected by bushings where it passes through metal and shall be so arranged that tension on the cable will not be transmitted to the connections. (6) Portable connection boxes. Portable connection boxes shall conform to the following: (A) The construction shall be such that no current-carrying part will be exposed. (B) Each receptacle shall have a current-carrying capacity of not less than 30 amperes, and shall be protected by overcurrent 258

Ch. T.25 314-10 

devices installed in an approved enclosure equipped with selfclosing doors. (C) Bus bars shall have a current-carrying capacity equal to the sum of the ampere ratings of all the receptacles. Lugs shall be provided for the connection of the master cable. (h) Portable switchboards on stage. (1) Supply. Portable switchboards shall be supplied only from outlets especially provided for this purpose. Such outlets shall consist of externally operable, enclosed fused switches or circuit breakers mounted on the stage wall or at the switchboard in locations readily accessible from the stage floor. (2) Overcurrent protection. Circuits from portable switchboards directly supplying apparatus containing incandescent lamps shall be provided with overcurrent devices with a rating or setting of not more than 15 amperes. Other circuits shall be provided with overcurrent devices with a rating or setting not higher than the current required for the connected load. (3) Construction. Portable switchboards for use on stages shall comply with the following: (A) Portable switchboards shall be placed within an enclosure of substantial construction which may be so arranged that the enclosure is open during operation. Enclosure of wood shall be completely lined with sheet metal of not less than No. 24 

USS gauge (.0239 inch), and if not of corrosion-resistant type shall be well galvanized, enameled, or otherwise properly coated to prevent corrosion. (B) Except as provided for dimmer face plates in paragraph (E) of this subdivision, there shall be no exposed live parts within the enclosure. (C) All switches shall be of the externally operable, enclosed type. (D) Overcurrent devices shall be provided in each ungrounded conductor of every circuit supplied through the switchboard. Enclosures shall be provided for all overcurrent devices in addition to the switchboard enclosure. (E) The terminals of dimmers shall be provided with enclosures, and dimmer face plates shall be so arranged that accidental contact cannot be readily made with the face-plate contacts. (F) All conductors within the switchboard enclosure shall 259

Ch. 31 be braided and, except for cables feeding to or from the switchboard, shall be asbestos-covered (Type A). Each conductor shall have a current-carrying capacity at least equal to the rating of the circuit breaker, switch, or cutout which it supplies, except for conductors for incandescent lamp circuits having overcurrent protection not exceeding 15 amperes. Conductors shall be enclosed in metal troughs or securely fastened in position and shall be bushed where they pass through metal. (G) A pilot light shall be provided within the enclosure and shall be so connected to the circuit supplying the board that the opening of the master switch will not cut off the supply to the lamp. This lamp shall be on an independent circuit having overcurrent protection of a rating or setting of not more than 15 amperes. (H) The supply to a portable switchboard shall be by means of flexible cord (types K or S) terminating within the switchboard enclosure or in an externally operable fused master switch or circuit breaker. The supply cable shall have sufficient currentcarrying capacity to carry the total load on the switchboard and shall be protected by overcurrent devices. (I) Cables shall be protected by bushings where they pass through enclosures and shall be so arranged that tension on the cable will not be transmitted to the connections. (J) Terminals to which stage cables are connected shall be so located as to permit convenient access to the terminals. At terminals not provided with approved pressure connectors the following construction shall be employed: (i) For conductors of No. 6 or larger, solder lugs shall be used. (ii) For conductors smaller than No. 6, the strands shall be soldered together when connected to clamps or binding screws not specifically approved as pressure connectors. (i) Emergency lights. (1) Emergency lights shall be installed in order that the public may have sufficient light to leave the theatre in case of panic. These lights shall be operated independently of the main lights so that they may continue to operate in case the main lights should not operate due to an emergency. (2) The emergency-light circuits shall be controlled by a switch located in the lounge or any other place near the main 260

Ch. 

T.25 § 314-11 entrance of the building and shall be handled only by authorized persons. (3) There shall be no other switch on those circuits providing current for the emergency lights. (4) No circuits for the emergency lights shall be connected or controlled by the switch of the stage lights. 

§ 314-11. General rules 

(a) No inflammable liquids will be allowed within a building used as a theatre. (b) Smoking is prohibited in the orchestra, boxes, corridors, front and rear balconies, and on the stage, except that the actors may smoke when the performance being presented so requires it. 

Lighting of matches or any other substance which may cause a fire is prohibited. (c) It is not permitted to sell a larger number of tickets than the number of seats in the theatre. (d) In those towns having aqueducts, 2 hose connections of 112inch diameter shall be installed and 50 feet of hose connected to same. (e) The carpeting on the corridors shall be firmly fixed to the floor to prevent accidents. (f) In the future no building may be used as a theatre without the approval of the Fire Chief. (g) All stairs, vestibules, corridors, alleys, and courtyards leading to the street shall, at all times, be kept unobstructed and free of rubbish, lumber, or any other objects which may obstruct passage through them. (h) All inside stairs, platforms, and corridors of same shall be kept illuminated at all times during the performance and until all persons have left the building. (i) The person, natural or artificial, who is the owner, representative, manager, or administrator of a theatre shall be responsible for strict compliance with this subchapter, through himself or through his employees, and shall incur the prescribed penalty for each violation if he does not comply with this subchapter or if he allows any spectator or employee to violate it. (j) Before starting construction or repairs of a building, being used or to be used as a theatre, duplicate plans containing all safety specifications, including the electric system, shall be submitted to the Fire Chief for his approval. After the plans have been approved 261

T.§ 314-11 

Ch. 31

INTERNAL SECURITY 

by the Fire Chief or by the person or office designated by him, said plans and specifications may not be altered in any way whatsoever except with the written consent of said authorized person. 

When the construction or repairs are finished, the Fire Chief shall be notified in writing that the building is ready for inspection. If upon the final inspection the building or repairs are found to have been carried out in accordance with the approved plans and specifications, a Certificate of Safety shall be issued for said building. 

SECTIONS 

No building constructed in the future to be used as a theatre shall be opened to the public or used in any way whatsoever without first having obtained the Certificate of Safety issued by the 

Fire Chief. 

DIVISION 2. PLACES OF ASSEMBLY
