§ 314-21. Definitions 

(a) "Places of assembly" include all buildings or parts of buildings used for the assembly of persons for entertainment or amusement, including all places where persons congregate such as dance halls, bars, cabarets, night clubs, restaurants, hotels, etc. (b) "Exit doorway" means the door or any other opening through which persons may pass safely from the place of assembly to street or to an open space which provides safe access to a street. (c) "Fire escape" means any inside or outside stairway used to go down from an upper story or a story above street level, leading to a street or to an open courtyard having access to a street. (d) "Story" means that part of any building comprised between any floor and the floor or roof next above. (e) "Ground floor" or "first floor" means the floor at or nearest the ground surrounding the building, unless the ground surrounding the building is irregular in grade, in which case the term shall mean, for the purpose of this subchapter, the floor which, having 262

Ch. 

T.25 § 314-22 one or more exits to the grade, is not more than 12 feet above the ground taken at the center line of the facade where the grade is lowest. "Ground floor" and "first floor" whenever used in this subchapter are used as synonymous terms. (f) "Owner" means the proprietor of the building, representative, or manager of the business, or any person who may own, administer, or represent it. 

§ 314-22. Exit doors 

(a) Every room, gallery, balcony, or other space having a capacity of 100 or more persons shall have at least 2 exit doorways. In existing places of assembly located on the first or ground floor, a single doorway may be used to provide exit for not more than 200 persons provided the doorway has a clear width of not less than 44 inches. The exit doorway shall be so located that no point in the room or space is more than 100 feet distant from said exit doorway, measured along the line of travel. (b) The aggregate clear width of exit doorways serving as required exits shall be not less than at the rate of 22 inches for every 100 persons to be accommodated. No exit doorway shall have a clear width of less than 44 inches. (c) Exit doorways shall be located at places recommended or approved by the Fire Chief, with proper regard to the safety of the occupants and ease of exits. The size and shape of the room or space, the accessibility of street and open spaces, the ability to use horizontal exits, and the desirability of good separation of exit doorways shall be considered. (d) All exit doors in rooms occupied by 50 or more persons and all exit doors in exit ways from places of assembly shall be hung to swing in the direction of exit travel, but this requirement shall not be construed to prohibit doors swinging both inwards and outwards. (e) Revolving doors are prohibited. (f) The owner, lessee, manager, or other person having charge or control of any cabaret, dance hall, night club, hotel, or any other place of amusement, shall, during any presentation or performance therein, and when any such place is open to the public, cause each and every door and means of exit for use in case of fire or panic to be kept unlocked, unbolted, and unfastened. Automatic release bolts may be used. 263

T.§ 314-22 Ch. 31 

INTERNAL SECURITY 

(g) Exit doors shall be provided with panic bar release devices, of a type approved by the Fire Chief. (h) The basis of exit requirements shall be 1 person to each 12 square feet of gross area occupied, not including storerooms. If at the time this subchapter is approved the existing exit facilities for any room or space of assembly are not sufficient on the above basis of 1 person to 12 square feet, the number of persons permitted shall be reduced in proportion to the exits existing. Where the place of assembly is largely occupied by chairs or chairs and tables, no greater number of persons shall be permitted than that for which exits have been provided. The term "chairs" shall include stools, benches, or any other seating arrangements. 

§ 314-23. Marking and lighting of exits 

(a) Exit doorways shall be plainly marked by approved exit signs located on the upper part of the door frame and shall be illuminated by electricity when the floor area is occupied by the public. The minimum size of the letters shall be 6 inches. (b) Directional signs shall be placed on walls or otherwise displayed in conspicuous locations as recommended by the Fire Chief to direct the occupants to exits. (c) Where the number of persons in any room exceeds 75, the artificial lighting of the room and the exit ways therefrom shall be illuminated by electricity so arranged and supplied that interruption of supply to any lighting circuit will not result in extinguishment of all lights in the room or all the lights along any exit way. 

§ 314-24. Stairways 

(a) When a place of assembly is located above a ground floor, inside stairways shall continue to the roof. Except in existing buildings, all inside stairways shall be constructed of noncombustible material, with solid steps. Both the steps and the landing of such stairways shall be constructed and maintained in a manner to prevent persons from slipping thereon. The total width of the stairways shall be not less than 22 inches for every 100 persons to be accommodated in such a stairway. The minimum required width is 36 inches. The risers shall be not more than 8 inches high and the treads shall be not less than 10 inches wide. Treads and risers shall be of the same size in every stairway. Stairways of the winding type are prohibited. When the place of assembly is located 264

Ch. 31

 T.25 § 314-28 

above the first floor at least one-half of the stairways shall be exterior fire escapes or staircases separated from the first floor by fireproof walls leading directly to the street. All exterior fire escapes shall be constructed of a fireproof material. (b) All stairways shall have a handrail not less than 30 inches high. (c) No part of a stairway, whether interior or exterior, or of a corridor, vestibule, balcony, or bridge, leading to a stairway or exit of any kind, shall be used in any way that will obstruct its use as an exit or that will present a fire hazard. 

§ 314-25. False openings 

No false opening giving the appearance of a door or window where none exists shall be placed in an assembly hall. 

§ 314-26. Decorative materials 

(a) All decorative combustible materials, including curtains, acoustic materials, streamers, cloth, straw, leaves, trees, moss, etc., shall be rendered flameproof, provided this shall not be required of material not exceeding 1/16-inch thickness applied directly to and adhering to a non-combustible base. (b) The use of imitation leather (or other material) consisting of or coated with pyroxylin base is prohibited. 

§ 314-27. Aisles 

For each room or space used with chairs alone or with tables and chairs, the arrangement shall be such as will provide for ready access by aisles to each exit doorway. Aisles leading directly to exit doorways shall have not less than 36 inches clear width which shall not be obstructed by chairs, tables, or other objects. 

§ 314-28. Fire appliances (a) The Chief of the Fire Service of Puerto Rico shall survey, or cause to be surveyed, all places of assembly as defined herein, and shall designate suitable fire appliances in and near boiler rooms, kitchens, storage rooms, and other occupied areas where such appliances are deemed to be needed. Such fire appliances may consist of automatic alarm system, standpipes and hose, buckets with sand, or portable extinguishers. (b) All fire appliances shall be kept in working condition; all extinguishers, buckets, hose, and similar appliances shall be in such visible and accessible places as designated by the Fire Service of Puerto Rico. 

265

T.§ 314-28 Ch. 31 

INTERNAL SECURITY 

(c) It shall be the duty of the owner and occupant of each building, or part of building, destined as a place of assembly, to train properly sufficient regular employees in the use of fire appliances so that such appliances can be quickly put into operation. 

§ 314-29. Ash trays 

There shall be provided on each table of places of assembly, suitable noncombustible ash trays or match receivers. 

SECTIONS § 314-30. Lighting 

Electrical installations shall be made in accordance with the National Electrical Code requirements for each type of construction in accordance with Act No. 36 of 1932 [20 L.P.R.A. § 901 et seq.]. 

An inspection of every place of assembly shall be carried out by the Fire Service of Puerto Rico and the proper type of electrical installation shall be required, as well as any modification or alteration to the one already in use, in order to conform it to the requirements herein provided.

§ 314-41. Application 

The stipulations provided in this Division shall be applicable to all natural persons, companies, societies, associations, or any other entity possessing, whether for private, industrial, or commercial use, flammable liquids of any kind whatsoever, even if they are not mentioned herein. The provisions of this Division shall apply to all new plants, stores, equipments, and installations; and, except 266

Ch. 

T.25 § 314-45 as otherwise specified, they shall apply also, wherever compliance with the sections of this Division is reasonably possible, to existing plants, stores, equipments, and installations which are not properly safeguarded and which constitute a distinct hazard to adjoining property. 

§ 314-42. Classes of flammable liquids 

For the purpose of this Division, flammable liquids shall be divided into three classes, according to the flashpoint, as follows: (a) Liquids with flashpoint below 25° F. (-4° C.) closed cup. tester, such as ether, carbon bisulphide, gasoline, naphtha, benzol, collodion, acetone. (b) Liquids with flashpoints above 25° F. (-4° C.) and below 

70° F. (21° C.) closed cup tester, such as alcohol, amyl acetate, toluol, ethyl acetate, and methyl acetate. (c) Liquids with flashpoint above 70° F. (21° C.) and below 

200° F. (93¼° C.) closed cup tester, such as kerosene, amyl alcohol, turpentine, and fuel oil. 

§ 314-43. Liquids manufactured in Puerto Rico 

All liquids manufactured within the territorial limits of Puerto 

Rico, such as paints, oils, varnishes, driers, cleaning solutions, insecticides, or polishing liquids, having among their ingredients some flammable liquid, shall be considered as such and be classified in one of the classes stipulated in sec. 314-42 of this title, in accordance with the flashpoint of their components. 

§ 314-44. Stores in buildings with residences 

The handling, storage, or mixture of the flammable liquids classified under items (a) and (b) of sec. 314-42 of this title, in open containers, shall not be permitted in stores located in buildings where more than two families reside; provided, however, that nothing herein contained shall be construed as prohibiting such handling, storage, or mixing of flammable liquids in the quantities specified in this Division in drugstores, when this is done in the preparation of prescriptions or medicines. 

§ 314-45. Storage; prohibited quantities 

The storage of flammable liquids classified under item (a) of sec. 314-42 of this title is absolutely prohibited in a quantity in excess of 1 gallon in dwellings or apartment houses, in excess of 267

T.§ 314-45 

Ch. 31

INTERNAL SECURITY 

6 gallons within any other building, and in excess of 10 gallons outside of any building.

The storage of flammable liquids classified under item (b) of sec. 314-42 is likewise prohibited in a quantity in excess of 5 gallons in dwellings or apartment houses, in excess of 10 gallons within any other building, and in excess of 25 gallons outside of any building.

The storage of flammable liquids classified under item (c) of sec. 314-42 is also prohibited in a quantity in excess of 25 gallons in dwellings and apartment houses, and in excess of 55 gallons in any other building. 

§ 314-46. Storage permits 

The storage of flammable liquids in quantities larger than those stipulated in sec. 314-45 of this title shall be allowed in buildings, tanks, or containers only with the written authorization of the Fire Chief pursuant to a written request wherein shall be contained the following information: 

(1) Name of applicant. 

(2) Kind of flammable liquid to be stored. (3) Exact location of premises or building. (4) Kind, size, and construction of building, tank, or container. (5) Maximum quantity of flammable liquid to be stored.

A detailed plan of the building or premises shall accompany the request and said plan shall indicate where the storage tank is to be installed or where the flammable liquid is to be stored, and also the location of all adjacent buildings, streets, and roads. 

§ 314-47. Requirements for storage permits 

In order to obtain the authorization of the Fire Chief for the storage of flammable liquids inside buildings in quantities in excess of those stipulated in sec. 314-45 of this title, the following requirements are indispensable: (1) That the building be illuminated entirely by electricity with wires enclosed in insulated tubes, so installed as to be explosionproof. (2) That no matches, resin, hemp, gunpowder, or any other explosives be retailed on the premises. (3) That no paints, oil, or lacquers be manufactured. Storage of these liquids will be permitted provided they are stored in their original containers. 268

Ch. 31

T.25 314-47 (4) That the walls, floors, and ceilings of inside rooms or buildings where flammable liquids classified under sec. 314-42 (a) and (b) are extensively mixed or processed be of concrete 8 inches thick, or of other fire-resistant material of a thickness affording the same measure of safety; that the doors and window frames be constructed of metal and the windows provided with wired glass and arranged to swing outward. (5) That the walls, floors, and ceilings of inside rooms or buildings where flammable liquids are mixed, processed, or stored be one of the following types of construction:

Walls. Metal lath encased in solid cement plaster not less than 

212 inches thick; gypsum or cement plaster at least 3/4 inch thick on each side of stud position; tile, gypsum, or concrete block (cement plaster on each side to a thickness of 1/4 inch); in lieu of the foregoing any type of partition that will afford one hour's protection against fire.

Floors. If of wood should be protected with not less than 2 inches of concrete.

Ceilings. Of construction equivalent to not less than threefourths of an inch of cement or gypsum plaster on metal lath. 

These construction requirements shall not be indispensable where storage of flammable liquids is maintained within the following limits: (A) Liquids classified under sec. 314-42(a) in sealed containers or cans of not more than 1 gallon capacity and not exceeding a total of 10 gallons. (B) Liquids classified under sec. 314-42 (b) in sealed containers of not more than 5 gallons capacity and in steel barrels, drums, or tanks not exceeding 60 gallons capacity. Total quantity stored in this manner in other than frame buildings is unlimited. (C) Liquids classified in sec. 314-42 (c) in sealed containers, drums, barrels, or tanks not exceeding 120 gallons capacity. Total quantity stored in this manner in other than frame buildings is unlimited. (6) That the building be provided with good ventilation.

Once the application and plans are in the possession of the Fire Chief, he shall have an inspection made by an authorized safety inspector of the buildings, premises, deposit, or tank wherein the flammable liquids are to be stored in accordance with this section. 269

§ 314-48. Storage outside buildings 

Except as otherwise permitted in this Division, storage of flammable liquids shall be outside buildings in underground or aboveground tanks; except that the storage in tanks aboveground is prohibited within congested districts; provided, that for existing tanks and outside storage areas within such districts, which are properly safeguarded, a permit shall be granted. 

§ 314-49. Underground tanks 

Tanks buried underground shall have the top of the tank not less than 2 feet below ground level or below any piping to which the tanks may be connected, except that instead of the required cover of 2 feet, tanks may be buried under 12 inches of earth and a cover of reinforced concrete at least 5 inches in thickness provided. Where tanks are buried under driveways subject to traffic of heavy vehicles the total coverage above the top of the tank shall be not less than 3 feet; provided, however, that where such driveways are paved with concrete not less than 5 inches in thickness, the total coverage may be reduced to 2 feet; provided, that for underground tanks otherwise properly safeguarded and existing on the date of enactment of this subchapter a permit shall be granted. 

§ 314-50. Aboveground tanks 

(a) [New constructions.] The provisions of this section apply to new constructions and not to installations existing as of the date of enactment of this subchapter. (b) Capacity and location of aboveground tanks. The location of an aboveground tank with respect to distance from tank shell to line of adjoining property or nearest building shall depend upon the construction, contents, equipment, and greatest dimension (diameter, length, or height) of the tank and shall be in accord with the following provisions:

Group A Tanks. Any all-steel, gas-tight tank constructed in compliance with these or equivalent standards and equipped either with (1) an approved, permanently attached extinguishing system or (2) an approved floating roof, which is to be used only for the storage of refined petroleum products or other flammable liquids not subject to boilover, shall be so located that the distance between shell of tank and property line or nearest building shall be not less 270

Ch. T.25 § 314-50 

than the greatest dimension (diameter, length, or height) of the tank, except that such distance need not exceed 120 feet. 

Group B Tanks. Any all-steel, gas-tight tank constructed in compliance with these or equivalent standards but not equipped either with (1) an approved, permanently attached, extinguishing system or (2) an approved floating roof, which is to be used only for the storage of refined petroleum products or other flammable liquids not subject to boilover, shall be so located that the distance between shell of tank and property line or nearest building shall be not less than 11½ times the greatest dimension (diameter, length, or height) of the tank, except that such distance need not exceed 175 feet. 

Group C Tanks. Any all-steel, gas-tight tank constructed in compliance with these or equivalent standards and equipped either with (1) an approved, permanently attached, extinguishing system or (2) an approved floating roof, which is to be used for the storage of crude petroleum or other flammable liquids subject to boilover, shall be so located that the distance between shell of tank and property line or nearest building shall be not less than twice the greatest dimension (diameter, length, or height) of the tank, except that such distance shall be not less than 20 feet and need not exceed 

175 feet.

Group D Tanks. Any all-steel, gas-tight tank constructed in compliance with these or equivalent standards and not equipped either with (1) an approved, permanently attached, extinguishing system or (2) an approved floating roof, which is to be used for the storage of crude petroleum or other flammable liquids subject to boilover, shall be so located that the distance between shell of tank and property line or nearest building shall be not less than three times the greatest dimension (diameter, length, or height) of the tank, except that such distance shall be not less than 20 feet and need not exceed 

350 feet.

The minimum distance between the shell of any two all-steel, gas-tight tanks shall be not less than one-half the greatest dimension (diameter, length, or height) of the smaller tank except that such distance shall not be less than 3 feet, and for tanks of 18,000 gallons or less the distance need not exceed 3 feet. (c) Material and construction of tanks. Tanks, including top, shall be constructed of steel or wrought iron of a thickness depending upon the capacity and to be figured in accordance with the following table or formula. No open tank shall be used. For liquids 271

Where it is proposed to construct a tank for the storage of flammable liquid under pressure exceeding 15 pounds per square inch (gauge) the inspection department having jurisdiction shall require the submittal of detailed plans and specifications supplemented by detailed information including the maximum pressure under which the liquid will be stored and the size and setting of the safety relief valve so as to permit the Fire Service to determine whether compliance with the Unfired Pressure Vessel Code of the A.S.M.E. should be required. 

Note. Vertical steel tanks with riveted shells constructed in accordance with A.P.I. standard No. 12-A are substantially equivalent to those specified in subsecs. (b) and (c) of this section and shall be considered as meeting these requirements. 

Tanks shall be protected against corrosion. (d) Opening in aboveground tanks. All aboveground tanks for storing flammable liquids over 100 gallons in capacity shall have vent openings excepting safety valves provided with noncorrodible wire screens (preferably 40 × 40 mesh, but not less than 30 × 30 mesh or its equivalent) so attached as to cover completely the openings. The screens on openings may be made removable but normally shall be kept firmly attached. (e) Breather vents. Tanks shall be equipped with a permanently open vent or an approved automatically operated vent, arranged to discharge to the open air, except that vent valves or reliefs of tanks fitted with floating roofs of acceptable design, which leave no considerable space above the liquid in which vapors may accumulate, need not terminate in flame arresters.

The function of the breather vent is to permit the proper outflow and inflow of air during filling and emptying operations and thus prevent the development of dangerous interior pressure, or possible collapse of the tank due to vacuum, and further to safely permit the normal expansion and contraction of the product stored due to varying temperature.

The required breathing capacity mainly depends upon a number 273

INTERNAL SECURITY 

Ch. 31 of well recognized factors, i.e., the volume of the vapor space; vapor pressure of the liquid stored; the rates of filling and emptying, or pumping rate; and the maximum rates of temperature rise or temperature drop of the tank vapor space and of the liquid surface. 

It follows, therefore, that the determination of the breathing requirements for any given tank is a matter of separate engineering consideration. (f) [Other openings.] All openings except vent openings and those for valves or pipe connections communicating with the interior of the tank, shall be equipped with substantial covers. Thiefing and gauging openings shall have approved self-closing covers, but manhole covers may be of either bolted or approved self-closing type. (g) Emergency pressure reliefs. With the exception of vertical cove-roof tanks having a roof slope less than 212 inches in 12 inches and in which the strength of the joint between roof and shell is no greater than that of the weakest vertical joint in the shell, all aboveground tanks shall have some form of relief for preventing the development of excessive internal pressure in case of exposure fire surrounding the tank. This may take the form of either a weak seam in the top or at the joint between the top and the shell of the tank or some other form of emergency relief construction. The 274

Three inches of water is probably the maximum pressure that should be placed on the ordinary type of cone roof on vertical steel tanks, while 1 pound per square inch is probably conservative for the pressure to be allowed in the ordinary type of horizontal tanks. 

Many storage tanks have been constructed as pressure vessels and can be vented safely at pressures above 5 pounds per square inch and still maintain a very high factor of safety. 

An emergency relief capacity of 410,000 cubic feet per hour is the maximum required for any tank regardless of size. This is based upon the fact that tanks having a capacity in excess of 735,000 gallons require so long a time to heat up the contents to a temperature where rapid ebullition starts (something over 3 hours with ordinary gasoline and much longer for heavier oils) that it is extremely unlikely that this point would ever be reached, and even if it should be, there would be ample time to take the necessary precautions to safeguard life and property. (h) [Signs.] Tanks containing flammable liquids flashing below 275

T.25 314 Ch. 31 

INTERNAL SECURITY 

70° (closed cup tester) except where located in oil refineries and large water terminals shall have painted conspicuously upon their side the wording "FLAMMABLE — KEEP FIRE AWAY”. 

(i) Foundations; grounding. (1) In each case the bearing capacity of the ground shall determine the type of foundation to be employed. Where there is any doubt the Fire Service may require borings in order to ascertain the sub-surface formation as a means of determining whether the proposed foundation is suited to ground condition on the site. 

Tanks with bottom more than 1 foot above the ground shall have foundation and supports of masonry or protected steel, except that wooden cushions may be used; no combustible material shall be permitted under or within 10 feet of any aboveground outside storage tank. (2) Unprotected steel as a support for tanks shall not be permitted. (3) All tanks shall be electrically grounded by resting directly on moist earth, or otherwise electrically grounded to permanent moisture in an approved manner. No insulated connections shall be permitted. All steelwork of reinforced concrete tanks and dikes shall be interconnected and grounded in an approved manner. (j) Piping. (1) Piping should be run as directly as possible and proper allowance made for expansion and contraction. (2) Piping when aboveground shall be protected against mechanical injury. (3) Each pipe attached to a tank shall be provided with a valve at the tank. There shall be no branches or outlets between the tank and valve. (k) Embankments and dikes. (1) All tanks containing crude oil or other liquids which have a tendency to boil over, and all tanks exceeding 50,000 gallons (1,200 barrels) capacity shall be adequately and properly diked with a dike having capacity not less than equal in volume to that of the tank or tanks surrounded; minimum height of earth dikes shall be 3 feet, and of masonry dikes, 30 inches. (2) Tanks of less than 50,000 gallons (12,000 barrels) capacity shall, when deemed necessary by the Fire Service, on account of proximity to streams, character of topography, or nearness to buildings of high value, be diked or the entire yard provided with 276

Ch. 

T.25 § 314-51 a curb or retaining wall or other suitable means taken to prevent the discharge of liquids onto other property in case of a rupture in tank or piping.

Small tanks with capacities of not over 18,000 gallons each may be grouped and a dike built around the group of tanks. (3) Dikes or walls required by this section shall be of earth or masonry, so constructed as to afford adequate protection. When dikes surround tanks containing crude oil, they shall have, in addition to the above capacity, suitable coping or deflector projecting inward, and so designed and constructed as to minimize the effect of a "boilover" wave. Dikes containing crude oil shall be not less than 50 feet from the shell of the tank or tanks surrounded. (4) The height of the dike and the distance from the inner surface of the dike to the shell of the tank or tanks surrounded shall be such as to assure the scouring action of the winds required to prevent the accumulation of combustible vapors within the dike. 

Masonry dikes with angular walls shall be provided with expansion joints constructed of single sheet noncorrosive metal. Where reinforced concrete is used, the steel reinforcing member shall be interconnected.

Earthen dikes shall preferably have a flat section at the top of not less than 3 feet and shall have a slope consistent with the angle of repose of the materials of which they are constructed. 

Embankments or dikes shall be continuous with no openings for piping or roadway. Piping shall preferably be laid over or under the dike. (1) Fire protection. When, in the opinion of the Fire Service, oil storage tanks are so located as to endanger adjacent property in case of fire, every such tank shall be protected by a permanently attached, approved, foam extinguishing system. The quantity of foam-producing chemicals to be maintained and stored convenient for use in emergency shall be in compliance with the Standards for 

Foam Extinguisher Systems. 

§ 314-51. Sand buckets

Every storage warehouse and every retail or wholesale establishment, where flammable liquids are stored or deposited, shall be provided permanently with buckets filled with sand kept in visible places and to be used in fighting fires. The Fire Chief shall determine the number of sand buckets in accordance with the quantity of flammable liquids stored. 277

T.§ 314-52 Ch. 31 

INTERNAL SECURITY 

§ 314-52. Foam fire extinguishers

Every storage warehouse and every establishment where flammable liquids are stored or sold shall be provided permanently, in visible and handy places, with a sufficient number of foam fire extinguishers, in proportion to the quantity of flammable liquid stored, at the discretion of the Fire Chief. 

§ 314-53. Smoking 

Smoking is absolutely prohibited in any place where flammable liquids are stored or mixed; signs to this effect shall be located in visible places. 

§ 314-54. Open containers 

Keeping flammable liquids in open containers in the zone reserved for piers for a period longer than 6 hours is prohibited. 

§ 314-55. Buildings of public assembly 

The storage of flammable liquids, classified under paragraphs (a) and (b) of sec. 314-42 of this title, in school buildings, religious buildings, theatres, moving picture houses, cabarets, night clubs, or other buildings of public assembly is prohibited. 

§ 314-56. Revocation of permit 

The Fire Chief shall have the right to revoke at any time any permit issued for the storage of flammable liquids in case any provision of this Division is violated or in case any other provision to be approved in the future is not complied with.

314-71. Permit

It shall be unlawful to store, house, or keep more than four motor vehicles in any building, shed, or enclosure, or to operate a motor 278

Ch. T.25 § 314-73 

vehicle repair shop without a permit issued by the Chief of the 

Fire Service. 

§ 314-72. Buildings not qualified for permit 

No permit for a storage garage, auto repair shop, or service station shall be issued for any building, shed, or enclosure: (1) which is occupied by a tenement house, hotel, or lodging house unless the space used for the garage, repair shop, or service station is separated from the rest of the building by walls, floors, and ceilings of fireproof or semi-fireproof construction; (2) where paints, varnishes, or lacquers are manufactured; (3) where dry goods or other highly inflammable materials are manufactured; (4) where resin, turpentine, hemp, cotton, or any other explosives are stored or kept for sale; or (5) which is situated within 20 feet of the nearest wall of a building occupied as a school, theatre, or other place of public amusement or assembly; provided, however, that a permit may be issued for places where the wall or walls of the garage, auto repair shop, or service station are constructed of brick, concrete, or any other noncombustible material.

ANNOTATIONS 

1. Municipal ordinances. A municipal ordinance was valid which prohibited the installation of new pumps at a distance of less than 300 meters from a school, hospital, clinic, etc., and which was therefore more restrictive than the 20 feet specified in this section of the regulations. Cabassa v. Rivera, 1948, 68 P.R.R. 654. 

§ 314-73. Dwellings 

A permit shall not be issued for a garage, auto repair shop, or service station in a building occupied as a dwelling unless the living apartments are separated from the garage, auto repair shop, or service station by fire-retarding walls and floors, and provided that there shall be an entrance to the living apartments direct from the street without passing through the garage, auto repair shop, or service station. In case the building is of nonfireproof construction and two families occupy two stories above the garage, auto repair shop, or service station, a fire escape or other secondary means of escape must be provided for each story above the garage, auto repair shop, or service station. 279

T.§ 314-74 

INTERNAL SECURITY

§ 314-74. Fire extinguishers 

Each garage, auto repair shop, or service station shall be equipped with chemical fire extinguishers of the type and capacity designated by the Chief of the Fire Service and fire buckets filled with sand, to be used only in case of fire, shall be kept in sufficient quantities as directed by the Chief of the Fire Service. 

§ 314-75. Metal cans 

Each floor of a garage, auto repair shop, or service station shall be equipped with self-closing metal cans, and all inflammable waste materials shall be kept therein until removed from the building. 

314-76. Exit doors

Every garage or auto repair shop containing 20 or more vehicles shall be provided with two exit doors in order that the vehicles may be removed quickly in case of fire. The size and location of said exit doors shall be designated by the Fire Service of Puerto Rico. 

§ 314-77. Repair shop 

(a) Flame torches (soldering irons) or smelting ovens shall be used in fireproof rooms or buildings separated by a fireproof wall from the rest of the repair shop. (b) Carpentry, upholstery, and painting work shall be performed in a room separated by fireproof partitions from the repair shop where work requiring heat is done. (c) Wood shavings from the carpenter shop installed in the repair shop shall be removed frequently. (d) Smoking is prohibited in garages, auto repair shops, and service stations, except in the offices, and "NO SMOKING" signs not smaller than 36″ x 12″ shall be posted in visible places. § 314-78. Washing automobiles or auto parts (a) The use of gasoline and other volatile flammable liquids for cleaning purposes shall be restricted as far as possible. To safeguard against fires and accidents preference should be given to systems for cleaning and washing which utilize compressed air, steam, water pressure, or nonflammable cleaning compounds. (b) Cleaning vats or systems utilizing nonflammable liquids which must be heated for effective removal of grease and oils from 280

Ch. 

T.25 § 314-91 automobile parts may only be installed within the storage section if specifically approved for use where flammable vapors may be present. (c) Washing operations involving the use of volatile flammable liquids shall be carried on in a separate room or section cut off from the storage section of the garage by a 2-hour fire partition. 

Such rooms shall be adequately ventilated. The floor of such room. or compartment shall be pitched to an oil separator or trap discharging to sewer. 

§ 314-79. Electrical installations 

Electrical installations shall be made in accordance with the National Electric Code requirements for each type of construction. 

Every garage, auto repair shop, and service station shall be inspected by the Fire Service of Puerto Rico and the proper type of electrical installation shall be required, as well as any modification or alteration to the one already in use in order to conform it to the 

National Electric Code requirements. 

SECTIONS 

It shall be unlawful to install any system of artificial lighting other than incandescent electric lights in any garage, auto repair shop, or service station. 314-91. 314-92.

(a) Where stock heights are 15 feet or less, clearance between top of stack and lower edge of roof rafters or ceiling joists shall be 

18 inches. Over 15 feet, clearance shall be 36 inches. (b) A clearance of 18 inches shall be maintained below automatic sprinkler heads where such protection is installed. such a manner that the conductors are exposed to mechanical injury, clearance shall be 18 inches. (e) Solid blocks of supplies bounded by aisles shall occupy not more than 7,750 square feet. (f) The depth from wall to aisle of stocks along exterior walls shall be limited to 30 feet. 

§ 314-92. Aisles 

Aisles shall be maintained in the following locations and with minimum widths as indicated: 

(1) Next to pier sidewalls 3 feet. (2) Across piers at each hose connection - 3 feet. (3) On either side of center line of railroad tracks 10 feet. (4) Access aisles to electric equipment, fire fighting equipment, and sprinkler valves 3 feet. (5) Between stacks and all interior fire walls between warehouse sections 2 feet. 

§ 314-93. Partitions 

(a) Partitions shall not be placed to prevent proper distribution of water from any sprinkler head. (b) Nothing shall be hung from or fastened to any part of the sprinkler system. (c) Fire doors shall be closed when warehouses are not occupied by personnel. Fire doors shall not be blocked or their free movement impeded at any time. (d) Where it is necessary to close and block doors (cargo or personnel) permission shall be obtained from the Fire Service of Puerto Rico and each door shall be conspicuously marked on the outside "THIS DOOR BLOCKED". At least one cross aisle and connecting exterior door shall be left open in each section. (e) Provision should be made to avoid any obstruction by storage which might prevent the effective operation of hose streams through windows. (f) No stock or equipment of any kind shall be stored or left unattended on any interior or exterior loading platform, stairway, fire exit, aisle, hose, or valve space. (g) Crating and packing materials shall be neatly stored in sites approved by the Fire Service of Puerto Rico and at no other location. 282

Ch. T.25 § 314-97 

 314-94. Electrical installations 

(a) No light, other than electric, shall be used in any warehouse or pier. Lampshades, other than metal, glass, or other noncombustible material, are prohibited. All extension-cord light bulbs shall be enclosed in metal guards securely fastened to socket. All portable floodlights shall be mounted on portable metal stands to prevent contact with combustible material. (b) Electric motors, generators, switchboards, and wiring shall be installed in accordance with the National Electric Code. § 314-95. Sparks and flammable liquids (a) [Vehicles.] Transient trucks and automobiles shall be allowed to remain on piers and warehouses only long enough to load and unload cargo. Such vehicles should be equipped with an approved one-quart extinguisher. The replenishment of fuel supply shall be prohibited on piers and in warehouses. Any automobile whose fuel supply is exhausted shall be towed from the pier in order to replenish the supply of fuel. 

(b) [Locomotives.] Locomotives using coal as fuel shall be prohibited from entering a superstructure on piers and warehouses. (c) Flammable liquids. Gasoline and other flammable liquids shall not be stored or handled on piers and warehouses except in substantial, sealed ICC containers or as cargo through steel pipelines and proper cargo discharge hoses. 

§ 314-96. Housekeeping General care and cleanliness 

Piers and warehouses shall be kept free from rubbish and waste materials. Such materials shall be removed at sufficiently frequent intervals to prevent dangerous accumulations. Particular attention should be directed to keeping clean the depression between tracks, areas under stairways, special rooms and enclosures, and all outof-the-way places. 

§ 314-97. Smoking 

Smoking, carrying, or possessing a lighted cigar, cigarette, pipe, or match, or any other flame-producing device on any pier, dock, or warehouse is prohibited, except on such portions thereof as may be specifically designated by the Fire Service of Puerto Rico. Signs reading "No Smoking" shall be conspicuously placed around the premises. 283

314-111. Construction

Fireproof construction is recommended for all buildings and shall be used throughout for all buildings 3 stories or more in height. Frame buildings shall not exceed 1 story in height. 

§ 314-112. Exits 

(a) Not less than two exits shall be provided for every floor of every building or section. All aisles and passageways leading to exits shall be direct and so arranged as to be conveniently accessible at all times to visitors, employees, and patients. Signs shall be provided to indicate direction of travel to exits. Aisles and corridors shall have a minimum width of 60 inches; shall be kept free of obstruction such as chairs, tables, scales, packages, or any other material which may impede persons attempting to use the passageways in an emergency. Aisles and corridors shall never be used for storage purposes. (b) Exit doors shall always be kept unlocked and suitably lighted. (c) All stairs shall have walls or well-guarded balustrades or 284

Ch. T.25 § 314-113 

guards, shall have handrails on both sides, and shall be at least 

44 inches wide. (d) Winding staircases are prohibited in all required stairs. § 314-113. Operating rooms, delivery rooms, and other places for surgical treatment (a) Temperature and humidity. (1) The temperature and humidity maintained in operating rooms shall be chosen on the basis of the well-being of patient and personnel. High humidity will reduce the hazard of electrostatic spark discharge under certain conditions but is not sufficiently reliable for their complete elimination. (2) The operating room shall be safeguarded against the ignition of any flammable air-vapor mixture by electric arcs or sparks, or static electricity sparks. (3) The anesthetic machine, the anesthetist, the nurse, the operating surgeon, and the operating table in the operating room are required to be grounded to the floor or water piping. (4) All lights, switches, motors, etc., within 7 feet of the floor shall be explosion-proof. (5) Use of nonconducting materials, if possible, is recommended where conditions are such that static electricity charges may accumulate. (b) Mattresses, pillows, cushions, etc. The coverings of all operating table and stretcher pads and of all pillows, cushions, and the like, shall be made from sheeting of conductive rubber or equivalent material. Such conductive material shall have a surface conductivity of not less than 10 microhms per square centimeter and a longitudinal resistivity of not more than 10,000 ohms per square centimeter. (c) Rubber tubing and other parts. All rubber or equivalent parts of operating room equipment, such as the masks, breathing tubes, breathing bags, and gaskets of anesthesia equipment, and all suction and pressure tubing not confined within a metallic sheathing, shall be of conductive rubber or equivalent material. 

Such conductive material shall have a surface conductivity of not less than 10 microhms per square centimeter and an internal resistivity of not more than 10,000 ohms per cubic centimeter. 

(d) Diathermy and X-ray equipment. Diathermy and X-ray equipment shall be provided with an approved form of grounded electrostatic shield. All switches and control devices for diathermy 285

T.§ 314-113 Ch. 31 

INTERNAL SECURITY 

and X-ray equipment shall be operated outside the hazardous location. (e) Cauterization equipment. Cauterization equipment either of the hot-wire or of the radio-frequency type shall be used only in nonhazardous locations. All hot-wire cauterization apparatus shall be operated on voltages of 6 volts or less. (f) Illuminating instruments. In any location, all instruments for providing electrical illumination which are brought into close contact with the bodies of persons, such as endoscopic instruments, head lamps, and the like, shall be operated at voltages of 6 volts or less. Switches and control devices for such instruments shall be operated at a distance of at least 3 feet from any portion of any system containing mixtures of explosive gases. (g) Definitions of hazardous locations. (1) A room in which any of the hydrocarbon anesthetic gases or any of the other compounds are stored or used is to be considered a hazardous location. (2) The hazardous condition may be considered as extending for a horizontal distance of 10 feet and to a height of 7 feet above the floor outside of any door opening into such a room. (3) Any corridor or room through which a patient is moved during the progress of anesthesia, or through which anesthesia equipment is moved while in operation is to be considered a location of limited hazard. 

§ 314-114. Ventilation 

(a) [Hazardous locations.] All hazardous locations shall be ventilated by mechanical means. Air shall be brought into the room by ducts opening not less than 6 feet from the floor, and removed from the room by ducts opening not more than 3 feet from the floor, and there shall be at least one duct at the ceiling. (b) [Change of air.] There shall be a change of air of not less than 20 cubic feet per person per minute, but in no case shall there be less than 12 changes of air per hour. 

(c) Storage and handling of gases. All cylinders containing com pressed gases, such as anesthetic gases, oxygen, or other gases used for medicinal purposes, whether these gases be flammable or not, shall be in accordance with the regulations of the Interstate Commerce Commission and of the Fire Service of Puerto Rico with respect to construction, testing, and fittings. 286

Ch. T.25 § 314-114 

(d) Marking of cylinders. (1) All cylinders containing compressed gases shall be clearly marked with the name of the gas contained therein. (2) Small cylinders, containing anesthetic gases, approximately 42 inches in diameter and 26 inches in length or smaller, for use on anesthesia machines shall also bear color markings to indicate the nature of the gas contained therein, applied to the shoulders of the cylinders so as to be clearly visible from above. (e) Storage of containers. All cylinders containing compressed gases and all cans containing volatile liquids should be stored in dry locations ventilated as recommended in subsec. (a) of this section. Under no circumstances should these cylinders be stored in the operating room. If stored in an adjoining room there should be a blank wall between such room and the operating room. In all cases the storage of compressed gases and of flammable liquids should be in strict accordance with the Safety Regulation of the 

Fire Service of Puerto Rico. 

(f) Location of containers. Cylinders containing compressed gases, or cans containing volatile liquids, should be kept away from radiators, steam pipes, and like sources of heat. Cylinders containing reducing gases, such as ethylene or cyclopropane, and cans containing flammable liquids, such as ether, should be kept out of proximity to cylinders containing oxidizing gases, such as oxygen or nitrous oxide. Flammable materials, such as wood and fabrics, except cylinder shipping crates, should not be stored or kept near cylinders containing oxygen. (g) Special care of oxygen cylinders. Great care must be exercised with cylinders containing compressed oxygen to prevent any accumulation of grease or oil on either the cylinder or any of the fittings attached thereto. Such cylinders and fittings should never be wiped or rubbed with any cloth, waste, or similar material likely to contain oil or grease. (h) Precaution in filling of cylinders. Compressed gas shall never be transferred from one storage cylinder to another on the hospital premises. (i) Piping systems for gases. (1) Systems for the distribution of gases shall, except as noted below, employ standard, full weight iron-pipesize brass pipe with substantial brass fittings, or approved seamless drawn well-annealed copper, brass, or other nonferrous tubing with approved fittings, 287

T.§ 314-114 

Ch. 31

INTERNAL SECURITY 

protected against mechanical injury in a manner satisfactory to the authorities having jurisdiction. In all piping systems proper allowance shall be made for expansion and contraction, jarring, and vibration. Brass used for such piping shall have a copper content of not less than 83%. Long runs of piping shall be avoided and cylinders shall be located as close as feasible to points of consumption. (2) An exception may be made in the case of nitrous oxide, for the distribution of which iron or steel tubing may be used. (3) An exception shall be made in the case of ethylene, for the distribution of which iron or steel tubing should be used. (4) Where threaded joints or fittings are used threads shall be in accordance with the American Pipe Thread Standard. All joints shall be sweated with solder. (5) Where anesthetic or other gases used for medicinal purposes are piped from building to building, pipes should preferably be placed in a separate tile duct used for no other purpose. If tunnels containing other piping are used for this purpose the anesthetic or other gases shall be segregated in a special baskettype metal duct for this use exclusively, having screened sides, top, and bottom, and conspicuously labeled at frequent intervals "DANGEROUS GASES". Such tunnels shall be well-lighted and ventilated. (6) All piping shall be tested and proven tight at one and onehalf times the maximum working pressure, but never at less than 100 pounds per square inch. Before being placed in service such piping shall be thoroughly blown out to insure freedom from foreign materials. 

§ 314-115. Identification of pipelines 

(a) [Painting.] All oxygen pipelines shall be painted one color, preferably green, and all anesthetic gas lines a different color. 

Where more than one anesthetic gas is piped, the lines distributing the different anesthetics shall be painted distinctive colors. (b) [Charts.] A chart identifying the various gases according to colors employed shall be prominently displayed. (c) Emergency shut-off valves. In addition to the shut-off valves within the operating room, a shut-off valve shall be provided outside thereof in each flammable gas and oxygen line, so located as to be accessible at all times for use in an emergency. These 288

Ch. T.25 § 314-119 

valves shall be so arranged that shutting off the supply of gas to any one operating room will not affect the others. Valves shall be of approved type, mounted on a pedestal or otherwise properly safeguarded against mechanical injury, and marked to discourage tampering or inadvertent closing. (d) General precautions. As defined in subsec. (g) of sec. 314-113, places where compressed flammable gases or flammable liquids are stored are considered as hazardous locations. The recommendations for the reduction of the electrostatic hazard shall, therefore, be rigorously observed. 

§ 314-116. Kitchens 

(a) All kitchens shall be provided with a ventilating system and ducts for carrying off greasy vapors and excess heat. Ducts shall be substantially built and separated 9 inches from all combustible materials, and shall have no connection with other house ventilating systems (i.e., stacks, chimneys, or flues used for other purposes). (b) Hoods over cooking or similar appliances shall be constructed of noncombustible materials to collect the smoke and fumes. (c) Every stove, heater, or furnace shall be connected to a chimney flue. (d) Ashes or any other combustible material shall never be collected or stored in combustible containers. Said containers shall be of metal. 

§ 314-117. Decorative materials 

All combustible decorative materials, including curtains, lamp shades, cloth, and other materials, in the laboratories, operating rooms, and X-ray rooms including floor covering shall be "fireproof". Paper lamp shades shall not be allowed. 

§ 314-118. Smoking 

(a) Smoking is prohibited in laboratories, operating rooms, drug storeroom, and storage room, except in such places thereof as may be specifically designated by the Fire Service of Puerto Rico. (b) Signs reading "NO SMOKING" shall be placed in the laboratories, drug-storage room, operating rooms, or any places where drugs and medicines are kept. 

§ 314-119. Cleanliness 

All premises in hospitals, clinics, and sanatoriums shall be kept 289

T.§ 314-119 Ch. 31 

INTERNAL SECURITY 

free from rubbish and waste materials. Such materials shall be removed at sufficiently frequent intervals to prevent dangerous accumulations. Particular attention shall be directed to keeping clean the depression between stairways, rooms, laboratories, storerooms, dormitories, and kitchens. 

§ 314-120. Fire extinguishers 

(a) Chemical extinguishers, portable water pumps, and any other fire equipment shall be installed by recommendation of the Fire 

Service of Puerto Rico. 

(b) Hospital assembly and conference room shall be equipped with fire-fighting apparatus as determined by the Fire Chief and shall have exit facilities according to the requirements for regular theatres and places of assembly. 

§ 314-121. Reduction of electrostatic hazard 

(a) [Purpose.] The recommendations of this section, which have been formulated for the purpose of reducing the possibility of electrostatic spark discharges and, hence, of the ignition of flammable gases by the energy liberated thereby, shall be followed in all hazardous locations and in all locations of limited hazard. 

(b) Furniture. 

(1) All furniture shall be constructed of metal or of other electrically conductive material. Surfaces on which movable objects may be placed shall be without paint, lacquer, or other insulating finish. All rubber used for caster tires, or leg tips, or for surface finishing shall be of the conductive type or of equivalent material. 

The resistance between the metallic frame of any piece of furniture, or any metallic object placed thereon, and a metallic plate placed under any one supporting member, but insulated from the floor, shall be not more than 250,000 ohms. (2) All furniture shall be equipped with conductive nonmetallic leg tips or casters. (c) Shoes. Shoes having nails which may make contact with the floor shall not be permitted in hazardous locations. (d) Wool. Blankets, sheets, covers, or outer garments of wool, or containing wool shall be excluded from all hazardous locations and from all locations of limited hazard. (e) Silk and synthetic textiles. Fabrics of silk or of synthetic textile material such as rayon, including "sharkskin", shall never 290

Ch. T.25 § 314-141 

D be permitted in hazardous locations, or in locations of limited hazard, as outer garments or for any other purpose. (f) Plastics. Parts of hard rubber, bakelite, or any plastic material which is a nonconductor of electricity shall not be used on any equipment or instrument except where necessary as an electrical insulator on an approved device. (g) Cover for anesthesia equipment. Covers of fabric or of any form of sheeting shall never be used on anesthesia equipment. 

§ 314-122. Electrical wiring and equipment 

(a) All electrical installations and equipment installed in operating rooms, delivery rooms, X-ray rooms, and other hazardous locations shall be installed as specified in articles 100 and 500 of the 

National Electric Code. 

(b) All service equipment, switchboards, or panelboards shall be installed in a nonhazardous location. (c) All overcurrent and other protective devices shall be installed in a nonhazardous location. (d) In any location all permanently installed electrical wiring shall be enclosed in a rigid conduit which is grounded in an approved manner. All wiring shall be installed as specified in sec. 

5014 of the National Electric Code. Special attention shall be given to sealing the conduits in accordance with sec.

5014-b of the 

National Electric Code.

§ 314-141. Construction 

(a) For the purpose of this subchapter the basement or ground floor shall be considered a story if the ceiling is 712 feet or more above the grade level at any point next to the building. (b) All buildings over 2 stories in height shall be of fireproof construction. 291

T.§ 314-141 Ch. 31 

INTERNAL SECURITY 

(c) Buildings of from 3 to 6 stories in height shall have fireproof floors, walls, and partitions, but doors and frames may be of wood, except where otherwise required. (d) In buildings of more than 2 stories all glass between rooms and corridors shall be wired glass. 

§ 314-142. Auditoriums and gymnasiums 

(a) Gymnasiums, if used for auditorium purposes, shall be classed as auditoriums. Auditoriums and gymnasiums should preferably be located on the first floor. (b) For auditoriums and gymnasiums, exit facilities shall be provided in general conformity with those specified for regular theatres and places of assembly. (See Divisions 1 and 2.) 

§ 314-143. Exits 

(a) Each floor, including the basement, shall be provided with at least two inside stairs or doors leading to the outside, and such stairs or doors shall be located as far as possible from each other. (b) All stairs and other exits shall be readily accessible and so arranged that the path of escape to the street is unmistakable. 

Signs (arrows) shall be provided to indicate direction of travel to exits where they are not visible from all parts of the floor area. 

Aisles, corridors, and stairways shall be kept unobstructed at all times and shall never be used for storage. Exit doors shall always be kept unlocked while buildings are occupied. Exits shall be suitably lighted. All stairs shall have landings and handrails and shall lead to the street without decrease in width. Stairs shall be at least 

44 inches wide. All such widths shall be clear of all obstructions except that handrails attached to walls may project not more than 31½ inches at each side within the required width. (c) Winding staircases shall not be permitted on stairs used by pupils irrespective of whether stairs constitute the required means of egress. In stairs where width exceeds 66 inches, intermediate handrails shall be provided. (d) Revolving doors are prohibited. (e) All exit doors shall open outwards and have only panic bolts for locks. If other locks are necessary, they shall never be locked while the building is in use. (f) Corridors shall be at least 8 feet wide. Where doors swing into corridors the clear, straight width shall be not less than 6 feet at any point.

Ch. T.25 § 314-149 

 § 314-144. Decorative materials 

(a) All decorative materials, including curtains, acoustic materials, cloth, straw, leaves, trees, moss, streamers, etc., shall be fireproof. (b) Paper lampshades are prohibited. 

§ 314-145. Smoking 

Smoking is prohibited in all classrooms, laboratories, dormitories, auditoriums, storage rooms, gymnasiums, libraries, manual training rooms, and locker rooms, except in such places thereof as may be specifically designated by the Fire Service of Puerto Rico. 

314-146. Cleanliness

All premises in schools shall be kept free from rubbish and waste materials. Such materials shall be removed at sufficiently frequent intervals to prevent dangerous accumulations. Particular attention shall be directed to keep stairways, laboratories, storage rooms, dormitories, and kitchens clean. 

§ 314-147. Fire protection 

(a) Chemical extinguishers, portable water pumps, and any other fire equipment shall be installed by recommendation of the 

Fire Service of Puerto Rico. 

(b) All laboratories, manual training and domestic science departments, kitchens, and dormitories shall be fireproof; otherwise they shall be equipped with fire extinguishers sufficient in number and distributed in accordance with the recommendation of the Fire 

Service of Puerto Rico. 

§ 314-148. Electrical installation 

(a) All electrical installations shall be in accordance with the requirements of the National Electric Code. 

(b) It is recommended that any temporary electrical installation used for special occasions be removed or dismantled within 48 hours after having served its purpose. 

§ 314-149. Recommendations 

It is hereby recommended that schools, supervised by an officer of the Fire Service of Puerto Rico, carry out a fire drill twice a year, preferably at the beginning and at the middle of the school year. 293

AMUSEMENT PLACES, SPORT PARKS, AND GYMNASIUMS 

Capacity Cleanliness

Fire protection

Electrical systems § 314-161. Exits 

(a) Exits shall be provided on the basis of 22 inches of exit width for every 100 persons. All exits, aisles, and passageways shall be readily accessible and so arranged that the path of escape to the street is unmistakable. Aisles, corridors, and stairways shall be kept unobstructed at all times, and no person shall be allowed to place a seat as an obstruction. Exit doors shall always be kept unlocked while buildings are occupied. (b) Stairs shall have landings, and handrails not less than 30 inches high. (c) The aisles shall have a width of not less than 20 inches for every 100 persons using them, plus an additional foot for easy passage through same. (d) Stairways shall be provided on the basis of 22 inches of stairway width for every 100 persons. If the stairs are 6 feet wide, one of these shall be equivalent to two stairs having a width of 3 feet. (e) Ramps may be substituted for stairways. 

§ 314-162. Exit doorways 

(a) In the main floor and balcony there shall be one exit door 3 feet 4 inches wide for every 300 persons or fraction thereof. (b) Exit doorways shall open in an outward direction and shall be located in such a way that the required width for exit corridors will not be reduced. (c) No doorways on any floor to be used by the public may be obstructed by metal bars, chains, iron grates, or screens. (d) All exit doors shall have an electrically illuminated red sign installed in a circuit independently of the general circuit with the red EXIT in letters not less than 6 inches high and these signs shall be illuminated during the performance. 294

Ch. T.25 314-168 

 § 314-163. Seats 

(a) The seats shall be located not less than 2 feet 6 inches from back to back measured in a horizontal direction. (b) The minimum width of the seats shall be 18 inches measured from the center of the armrests. If benches are used (wood or concrete), the seating capacity shall be determined in the proportion of one seat for every 18 inches of length. (c) All seats, chairs, or benches, except the box seats, shall be firmly fixed to the floor. 

§ 314-164. Capacity 

It is not permitted to sell a larger number of tickets than the number of seats in the amusement place, sport park, or gymnasium. 

§ 314-165. Cleanliness 

(a) Aisles, passageways, ramps, and stairs shall be kept clean and orderly and free from obstruction. (b) Floors shall be kept free from protruding nails, splinters, holes, and loose boards and shall not be uneven. (c) Lockers and storerooms shall be kept free from rubbish and papers. (d) Metal refuse cans shall be provided and used, and shall be emptied daily. (e) Whether inside or outside of buildings, materials which are stored shall be so placed and so piled that they will not create hazards. 

§ 314-166. Fire protection 

Chemical extinguishers, portable water pumps, and any other necessary fire equipment shall be installed by recommendation of the Fire Service of Puerto Rico. 

§ 314-167. Decorative materials 

All decorative materials, including curtains, acoustic materials, straw, leaves, banners, etc., shall be fireproof. 

§ 314-168. Electrical systems 

All lighting facilities in amusement places, sport parks, and gymnasiums shall be in strict accord with the National Electric Code, which calls for two systems with independent current supply. An emergency lighting system in these places includes exits and light- 295

T.25 314 

Ch. 31

INTERNAL SECURITY 

ing equipment commonly called "emergency lights", the purpose of which is to provide sufficient illumination in the auditorium, passageways, stairways, and fire escapes to permit persons to leave the building safely.

SECTIONS § 314-169. Permit 

No license or occupancy permit shall be issued for any amusement place, sport park, or gymnasium until an inspection has been made by the Fire Service of Puerto Rico. 

DIVISION 9. CHURCHES 

314-181. Seats and aisles 314-182.

Exits 

314-183. Fire protection 314-184. 

Electrical installations § 314-181. Seats and aisles 

In every church the seats shall be located in such a way that the occupants may evacuate the building in a short period of time. There shall be not more than 20 transverse rows of seats between the aisles and rows of seats between aisles shall have not more than 12 seats. Seats without dividing arms shall have their capacity determined by allowing 18 inches per person. The minimum width of the aisles shall be 36 inches. 

§ 314-182. Exits 

(a) There shall be at least two exits of a size determined by the Fire Service of Puerto Rico and in proportion to the number of people to be accommodated in every church, as remote from each other as practicable. Where more than 600 persons are accommodated there shall be at least three such exits. The number of persons shall be taken at not less than one per 6 square feet net floor area used for seating. (b) The required exits shall provide free and unobstructed access to the street or other place of safety. 

§ 314-183. Fire protection 

Where the construction is not fireproof, adequate fire protection must be provided. Chemical extinguishers, portable water pumps, and any other fire fighting equipment shall be installed by recom mendation of the Fire Service of Puerto Rico.

DIVISION 10. LUMBER YARDS 

314-201. 314-202. Lumber storage Cleanliness 314-203. 

Fire extinguishers

Smoking 314-204. 

314-205. Electrical equipment 

§ 314-201. Lumber storage 

(a) The storage of lumber in open areas shall conform to the following regulations: 

(1) Lumber shall be stacked in neat, individual piles, the length of which shall be limited by uniform lengths of the stick forming the pile. (2) The width of the stack shall be limited to 10 feet, each stack being separated from the neighboring one in that row by a distance equal to one-half of the width of the stack. (3) No stack shall be higher than 15 feet and each shall have a binder course every 4 feet in height. (4) Each block of lumber in the yard shall be limited to 2 stacks in length and shall be separated by roadways not less than 20 feet wide. The 2 rows in the block shall be separated by an aisle not less than 6 feet wide. 

§ 314-202. Cleanliness 

(a) Lumber yards shall be kept in a clean and orderly condition, free from obstruction which may constitute a fire hazard. 

This will prevent the accumulation of rubbish which increases the fire hazard. Grass or weeds shall not be allowed to grow in the yard. 

Waste wood shall be disposed of and never allowed to accumulate in any considerable quantity. (b) When vehicles or supplies are placed in open storage between buildings, clear access to all sides of buildings, fire hydrants, and entrance and exit doors shall be maintained. (c) A watchman is required to make frequent rounds of inspection around the yard. 

§ 314-203. Fire extinguishers 

(a) All fire lanes and patrol aisles shall be maintained in a clean manner for the free passage of watchman and fire apparatus. 297

T.§ 314-203 Ch. 31 

INTERNAL SECURITY 

(b) The employees shall be familiar with the use of the fire equipment. (c) Hydrants, properly placed in the yard, with sufficient hose, shall be installed. (d) Chemical extinguishers, portable water pumps, and any other fire equipment shall be installed by recommendation of the 

Fire Service of Puerto Rico. 

SECTIONS § 314-204. Smoking 

(a) Smoking shall be prohibited in lumber yards. (b) Signs reading "NO SMOKING" shall be distributed around. the yard. (c) No flammable liquids or oils shall be stored or transported in open containers in the lumber yards. 

§ 314-205. Electrical equipment 

All electrical installations shall be in accordance with the requirements of the National Electric Code.

It shall be unlawful to manufacture distilled liquors, spirits, or alcohol of any kind, by distillation or rectification, without a permit; or to store or keep distilled liquors, spirits, or alcohol of any kind, in quantities aggregating more than 10 barrels of 50 gallons each, without a permit. § 314-222. Building not qualifying for permit

No permit shall be issued for the manufacture, distillation, rectification, or storage of distilled liquors, spirits, or alcohol in any building: (1) which is situated within 50 feet of the nearest wall of any building occupied as a hospital, school, theatre, or other place of public amusement or assembly; (2) which is of wooden construction; 298

§ 314-223. Storage 

It shall be unlawful to store distilled liquors, spirits, or alcohol of any kind in excess of 1 barrel for each 4 feet of floor space; and barrels containing liquors, spirits, or alcohol shall not be stacked more than 2 high. 

§ 314-224. Open flame 

It shall be unlawful to distill or rectify liquors, spirits, or alcohol in any room or compartment in which there is an open flame.

§ 314-241. Definition 

The term "laundry" shall include all laundries, dry cleaning, and dry dyeing establishments, whatever process of cleaning is used by said establishments. 

§ 314-242. Permit 

It shall be unlawful to maintain or operate a laundry without a permit issued by the Fire Service of Puerto Rico. 

§ 314-243. Restrictions 

No permit to maintain or operate a laundry shall be issued for any building: (1) in which the compartment wherein the volatile inflammable oil is used is situated within 50 feet of the nearest wall of any building occupied as a school, hospital, theatre, or other place of public amusement or assembly; (2) which is occupied as a tenement house, dwelling, or hotel; 299

T.§ 314-243 Ch. 31 

INTERNAL SECURITY 

(3) which is of wooden construction; (4) in which the compartment wherein the volatile inflammable oil is used is artificially lighted by any other means than electricity; (5) where drugs, cigars, ciragettes, or tobaccos are kept for sale; (6) where paints, varnishes, or lacquers are manufactured, stored, or kept for sale; (7) where dry goods or other highly inflammable materials are manufactured, stored, or kept for sale; (8) where matches, resin, turpentine, hemp, cotton, or any other explosives are stored or kept; or (9) which is not equipped with a system for storing and handling all volatile inflammable oils used or stored in such an establishment, said system to be approved by the Fire Service. 

§ 314-244. Equipment 

(a) Certificate of approval. It shall be unlawful to install any system for the storage of volatile inflammable oils in any building used as a laundry, unless it be of a type approved by the Fire 

Service. 

(b) Settling tank. At the close of each day, all volatile inflammable oils in the wash tank and extractors shall be transferred through continuous piping to an underground tank. Volatile inflammable oils in a laundry shall not be kept outside the dry cleaning room except in an approved storage system, and shall not be transferred except by pumping directly from an approved storage system. (c) Wash tank room. Each room or compartment wherein a washing tank is located shall be properly ventilated and shall be equipped with fireproof, self-closing doors and windows that can be easily opened from the outside. (d) Asbestos cloths or blankets. Each room or compartment in which a washing tank is located shall be equipped with one or more asbestos cloths or blankets for smothering fire; the number and size of which shall be prescribed by the Fire Chief. (e) Portable containers. All portable containers used to convey goods from washer to extractors shall be equipped with rubber, wooden, or fiber rollers. (f) Extractors. All extractors shall be constructed so that the gasoline extracted shall flow by gravity through the pipe into the settling tank of an approved storage system. 300

Ch. T.25 § 314-246 

(g) Drying tumblers. Drying tumblers shall not be permitted in rooms containing wash tanks, and shall be independently connected with the outer air in the manner prescribed for drying rooms. In no case shall they be heated above 150° F. (h) Fire fighting equipment. Proper equipment to prevent or extinguish fires shall be prescribed by the Fire Chief. 

§ 314-245. Operation 

(a) Settling, filtering, and distilling. All volatile inflammable oil which has been used in the process of dry cleaning shall be settled, filtered, or distilled in a machine or apparatus of a type approved by the Fire Service. (b) Sewer protection. It shall be unlawful to discharge any volatile inflammable oil into any public drain or sewer. 

§ 314-246. Fire prevention 

(a) Extinguishing appliances. Each room or compartment where a washing tank is located shall be equipped with suitable fire fighting appliances approved by the Fire Service. (b) Buckets of sand. All premises in which a laundry is located shall be equipped with buckets filled with sand for use in extinguishing fires. A quantity of sand shall also be left on each floor for absorbing waste oils. The number of buckets and the quantity of sand shall be determined by the Fire Service. (c) Artificial lighting. It shall be unlawful to install any system of artificial lighting other than incandescent electric lights in any building or any portion thereof used as a laundry. All incandescent lights shall be fitted with keyless sockets and all electric switches and plugs shall be placed at least 4 feet above the floor. All electric switches shall be placed outside the room containing wash tanks and outside all drying rooms. (d) Exposed flame or spark. It shall be unlawful to allow any stove, forge, torch, or other device employing flame or fire, or any electric or other apparatus which is likely to produce an exposed spark in any building or portion thereof used as a laundry, unless it be placed in a room or compartment separated from the remainder of the building by a partition constructed of fire-retarding material and provided with a self-closing door; provided, however, that electric motors of the fully enclosed type may be allowed. It shall be unlawful to locate any boiler or furnace in any such laun- 301

T.§ 314-246 

Ch. 31

INTERNAL SECURITY 

dry unless separated from the remainder of the building by an unpierced fireproof wall consisting of solid masonry or its equivalent, of at least 8 inches in thickness; provided, however, that where the construction of such unpierced wall shall be impracticable, the Fire Chief may permit such openings in the wall as may be necessary, and prescribe such protection therefor as in his judgment the particular case shall require. (e) Matches. It shall be unlawful to carry matches into any room or compartment in which volatile inflammable oil is used or stored, and the manager of the establishment shall be responsible for the enforcement of this rule. He shall also see that all clothing intended to be dry cleaned is searched and all matches removed therefrom before being brought into the compartment where volatile inflammable oils are stored or used. Smoking on the premises shall be prohibited and "NO SMOKING" signs shall be posted.

§ 314-301. General rules 

The use of sirens in any vehicle, public or private, of the Commonwealth or Municipal Governments, or the Government of the Capital, or on bicycles is prohibited, excepting in those vehicles used as ambulances, fire trucks, and other vehicles belonging to the 

Fire Service of Puerto Rico and the Police. The use of sirens in radio programs is likewise prohibited; provided, that when the siren of any Fire Service vehicle is sounded, every driver or chauffeur shall drive his vehicle towards the curb on his right and stop the vehicle, in order to clear the way for the Fire Service vehicle. 

§ 314-302. Fire hydrants, parking 

The parking of motor or any other kind of vehicles within 10 feet of a fire hydrant is prohibited. Access to hydrants shall always be kept free and no obstruction shall be allowed. 

314-303. False alarm

Giving false information to a fire station about the existence of a fire is absolutely prohibited. § 314-304. Driving over hose

No motor vehicle shall drive over fire hose lines extended on the streets, except when authorized by the Chief or officer in command of the Fire Service of Puerto Rico.

INTERNAL SECURITY 

Ch. 31 § 314-305. Burning of waste material

The burning of waste material, straw, or any other garbage is hereby prohibited. 

§ 314-306. Inspections 

The Fire Chief or employees designated by him shall inspect periodically those industries, businesses, or other establishments not specifically mentioned in this subchapter and shall require whatever repairs, modifications, or installations are deemed necessary for the safety of the occupants and general public. If said requirements are not met within the period of time granted to effect such repairs, modifications, or installations or if the reasons for nonfulfillment are not sufficient in the judgment of the Fire Chief, it shall be considered that a violation against this subchapter has been committed and the violator shall be subject to the corresponding punishment. 

§ 314-307. Punishment 

The violation of any provision of the rules contained in this subchapter shall be punishable by a fine of not less than $5 nor more than $100, or in default thereof, by imprisonment in jail for a term of not less than 5 days nor more than 90 days, or by both penalties, at the discretion of the Court. 306

"The Weapons Act of Puerto Rico [25 L.P.R.A. §§ 411 to 

454] provides that, among other persons, the Superintendent of Prisons, heads of Commonwealth penitentiaries, jail wardens, penal guards and convict guards may lawfully have, possess, bear, transport and carry firearms, under the regulations provided by the Secretary of Justice. "Under the duties imposed upon and the power vested on me by Article 20 of said Act No. 17, of January 19, 1951, as amended by Act No. 149, of April 30, 1952 [25 L.P.R.A. § 

430], I promulgate the present regulations for the possession, 1969
