Ch. 51

INTERNAL SECURITY 

bearing, carrying and transportation of firearms by the Penal 

Guards in the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico. 

"By reason of the protective function discharged by the 

Penal Guards, as well as by the imminent and constant risk taken by them, the lawmaker recognized the need they have for carrying firearms. There have been several instances of penal guards who have been attacked and injured, and who have not been able to repel the aggression in the proper manner, risking thus, besides their own personal security, that of the other penal guards and the community. Recently a penal guard died at the hands of a released inmate as the result of several stab wounds inflicted by the aggressor. 

The provision requiring from the Secretary of Justice to determine the circumstances and conditions for such carrying of firearms, recognizes that the aspects of the responsibility, danger and risk entailed by the use and handling of firearms for the custody of inmates and the protection of penal institutions are uncommonly greater." 

§ 430-2. Training 

The penal guards shall receive the needed training to guarantee their efficiency in the use, care and handling of firearms. They also shall receive training and instructions regarding those situations in which the use of firearms may be justified. They will not be considered ready to have or carry firearms, nor shall they be authorized to do so, until they have passed the training tests and this be certified on the penal guard personal record. 

§ 430-3. Weapons-Ownership 

The firearms to be used by the penal institutions personnel shall be official weapons exclusively, and the property of the government of the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico. Said weapons shall be issued against a receipt, one copy of which shall be included in his personal record and another in the files of the institution weapons' keeper who also shall keep a registry of the weapon assigned to every penal guard. 

§ 430-4. -Custody and maintenance 

Every penal institution shall be supplied with firearms and ammunition, according to the security needs thereof; the head of the institution shall have the responsibility of the custody, maintenance and care of said firearms and ammunition, and that no defective weapon be issued to the personnel in active service. § 430-5. Armories; security measures

Armories shall be under essential security measures. They shall be located in areas out of reach by the penal population, and the 1969 

Vol. 8, No. 3 306.2

Ch. 

WEAPONS 

T.25 § 430-8 cabinets, vaults or safes where the firearms are kept, shall remain under lock. 

§ 430-6. Guards-Personal responsibility 

Every penal guard shall be personally responsible for the custody of the assigned firearm. He shall report to his immediate superior officer of any defective performance or imperfection of the firearm, of any accidental discharge of it, of its disappearance, or any other similar happening, following the event. § 430-7. Checking

The penal guards shall submit their firearms to be checked by the commander on duty at the institution, when they report for every turn of service. § 430-8. Certificates authorizing the carrying of firearms (a) There shall be a Board, at the level of the Correction Division of the Department of Justice, integrated by the Director of Correction and 2 other officers of the Correctional System appointed by the Secretary of Justice, who shall be responsible for evaluating every application to carry official weapons submitted by members of the Penal Guard, and the Board shall submit its recommendations to the Secretary of Justice, or his duly authorized representative, for the granting or denial of said permit to carry weapons. 

The Board shall be empowered to investigate every case before recommending the carrying of weapons. The Board may also notify the public through the press media of the country about the applications made for carrying weapons. The Board shall follow the standard of not recommending individual carrying of weapon by penal guards who are going through a probatory period, unless warranted circumstances exist which make it advisable or necessary to recommend said carrying of weapons. Likewise, the Board shall be empowered to investigate and recommend to the Secretary of Justice, or his duly authorized representative, the revocation at any time of any permit for possession or carrying of a weapon, as contemplated by this division. (b) The head of every penal institution shall recommend to the said Board to grant authorization for the carrying of official weapons to those penal guards who, after getting the necessary training as provided in sec. 430-2 of this title, have proved to be apt to possess or carry a weapon. The recommendation on weapon. carrying shall be submitted by the head of the institution to the 1970 306.3

The Board shall evaluate every case individually and shall submit its recommendation to the Secretary of Justice or to his duly authorized representative for the granting or denial of said permit for the possession, bearing, carrying or transportation of firearms by the penal guards. § 430-9. Carrying of firearms-Guards in contact with inmates

The penal guards in direct contact with the inmates inside a penal institution shall not carry firearms, excepting those emergency occasions demanding it, and after being duly authorized by the head of the institution for such a purpose. § 430-10. 

Guards doing sentry duty outside the penal structure As the head of the institution may order, the penal guards shall be armed while doing sentry duty outside the penal structure; when conveying inmates under their custody to a Court of Justice, to another penal institution, to hospitals, or any other place directed to; during the search for and pursuit of fugitives, and in any other situation in which the head of the institution may consider it advisable and necessary to carry firearms. 

§ 430-11. Guards off duty 

The penal guards authorized by this division to carry firearms may carry them when off duty, with the following exceptions: in activities where alcoholic beverages are served; in places where the main business is the dispensing of intoxicating liquor to be consumed on the premises; in gambling places or where bets are made; or in places where illegal activities known to them are carried out, though they are not participants. The penal guards authorized by these regulations to carry firearms may carry them in the places mentioned in the preceding sentence, even if they are off duty, whenever they are carrying out functions of an official nature. 1970 

Vol. 9, No. 4 306.4

Ch. 

WEAPONS 

T.25 $ 430-21

The provisions embodied in this division shall not be construed as authorizing the use or carrying of firearms in violation of the Law 

[25 L.P.R.A. §§ 411 to 454]. 

§ 430-12. 

Leather sheath

In every instance when the penal guard is carrying the firearm according to the preceding stipulations, he shall carry said firearm inside a leather sheath, properly clasped or buttoned, fastened to the belt, excepting the case of women guards who could carry the firearm in their handbag or in another fashion under written authorization. § 430-13. -Carelessness or negligence 

Any carelessness or negligence in the carrying, use and safekeeping of the firearms, as provided herein, as well as any violation of the provisions of this division shall be sufficient cause for disciplinary or judicial action, or both, as the case may be. Provided, also, that the penal guards shall be accountable for the value of the firearms if the same were lost or damaged due to carelessness or negligence on their part. The penal guards should take the greatest measure of care in connection with the official firearms, avoiding to leave them in their homes within the reach of children or other persons. 

§ 430-14. Authorization and revocation 

Notwithstanding the preceding provisions, the Secretary of

Justice reserves the prerogative of, after the study of every individual application for carrying firearms, authorizing or denying the permit to carry them. Likewise, the Secretary of Justice may revoke at any time the permit to possess or bear firearms. § 430-15. Heads of penal institutions; compliance with provisions 

The heads of the penal institutions shall be vigilant of the full compliance with this division, notifying the Director of Correction of any violation, who in turn shall notify the Secretary of Justice, submitting at the same time his recommendations upon the matter.

Preamble. Regulations, File No. 1362, set out in this division, contained the following preamble: "The bearing of firearms by the Director of Correction, and by the Wardens and Superintendents of the penal institutions is a necessary measure for the security and protection of themselves, the public in general, the personnel, and the inmates whose custody has been entrusted to the Sec retary of Justice (Attorney General). 

"However, the lawmaker, recognizing the great responsibility and the seriousness of the risks entailed by the use of firearms in the custody of inmates and the protection of penal institutions, entrusted the Secretary of Justice with powers to establish the pertinent rules. 

"By virtue of Act No. 17, of January 19, 1951, (Arti cle 20), as amended by Act No. 149, of April 30, 1952 [25

L.P.R.A. § 430], I hereby authorize the Director of Cor rection, and the Wardens and Superintendents of the penal institutions of the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico, to bear, carry and transport firearms pursuant to the following rules and regulations:" 2 1971

WEAPONS 

T.25 § 430-24 § 430-22. 

Festivities, dispensing of liquor and gambling places (a) The officers hereby authorized to carry firearms shall not carry them during festive activities, whether public, official or private, wherein intoxicating liquor is consumed, nor in places the same is dispensed; nor in gambling places or where bets are made. The functionaries authorized by this division to carry firearms may carry them in the places mentioned in the preceding sentence whenever they are discharging official functions. (b) The provisions embodied in this division shall not be construed as authorizing the use or carrying of firearms in violation of law. 

§ 430-23. Official weapon 

The firearm authorized to be carried shall be an official weapon, property of the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico. Said weapon shall be issued against a receipt and this fact recorded in the Weapon's Keeper Registry. Under no circumstances the use of a firearm, not the property of the Commonwealth, shall be authorized. § 430-24. Board; composition and powers (a) There shall be a Board, at the level of the Department of 

Justice, Division of Correction, formed by the Director of Cor rection and 2 other functionaries from the Correctional System, as designated by the Secretary of Justice, who shall be responsible for the evaluation of every application for the carrying of an official weapon, submitted by the functionaries covered by this division, and they shall submit their recommendations to the Secretary of Justice, or to his legal representative, for the granting or refusal of such carrying permit. In the specific case where any member of the Board should appear as petitioner for the carrying permit, the Secretary of Justice shall be the judge in taking the final determination. The Board shall be empowered to investigate every case before recommending the granting of a weapon carrying permit. Likewise, the Board shall be empowered to investigate and recommend to the Secretary of Justice, or his legal representative, the revocation at any time of any permit for weapon carrying or possession, as provided by this division. (b) The concerned functionary shall submit his weapon carrying written application to said Board, stating that he has complied with the provisions of this division for the possession and bearing of a weapon, and furnishing also information on the type of the fire- 1971 306.7

T.§ 430-24 

INTERNAL SECURITY 

Ch. 51 arm, its caliber, serial number, and the Police District folio where it is registered. The Board shall evaluate each individual case and shall submit recommendations to the Secretary of Justice, or his legal representative, for the granting or refusal of the permit for the possession, bearing, transportation and carrying of a firearm by the functionaries covered by this division. After the permit is granted by the Secretary of Justice, or by his legal representative, to a functionary for the possession, bearing, carrying or transportation of a firearm, said permit shall not be transferable and must be carried every time the firearm is borne. 

§ 430-25. Training 

The functionaries thus authorized shall previously have received the necessary training in the use and handling of firearms. § 430-26. Manner of carrying the firearm

The firearm shall be carried discreetly inside a leather sheath, properly clasped and fastened to the belt, except in the case of female functionaries who should carry the firearm in handbags. § 430-27. Transfer of functionary

When the functionary is transferred from one institution to another, he may carry the firearm with him, providing he immediately takes the proper steps for the transfer of the registration thereof from the Weapons Keeper Registry in one institution to that of the other institution. 

§ 430-28. Maintenance and responsibility 

The functionary authorized to carry a firearm shall be responsible for the maintenance thereof, and in the case of the weapon's disappearance he shall be held accountable for the value thereof if it is determined that the loss was due to carelessness or negligence on his part, irrespective of the disciplinary or judicial action that might be brought against him. § 430-29. Director of Correction; compliance with provisions

The Director of Correction shall be vigilant of the full compliance with this division and he shall notify the Secretary of Justice of any violation, submitting his recommendations on the matter. 

§ 430-30. Penalties 

Any carelessness or negligence in the carrying or use of firearms, as provided by this division, as well as any violation thereof, shall be cause for disciplinary or judicial action, as the case may be. 1971

584-21. Definitions $ 584-21. Definitions

To the effects hereof, the following terms and phrases shall have the meaning herein below indicated, unless their context clearly indicates otherwise. 

(1) “Act”. Act No. 134 of June 28, 1969 [25 L.P.R.A. §§ 561 to 

593]. (2) "Regulations". The regulations for the administration, imple mentation and supervision of the Puerto Rico Explosives Act [this division]. 1971 

Vol. 10, No. 5 309

T.§ 584-21 

INTERNAL SECURITY 

Ch. 59 (3) "Explosives". (A) Shall include any chemical compound or any mixture which contains oxidizing, reducing units and combustible substances or other ingredients in such proportions, quantities or packing that an ignition by fire, friction, concussion, percussion or detonator of any part of the compound or mixture may cause sudden decomposition, with the generation of high heat and highly heated gases, so that the resultant gaseous pressures are capable of producing destructive effects upon life, limb or contiguous objects; or any chemical compound or mechanical mixture containing any oxidizing and reducing unit and combustible, or other ingredients, or any substance that by itself or mixed with another may become inflammable, regardless of the quantities or proportions which such chemical compound or mixture contains, so that an ignition by fire, friction, concussion, percussion or detonator is capable of producing or starting a fire. (B) For the purposes of this division, the following substances shall not be considered explosives: gasoline, kerosene, naphtha, turpentine, ammonium nitrate in its pure form, benzine, carbon bisulphide, ether, petrol ether, colloided nitrocellulose in sheets, rods or grains not under 18 of an inch in diameter, and wet nitro starch containing 20 percent or more of moisture, or wet picric acid containing or having 10 percent or more of moisture. Provided, however, that for the purposes of secs. 26, 27, 32 and 33 of the 

Act [25 L.P.R.A. §§ 586, 587, 592 and 593], the term "explosives" shall include said substances, when it is shown that they are used or possessed for the intentions expressly provided in secs. 26 

and 27 of the Act [25 L.P.R.A. §§ 586 and 587]. 

(4) "Percussion cap or detonator" means: Metallic device containing a high explosive used for detonating or exploding a less sensitive explosive. There are two types of detonators: electric and non-electric. The electric one is exploded by an electric charge. The non-electric is ignited or exploded by a time device, by heat or any chemical agent or substance. (5) "Bomb". Is an explosive substance or substances used within a container with an electric, mechanical or chemical device, or combination thereof, to make it explode. (6) "Factory" means: Every building or structure used for the total or partial manufacture of explosives or substances that may be used for manufacturing explosives. (7) "Magazine". Every building or any other structure, other than a factory, used for the storage of explosives. 1971 310

SUBDIVISION 5. APPLICATION FOR A PERMIT SECTIONS 

584-51. Requirements 

584-52. Issuance or denial 

§ 584-51. Requirements 

(a) Upon applying for a permit to carry out the activities set forth in sec. 3 of the Act [25 L.P.R.A. § 563], or sell, donate, deliver, or in any manner transfer the possession of explosives or any substance that may be used for manufacturing explosives, applicant or his agent shall file with the Police Superintendent the corresponding forms prescribed by him. Said application shall be sworn to before notary or any official authorized to administer oaths, and shall contain the following information: (1) Name, address and age of applicant; (2) Name, address and age of the agent authorized by applicant to receive, use, store, possess or transport the explosives or substances that may be used for manufacturing explosives; (3) Place where, and purpose for which the explosive or substances that may be used for manufacturing explosives shall be used, stored or transported; (4) Name and quantity of explosives for which permit is requested; (5) Signature of applicant; (6) Declaration of applicant and of each one of his agents, stating whether he has been convicted of a felony inside or outside 

Puerto Rico, during the past 15 years; (7) Activities for which permit is requested. 1971 310.3 

Vol. 10, No. 5

T.§ 584-51 

INTERNAL SECURITY 

Ch. 59 (b) In addition to said information, applicant and each one of his agents shall accompany with the application 3 recent photographs, 2″ × 2″, his fingerprints, certificate of good behavior and such other information as the Superintendent may deem necessary in order to properly evaluate the application. 

§ 584-52. Issuance or denial 

The Superintendent shall issue the permit applied for when, to his satisfaction, applicant or his agent show that he has the appropriate means to carry out the activities specified in the application. Likewise, applicant shall show that he knows the activities for which he is requesting a permit. If from the investigation carried out by the Superintendent it is determined that granting the permit could constitute a hazard to the public safety, the Superintendent shall deny said permit.

SUBDIVISION 7. ISSUANCE, RENEWAL AND DENIAL OF PERMITS SECTIONS 

584-71. Issuance or renewal 584-72. 584-73. 584-74. 

§ 584-71. Issuance or renewal 

Every person interested in the issuance or renewal of a permit shall submit all such pertinent information as the Superintendent may deem necessary or convenient for processing the permit application. 

Denial-Failure to submit information -Noncompliance with conditions -Unfavorable experience § 584-72. Denial-Failure to submit information

Failure to submit the additional information requested by the Superintendent shall constitute sufficient basis for denial of the permit application or renewal, as the case may be. § 584-73. -Noncompliance with conditions

Every permit issuance or renewal shall be conditioned to the fact that applicant complies with all restrictions or conditions imposed by the Superintendent. Noncompliance with said restrictions or conditions shall constitute sufficient basis for the denial or revocation of the permit. § 584-74. 

Unfavorable experience

The Superintendent may deny any permit renewal when experience shows that the manner in which applicant or his agent has handled or used the explosives or substances that may be used for manufacturing explosives constitutes a hazard to the public safety.

SECTIONS SUBDIVISION 8. PERMIT RENEWAL AND EXTENSION 

584-81. Filing date 584-82. Extension 1971 

Vol. 10, No. 5 310.6

Ch. 

T.25 584-101 

EXPLOSIVES 

§ 584-81. Filing date 

Any person interested in renewing any permit issued under the provisions of the Act and this division thereof, shall, 30 days prior to the due date of the permit in effect, request it from the Superintendent, following the same proceeding prescribed for the application for permits. If the permit is not requested in the aboveexpressed manner, it shall be considered revoked from its due date, unless applicant shall have obtained the permit renewal before its due date. 

$ 584-82. Extension 

The Superintendent may extend the effectiveness of the permit for a maximum period of 60 days, provided that an application is filed in writing before the due date of the permit in effect. The reasons for such a request shall be justified.

SUBDIVISION 9. PERMIT SUSPENSION OR REVOCATION SECTIONS 

584-91. Suspension or revocation 

584-92. Investigation 

§ 584-91. Suspension or revocation 

A violation of the terms and/or provisions of the Act or this division thereof, or when the manner in which said person or his agent or agents use, sell, store, transport, or otherwise handle or dispose of the explosives or any substance that may be used for manufacturing explosives, constitutes a hazard to the public safety, shall be sufficient basis for the suspension or revocation of the permit in effect.

SECTIONS § 584-92. Investigation 

In the cases set forth in sec. 584-91 of this title, the Superintendent shall carry out the pertinent administrative investigation, and if it is found that the terms or provisions of the Act or this division thereof have been violated, the permit shall then be suspended, revoked or cancelled, as the case may be. The applicant or agent whose permit is suspended, cancelled or revoked may petition for a reconsideration before the Superintendent, as provided in sec. 23 of the Act [25 L.P.R.A. § 583].

SUBDIVISION 12. REQUIREMENTS FOR THE SALE OR TRANSFER OF EXPLOSIVES OR SUBSTANCES THAT MAY BE USED IN THE MANUFACTURE OF EXPLOSIVES, REGISTERS SECTIONS 

584-121. Record book 

§ 584-121. Record book 

Any person who uses, sells, donates, delivers or in any manner conveys the possession of explosives or any substance that may be used for manufacturing explosives, shall keep in his main office or place of business, a register or record book wherein a brief resume of the use and each transaction or delivery shall be clearly stated in writing, including: (1) Date of the transaction; (2) Kind and quantity of explosives or substances that may be used for manufacturing explosives, the object of the transaction or delivery; (3) Name and address of the acquirer; name and address of the agent receiving said explosives or substances that may be used for manufacturing explosives, if any; (4) Name and address of the public carrier that transports the explosives or substance that may be used for manufacturing explosives, and the number of the license plate of the vehicle to be used; (5) Use that the acquirer or his agent shall give to the explosives or substance that may be used for manufacturing explosives; (6) Number of the permit to receive said substances that may be used for manufacturing explosives; (7) Said journal or record book shall be subscribed by the acquirer or his agent, as well as by the person who uses, transfers or delivers said explosives or substances that may be used for manufacturing explosives; (8) The journal or record book shall be kept for a period not less than three years from the date of the last transaction; (9) The persons who carry out the transactions referred to in this subdivision shall comply with the provisions of sec. 584-51 of this title.

The journal or record book referred to in sec. 584-71 of this title shall at all times be available for inspection by the Superintendent or his representative. § 584-132. Monthly reports

Any person who uses, sells, donates, delivers, or in any manner conveys in Puerto Rico explosives or substances that may be used for manufacturing explosives, shall render monthly reports to the Superintendent on each and every transaction or delivery, and the remaining balance, wherein shall be included all data appearing in said journal or record book. § 584-161. Requirements 

The storage of explosives or substances that may be used for manufacturing explosives shall be made in a magazine with adequate capacity, built according to the norms and specifications of the model plan of the Department of Public Works and the regulations of the Planning Board and the Building Regulations [23 

R.&R.P.R. §§ 43-1 to 43-2571], and approved by the Police 

Superintendent. No quantity of explosives or any substances that may be used for manufacturing explosives may be deposited or stored in any magazine which has not been previously inspected and approved by the Police Superintendent and has a certificate of compliance. § 584-162. SUBDIVISION 17. BLASTING OR DETONATING CAPS SECTIONS SECTIONS 

584-171. Storage 

§ 584-171. Storage 

Blasting or detonating caps to blow, explode or cause explosion, in quantities of 1,000 or more, shall be kept or stored in a separate magazine where no explosives or substances that may be used for manufacturing explosives are stored, and it shall be necessary to obtain from the Superintendent of Police a certificate of compliance. Blasting or detonating caps in quantities less than 

1,000 shall be kept in a safe affixed in concrete with label "EXPLOSIVES”.

§ 584-181. Magazines 

(a) Magazines for legally keeping or storing explosives or any substance that may be used for manufacturing explosives shall be built of cement blocks and iron, and shall not have any openings except for ventilation and entrance. (b) A magazine in which from 1,000 to 25,000 pounds of explosives or any substance that may be used for manufacturing explosives are stored, shall be at least 100 feet distant from any other magazine, increasing said distance by 50 feet for each additional 25,000 pounds or fraction thereof. The quantity of explosives that may be stored in a factory building or magazine shall depend upon its distance from the closest building, railroad or public thoroughfare. The distance at which a quantity of explosives or any substance that may be used for manufacturing explosives appearing in columns (1), (2), (3), and (4) of the following table may be stored in the closest building, railroad or public thoroughfare, appear in the same line in columns (5), (6) and (7). § 584-182. Permit 

(a) (1) No person may possess, keep or store explosives or any substance that may be used for manufacturing explosives, unless he has obtained a certificate of compliance from the Superintendent. 

The Superintendent shall carry out an investigation on the qualifications of any applicant and shall not issue a certificate of compliance in favor thereof unless he is convinced that applicant is a person of unquestionable repute and good behavior, that his fingerprints have been taken and or checked in the Police files, and unless in the judgment of the Superintendent there is no reason to deny said application. 1971 

Vol. 10, No. 5 310.15

T.§ 584-182 

INTERNAL SECURITY Ch. 59 

(2) Each person shall advise the Superintendent on forms to be supplied by the latter, as follows: (A) Place where the magazine is built or where it is intended to be built. (B) Kind and maximum quantity of explosives or substances that may be used for manufacturing explosives, stored or intended to be stored in the magazine. (C) Distance from the magazine to another magazine, building, railroad or closest thoroughfare. 

(b) Issuance of certificate. The Superintendent shall, after receiving said report, inspect the magazine, and if he should find that it is located and built pursuant to the Explosives Act and this division, he shall determine, according to the table on quantity and distance appearing in this division, the amount of explosives or any substances that may be used for manufacturing explosives that can be stored in said magazine, and he shall issue a certificate to the applicant who shows compliance with the law, this division and with the maximum quantity of explosives or substances that may be used for manufacturing explosives, that can be stored in the magazine. The certificate of compliance shall be posted on the magazine. 

(c) Modification or cancellation of certificate. The certificate of compliance shall be valid until there arises any cause for its cancellation, as follows: When for reasons of changes in the physical conditions surrounding the magazine, such as the construction of buildings, the operation of railroads or the opening of public thoroughfares closer to the magazine, the Superintendent shall modify or cancel the certificate, pursuant to the conditions changed; or when a person to whom a certificate has been issued fails to pay within 30 days the annual license fee; or when a person to whom a certificate has been issued, keeps or stores explosives or any substance that may be used for manufacturing explosives, in excess of the quantity authorized in the certificate. When the certificate is cancelled, the owner shall immediately withdraw from the magazine all explosives or substances that may be used for manufacturing explosives. The owner or person using the magazine shall promptly notify the Superintendent of any change in conditions. (d) Annual license fee. The owner or person using the magazine shall annually pay, in advance, to the Superintendent, the license fee prescribed in section 584-211 of this title. The Commonwealth 1971 310.16

T.25 § 584-183 of Puerto Rico departments, agencies and instrumentalities are exempt from the payment of said fee. § 584-183. Precautions to be taken around magazines (a) Every magazine storing any quantity of explosives or substances that may be used for manufacturing explosives shall be kept under surveillance day and night, by means of guards, of full age, physically and mentally qualified and a wall not less than 10 feet high shall be continuously placed and maintained 6 feet from the horizontal distance of the magazine, with cement or wooden posts, each one 6 feet apart from the other, and barbed wire spaced 6 inches from center to center, and a gate with patented locks, aside from the 3 locks on the magazine, pursuant to the model plan of the Department of Public Works and the regulations of the Planning Board and the Building Regulations. In one case or the other, the owner of the magazine shall be responsible for having the storage or withdrawal of explosives or substances that may be used for manufacturing explosives conforms to the Explosives Act and this division thereof. In case of theft of explosive substances, or of any irregularity in the safety measures required by law and this division, the Police of Puerto Rico shall be notified, for the corresponding action, within 4 hours after taking cognizance of such fact. (b) The doors of magazines shall always be kept closed and locked, except when they are opened by those persons legally entitled to enter them, for storing or withdrawing explosives or substances that may be used for manufacturing explosives.

Enough openings shall be provided in magazines for ventilation, and they shall be protected to avoid the entrance of sparks, except the magazines for black powder only, which shall be constructed without the ventilation openings. On each end of the magazine, higher than its side walls, or over its barricades, there shall always be displayed, in a conspicuous place, a sign with words "Magazine, Explosives, Danger" clearly printed in letters at least 6 inches high. At no time may matches or fire of any kind be allowed in any magazine. No kind of blasting caps shall be kept or stored in any magazine where other explosives or substances that may be used for manufacturing explosives are kept or stored. At no time may any package of explosives or substances that may be used for manufacturing explosives be opened within a radius of 50 feet from the magazine; nor may any explosives or substances that may be used for manufacturing explosives be kept in it if they are not 1971 310.17 Vol. 10, No. 5

T:§ 584-183 

INTERNAL SECURITY 

Ch. 59 in their original wrapping. No person shall fire any firearms at a distance of 500 feet from a magazine or factory building, or in the direction of or aiming at, any of said buildings or magazines. 

SUBDIVISION 19. TRANSPORTATION SECTIONS 

! 584-191. Rules 

§ 584-191. Rules 

The transportation of explosives and substances that may be used for manufacturing explosives, and blasting and detonating caps, shall be made according to the following rules: (1) It shall be the duty of every person interested in transporting explosives or any substance that may be used for manufacturing explosives to any magazine or from one magazine to the consumption place, as well as of the driver of the motor vehicle used for such purpose, to request and obtain from the Police Superintendent the corresponding permit, complying with the requirement set forth in section 584-51 of this title. (2) Every motor vehicle engaged in the transportation of explosives or any substances that may be used for manufacturing explosives shall be in good operating condition. (3) The driver of a vehicle that transports any quantity of explosives or substances that may be used for manufacturing explosives shall exercise extreme care in driving, and shall follow the safest and less congested route, avoiding vehicular and person congestion, and the presence of anything that may cause an accident. (4) Blasting or detonating caps shall be kept apart from the dynamite, being transported in separate vehicles, and they shall be stored in separate magazines until their use. (5) Upon unloading the explosives or any substance that may be used for manufacturing explosives from the vehicle, the persons in charge of said operation shall avoid all possibility of friction, impact with the explosives or substances that may be used for manufacturing explosives, or sparks which may cause an explosion. (6) The driver of the motor vehicle being used in the transportation of explosives or substances that may be used for manufacturing explosives referred to in this division, as well as the workers carrying, or near, the explosives or substances that may be used for manufacturing explosives, shall not smoke nor carry any device that may cause sparks or a flame. 1971 

Vol. 10, No. 5 310.18

Ch. 

EXPLOSIVES 

T.25 § 584-191 (7) The boxes containing the explosives or substances that may be used for manufacturing explosives shall always be carefully lifted and placed without letting them fall from one level to another, nor slide one over the other. (8) No person shall approach a vehicle carrying explosives or substances that may be used for manufacturing explosives, shall get on it or travel on it, or shall carelessly or recklessly load or unload it, or while smoking or under the influence of intoxicating beverages. (9) No vehicle carrying explosives or substances that may be used for manufacturing explosives shall travel on the public thoroughfares without a red flag at least 18 inches wide and 30 inches long, bearing the word "DANGER” in white letters at least 12 inches high, and placed in the front, on a vertical flagstaff and at such a distance that it can be seen from all directions. It shall also carry signs on its side and rear, with the word "EXPLO- SIVES" in white letters 8 inches high. Said vehicle shall also be equipped with at least 2 fire extinguishers of the 6 B-C type, in adequate condition and conveniently placed in the vehicle for their immediate use. No vehicle may travel the public thoroughfares carrying explosives or substances that may be used for manufacturing explosives during the hours of the night. No vehicle carrying explosives or substances that may be used for manufacturing explosives shall carry any passenger or passengers in or on it. The speed of said vehicles shall not exceed 35 miles per hour in the rural zone. Said vehicles shall also comply with the additional safety requirements already established by this division and the 

Vehicle and Traffic Act [9 L.P.R.A. § 301 et seq.]. 

(10) No person may place or carry, or cause to be placed or carried, in or on a vehicle containing an explosive or substance that may be used for manufacturing explosives, any metal tool, piece of metal, fire, or match exploder, detonator, blasting cap, nor any other device which can produce sparks, flames or heat, except the tools used for the operation and repair of said vehicle. (11) When the platform of a vehicle that will transport explosives or substances that may be used for manufacturing explosives is made of metal, wooden boards shall be used for covering said metal, so that the boxes of explosives or substances that may be used for manufacturing explosives are placed on top of them. The sides and ends of the vehicles shall be sufficiently high to prevent 1971 

Vol. 10, No. 5 310.19

T.§ 584-191 

INTERNAL SECURITY 

Ch. 59 the boxes of explosives or substances that may be used for manufacturing explosives from falling.

SUBDIVISION 20. ABANDONMENT OR DISPOSAL OF EXPLOSIVES SECTIONS 

584-201. Prohibition 

§ 584-201. Prohibition 

No person may abandon or dispose of explosives or substances that may be used for manufacturing explosives in such a manner that they endanger and threaten the public safety. Every person having in his possession or under his control explosives or substances that may be used for manufacturing explosives and who does not have any immediate or future use for them, shall immediately notify the nearest Police Headquarters, so that its authorized agents dispose of them, depositing them in any magazine if they are to be used in the near future, or destroying them if said person does not have any future use for them, in the form and manner determined to that effect. 

SECTIONS SUBDIVISION 21. RECONSIDERATION AND REVIEW 

584-211. Board; composition and duties 

Petition of reconsideration 584-212. 

584-213. On the filing 

584-214. On the notice of reconsideration § 584-211. Board; composition and duties

By virtue of the authority vested in the Police Superintendent by sec. 24 of the Act [25 L.P.R.A. § 584], there is hereby established a quasi-judicial Board, to be composed of 3 members and one secretary appointed by the Police Superintendent. One of the members of the Board will be a representative of the industrial sector affected and will be appointed ad hoc. This Board will be presided by a Police attorney or legal adviser. 

(1) Duties of the Board. 

(A) The Board shall have the necessary personnel to carry out the duties entrusted thereto by the Act and this division. (B) The Board shall have jurisdiction of reconsideration in all cases of persons aggrieved by any order or decision issued by the Superintendent under the Act and this division. (C) Such reconsiderations shall be heard at public hearing, and the person requesting said hearing shall have the right to be 1971 310.20 

Vol. 10, No. 5

Ch. T.25 § 584-212 

EXPLOSIVES 

assisted by counsel, and to produce and cross-examine witnesses and produce evidence. (D) It may issue subpoenas to require the presence of witnesses, the presentation of documents, books, papers or any other tangible property containing relevant evidence. (E) It shall have its official seal. (F) The decisions of the Board shall be by a majority. (G) Its offices shall be located in the Office of the Police Superintendent. 

(2) Duties of the Secretary of the Board. 

(A) The Secretary is the custodian of all documents, books, papers, and property of the Board. He shall certify resolutions, minutes and agreements of the Board. (B) He shall write up the minutes at every meeting. (C) He shall notify all agreements and resolutions of the Board and issue certificates on agreements, resolutions or facts appearing from the books, documents, records and files of the Board. (D) He shall prepare and keep a book or register of filings to be known as the Registry of Reconsideration Matters. (E) He shall prepare the calendars of matters before the 

Board and shall notify the assignations. (F) He shall subpoena witnesses, and issue summons, warrants, and notices concerning matters before the Board. (G) He shall notify the Chairman and the other 8 members of the Board of any petition within 48 hours after its filing. (H) He shall administer oaths to witnesses. (I) The meetings of the Board shall be held at the offices of the Police Superintendent. 

§ 584-212. Petition of reconsideration 

(a) The reconsideration shall be made in the cases and manner prescribed by sec. 23 of the Act [25 L.P.R.A. § 583]. 

(b) The petition for reconsideration shall state the bases of said petition for reconsideration, and shall accompany a certified copy of the order, decision or action of which reconsideration is being requested. (c) The petition for reconsideration shall be filed in original and 3 legible copies. 1971 

Vol. 10, No. 5 310.21

INTERNAL SECURITY 

(d) Said petition shall state clearly the full name of petitioner, his postal or residential address, and the name and postal address of his counsel. § 584-213. On the filing (a) The petition for reconsideration shall be filed in the office of the Secretary within 10 days from the notice of the order, decision or action being challenged. (b) If the petition for reconsideration is sent by mail it will be considered filed on the date it is stamped by the post office. 

§ 584-214. On the notice of reconsideration 

(a) Petitioner or his counsel shall notify the Police Superintendent, through the Secretary of the Board, with copy of the petition for reconsideration, not later than 2 days following the date on which the reconsideration was filed. (b) The Superintendent shall submit the entire file of the record of the case to the Board, within 5 days from the date on which the reconsideration was notified thereto. (c) The filing of the petition for reconsideration or review shall not stay the effects of the order, decision or confiscation being challenged. (d) The Board shall issue its decision on the petition for reconsideration within 30 days reckoning from the date of the filing of said request. If no decision is issued within the term of 30 days. prescribed herein, it shall be understood that the reconsideration prosecuted was awarded in favor of petitioner. (e) (1) Petitioner not in accordance with the decision issued by the Board and the Superintendent, and a request or hearing for reconsideration has been denied, may petition for a review of the Superior Court of Puerto Rico, which petition shall be filed with the Board within a term of 30 days reckoning from the receipt of the notice from the Board or from the Superintendent. (2) The highest authority in the administration, implementation and supervision of the Act and this division lies with the Police Superintendent, but said authority is delegable as prescribed by the Act.

SUBDIVISION 27. CONFISCATION FOR ILLEGAL POSSESSION SECTIONS 

584-271. Grounds 

584-272. Inventory and receipt 584-273. Reconsideration 

§ 584-271. Grounds 

The Police Superintendent shall confiscate every explosive, substance that may be used for manufacturing explosives, and every blasting or detonating cap manufactured, used, possessed, stored, transported, sold, or in any manner conveyed in Puerto Rico in violation of the provisions of the Act or this division. 

§ 584-272. Inventory and receipt 

The Superintendent shall take an inventory and shall deliver the corresponding receipt to the owner of every confiscated explosive or substance that may be used for manufacturing explosives. To safeguard the public safety, the confiscated material shall be deposited in the magazine of the Police of Puerto Rico prepared for such purpose. In any case in which every explosive or substance that may be used for manufacturing explosives must be returned by the Police, the owner shall have to pick it up at said magazine. 

SECTIONS § 584-273. Reconsideration 

Every person aggrieved by said occupation or confiscation may petition for reconsideration from the decision of the Superintendent, following the procedure prescribed in sec. 23 of the Act [25 

L.P.R.A. § 583].

INTERNAL SECURITY § 584-281. General safety 

(a) Only persons of proven experience and ability shall supervise and direct the transportation, handling, storage and use of dynamite and other substances that may be used for manufacturing explosives. (b) The area where explosions are to take place shall be studied in order to know whether families live in that area, where their residences are located and places where they work, such as barns, fields or other places, such as the common washing place in rivers, and also to know the paths and trails so that entrance thereunto is forbidden in times of danger. (c) Every contractor who will carry out a construction where he will eventually use dynamite or any other substance that may be used for manufacturing explosives or for breaking up rocks and carry out other types of road work, shall publish instructions, whether through the use of hand bills or other type of communication, so as to familiarize those living nearby with the measures of safety to be taken, signals and notices of firing so that they obey the same when dynamite is blown up. (d) Once the instructions described in the preceding subsection have been published, and after all persons have moved to strategic places (which shall include all paths leading to the affected area), a bugle shall be blown half an hour before firing, so as to warn the neighbors of said area to move to safer places previously designated by the contractor. At that time, the contractor shall send his personnel to inspect the affected area to ascertain that all persons have left the danger zone. The bugle shall be blown 3 times, for one minute each time, with 30 seconds of silence in between each blow.*

The purpose of this second signal is to warn the employer's personnel that only 5 minutes remain for the firing and that they must leave the area. Likewise, personnel stationed in the neighborhood where persons and vehicles move shall suspend all traffic immediately. (e) The contractor shall draw up a plan for the use of the guards entrusted with this work, showing the places intended to be dynamited, at least 72 hours before the date and exact time of firing. In that manner the inspector shall have enough time to make all pertinent arrangements and inspect the place where the firings 

The text in Spanish contains the following sentence: "Cinco minutos antes del disparo se volverá a sonar la corneta, esta vez será 2 minutos contínuos." 1971 

Vol. 10, No. 5 310.26

Ch. 

EXPLOSIVES 

T.25 § 584-282 are to take place and investigate if all safety measures applying in such cases have been complied with. (f) A second signal shall be made one minute before firing, which will constitute a second warning. (g) After the explosion, and once the dynamiter has carried out an inspection to make sure that there has been no backfiring, and that there are no rocks or stones which may affect the safety of the persons, he shall give a last signal indicating the all clear. This process shall be explained to all persons that may be affected by the firing before it is carried out. (h) Once the persons affected are notified of the date and exact time of a firing, said plans shall not be changed, so as to avoid having the notified persons become confused as to the date and time of the firing. (i) In those places where buildings or houses are located, and animals and persons move, small protecting meshes and sand bars shall be used in order to reduce the possibility of rocks and stones flying and affecting the safety thereof. 

§ 584-282. Storage 

(a) Before explosives or any substance that may be used for manufacturing explosives are brought into the project area, the engineer and/or person in charge of the project shall give his approval. (b) Different magazines shall be used for the storage of dynamite and blasting caps. Said magazines shall be built following the norms and specifications of the model plan of the Department of Public Works and the regulations of the Planning Board and the 

Building Regulations [23 R.&R.P.R. §§ 43-1 to 43-2571], and after the corresponding permit of the Police Superintendent has been obtained. (c) Boxes containing explosives or substances that may be used for manufacturing explosives shall be placed in the magazine so that the ones stored longer are used first. (d) Having matches, firearms, open flames or any other device which produces sparks, or any substance that may be used for manufacturing explosives, less than 100' from the magazine is hereby prohibited. (e) Storing explosives or any substance that may be used for manufacturing explosives, or fuses, in a humid or wet place or close 1971 310.27 

Vol. 10, No. 5

T.§ 584-282 

INTERNAL SECURITY 

Ch. 59 to oils, gasoline, fluid or solutions for cleaning vapor tubing, stoves or other sources of heat, is hereby prohibited. (f) Storing a metal causing sparks or tools made of metal in a magazine is hereby prohibited. (g) Smoking, carrying matches, open lights or other forms of fire or flames inside a magazine or close thereto is hereby prohibited. (h) The accumulation of leaves, grass, bushes or rubbish within a radius of 25' around a magazine is hereby prohibited. (i) If the explosives or substances that may be used for manufacturing explosives become deteriorated and nitroglycerin gets on the floor of the magazine, the manufacturer or his representative shall be consulted and the floor shall be washed with a solution specially prepared therefor, so as to render the nitroglycerin insensible. 

§ 584-283. Handling 

(a) Opening boxes of explosives or of any substance that may be used for manufacturing explosives within 50′ of a magazine, or using metal tools causing sparks for opening said boxes, is hereby prohibited. (b) Smoking or carrying matches, kerosene lamps or any other form of firearm or flame near places where explosives or substances that may be used for manufacturing explosives are being handled or used is hereby prohibited. (c) Carrying explosives or any substance that may be used for manufacturing explosives in the pockets of the clothing being worn or in any other part of the body is hereby prohibited. (d) Striking, or trying to alter, take out or examine the contents of the common electric blasting caps or trying to pull out the wiring thereof is hereby prohibited. (e) The presence of children or any nonauthorized or unnecessary personnel in places where explosives or substances that may be used for manufacturing explosives are handled or used is hereby prohibited. (f) All boxes or containers of explosives or substances that may be used for manufacturing explosives shall be covered after use. (g) Inserting into the open end of the caps anything other than the fuse is hereby prohibited. 1971 

Vol. 10, No. 5 310.28

Ch. 

EXPLOSIVES 

T.25 § 584-284 (h) Handling, using or remaining near explosives or substances that may be used for manufacturing explosives during or near an electric storm is hereby prohibited. (i) Using explosives or substances that may be used for manufacturing explosives, or equipment for blowing up, that show signs of deterioration or damage is hereby prohibited. (j) Using fuses, common or electric blasting caps, or any other explosive or substance that may be used for manufacturing explosives after they have become wet, even after they have been dried, is hereby prohibited. 

§ 584-284. Perforation and charge 

(a) All drill holes shall be of a larger diameter than that of the cartridge of explosives to be used. (b) Drill holes shall not be made in an area where firing took place, until the blown-up drills have been examined so as to find out if some charges have failed. Do not try to drill or sledge the rock if there are unexploded explosives or substances that may be used for manufacturing explosives. (c) Before charging the drill holes with explosives or substances that may be used for manufacturing explosives, they shall be inspected to see if they are wet or contain water. (d) If any water is found inside the hole it should be dried as soon as possible before charging it. (e) Taking out explosives or substances that may be used for manufacturing explosives from their cartridge and ramming dynamite taken out of said cartridges is hereby prohibited. (f) Using metallic tools of any kind for ramming is hereby prohibited. Wooden tools not having any uncovered metal part shall always be used. (g) The front of the rock should always be examined before perforation, so as to discover the presence of any unexploded explosives or substances that may be used for manufacturing explosives. (h) All drill holes shall be carefully examined before charging, so as to find out their condition, using therefor a wood rammer or measuring tape. (i) Piling remaining explosives or substances that may be used. for manufacturing explosives within the working zone while the drill holes are being charged is hereby prohibited. 1971 310.29 

Vol. 10, No. 5

T:§ 584-284 

INTERNAL SECURITY 

Ch. 59 (j) Before inserting the rest of the explosive charge, the line of the detonating Primacord fuse shall be cut off the coil once it enters the drill hole. (k) Drill holes shall not be charged with explosives or substances that may be used for manufacturing explosives after reaming (enlarging the drill hole) or upon ending the perforation, without first making sure that it is fresh and does not contain hot metal nor burning or smoking material. Temperatures exceeding 150° and (65.5°C) are dangerous. (1) Perforating a drill hole near another drill hole charged with explosives or substances that may be used for manufacturing explosives is hereby prohibited. (m) Cartridges, explosives or substances that may be used for manufacturing explosives shall not be forcefully pushed to introduce them into the drill hole or to pass them through an obstruction in the drill hole. (n) Primer should not be perforated, deformed or ill treated, or allowed to fall, or heavy loads allowed to fall on it. (0) The person or persons engaged in the charging operation should avoid having part or parts of their body exposed over the drill hole being charged, or placing themselves in the direction of the drill hole. § 584-285. Before and after firing (a) No one should return to the firing area until all smoke and gases have dissipated. (b) A failure shall not be investigated too soon. Comply with recognized ordinances and regulations or, in their absence, wait at least one hour. (c) A charge of explosives or substances that may be used for manufacturing explosives which has failed shall not be perforated, passed through or taken out. Failures shall be handled only under the direction of a qualified and experienced person. 

§ 584-286. Firing electrically 

(a) The wiring shall not be uncoiled nor the electric blasting caps used during dust whirls or close to other sources of high charges of static electricity. (b) The wiring shall not be uncoiled nor the electric exploders used near radio-frequency transmissions, except at a safe distance. 

Consult the manufacturer. 1971 

Vol. 10, No. 5 310.30

Ch. 

EXPLOSIVES 

T.25 § 584-287 (c) The firing circuit shall be checked totally isolated from the floor or from other conductors such as bare wire, rails, tubing and other means of carrying disperse currents. (d) No electric wires or coils shall be placed close to electric exploders of explosives or substances that may be used for manufacturing explosives until the very moment of preparing the explosion, and then only for this purpose. (e) All electric detonating caps shall be tested, one by one or connected in a circuit, using only the galvanometer specially designed for this purpose. (f) No electric exploders shall be used in the same circuit if manufactured by different manufacturers or, if of a different style or operation but manufactured by the same manufacturer, except when the manufacturer has approved said procedures. (g) No electric exploders circuit shall be fired with less than the minimum current specified by the manufacturer. (h) Before making an electric connection it shall be ascertained that the ends of the wires are completely clean. (i) The wires of the electric exploder or of condition shall always be maintained in short circuit until the blasting for the shot is ready. § 584-287. Firing with fuse (a) The fuse shall always be handled with care, without harming the cover. (b) No short fuse nor lays smaller than 2 feet (60 cm.) shall be used. Know the time it takes for the fuse to burn, and check it so that you will have time to reach a safe place. (c) The fuse shall not be shortened except immediately before inserting it into the detonating cap. Cut 3 or 4 centimeters off the tip to make sure that it is dry. Cut the fuse and angle using a sharpened and clean knife or blade. Insert the fuse until touching again the charge of detonating caps and once it has been placed, avoid twisting it. (d) Always attach blasting caps to the fuse with the proper equipment. Make sure the blasting cap is well tied to the fuse. (e) The fuse shall be lit with an appropriate lighter. If a safety match is not used, the end of the fuse should be split and the head of the match inserted within the crack. Then strike the head of the match against a surface, to light the fuse. 1971 310.31 

Vol. 10, No. 5

T.§ 584-287 Ch. 59 

INTERNAL SECURITY 

(f) The fuse shall not be lit before the explosives or substance that may be used for manufacturing explosives is covered with enough plug to prevent the sparks or heads of matches from making contact with the explosive. (g) No explosives or substances that may be used for manufacturing explosives shall be held in the hand when lighting the fuse. 

§ 584-288. Underground works 

(a) Explosives of the type called "permissible" or "permitted", or substances that may be used for manufacturing explosives, shall be used in the manner prescribed for this type of explosive or substance that may be used for manufacturing explosives. (b) No excessive amount of explosives or substances that may be used for manufacturing explosives shall be carried into the same tunnel. (c) No blasting powder or lump powder shall be used in the coal mines in the same drill hole with "permissible" explosives or any other dynamite or substance that may be used for manufacturing explosives. § 584-289. During the preparation of the primer (a) Primers shall not be prepared inside a magazine or near excessive quantities of explosives or substances that may be used for manufacturing explosives, nor shall a larger amount of primers be prepared than that to be used immediately. (b) A detonating cap or an electric cap shall not be forced inside a dynamite cartridge. Insert the cartridge shell inside a hole in the cartridge with a plier adequate for said purpose, which may be made of wood, copper, bronze or any metal alloy that does not produce sparks. (c) Primers shall be made according to proven and established methods, and it shall be ascertained that the cartridge shell is completely enclosed in the dynamite cartridge. Also make certain that during the charge there is no tension of the wires and the cartridge shell. § 584-290. Getting rid of explosives (a) Explosives or substances that may be used for manufacturing explosives shall not be abandoned. (b) Explosives or substances that may be used for manufacturing explosives shall not be destroyed or disposed of except under approved methods. Consult the manufacturer. 1971 

Vol. 10, No. 5 310.32

Ch. 

EXPLOSIVES 

T.25 584-293 (c) Explosives or substances that may be used for manufacturing explosives, cartridges, empty boxes, liners and other materials used for packing explosives or substances that may be used for manufacturing explosives shall not be left within the reach of children or nonauthorized persons or domestic animals. (d) Wooden, paper or fibrous materials used for packing explosives or substances that may be used for manufacturing explosives shall not be burned in a stove, stack or any other enclosed place, nor shall they be used for any other purpose. Said materials shall be burned in an isolated place, outdoors, and no one shall approach within 100 feet (30 meters) thereof once the material is burning. (e) Noncompliance with these safety provisions shall constitute a violation of the Law or of this division and shall be sufficient basis for the cancellation by the Superintendent of any permit or application granted or approved.

§ 584-292. Constitutional interpretation 

The provisions of this division are individual. Thus, in case any provisions, subdivision, section, clause, rule, or part hereof, or the application thereof to any juridic or natural person or circumstance is challenged or declared unconstitutional or void, said judgment or invalidity shall not affect the rest of this division or the application of the rest of the provisions hereof, but its effect shall be limited to said provisions, subdivision, section, clause, rule, or part hereof thus declared unconstitutional. § 584-293. § 904-1. Purpose 

To provide a procedure for hearings and review of cases brought before the Puerto Rico Crime Commission involving refusal or termination of subgrants for law enforcement projects.

§ 904-3. Definition of terms 

For the purpose of this division the following terms shall have the meanings hereinafter expressed: 

(1) "Commission": The Crime Commission of the Common wealth of Puerto Rico. (2) "Executive Director": Executive Director of the Crime Commission of the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico. (3) "Subgrant": Financial assistance for the development of law enforcement activities granted or provided by the Puerto Rico 

Crime Commission from Federal and/or Commonwealth of Puerto 

Rico funds. (4) "Applicant": Any unit of government of the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico, private nonprofit organizations or institutions requesting funds for the development of law enforcement activities. (5) "Subgrantee": An applicant to whom funds have been granted by the Puerto Rico Crime Commission. (6) "Denial": Disapproval by the Puerto Rico Crime Commission of an application for funds for the development of law enforcement activities.

§ 904-4. Notice 

(a) The Commission will notify the applicant or subgrantee either by: (1) certified mail with return receipt requested, (2) telegram, or (3) special messenger, that the financial assistance has been denied or terminated. (b) The notice shall advise the applicant or subgrantee of the action taken and the reason for such action. (c) Notice of denial or termination of financial assistance should be issued to the applicant or subgrantee within 10 days following such action taken by the Commission. § 904-5. Request for hearing

Within 30 days after receiving the notice the applicant or subgrantee may file with the Executive Director a written petition to the Commission requesting a hearing to plead in support of the 1971 

 310.37

T.§ 904-5 

INTERNAL SECURITY 

Ch. 91 need of establishing or continuing the law enforcement activities for which funds were requested and/or granted originally. 

§ 904-6. Hearing procedure 

(a) Time and place. (1) The Commission through its Executive Director will designate the date of the hearing to take place within 30 days of receipt of such request, or at any later date mutually agreed upon. 

However, this period should never exceed 60 days. (2) The Executive Director will designate the place where the hearing is to be held, unless the parties mutually agree otherwise on this matter. (b) Official notice of hearing. (1) The applicant or subgrantee will be officially informed of the time and place designated for the hearing at least 10 days notice. (2) Notice of the hearing can be served personally, by certified mail with return receipt requested or by telegram. (c) Hearing officer. (1) The hearing shall be presided by a hearing officer appointed by the President of the Commission. (2) The hearing officer could be a public officer versed in administrative law, preferably a lawyer. (3) The hearing officer shall decide on any question of fact and issues of law that may arise, as well as on the admission of evidence. The rules of evidence and of procedure shall not be strictly followed as they are applied in the Courts of Puerto Rico. (4) He may, at his discretion, apply such rules in specific cases where their application may result in the furtherance of the public interest. (d) Proceeding for conducting hearing. (1) The applicant or subgrantee has the burden of proof. 

However, he may be represented and/or advised by a legal counsel. (2) Every applicant or subgrantee appearing at the hearing will do so personally, and may present oral and/or expert testimony as well as documents, books, papers or any other material containing relevant data. (3) Records of the proceedings shall be taken in shorthand or by any electronic device. 1971 

310.38

Ch. T.25 904-10 

COMMITTEE TO FIGHT CRIME § 904-7. Hearing officer report 

(a) The hearing officer shall submit a report of the proceedings to the Commission within 20 days after the termination of the hearing. Excerpts of each oral testimony rendered and a description of supporting data accepted during the proceedings are to be compiled in his report. (b) The findings of fact and conclusions of law should be stated separately with sustained recommendations that the hearing officer may deem appropriate. (c) The findings of fact shall be based exclusively on the evidence submitted. 

§ 904-8. Commission adjudication 

(a) After receiving the hearing officer's report the Commission or the Committee appointed for such purpose shall make a decision on the matter. (b) The Commission or the Committee may either accept, modify or reject the recommendations of the hearing officer. In case of a rejection the Commission or the Committee shall order another hearing. (c) A copy of the decision shall be mailed to the applicant or subgrantee not later than 40 days after the closing of the hearing. 

§ 904-9. Request for rehearing 

(a) Applicant or subgrantee may, upon justified grounds, file with the Commission a petition for rehearing within 15 days after the notification of such decision. (b) The petition must be made in writing, must state in detail the reason for seeking a review or additional available information considered pertinent to the matter involved that makes it advisable or necessary to hold such rehearing. 

§ 904-10. Rehearing procedure 

(a) Time and place. The Commission or the Committee appointed for such purposes will designate the date and place of the rehearing within 20 days of receipt of such request. (b) Official notice of the rehearing. The applicant or subgrantee will be given 10 days notice of the time and place of the rehearing. 

The notice may be served personally, by certified mail with return receipt requested or by telegram. 1971 

 310.39

T.25 904 Ch. 91 

INTERNAL SECURITY 

(c) Proceeding for conducting rehearing. (1) The Commission or Committee may, at its discretion, allow parties to make an oral presentation and/or allow the filing of briefs and arguments. Applicant or subgrantee shall have the right to be represented by counsel or other authorized representative. (2) On all the rehearings the Commission or Committee shall meet as many times as it may deem necessary. (3) The Commission or the Committee may, on the basis of the new evidence submitted, affirm, modify or revoke its previous decision. (4) Records of the rehearing shall be taken in shorthand or by any electronic device. § 904-11. Notification of the final action of the Commission (a) The Commission shall furnish to applicant or subgrantee, by certified mail with return receipt requested, or telegram or personally served, copy of its decision. (b) It will be rendered not later than 10 days after the conclusion of the rehearing of the case. (c) The decision of the Commission shall be final and shall not be subject to further reconsideration. § 904-12. Effective date

This division shall become effective and will have force of law after the provisions of Act No. 112 of June 30, 1957, known as the 

"Rules and Regulations Act of 1958" [3 L.P.R.A. §§ 1041 to 1059], as amended, have been complied with.

204-11. Duties and powers of Presiding Officer and counsel of Commissioner 204-12. 

Witnesses and subpoenas § 204-1. Filing of complaint 

(a) Any person may file before the Commissioner a complaint charging violations to the Insurance Code [26 L.P.R.A.] and its 

Regulations [this subchapter]. Such complaint shall be made in writing. (b) The complaint shall contain the full name and the corporate name, in the case of a legal person, the address of the complainant and the respondent, and a clear and concise statement of the facts upon which the complaint is based. (c) Following the filing of a complaint the Commissioner shall cause to be made a preliminary investigation of the charges set forth therein. The Commissioner shall decide whether or not a complaint should be issued. (d) Should the Commissioner decide that the complaint should be issued, he shall order, according to the Insurance Code of Puerto 

Rico, sec. 2.220 [26 L.P.R.A. § 222], a hearing to be held and shall cause a counsel of his Office to process such complaint and serve it with a copy to the respondent, the complainant, and to all persons directly affected by such hearing. (e) Should the Commissioner decide that a complaint will not be issued he shall so notify the person filing the complaint by issuing a "Notice of Dismissal of the Complaint." In the event of such dismissal the person filing the complaint, within 10 days after the 313 [T.26]

T.§ 204-1 

INSURANCE 

Ch. 2 date of the "Notice of Dismissal," may request from the Commissioner that a hearing be held for the purpose of the reconsideration of his order, according to the provisions of sec. 2.220 (c) of the Insurance Code of Puerto Rico [26 L.P.R.A. § 222 (c)]. The 

Commissioner may concede additional time if timely written request is made in which reasonable grounds to sustain it are stated. (f) Amendments. Any complaint may be amended by the person who filed it. (g) Withdrawal. A complaint may be withdrawn only with the approval of the Commissioner.
