§ 204-2. Issuance of complaint; notice of hearing; answer (a) The issuance of a complaint shall be accompanied by a "Notice of Hearing," which shall fix a date and place for the hearing, specifying the matters to be considered thereat. The hearing shall not be held until a period of 15 days has elapsed after the complaint is notified, excluding Sundays and holidays. (b) The complaint shall be issued by the Commissioner in the name of the complainant or in the name of the Commissioner as he may determine. After the commencement of the hearing the complaint may be amended only with the consent of and upon such terms as the Commissioner or the Presiding Officer appointed to conduct the hearing may require. 314

Ch. T.26 § 204-4 

כ, כ. (c) Answer. The respondent may answer the complaint or its amendments. Such answer shall be in writing and shall contain an admission or denial of the facts set forth in the complaint or its amendments together with any affirmative matter alleged as a defense or relied on by the respondent, to avoid or negate the facts set forth in the complaint. Such answer shall be filed with the 

Office of the Commissioner within 15 days after the notice of the complaint. The original thereof shall be signed by the respondent or his duly authorized representative. The respondent shall serve copies of any answer or amendment thereof upon the complainant and all persons who are parties to the proceeding, and shall file proof of such service with the Office of the Commissioner. Any allegation of any complaint or amendment thereof not denied by the answer shall be deemed admitted by the respondent, and the Commissioner may thereupon make findings of facts and conclusions of law based upon such admission. Upon application of the respondent the Commissioner may extend the time for filing the answer. Prior to the hearing the answer may be amended by the respondent. After the commencement of the hearing the answer may be amended with the consent of and upon such terms as the 

Commissioner or the Presiding Officer appointed to conduct the hearing may require.

Amendments. Subsec. (b) of this section was amended by 

1958 amendments, File No. 511, cited under § 204-1. 

§ 204-3. Intervention 

Prior to the opening of any hearing any person having a valid interest in the proceeding and desiring to intervene in any proceeding or hearing shall file with the Commissioner a motion in writing setting forth the grounds upon which such person claims to be interested in such proceeding, and the extent of such interest. The 

Commissioner, if good cause is shown, may permit such person to intervene, appear and be heard in a hearing. The Presiding Officer appointed to conduct the hearing shall rule upon such motion if it is made while the hearing is being held. 

§ 204-4. Motions 

The Commissioner shall rule upon all motions made prior to the commencement of the hearing. The Commissioner or the Presiding 

Officer appointed to conduct the hearing shall rule upon all motions made during the hearing. 315

T.§ 204-5 Ch. 2 

INSURANCE § 204-5. Consolidation or severance 

Whenever the Commissioner deems it necessary in order to effectuate the purposes of the law he may, at any time after a complaint is filed, order that such complaint or any other proceeding which may have been instituted in respect thereto: (1) be consolidated for the purpose of hearing or for any other purpose with any other proceeding which may have been filed with the Office of the Commissioner; or (2) be severed from any other proceeding with which it may have been consolidated. 

§ 204-6. Prehearing conferences 

The Commissioner or the Presiding Officer, motu proprio or by request of the parties, may hold prehearing conferences for the settlement or simplification of the issues or for the purpose of the settlement of the case. In such conference will be considered the issues to be discussed, the position of each party, the simplification of proof, the exchange of exhibits and all other matters which may be of help to the course and final disposition of the case. The Commissioner or the Presiding Officer shall prepare a report, containing the matters agreed upon, which will control the subsequent course of the proceedings. 

§ 204-7. Hearings Hearings shall be held before the Commissioner or the Presiding 

Officer appointed by him. At any time the Commissioner, for just cause, may designate another Presiding Officer to conduct the hearing in place of the Presiding Officer previously appointed. 

All hearings shall be public.

Any person in the proceeding shall have the right to appear at such hearing in person or by counsel. Such person will have the right to call, examine, and cross-examine witnesses, and to introduce into the record documentary or other evidence. Formal rules of pleading or evidence need not be observed in the hearing. In any such proceeding stipulations of facts may be introduced in evidence with respect to any issue. Any objection with respect to the conduct of the hearing, including any objection to the introduction of evidence, may be stated orally or in writing accompanied by a short statement of the grounds of such objection, and included in the record. Any of the parties shall be entitled, upon request made at or before the close of the hearing, to file a brief with the Com- 316

Ch. T.26 § 204-11 

כי missioner or Presiding Officer, who may fix the time for such filing. 

In the discretion of the Commissioner or the Presiding Officer, the hearing may be continued from day to day, or adjourned to a later date or to a different place, by announcement thereof at the hearing by the Commissioner or Presiding Officer or by other apropriate notice. The Commissioner may, at any time prior to the service of his resolution, upon appropriate notice to the parties, direct that the hearing be reopened. 

§ 204-8. Exclusions from hearing 

It shall be sufficient reason for exclusion from the hearing for any person to engage in disorderly, disrespectful or contemptuous. conduct before the Commissioner or the Presiding Officer. 

§ 204-9. Record of proceedings 

The Commissioner or the Presiding Officer shall keep a true and concise record of the proceedings of the hearings. § 204-10. Decision of Commissioner; rehearing (a) Within 60 days after the termination of the hearing the

Commissioner shall make his order or resolution thereon. Such order shall contain his findings of fact and conclusions of law, and shall set forth the action taken and the effective date of such action. 

A copy of such order shall be sent to each person to whom notice of the hearing was given. (b) Within 10 days after notice of the order or resolution of the Commissioner is given, at the written request of a party to a hearing, the Commissioner may grant a rehearing or reargument on the matters involved in such hearing. 

§ 204-11. Duties and powers of Presiding Officer and counsel of 

Commissioner It shall be the duty of the Commissioner and/or the Presiding Officer to inquire fully into the facts as to whether the respondent has engaged in or is engaging in any violation, set forth in the complaint, of the Insurance Code of Puerto Rico or its Regulations. 

For this purpose the Commissioner or the Presiding Officer shall have the power to call, examine and cross-examine witnesses and to introduce into the record documentary or other evidence. 

It shall be the duty of the counsel of the Legal Division of the Commissioner who prepares the complaint to represent the Commissioner and the public policy of the statute in the hearing. For 1962 317 Vol. 1, No. 4

T.§ 204-11 Ch. 2 

INSURANCE 

this purpose he shall have the power to call, examine and crossexamine witnesses and to introduce into the record documentary or any other evidence. For this purpose he shall have the power to amend the complaint at the request of the complainant and make any motion in connection with the hearing, subject to the provisions of this subchapter. 

§ 204-12. Witnesses and subpoenas 

(a) Witnesses shall be examined orally under oath or affirmation except that for good cause shown the Commissioner or the Presiding Officer may permit their testimony to be taken outside the hearing by deposition under oath. Any such deposition shall be taken in accordance with the procedural requirements under the laws of 

Puerto Rico for the taking of depositions. (b) Applications for the issuance of subpoenas may be filed by any party to the proceedings prior to the hearing with the Office. of the Commissioner or during any hearing with the Presiding 

Officer. Such applications shall be timely filed before the date of the hearing specifying the name and address of the witnesses and the nature of the facts to be proved and must specify the documents, the production of which is desired, with such particularity as will enable them to be identified for the purpose of production, and the necessity for the issuance of the subpoena.

§ 204-101. Kinds of examinations 

The Commissioner shall offer examinations for the licensing of agents, adjusters, brokers and solicitors in the following kinds of risks: 

(A) Agents and Solicitors: 

(1) Life Insurance (Including Individual and Group) (2) Life Insurance limited to Industrial Plans (3) Life and Disability Insurance (Individual and Group) (4) Disability Insurance 

(5) All other classes of risks, but Life 

(6) Life and Disability Insurance limited to Industrial Plans. 

(B) Brokers: 

(1) Life and Disability Insurance 

(2) All Kinds of risks, but Life 

(3) All Kinds of Insurance Risks. 

(C) Adjusters: 

(1) Automobile and Casualty Insurance (2) Marine and Transportation, Fire and Allied Lines (3) All Kinds of Insurance Risks.

§ 204-102. Dates of examinations; notice to applicants

Examinations for brokers and adjusters shall be offered the last Friday of every month, but if a holiday, they shall be offered the day before. Examinations for agents and solicitors shall be

offered on the last Saturday of January, March, May, July, September and November; provided that the Commissioner may, for just cause and on previous notice, change the dates of these examinations. Applicants shall be notified in writing as to date, hour, and place where the examination will be held. In any case the only applicants who shall be called to an examination shall be those formally applying for it and whose applications are received in the Office of the Commissioner of Insurance at least 2 weeks before the date in which the examination is to take place and who otherwise qualify for the desired license. The applicant for an agent's or solicitor's license who appears to take an examination on the date assigned to him, failing to pass it, may take it again approximately 3 weeks later, upon written notice to that effect.

SECTIONS 

§ 204-104. New examinations after failing twice

An applicant who fails twice the corresponding examination within a period of 6 months shall not be admitted to a new examination for 5 months after having failed the last examination. The applicant admitted to a new examination shall pay the examination fees as stated in sec. 7.010 of the Law [26 L.P.R.A. § 701], as if it were his first examination. 

Amendments-1966. This section, which formerly was section 204-103 of this title, was amended by deletion of reference to admission to new examination through written application, by art. 4 of Rule III of Regulation File No. 1053, cited in 1966 amendment note under § 204-101 of this title.

SUBDIVISION 4. CANCELLATION OF SOLICITOR'S LICENSE SECTIONS 

204-251. Request for cancellation; notice § 204-251. Request for cancellation; notice

A solicitor's license shall be cancelled upon request therefor in writing filed with the Commissioner by either the solicitor himself or the agent or broker who named him. If the request for cancellation is by the agent or broker, the request shall be accompanied by proof that notice of such request has likewise been mailed to the solicitor, and no such cancellation shall become effective until after the solicitor, in regular course of mails, should have received the notice. Such request by an agent or broker may state the causes for such cancellation, and information so furnished the Commissioner shall be privileged and shall not be used as evidence in any action against the agent or broker or any of their representatives.

cited under § 204-1.

Every automobile club or association operating or organized in accordance with Chapter XXI, as it has been added to the Insur ance Code of Puerto Rico by Act No. 68, approved June 15, 1961

§ 204-712. Records and essential documents 

The following records and documents shall be an essential part of the accounting system of every automobile club or association: (a) A copy of every contract issued to its members or associates, which shall be numbered and kept in numerical order. (b) A copy of the invoice, which shall be numbered and kept in numerical order and shall constitute a voucher of original entry. 

The invoice shall contain the date and contract number; member's name and address; period covered; kinds of services and premiums or fees charged; name of producer, and commission paid. (c) A register of contracts issued. It shall contain the date of entry, contract number, member's name and address, effective date, term, kinds of services, premium or fees charged, producer and commission paid. (d) A register of premiums or fees written and premiums or fees in force. This register shall contain the contract number, effective date and term, premiums or fees written, premiums or fees cancelled, expirations, premiums or fees in force and a distribution of these into earned and unearned. (e) A register of claims received. This register shall contain the date and number of the claim, claimant, contract number, kind of service covered, estimated reserve, columns to indicate if service was rendered or not and date of such action.

§ 204-721. Bonds and stocks 

In the preparation of the annual statement of economic condition. of any insurer, likewise in the preparation of any other financial statement, the bonds and stocks held and maintained by the insurer as eligible and legal investment, shall be valued in accordance with the procedures and instructions established in the manual “Valuation of Securities" promulgated by the Committee on Valuation of Securities of the National Association of Insurance Commis sioners.

§ 204-1003. Correction of erroneous advertisements 

If on any occasion the Commissioner should determine that an advertisement has been released by any insurer, general agent, broker, solicitor or adjuster violating any provision of the Insurance Code, in addition to any other penalty which may be imposed, the person responsible for such violation shall have to publish an advertisement in the same form and manner in which the original advertisement was made, correcting any error incurred. 

Amendments 1960. Section is former § 204-1002 of this title renumbered by amendments File No. 683, cited under § 204-51 of this title. 

§ 204-1004. Definitions 

(a) “An advertisement" for the purpose of these standards shall include printed and published material and descriptive literature, statements, depictions or illustrations used in newspapers, magazines, radio, television, bulletin boards, billboards displayed on public roads, vacant lots, buildings and similar displays whether they are published by, or in the name of, an insurer, general agent, agent, broker, solicitor or adjuster. (b) "Policies" for the purpose of these standards shall include any policy, plan, certificate, contract, agreement, endorsement or rider which provides evidence of insurance. 

Amendments 1960. Section was added by amendments File No. 683, cited under § 204-51 of this title. 

§ 204-1005. Advertisements of benefits payable, losses covered or premiums payable (a) Deceptive words, phrases or illustrations. Words, phrases or illustrations shall not be used in a manner which misleads or has the capacity and tendency to deceive as to the extent of any policy benefit payable, loss covered or premium payable. An advertisement relating to any policy, benefit payable, loss covered or premium payable shall be sufficiently complete and clear as to avoid deception or the capacity and tendency to deceive. 

(b) Exceptions, reductions, and limitations. Whenever an advertisement refers to any dollar amounts, length of time for which any benefit is payable, cost of policy, or specific policy benefit or 1962 Vol. 1, No. 4 334.1

T.§ 204-1005 Ch. 2 

INSURANCE 

the loss for which such benefit is payable, it shall also disclose those exceptions, reductions and limitations affecting the basic provisions of the policy without which the advertisement would have the capacity and tendency to mislead or deceive. 

Amendments 1960. Section was added by amendments File No. 683, cited under § 204-51 of this title. 

§ 204-1006. Method of disclosure of required information

All information required to be disclosed by those standards shall be set out conspicuously and prominently and in close conjunction with the statement or representations to which such information relates so that such representations shall not be deceitful or give margin to deceit.

Amendments 1960. Section was added by amendments File No. 683, cited under § 204-51 of this title. 

§ 204-1007. Testimonials 

Testimonials used in advertisements must be genuine, represent the current opinion of the author, be applicable to the policy advertised, and be accurately reproduced. The insurer, in using a testimonial, makes as its own all the statements contained therein, and the advertisement including such statements is subject to all the provisions of these standards.

Amendments 1960. Section was added by amendments File No. 683, cited under § 204-51 of this title. 

§ 204-1008. Use of statistics 

An advertisement relating to the dollar amounts of claims paid, the number of persons insured, or similar statistical information relating to any insurer or policy shall not be used unless it accurately reflects all of the relevant facts. Such an advertisement shall not imply that such statistics are derived from the policy advertised unless such is the fact. 

Amendments 1960. Section was added by amendments File No. 683, cited under § 204-51 of this title. 

§ 204-1009. Disparaging comparisons and statements 

An advertisement shall not directly or indirectly make unfair or incomplete comparisons of policies or benefits or otherwise falsely disparage competitors, their policies, services or business. methods.

Amendments 1960. Section was added by amendments File No. 683, cited under § 204-51 of this title. 

1962 Vol. 1, No. 4 334.2

Ch. T.26 204-1051 

•2 

§ 204-1010. Identity of insurer 

The identity of the insurer shall be made clear in all its advertisements. An advertisement shall not use a trade name, service mark, slogan, symbol or other device which has the capacity and tendency to mislead or deceive as to the true identity of the insurer. 

SECTIONS Amendments 1960. Section was added by amendments File No. 683, cited under § 204-51 of this title. 

§ 204-1011. Service facilities 

An advertisement shall not contain untrue statements with respect to the time within which claims are paid or statements which imply that claim settlements will be liberal or generous beyond the terms of the policy. 

Amendments 1960. Section was added by amendments File No. 683, cited under § 204-51 of this title.

§ 204-1202. Persons other than Commissioner's staff

SECTIONS § 204-1203. Examinations outside Puerto Rico 

The examinations performed outside the territorial limits of Puerto Rico shall take into consideration, among others, the transportation expenses between Puerto Rico and the place of the examination, lodging expenses, per diems, payment of the assigned personnel, use of telephone, cablegrams, taxicabs, and other expenses associated with the examination. 

§ 204-1204. Time for payment 

The person examined shall make the corresponding payment within a period of 30 days after presentation by the Commissioner of the proper account.

SUBDIVISION 8. INDIVIDUAL EXPERIENCE RATING PLANS FOR AUTOMOBILE INSURANCE

§ 204-1251. Preferred risk rating plan defined 

The rating plan for preferred risks, known as the "preferred risk rating plan", means that every driver, owner or operator of an automobile for private use that is insured against the risk of public liability will be considered as a preferred risk if he has not had, in the period considered for determining the experience, an accident involving bodily injury or more than one accident, no matter if they involve bodily injury or property damage and as a consequence of that: (a) a quantity has been paid, (b) a quantity

Sept. 30, 1963 

337 

Vol. 2, No. 6

T.§ 204-1251 Ch. 2 

INSURANCE 

is separated as a reserve for losses by the insurance company, (c) a deposit is required by law for the payment of a loss and (d) that a civil suit is pending against the insured or applicant. (A) Every driver who does not qualify for preferred risk within the terms of the mentioned plan will be subject to the surcharge provided by the plan. (B) To the drivers covered by this Regulation the rate to be applied shall be the rate as provided for in the plan and the forfeiture of such charges by those drivers who become subject to penalty will not be permitted in any way. (C) In order to get the most strict accomplishment of this plan, every general agent will observe the following provisions: (1) If the applicant is a nonpreferred risk, no insurer shall issue or renew the policy except with the corresponding charges. 

Source. §§ 204-1251 to 204-1255: Rule XLIII formerly XX-A of Regulation File No. 481, as added by 1958 and 1963 

amendments, File Nos. 511 and 857 respectively, see notes under § 204-1 of this title and under this section.

§ 204-1252. Other merit rating plan 

In lieu of the "preferred risk rating plan" described in sec. 

204-1251 of this title any insurer or rating organization may file for the approval of the Commissioner of Insurance another merit rating plan provided any such plan complies with the following provisions: (A) The plan shall be applicable only to automobiles classified and specifically rated as private passenger cars not subject to fleet experience rating plans. (B) The plan shall provide for modifications in the rates to surcharge them in accordance with some schedule of accidents or violations to traffic laws. (C) The plan may provide for the granting of credits in the rates to those drivers with good experience. (D) No plan shall be based on the record of accidents or violations to traffic laws for over a period of three years. 

Sept. 30, 1963

(F) The plan shall be consistent with the rating system filed by the insurer or rating organization.

Amendments 1963. The text of this section is completely new and former provisions relating to drivers not qualifying as preferred risks are now part of § 204-1251 of this title. 

All these changes were made by amendment File No. 857, cited in 1963 amendment note under § 204–501 of this title. 

§ 204-1253. Cancellation or nonrenewal of a policy 

Every cancellation or nonrenewal of a policy subject to a surcharge no matter what the reasons are shall be immediately notified by the insurer or his representative to the Office of the Commissioner of Insurance in the model furnished to him by the office and which shall indicate the following: (1) Number of the cancelled policy. (2) Name and address of the insured. (3) Description of the vehicle, as it appears in the policy. (4) Date and kind of accident (B.I. and P.D.). (5) Per cent of surcharge. (6) Any additional information that the insurer thinks can be useful to prevent the affected person from evading compliance with the mentioned plan.

Amendments 1963. This section contains the provisions previously established in subsec. (c) of § 204-1254 of this title, with the change that the model to be used to notify the Office of the Commissioner, of every cancellation or nonrenewal of a policy, shall be the model furnished by such office. Former provisions of this section relating to rate for preferred risks are now part of § 204-1251 of this title. All these changes were made by amendment File No. 857, cited in 

1963 amendment note under § 204-501 of this title. 

§ 204-1254. Information to general agent

Each general agent authorized to sell automobile insurance will receive from the Commissioner of Insurance the information respecting each of the notifications that he receives. At the receipt of this information by each general agent, he shall not issue any policy covering the risk involved unless the corresponding penalty is applied.

204-1403. General requirements § 204-1401. Letter of transmittal for rate filings

All rate filings shall be accompanied by a letter of transmittal setting forth: (a) The name of the rating organization or insurer making the filing under the signature of a person duly authorized to make such filing. (b) The manual, manual section, page number, rule number and classification or rate of the filing, and if the filing proposes a change or revision, such fact shall be noted indicating clearly the difference from the previous filing. (c) In the case of new insurance and in other appropriate cases, a summary of the coverage contemplated. (d) Statistical data on which it is based, if any, and facts or reasons justifying the filing. (e) The proposed effective date and rule of application. If this information cannot be determined at the time of the initial filing it shall be furnished as soon as possible.

SUBDIVISION 2. DEVIATIONS 

Application for permission to file deviation 

Premium and losses

§ 204-1451. Application for permission to file deviation 

Every application for permission to file a deviation shall be accompanied by information about: (a) The earned premium and incurred losses by the applicant in Puerto Rico for direct business, assuming that the insurance were written at the rates in force when the application is made. (b) The earned premium and incurred losses by the applicant in all states for direct business. (c) The incurred expenses specifically assignable to Puerto Rico. (d) The total incurred expenses specifically assignable to each state. A breakdown by state is not required. (e) The total incurred expenses that are not specifically assignable to each state. (f) Any other information on which the application is based. 

Sept. 30, 1963 

Vol. 2, No. 6 340.2

Ch. T.26 § 204-1501 

Source. §§ 204-1451 to 204-1456: Rule XXII of Regulations (File No. 481) cited under § 204-1. 

Authority. §§ 204-1451 to 204-1456: Ins. Code § 12.140; 26 L.P.R.A. § 1214. 

§ 204-1452. Premium and losses 

The information on premium and losses shall include data for each one of the last six calendar years on which it is available. 

§ 204-1453. Expenses 

The information on expenses shall include data for each one of the last three years on which it is available and shall be subdivided in the categories of commissions, claim adjustments, taxes, bureau and advisory organizations, and general administrative expenses. 

§ 204-1454. Information for shorter periods 

In those cases in which the insurer has not transacted insurance business during the total periods referred to in secs. 204-1452 and 

204-1453, the Commissioner may require said information for shorter periods. 

§ 204-1455. Dividends 

If the applicant is paying dividends, the dividend being paid shall be reported with indication of how it will be affected in case the application is approved. 

§ 204-1456. Forms 

The information required by this Subdivision shall be submitted on the blank forms prescribed by the Commissioner for said purpose.

§ 204-1501. State Insurance Contracts generally Insurance covering risks of the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico, 341

T.26 204 Ch. 2 

INSURANCE 

its dependencies, entities, authorities and municipalities (hereinafter referred to as State Insurance Contracts) shall be subject to the rules in this Subdivision. 

Source. §§ 204-1501 to 204-1506: Rule XXIII of Regulations (File No. 481) cited under § 204-1. 

Authority. §§ 204-1501 to 204-1506: Ins. Code § 12.020 (3); 

26 L.P.R.A. § 1202(3). 

§ 204-1502. Rates 

Rates filed with the Commissioner, and the rates in use by insurers for which filing is not required by law, shall not apply to the State Insurance Contracts. 

§ 204-1503. Quotation of rates 

Insurers or their agents or general agents shall quote for the State Insurance Contracts such rates as shall be deemed to be the most just and adequate, taking into consideration the amount of risk and the reasonable administration and production expenses. 

Due consideration shall be given also to the fact that there will be no intermediaries involved in the placing of this insurance. 

§ 204-1504. Approval of policies, etc. 

Policies, endorsements, and other documents forming part of the 

State Insurance Contracts shall be subject to approval by the 

Commissioner in the same manner as are the forms used for insuring private interests. 

§ 204-1505. Copies for Secretary of the Treasury 

When writing State Insurance Contracts, whether through auction or by other means, insurers, their general agents, or other representatives shall submit with the contract written an extra copy in addition to the ones required for private insurance. This copy, which is intended for the Secretary of the Treasury, may be a memorandum of insurance or similar document stating the risks covered, endorsements, limits of insurance, rates, premium, coinsurance (when applicable), deductions or any other information relative to the risk. 

§ 204-1506. Records of departments, etc. 

Every department, dependency, entity, corporation and authority of the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico shall keep the following records and shall submit the following information: 342

Ch. T.26 204-1506 

(A) Policy Register. (a) Every policy shall be registered in a Policy Register containing the information below: (1) Policy number: (2) Name of insurance agency. (3) Name of insurance company. (4) Kind of insurance. (5) Amount of insurance or liability limits if a liability policy. (6) Effective date of insurance. (7) Policy term (one year, two years. etc.). (8) Amount of premium. (9) Observations: Any comment, observation or note clarifying the detailed information shall be written in this space. (b) The policies will be recorded in said register immediately after delivery is made by insurer. 

(B) Model Form of Policy Register. 

(a) The model form furnished by the Commissioner shall be used for simplifying the compilation of the data requested in subsection (A). (b) The organizations from which the register is required are free to select the kind of paper, size of it, either loose-leaf or bound. (c) It is compulsory and indispensable that said register contains all the information in the model form with identical headings. (d) For a better understanding of its use, brief but clear instructions are printed in the back of the model form. (C) Loss Register. (a) Every claim made to an insurance company shall be duly registered in a loss register, which shall include the following information: (1) Number of the policy under which the claim is made. (2) Claimant's name, the same as insured's name or a third person depending on the kind of insurance. (3) Date of accident or of the event which caused the claim to be made. (4) Estimate of the damages. An estimate of losses is made either by the insurance company or by an adjuster for every loss. The amount of said estimate shall be shown in this column. 343

T.§ 204-1506 Ch. 2 

INSURANCE 

(5) Date of payment, be it partial or total payment. (6) Amount paid. In case of partial payment, every payment shall be individually registered indicating in the observation column that the same is partial. 

(7) Observations: Any comment or note shall be indicated in this space. (b) Every claim made shall be immediately registered and all information completed in such a way that the insured knows at all times the losses had by the insurance company under every one of its policies in force. 

(D) Model Form of Loss Register. 

(a) The model form furnished by the Commissioner shall be used for simplifying the compilation of the data requested in subsection (C). SUBDIVISION 5. DURATION OF BINDERS SECTIONS 

204-1601. Duration 

204-1602. Renewal 

§ 204-1601. Duration 

The duration of binders shall be limited according to the following: (a) Written binders shall have a maximum duration of 30 days. (b) Oral binders shall have a maximum duration of 5 days.

In the case of both written and oral binders holidays are included in the duration period.

Source. §§ 204-1601, 204-1602: Rule XXV of Regulations (File No. 481) cited under § 204-1. 

Authority. §§ 204-1601, 204-1602: Ins. Code § 11.210; 26 L.P.R.A. § 1121. 

SECTIONS § 204-1602. Renewal 

Renewal of binders is permitted with the exception of oral binders, but in no case shall binders be issued to cover a total period for all binders which extends beyond 90 days. 

SUBDIVISION 6. CALCULATION OF CASH SURRENDER VALUES 204-1651. Statements in policies 

204-1652. Amount of cash surrender value 

204-1653. Adjusted premiums 

§ 204-1651. Statements in policies 

Every life insurance policy shall contain a statement indicating the mortality table and rate of interest used in the calculations of the cash surrender values and the paid-up nonforfeiture benefits. 

Source. §§ 204-1651 to 204-1653: Rule XXVI of Regulations (File No. 481) cited under § 204-1. 

Authority. §§ 204-1651 to 204-1653: Ins. Code § 13.280; 26 L.P.R.A. § 1328. 

§ 204-1652. Amount of cash surrender value 

Any cash surrender value available under the policy in the event of default in a premium payment due on any policy anniversary shall be an amount not less than the excess, if any, of the present 346

Ch. T.26 § 204-1653 

כי value, on such anniversary, of the future guaranteed benefits which would have been provided for under the policy, including any existing paid-up additions over the sum of: (a) the then present value of the adjusted premiums as hereinafter defined, corresponding to premiums which would have fallen due on and after such anniversary; (b) the amount of any indebtedness to the insurer on the policy. Any cash surrender value available within 30 days after any policy anniversary under any policy paid up by completion of all premium payments or any policy continued under any paid-up nonforfeiture benefit, shall be an amount not less than the present value, on such anniversary, of the future guaranteed benefits provided under the policy, including any existing paid-up additions, decreased by any indebtedness to the insurer on the policy. 

§ 204-1653. Adjusted premiums 

The adjusted premiums for any policy shall be calculated on an annual basis and shall be such uniform percentage of the respective premiums specified in the policy for each policy year, excluding any extra premiums charged because of impairment or special hazards, that the present value, at the date of issue of the policy, of all such adjusted premiums shall be equal to the sum of: (a) the then present value of the future guaranteed benefits provided for by the policy; (b) 2 per cent of the amount of insurance, if the insurance be uniform in amount, or of the equivalent uniform amount, as hereinafter defined, if the amount of insurance varies with the duration of the policy; (c) 40 per cent of the adjusted premiums for the first policy year and (d) 25 per cent of either the adjusted premium for the first policy year or the adjusted premium for a whole life policy of the same uniform or equivalent uniform amount with uniform premiums for the whole of life issued at the same age for the same amount of insurance, whichever is less. Provided, however, that in applying the percentages specified in (c) and (d) above, no adjusted premium shall be deemed to exceed 4 per cent of the amount of insurance or level amount equivalent thereto. The date of issue of a policy for the purpose of this rule shall be the date as of which the rated age of the insured is determined. In the case of a policy providing an amount of insurance varying with the duration of the policy, the equivalent uniform amount thereof for the purpose of this rule shall be deemed to be the level amount of insurance provided by an otherwise similar policy, containing the same endowment benefit or benefits, if any, 1962 347 Vol. 1, No. 4

T.§ 204-1653 Ch. 2 

INSURANCE 

issued at the same age and for the same term, the amount of which does not vary with duration and the benefits under which have the same present value at the date of issue as the benefits under the policy; Provided, however, That in the case of a policy providing a varying amount of insurance issued on the life of a child under age 10, the equivalent uniform amount may be computed as though the amount of insurance provided by the policy prior to the attainment of age 10 were the amount provided by such policy at age 10, or at expiry, if earlier. All adjusted premiums and present values referred to in this rule shall be calculated on the basis of the Commissioners' 1941 Standard Ordinary Mortality Table for ordinary insurance and the 1941 Standard Industrial Mortality Table for industrial insurance and the rate of interest, exceeding three and one-half per cent per annum, specified in the policy for calculating cash surrender values and paid-up nonforfeiture benefits. Provided, however, that in calculating the present value of any paid-up term insurance with accompanying pure endowment, if any, offered as a nonforfeiture benefit, the rates of mortality assumed may be not more than 130 per cent of the rates of mortality according to such applicable table. Provided, further, that for insurance issued on a substandard basis, the calculation of any such adjusted premiums and present values may be based on such other tables of mortality as may be specified by the insurer and approved by the Commissioner.

Amendments 1960. Changes in wording were made without altering provisions contained in this section by amendments File No. 683, cited under § 204-51 of this title. 

SUBDIVISION 7. DEFINITION OF MARINE INSURANCE 

204-1701. Marine insurance § 204-1701. Marine insurance

Marine and/or transportation policies may cover under the following conditions:

OCEAN MARINE 

(A) Imports. (1) Imports on consignment may be covered wherever the property may be and without restriction as to time, provided the coverage of the issuing companies includes hazards of transportation. 1962 Vol. 1, No. 4 348

Ch. T.26 § 204-1701 

·) 2 A shipment "on consignment" shall mean property consigned and intrusted to a factor or agent to be held in his care, or under his control for sale for account of another or for exhibit 1962

348.1

T.26 § 204-1701 or trial or approval or auction, and if not disposed of, to be returned. (2) Imports not on consignment in such places of storage as are usually employed by importers, provided the coverage of the issuing companies includes hazards of transportation. 

Such policies may also include the same coverage in respect to property purchased on C.I.F. terms or "spot" purchases for inclusion with or in substitution for bona fide importations. 

An import, as a proper subject of marine or transportation insurance, shall be deemed to maintain its character as such so long as the property remains segregated in the original form or package in such a way that it can be identified and has not become incorporated and mixed with the general mass of property in the United States, and shall be deemed to have been completed when such property has been: (a) Sold and delivered by the importer, factor or consignee; or (b) Removed from place of storage as described in paragraph (2) above and placed on sale as part of importer's stock in trade at a point of sale distribution; or (c) Delivered for manufacture, processing or change in form to premises of the importer or of another used for any such purposes. (B) Exports. (1) Exports may be covered wherever the property may be without restriction as to time, provided the coverage of the issuing companies includes hazards of transportation.

An export, as a proper subject of marine or transportation insurance, shall be deemed to acquire its character as such when designated or while being prepared for export and retain that character unless diverted for domestic trade, and when so diverted, the provisions of this ruling respecting domestic shipments shall apply, provided, however, that this provision shall not apply to long established methods of insuring certain commodities, e.g., cotton. 

INLAND MARINE (C) Domestic Shipments. 

(1) Domestic shipments on consignment, provided the coverage of the issuing companies includes hazards of transportation. (D) Bridges, tunnels and other instrumentalities of transportation and communication (excluding buildings, their furniture and furnishings, fixed contents, and supplies held in storage) unless fire, tornado, sprinkler leakage, hail, explosion, earthquake, riot and/or civil commotion are the only hazards to be covered. § 204-1906. Tax on surplus lines; payment

In those cases where the premium on the surplus lines coverage procured is payable in installments during the policy year, it shall be the duty of the surplus lines broker to reasonably determine or estimate the total premium for the policy year and pay the tax on this amount as provided by sec. 10.130 of the Insurance Code 

[26 L.P.R.A. § 1013] and § 204-1908 of this title. Provided, that should the premium estimated or determined result higher or lower than the total premium collected, the broker shall report the difference to this Office within the 30 days immediately following the maturity date of the policy including the amount of any additional tax due on such difference. Provided further that in those cases where the difference results in a credit, such credit shall be granted on future remittances.

The renewal of a surplus lines insurance shall be accomplished following the established method, as if it were a new insurance.

Any license application shall be accompanied with evidence as to the last grade completed by the applicant, in the case of an individual, or by the persons that shall act in the name of the applying entity, in the case of a corporation or firm. § 204-2152. Examinations 

(a) Every mutual aid and relief association shall keep books and records in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles and practices. (b) It shall keep those indispensable and necessary statistics for the management of this type of associations and produce those statistics and statements of income and expenses which the Commissioner of Insurance may require. (c) The accounting system shall include, in addition to those books and records prescribed in subsec. (a) above, those that may be required by the Commissioner of Insurance so that the latter, through his examiners, may carry out the examinations called for by law. 

§ 204-2153. Contingency reserve fund 

(a) Every association shall maintain a contingency reserve fund which shall amount to 35 percent of all direct and indirect costs related to services rendered to the members during the immediate preceding year. The determination of such costs shall be subject to review by the Commissioner of Insurance. 

Dec. 31, 1966 

Vol. 5, No. 10 360.2

Ch. 

T.26 § 204-2153 (b) Said reserve fund will be constituted in the following manner: (1) By the separation, on or before December 31, 1959, of $50,000 in cash or in acceptable investments. (2) By the separation, in subsequent months, of 4 per cent of all dues accrued or collected from the members of the association until the amount stipulated in subsec. (a) of this section is accumulated. (c) Said reserve fund will be deposited in one or more special accounts against which accounts no drawing may be made without the previous authorization of the Commissioner of Insurance, and only for the following purposes: (1) To cover the costs incurred in cases of epidemic or catastrophe. (2) To cover extraordinary expenses, not related to epidemics or catastrophes, duly justified to the Commissioner of Insurance, and only in accordance with the plan that he may authorize for the disbursement and reimbursement to the fund. (d) It shall be understood that above-described reserve is in addition to all reserves necessary for known and existing liabilities, indeterminate, such as reserves for dues collected in advance, reserves for unreported claims incurred, and others. (e) The reserve fund may be constituted only by cash deposited in banks or by investments of the same type and quality as those required by the Insurance Code of Puerto Rico from life insurance companies. (f) In case the reserve fund is created and maintained in the form of bonds or similar investments, said bonds or investments shall be deposited with the Secretary of the Treasury of Puerto

Rico, through the Office of the Commissioner of Insurance. Regis tered securities or titles included in any such deposit shall be registered in the name of the Secretary of the Treasury of Puerto

Rico, in trust for the purpose contemplated by this section, and all securities payable to bearer shall be accompanied by assignment to such Secretary in trust for such purpose.

§ 204-2201. Preferred rate or premium

No insurer, admitted or nonadmitted, shall make available through any rating plan or through any fire, surety or casualty insurance policy form to any firm, corporation or association of individuals any preferred rate or premium based upon any fictitious grouping of such firm, corporation or association of individuals, and no fire, surety or casualty master policy, series of policies or certificates of insurance issued to any fictitious grouping at any preferred rate or policy form shall include any Puerto Rico resident or group of Puerto Rico residents.

§ 204-2202. Fictitious grouping, definition 

Fictitious grouping is hereby defined and declared to be any grouping by way of membership, license, franchise, contract, agreement or any other method or means other than financial control by common majority ownership. Provided, that other groupings may be allowed by prior approval of the Commissioner of Insurance where it has been demonstrated to the satisfaction of the Commissioner of Insurance that such groupings would not result in unfair discrimination.

Amendments -1963. To this section was added the proviso relating to other groupings that may be allowed when it has been demonstrated to the satisfaction of the Commissioner of Insurance that such groupings would not result in unfair discrimination. All these changes were made by amendment File 

No. 857, cited in 1963 amendment note under § 204-501 of this title. 

§ 204-2203. Disability insurance 

This rule is not applicable to disability insurance.

§ 204-2351. Establishment 

Every life insurer duly authorized in Puerto Rico shall establish an adequate reserve to face possible losses in its investment in bonds and stocks due to market price fluctuations or similar causes.

Such reserve, which shall be known as the Mandatory Securities Valuation Reserve, shall be established by an allocation from unassigned surplus and shall constitute a liability of the insurer in its balance sheet.

Source. §§ 204-2351 to 204-2353: Rule XXXVII, Mandatory Securities Valuation Reserve, added to the Regulations of the Office of the Commissioner of Insurance by amendments File No. 683, cited under § 204-51 of this title.

§ 204-2353. Foreign insurer 

This subdivision shall not be applicable to a foreign insurer not organized under the laws of a state of the United States, but which is authorized to transact insurance in one or more of such states.

§ 204-2381. Definition 

The term “multiple line policy" shall be defined as an integrated package of coverages which includes any two or more of the following lines of insurance, or parts thereof, using their customary trade-usage definitions: (1) Fire and allied lines. (2) Casualty and surety (including automobile physical damage). 

(3) Inland marine. 

The term "multiple line policy" shall include but is not limited to homeowners' policies and forms.

Source. §§ 204-2381 to 204–2385: Rule XL, Filing of Multiple Line Contracts, added to the Regulations of the Office of the Commissioner of Insurance by amendment File No. 

857, cited in 1963 amendment note under § 204-501 of this title. 

Authority. §§ 204-2381 to 204-2385: Ins. Code §§ 11.140, 

12.040, 12.050, and 12.180; 26 L.P.R.A. §§ 1114, 1204, 1205 and 1218. 

§ 204-2382. Procedure 

Any multiple line company which is properly licensed may file any given multiple line program by any of the following methods, each one of which is exclusive of all others: (1) Affiliate with any single rating organization which has filed or may file any package the company may wish to write. (2) Affiliate with each of the participating rating organizations which have developed or may develop a so-called (a) "hand-in-hand" 

Sept. 30, 1963

Vol. 2, No. 6 

360.7

T.§ 204-2382 Ch. 2 

INSURANCE 

or (b) "agency" filing procedure for any multiple line package program which the company may wish to write. (3) Specifically authorize any single, properly licensed rating organization which is participating in a "hand-in-hand" or in an "agency" filing to file the whole of any given package (all portions) on behalf of the company when such company is not affiliated with all the bureaus participating in the particular filing. (4) File an entire package independently. 

§ 204-2383. Subscriptions 

If a company elects to subscribe to a rating organization for one or more component coverages of a multiple line package, but to file the package independently under subdiv. (4) of sec. 2042382 of this title, or through another rating organization under subdiv. (1) of sec. 204-2382 of this title, the company shall give such rating organization or organizations appropriate written notice as to the coverage or coverages to which its affiliation with each applies. A copy of such notice shall be mailed to the Office of the Commissioner of Insurance of Puerto Rico and the effective date of such partial subscribership shall be no later than the effective date of the specific multiple line package filing. 

§ 204-2384. Deviations 

(1) Applications to deviate from the filings of rating organizations on multiple line package programs will be treated separately and apart from any other deviations. (2) When the deviation application relates to a filing made in its entirety by a single rating organization, under subdiv. (1) of sec. 204-2382 of this title, a complete copy of this application shall be forwarded to such organization by the applicant. (3) When the application relates to a filing made on the "handin-hand" basis by more than one rating organization, under subdiv. (2) of sec. 204-2382 of this title, a copy of the application shall be forwarded to each of the participating organizations. (4) When the application relates to a filing made on the "agency" basis by more than one rating organization, under subdiv. (3) of sec. 204-2382 of this title, a copy of the application shall be forwarded to the "filing organization" designated by the other participating organizations.

§ 204-2401. Issuing of policies 

Except as provided in sec. 204-2405 of this title, no authorized insurer shall issue in Puerto Rico any individual or group policy of credit life insurance at a premium rate greater than that hereinafter provided. With respect to group policies of credit life insurance in force at the effective date of this subdivision, and subject to sec. 204-2407 of this title no authorized insurer shall charge a premium rate under such group policies for any renewal period greater than the premium rate hereinafter provided, unless it files an application for deviation pursuant to sec. 204-2405 of this title.

An authorized insurer may, without prior approval of the Commissioner of Insurance, reduce any premium rate filed not subject to the provisions of sec. 204-2405 of this title under a group policy of credit life insurance for the second and subsequent policy years, provided that such reduced premium rate is equitable and nondiscriminatory.

§ 204-2402. Maximum premium

The premium rate of $0.75 per annum per each $100 of initial indebtedness is set forth as the maximum premium rate to be charged by any authorized insurer in Puerto Rico for decreasing term credit life insurance and any premium rate now filed or subsequently filed not greater than the maximum premium rate herein 

Sept. 30, 1963 360.9 

Vol. 2, No. 6

T.§ 204-2402 Ch. 2

set forth shall prima facie be deemed not to be excessive in relation to the benefits provided. 

§ 204-2403. Other premium rates 

Premium rates for other credit life insurance providing coverages of a different nature or with a premium basis other than that set forth in sec. 204-2402 of this title shall be actuarially consistent with the maximum premium rate set forth in sec. 204–2402 of this title. 

§ 204-2404. Refunds 

In the event of the termination of the insurance prior to the scheduled maturity date of the indebtedness, any refund of the amount paid by the debtor for insurance shall be promptly paid or credited to the person entitled to such refund; provided, however, that no authorized insurer shall have to make any refund if the amount thereof is less than one dollar. § 204-2405. Deviation from the maximum premium rate

Section 204-2402 of this title, notwithstanding, any authorized insurer may file with the Commissioner an application for deviation from the maximum premium rate set forth in said section. Said application for deviation shall contain the basis and information in support of the proposed deviation. § 204-2406. Premium rate schedules

Every insurer authorized to write credit life insurance shall file with the Commissioner of Insurance the premium rate schedules and policy forms to be used in relation with such insurance. Any revision of such premium rate schedules shall be filed before it may become effective. The filing or revision of such premium rate schedules shall be subject to the applicable provisions of this subdivision. § 204-2407. Applicability

This subdivision shall be applicable to any contract commencing or renewed ninety (90) days after the effective date of this subdivision.

§ 204-2421. Instruction to agents 

All insurers licensed to transact life insurance business in Puerto Rico are required to issue written instruction to their agents regarding the rules and safeguards which are to be observed by them in the preparation and use of cost illustrations, comparisons, advertising and other promotional material. The insurers shall require their agents, through such instructions, to furnish their prospects with a proper, full and clear presentation of the costs, benefits and other policy provisions. A copy of such instructions must be kept on file in the office of the general agent or manager of each insurer in Puerto Rico and made available on request of the Commissioner of Insurance. 

Source. §§ 204-2421 to 204-2423: Rule XLII, Replacement of Existing Life Insurance Policies, added to the Regulations of the Office of the Commissioner of Insurance by amendment File No. 857, cited in 1963 amendment note under 

§ 204-501 of this title. 

Authority. §§ 204-2421 to 204-2423: Ins. Code § 27.150; 26 L.P.R.A. § 2715. 

§ 204-2422. Replacement of policy 

Every licensee authorized to solicit life insurance in Puerto Rico, in soliciting coverage where the replacement or other change in an existing policy or policies is suggested, must present to the prospect a written proposal signed by him setting forth all the facts, including a clear and concise summary of the advantages and disadvantages in making the replacement or change. A copy of this proposal must be retained by the licensee for not less than two years and he must submit it on request of the Commissioner or make it available to his examiners or employees. § 204-2423. Notice to insured

When such replacement or change in an existing policy or policies is suggested, the licensee must deliver to the insured the following notice: 

Notice to Policyholder (1) This notice to you is for your protection and is required by 

Rule XLII of the Regulation of the Commissioner of Insurance of Puerto Rico [§§ 204–2421 to 204–2423 of this title]. 

(2) You are entitled to and should receive from the person soliciting your life insurance a written proposal signed by him. setting forth all the facts relating to your present insurance cov- 

Sept. 30, 1963 360.11 Vol. 2, No. 6

T.§ 2422 Ch. 2 

INSURANCE 

erages and the advantages and disadvantages of substituting them for the proposed coverage. (3) In every case, it shall be to your advantage to secure the advice and recommendations of the company with whom you are presently insured, or of its general agent in Puerto Rico, regarding the proposed replacement or change in your existing policy. You may secure such recommendations by notifying your present insurer or its general agent in Puerto Rico. If the suggestion of a replacement or change is made by a person representing the company in which you are presently insured, you are entitled to secure the views of the company or of its general agent in Puerto Rico regarding the desirability of such replacement or change.

§ 204-4003. Disclosure of equivalent information

Unless proxies, consents or authorizations in respect of a stock of a domestic insurer subject to section 204-4001 of this title are solicited by or on behalf of the management of such insurer from the holders of record of stock of such insurer in accordance with this division and the schedules thereunder prior to any annual or other meeting, such insurer shall, in accordance with this division and/or such further regulations as the Commissioner may adopt, file with the Commissioner and transmit to all stockholders of record information substantially equivalent to the information which would be required to be transmitted if a solicitation were made. 

§ 204-4004. Definitions 

(a) The definitions and instructions set out in Schedule SIS, as promulgated by the National Association of Insurance Commissioners, shall be applicable for purposes of this division. (b) The terms "solicit" and "solicitation" for purposes of this division shall include: (1) Any request for a proxy, whether or not accompanied by or included in a form of proxy; or (2) Any request to execute or not to execute, or to revoke, a proxy; or (3) The furnishing of a proxy or other communication to stockholders under circumstances reasonably calculated to result in the procurement, withholding or revocation of a proxy. (c) The terms "solicit" and "solicitation" shall not include: (1) Any solicitation by a person in respect of stock of which he is the beneficial owner. (2) Action by a broker or other person in respect to stock carried in his name or in the name of his nominee in forwarding to the beneficial owner of such stock soliciting material received from the company, or impartially instructing such beneficial owner to forward a proxy to the person, if any, to whom the beneficial owner desires to give a proxy, or impartially requesting instructions from the beneficial owner with respect to the authority to be conferred by the proxy and stating that a proxy will be given if the instructions are received by a certain date. (3) The furnishing of a form of proxy to a stockholder upon the unsolicited request of such stockholder, or the performance by 

Dec. 31, 1966 360.14 

Vol. 5, No. 10

כי Ch. T.26 § 204-4006 

any person of ministerial acts on behalf of a person soliciting a proxy. § 204-4005. Information to be furnished to stockholders (a) No solicitation subject to this division shall be made unless each person solicited is concurrently furnished or has previously been furnished with a written proxy statement containing the information specified in subdivision 1. (b) If the solicitation is made on behalf of the management of the insurer and relates to an annual meeting of stockholders at which directors are to be elected, each proxy statement furnished pursuant to subsection (a) hereof shall be accompanied or preceded by an annual report (in preliminary or final form) to such stockholders containing such financial statements for the last fiscal year as are referred to in Schedule SIS under the heading "Financial 

Reporting to Stockholders." Subject to the foregoing requirements with respect to financial statements, the annual report to stockholders may be in any form deemed suitable by the management. (c) Two copies of each report sent to the stockholders pursuant to this section shall be mailed to the Commissioner, not later than the date on which such report is first sent or given to stockholders or the date on which preliminary copies of solicitation material are filed with the Commissioner pursuant to subsection (a) of sec. 

204-4007 of this title, whichever date is later. 

§ 204-4006. Requirements as to proxy 

(a) The form of proxy (1) shall indicate in boldface type whether or not the proxy is solicited on behalf of the management, (2) shall provide a specifically designated blank space for dating the proxy and (3) shall identify clearly and impartially each matter or group of related matters intended to be acted upon, whether proposed by the management, or stockholders. No reference need be made to proposals as to which discretionary authority is conferred pursuant to subsection (c) of this section. (b) Means shall be provided in the proxy for the person solicited to specify by ballot a choice between approval or disapproval of each matter or group of related matters referred to therein, other than elections to office. A proxy may confer discretionary authority with respect to matters as to which a choice is not so specified if the form of proxy states in boldface type how it is intended to 

Dec. 31, 1966 

Vol. 5, No. 10 360.15

T.§ 204-4006 Ch. 2 

INSURANCE 

vote the shares or authorization represented by the proxy in each such case. (c) A proxy may confer discretionary authority with respect to other matters which may come before the meeting, provided the persons on whose behalf the solicitation is made are not aware a reasonable time prior to the time the solicitation is made that any other matters are to be presented for action at the meeting and provided further that a specific statement to that effect is made in the proxy statement or in the form of proxy. (d) No proxy shall confer authority (1) to vote for the election of any person to any office for which a bona fide nominee is not named in the proxy statement or (2) to vote at any annual meeting to be held more than 3 years after the date on which the proxy statement and form of proxy are first sent or given to stockholders. (e) The proxy statement or form of proxy shall provide, subject to reasonable specified conditions, that the proxy will be voted and that where the person solicited specifies by means of ballot provided pursuant to subsection (b) hereof a choice with respect to any matter to be acted upon, the vote will be in accordance with the specifications so made. (f) The information included in the proxy statement shall be clearly presented and the statements made shall be divided into groups according to subject matter, with appropriate headings. All printed proxy statements shall be clearly and legibly presented. § 204-4007. Material required to be filed (a) Two preliminary copies of the proxy statement and form of proxy and any other soliciting material to be furnished to stockholders concurrently therewith shall be filed with the Commissioner at least 10 days prior to the date definitive copies of such material are first sent or given to stockholders, or such shorter period prior to that date as the Commissioner may authorize upon a showing of good cause therefor. (b) Two preliminary copies of any additional soliciting material relating to the same meeting or subject matter to be furnished to stockholders subsequent to the proxy statements shall be filed with the Commissioner at least 2 days (exclusive of Saturdays,

Sundays or holidays) prior to the date copies of this material are first sent or given to stockholders or a shorter period prior to such date as the Commissioner may authorize upon a showing of good cause therefor.

Vol. 5, No. 10 360.16

Ch. T.26 § 204-4009 

(c) Two definitive copies of the proxy statement, form of proxy and all other soliciting material, in the form in which this material is furnished to stockholders, shall be filed with, or mailed for filing to, the Commissioner not later than the date such material is first sent or given to the stockholders. (d) Where any proxy statement, form of proxy or other material filed pursuant to this division is amended or revised, two of the copies shall be marked to clearly show such changes. (e) Copies of replies to inquiries from stockholders requesting further information and copies of communications which do no more than request that forms of proxy theretofore solicited be signed and returned need not be filed pursuant to this section. (f) Notwithstanding the provisions of subsections (a) and (b) of this section and of subsection (e) of sec. 204-4010 of this title, copies of soliciting material in the form of speeches, press releases and radio or television scripts may, but need not, be filed with the Commissioner prior to use or publication. Definitive copies, however, shall be filed with or mailed for filing to the Commissioner as required by subsection (c) hereof not later than the date such material is used or published. The provisions of subsections (a) and (b) hereof and subsection (e) of sec. 204-4010 of this title shall apply, however, to any reprints or reproductions of all or any part of such material. 

§ 204-4008. False or misleading statements 

No solicitation subject to this division shall be made by means of any proxy statement, form of proxy, notice of meeting, or other communication, written or oral, containing any statement which at the time and in the light of the circumstances under which it is made, is false or misleading with respect to any material fact, or which omits to state any material fact necessary in order to make the statements therein not false or misleading or necessary to correct any statement in any earlier communication with respect to the solicitation of a proxy for the same meeting or subject matter which has become false or misleading. § 204-4009. Prohibition of certain solicitations

No person making a solicitation which is subject to this division shall solicit any undated or postdated proxy or any proxy which provides that it shall be deemed to be dated as of any date subsequent to the date on which it is signed by the stockholder. Dec. 31, 1966

INSURANCE § 204-4010. Special provisions applicable to election contests 

(a) Applicability. This section shall apply to any solicitation subject to this division by any person or group for the purpose of opposing a solicitation subject to this division by any other person or group with respect to the election or removal of directors at any annual or special meeting of stockholders. (b) Participant or participant in a solicitation (1) For purposes of this section the term "participant" and "participant in a solicitation" include: (i) the insurer; (ii) any director of the insurer, and any nominee for whose election as a director proxies are solicited; (iii) any other person, acting alone or with one or more other persons, committees or groups, in organizing, directing or financing the solicitation. (2) For the purposes of this section the terms "participant" and "participant in a solicitation" do not include: (i) a bank, broker or dealer who, in the ordinary course of business, lends money or executes orders for the purchase or sale of stock and who is not otherwise a participant; (ii) any person or organization retained or employed by a participant to solicit stockholders or any person who merely transmits proxy soliciting material or performs ministerial or clerical duties; (iii) any person employed in the capacity of attorney, accountant, or advertising, public relations or financial adviser, and whose activities are limited to the performance of his duties in the course of such employment; (iv) any person regularly employed as an officer or employee of the insurer or any or its subsidiaries or affiliates who is not otherwise a participant; or (v) any officer or director of, or any person regularly employed by any other participant, if such officer, director, or employee is not otherwise a participant. (c) Filing of information required by Schedule B [secs. 204-4101 

et seq. of this title]. 

(1) No solicitation subject to this section shall be made by any person other than the management of an insurer unless at least five business days prior thereto, or such shorter period as the Commissioner may authorize upon a showing of good cause

Where preliminary copies of any materials are filed, distribution to stockholders should be deferred until the Commissioner's comments have been received and complied with. (2) Within five business days after a solicitation subject to this section is made by the management of an insurer, or such longer period as the Commissioner may authorize upon a showing of good cause therefor, there shall be filed with the Commissioner by or on behalf of each participant in such solicitation, other than the insurer, and by or on behalf of each management nominee for director, a statement in duplicate containing the information spec ified by Schedule B [subd. 3]. 

(3) If any solicitation on behalf of management or any other person has been made, or if proxy material is ready for distribution, prior to a solicitation subject to this section in opposition thereto, a statement in duplicate containing the information specified in Schedule B [subd. 3] shall be filed with the Commissioner by or on behalf of each participant in such prior solicitation, other than the insurer, as soon as reasonably practicable after the commencement of the solicitation in opposition thereto. (4) If, subsequent to the filing of the statements required by paragraphs (1), (2) and (3) of this subsection, additional persons become participants in a solicitation subject to this rule, there shall be filed with the Commissioner by or on behalf of each such person, a statement in duplicate containing the information specified by Schedule B, within three business days after such person becomes a participant, or such longer period as the Department may authorize upon a showing of good cause therefor. (5) If any material change occurs in the facts reported in any statement filed by or on behalf of any participant, an appropriate amendment to such statement shall be filed promptly with the Commissioner. § 72-1. Definitions 

(a) The words and terms used in this Division in a singular sense shall have a plural meaning or vice versa, as the case may be. (b) The following terms, whenever used or referred to in this. 

Division, shall have the meaning hereinafter expressed, except when the context clearly indicates otherwise: (1) "Commission" shall mean the Public Service Commission of Puerto Rico. (2) "Public warehousing" as defined in sec. 2 of Act No. 70, approved December 6, 1917, as amended by Act No. 448, approved 

April 25, 1946 [27 L.P.R.A. § 2], includes any and every service for compensation or profit connected with the receipt, transportation, lifting, transshipment in transit, ventilation, refrigeration, [T.27] 363

T.§ 72-1 Ch. 5 

PUBLIC SERVICE 

The cost pe storage, handling, delivery, conveyance, and deposit of all kinds of goods. (3) "Company" includes every natural or artificial person engaged in Puerto Rico in the business of public warehousing. (4) "Warehouse" includes any type of building, structure, lot, or grounds used by a company to store goods, with the exception of piers, docks, or wharves as defined in "Storage and Demurrage Tariffs and Fees in the Public Service Docks", approved by the Public Service Commission on November 5, 1941. 

(5) "Goods" means chattels, wares, or merchandise in storage, or which has been or is about to be stored.

April 20, 1948, by Governor June 8, 1948, eff. upon approval by Governor. Filed with Secretary of State, Sept. 19, 1957;

File No. 95. 

Authority. Act Dec. 6, 1917, No. 70, p. 432, § 24; 27 L.P.R.A. 

§ 72.
