For fees and charges on piers, docks, or wharves, see § 336-1 et seq. of Title 23. 

Text references. Regulation of the Public Service Commis sion approved Nov. 5, 1941, referred to in text, was not filed with the Secretary of State and is not included in this compilation.

Separability. Sec. 26 of Regulation File No. 95, set out in this Division, provided: 

"Should any provision of these Regulations be declared void, illegal or unconstitutional by final decree of a court of competent jurisdiction, such holding or decision shall not apply to the remainder, and to said effect it is hereby declared that the provisions of these Regulations are severable one from another.” 

§ 72-2. Franchises 

It shall be unlawful for any company to carry on the business of a public warehouseman 90 days after the approval of this Division without first providing itself with a franchise or provisional permit therefor, issued by the Commission. 

§ 72-3. Application by company 

Any company engaged in the public warehousing business upon the date of approval of this Division shall, as prerequisite in order to provide itself with a franchise or corresponding authorization, file with the Commission within a period of 90 days subsequent to said date, a verified application setting forth the following: (1) Name and post-office address of the company. (2) If a corporation, name and post-office address of its direc- 364

•) Ch. T.27 § 72-5 

tors, or the name and address of the partners, if a partnership. (3) Financial statement of the company at the closing of operations for the last fiscal or calendar year. (4) Period of time during which the public storage service has been performed. (5) Number of buildings operated as warehouses and a detailed description and location of the same. Structural plans shall be made to form part of the petition. (6) Specification of the original cost of the structures, facilities, equipment, and accessories used in rendering service, as well as any other estimate of the value of said structures, facilities, equipment, and accessories which the company may deem fit to submit. 

If it is not possible to report the original cost, the reason for not doing so shall be stated and an estimate of the same or of its replacement cost less accrued depreciation shall be submitted. (7) Tariff schedules of prices, charges, rates, fares, or any other compensation that the company is charging, exacting, or receiving for the services being rendered at the time of approval of this 

Division. 

(8) Any other data, information, documents, etc., which the company deems pertinent to be taken into account by the Commission in order that the latter may act equitably regarding the regulation of the operation of public warehouses. (9) The application shall be accompanied by a copy of the charter of organization and certificate of incorporation in the case of a corporation or a certified copy of the partnership deed in the case of a partnership. 

§ 72-4. Requirement of franchise 

Any natural or artificial person desiring to carry on the business of a public warehouseman shall not be entitled to do so upon the date of approval of this Division without first obtaining a franchise or authorization therefor, issued by the Public Service Commission. § 72-5. Application to operate public warehouse 

Applications for authorization to operate a public warehouse shall be personally verified by a party thereto and are to be addressed to the Public Service Commission. Said application shall state and set forth the following: (1) Name and post-office address of the petitioner. 365

T.§ 72-5 

PUBLIC SERVICE 

Ch. 5 (2) If a corporation, name and post-office address of its directors. A copy of the charter of organization, a certificate of incorporation and a certification of the paid-in capital by the treasurer of the corporation shall be forwarded therewith. If a partnership, name and post-office address of the partners and a certified copy of the partnership deed. (3) Detailed plans and descriptions of the warehouses, properties, facilities, and accessories to be used in rendering the service and location of the same. (4) Specification as to the original cost or an estimate of the purchase price or building cost of said warehouses, properties, facilities, and accessories. (5) Proposed rate schedules or charges under which the service is to be rendered. (6) Any other data, information, documents, etc., which the applicant deems pertinent for the Commission to take into consideration so that it may act equitably regarding the regulation of the operation of public warehouses.

A notice relative to the application shall be published in one or more newspapers of general circulation edited in Puerto Rico in accordance with the provisions of the Rules of Procedure of the Commission. Compliance with all other procedural requirements pertaining to franchise applications shall be required. 

§ 72-6. Temporary permits 

The Commission may issue temporary permits to engage in the business of operating a public warehouse pending final disposition of any application for franchise filed pursuant to the provisions of sec. 72-3 of this title. In addition thereto the Commission may issue temporary permits during emergencies and when, in its judgment, public interest and convenience so require. 

§ 72-7. Tariff schedules 

The tariff schedules filed with the Commission by a company in compliance with the provisions of paragraph (7) of sec. 72-3 of this title are to be deemed lawful and final until the Commission shall, on its own motion or upon petition of the company or of an interested party, repeal, alter, modify, or amend the same pursuant to the legal or regulatory procedure. § 72-8. Copy of storage charges to customer

Every company subject to the provisions of this Division shall, 366

Ch. 

T.27 § 72-14 upon request of its customers, furnish the same with a copy of the rate of storage charges in force. 

§ 72-9. Change of rates 

No company, its agents, officials, or employees shall increase or reduce the rates in force or fixed by the Commission without first having obtained the latter's approval thereof. § 72-10. Higher rate

No company, either directly or through its agents, officials, or employees, shall exact, demand, or charge a higher rate than the one approved by the Commission. 

§ 72-11. Warehouse bonds 

Every company shall furnish a mortgage bond or execute a surety bond with a bonding company duly licensed to do business within Puerto Rico for a minimum amount to be fixed by the Commission for each warehouse after hearing the company involved. Said mortgage or surety bond shall be held as a guarantee for damages caused to stored goods through fault or negligence of the company, or of any agents, officials, or employees thereof. 

§ 72-12. Due care 

Every company shall exercise at all times due care and vigilance in the safekeeping of the goods entrusted to it, as it would exercise in regard to similar goods of its own. § 72-13. Rejection of goods; discrimination

Every company shall make its warehousing facilities available to the general public without exercising any kind of discrimination. 

Nothing herein contained, however, shall be understood as subjecting any company to the duty of accepting in its warehouse any goods of a class, type, or nature different from the kind usually stored therein. No company shall be obliged to receive goods in its warehouse which because of their condition may contaminate or affect goods therein stored. 

§ 72-14. Hours 

Every company shall open its warehouse to the public for the purpose of receiving and delivering goods during all working days. 

If the warehouse is not kept open from 8:00 a.m. through to 6:00 p.m. the company shall display conspicuously at the entrance there- 367

T.§ 72-14 Ch. 5 

PUBLIC SERVICE 

of a notice of the hours in which it will be open. If for due cause the warehouse is to remain closed a notice shall be posted at its entrance indicating the period of time and stating the name and address of a person in the community authorized to deliver the goods upon lawful demand made by the depositor or holder of a receipt thereof, as the case may be. 

872-15. Accounts 

Every company shall adopt and keep in its warehouse a system of accounts approved by the Commission, which may, after hearing on its own motion or upon petition of the company involved, modify, alter, amend, or revise the same. 

§ 72-16. Annual report 

Every company shall submit to the Commission an annual report covering the condition, contents, operations, and business of its warehouses, or any other pertinent data and additional reports required by the Commission. 

§ 72-17. Inspection 

Every company shall allow any agent or officer of the Commission, authorized so to do, to enter upon the premises, inspect, and examine, during working days or hours, the contents of a warehouse and of the books, records, documents, and accounts kept in connection with the same. It shall also supply the agent the necessary help to perform the said inspection and examination. § 72-18. Safe-deposit box; files

Every company shall have a fireproof safe-deposit box in which shall be kept the records, books, and papers concerning the goods in storage, including the receipt book and copies of the receipts issued not in use. All cancelled receipts shall be filed in numerical order as soon as possible after their cancellation and kept in metal files for a period of not less than one year. 

§ 72-19. Change of ownership, tenure 

No change shall take place regarding the ownership, tenure, or right to operate under a franchise or authorization of the Commission granted in accordance with the provisions of this Division, unless approval is previously requested under oath from the Commission and such approval and consent is obtained. 368

•) T.§ 72-25 Ch. 5 

 - POLYVORNICZYCA, SOM § 72-20. Notice to consignee 

Every company receiving in its warehouse goods deposited by a shipping concern or airline consigned to a third person, shall remit a notice to the consignee within 24 hours after receipt of the same. 

If within 15 days after remittance of the notice or announcement no communication whatsoever is received from the consignee regarding the stored goods, the company shall remit a second notice. 

If within 15 days after remittance of the second notice no communication is received from the consignee, the company shall remit a third notice by registered mail. 

§ 72-21. Construction with other laws 

None of the provisions contained in this Division shall be construed in any way to abridge or impair any of the obligations, duties, or liabilities of any warehouseman or in any way alter the rights of any such person under the provisions of Act No. 9, enacted on February 21, 1918, known as the "Uniform Warehouse 

Receipts Act" [10 L.P.R.A. §§ 391-452]. 

§ 72-22. Powers of Commission 

None of the provisions contained in this Division shall in any way abridge or alter the general or inherent powers of the Commission which hereby reserves the power to issue any orders deemed pertinent for the regulation of the public warehousing business in 

Puerto Rico. 

§ 72-23. Exemptions 

Notwithstanding the provisions of this Division, the Commission herein reserves the power to exempt any company, through order to said effect, from compliance thereof when it deems it just and convenient. 

§ 72-24. Penalties 

Any violation of this Division shall be subject to the penal sanc tion established by the "Public Service Law of Puerto Rico [27 

L.P.R.A. §§ 1-255]; notwithstanding, the Commission may, after a public hearing is held, suspend or cancel temporarily or permanently the corresponding permit or franchise. 

§ 72-25. Effectiveness 

This Division shall go into effect immediately after approval by the Public Service Commission of Puerto Rico and by the Governor of Puerto Rico.

§ 72-102. Definitions 

The following terms whenever used in this Division shall have the meaning hereinafter set forth, except where the context clearly indicates otherwise and when used in singular number should be construed in plural, as the case may be: (1) "Commission" means the Public Service Commission of 

Puerto Rico. (2) "Omnibus" means any motor vehicle on wheels and with capacity for more than 10 passengers engaged or intended to be engaged in the transportation of passengers as public carriers. 

It does not include vehicles of the type engaged in the transportation of students exclusively. (3) "Company" means any person who, or association, partnership, corporation, cooperative, or any organization of any kind which engages or intends to engage in omnibus service. (4) "Operator" means the person who drives or controls an omnibus. (5) "Collector" means the person who collects the fare. (6) "Cooperative" means any association or group of persons organized in accordance with the General Cooperative Associa tions Act of Puerto Rico No. 291, approved on April 9, 1946 [5 L.P. 

R.A. §§ 881-909], for the purpose of engaging in omnibus service. (7) "Association" means a group of omnibus owners organized for the purpose of using common facilities, business name, colors, insignia or emblems. (8) "License" means franchise, certificate, permit, right, privi- 372

Ch. 5

T.27 § 72-105 

•) lege, or authorization granted by the Commission to engage in omnibus service irrespective of the number of omnibuses or to act as an operator. 

§ 72-103. Omnibus license 

Requirement

From the date this Division is in force, no company shall engage any motor vehicle in omnibus service unless the vehicle has a valid omnibus license issued by the Commission and has complied with the requirements established by this Division with regard to insurance, equipment, labels, colors, and insignia. The license must be renewed semiannually. Once an omnibus license is granted, the omnibus must be operated within 30 days. 

§ 72-104. -Requirements for obtaining 

The following requirements shall be complied with to obtain an omnibus license: (1) File with the Commission a sworn statement containing the following facts: Name and address of the applicant; his financial status; number of omnibuses he intends to operate and the passenger capacity of each omnibus; points between which the service will be rendered; description of the terminals and the specific routes to be followed; detailed rates to be charged and the timetable which shall govern the vehicles that are to render service. (2) To explain clearly the facts that will attempt to show that the exercise of the privilege requested is necessary and adequate for the service, comfort, convenience, and safety of the public. (3) To give the name under which the service will be rendered, the identification design or emblem and the colors to be used. (4) If the applicant is a natural person, he must file a certificate of conduct issued by the Police Department. The Commission may also require such certificate from the owners, partners, shareholders, or directors of artificial persons, when it deems convenient. (5) To publish a notice in regard to the petition once a week for 2 weeks in two newspapers of general circulation in Puerto Rico. 

§ 72-105. Substitute omnibus - Authorization 

The Commission may authorize a company to operate an omnibus to substitute for a licensed omnibus when the latter is not in condition to operate. 373

T.§ 72-106 

PUBLIC SERVICE 

Ch. 5 

§ 72-106. 

Number of substitute omnibuses

In no instance shall more than one substitute omnibus be authorized for every three licensed omnibuses. 

§ 72-107. 

Requirements for substitute omnibus

To operate a duly authorized substitute omnibus the company shall comply with the following requirements: (1) To comply with the requirements in regard to insurance and safety required by this Division for the licensed omnibus. (2) To display on the top over the windshield or in the space specially used to display the routes and also on the top over the rear window or on the rear window in capital letters of a size readable at a reasonable distance and in a color different than that of the omnibus the word "SUBSTITUTE”. (3) To display in the inner parts of the substitute omnibus, in a place visible to the passengers, a copy of the semiannual license issued by the Commission and in which shall be listed the omnibuses that the company is authorized to substitute, the number of its licenses issued by the Secretary of Public Works and the Commission and the routes which each omnibus is authorized and must serve. (4) To display the identification badge supplied by the Secretary of the Commission for the regular omnibus being substituted. 

When the substitution is for one day it is not necessary to comply with this requirement. (5) To display on the front of the omnibus a sign stating the route to be served. 

§ 72-108. Transfers 

No transfer of ownership of a licensed omnibus shall be made without the prior authorization of the Commission. Noncompliance of this provision shall be sufficient cause for the revocation of the license. 

§ 72-109. Accident insurance 

(a) Every company shall furnish a guaranty in the form of a first mortgage on real property, an insurance policy with an insurance company duly authorized to do business in Puerto Rico, or in cash to cover such a minimum amount as the Commission may determine for each omnibus for the payment of any compensation 374

Ch. 

T.27 § 72-113 כי to any person who suffers injuries or damages in any accident caused by the careless or negligent use or operation of the omnibus or defects of it. The insurance companies shall notify the 

Commission of all cancellations of insurance policy for default in payment. Said insurance companies shall not cancel any insurance policy for any cause other than default in payment without the previous approval of the Commission, or without having notified the Commission of its intention to cancel said policy, at least 15 days before the date of such cancellation. This provision shall be a condition of the insurance policy. While this Division is in effect, no omnibus shall operate until its surety is approved by the Commission. (b) The Commission shall not approve any insurance policy issued by any insurance company which has not complied with the provisions relative to insurance contracts required by this section. (c) In the event that the Commission cancels an omnibus license, the insurance contract shall remain in effect until all claims, due to acts or omissions occurring before the cancellation, have been decided by the courts. 

§ 72-110. Rates - Filing 

Every company shall file with the Commission the rates to be approved. Once approved, the rates shall not be altered by the company, its agents, officials, or employees, without the prior approval of the Commission. § 72-111. Posting of rates

The companies shall post permanently inside of each omnibus, in a place visible to the passengers, the rates in force. 

§ 72-112. Refunds 

The fare entitles the passenger to the complete trip for which he has paid. In case the omnibus cannot make the full trip it is the duty of the company, operator, or collector to refund the amount of the fare corresponding to those parts of the trip not travelled to. The passengers, however, shall pay for those parts of the trip which were travelled. 

§ 72-113. 

Free travel

The inspectors of the Commission, its messengers when on official business, policemen, and firemen of the Fire Service of Puerto 

375

T.§ 72-113 Ch. 5 

PUBLIC SERVICE 

Rico, while in uniform and on official business; the court constables and deputies on official business and the penal guards in uniform and while conveying prisoners shall have the right to travel gratuitously in the omnibus. 

§ 72-114. Ownership of vehicle 

The companies chich have obtained certificates of public convenience and necessity to render services subject to this Division shall be the owners of the omnibuses operated in the service. They shall use omnibuses not owned by the company only when authorized by the Commission. 

§ 72-115. Equipment, colors, and insignia - Condition of vehicle 

Every omnibus shall be kept clean and in good mechanical and safe condition, with seats, brakes, tires, body, windshield wipers, electric system, front, rear and brake lights in good condition. They shall always be supplied with sufficient fuel and oil, one spare tire and tools. 

§ 72-116. 

Display of licenses 

Every omnibus shall display in its interior and in a place visible to the passengers its license, the operator's license with his photograph, the collector's license, if any, and the conditions under which it is authorized to operate. The operator and collector must appear in the photograph as they do in the omnibus. 

§ 72-117. — Display of notices and signs 

Every omnibus shall display in its interior and visible to the passengers the authorized passenger capacity. In the same manner, it shall display the notices and signs required by secs. 72-168 and 

72-170 of this title. 

§ 72-118. 

Badge or identification

Every omnibus shall have the badge or identification required by the Commission and which shall be furnished when it is authorized to operate. 

§ 72-119. Outside name and number 

Every omnibus shall display on each outer side an emblem or design to identify it or the name under which it does business and the name of the company operating it. When a company operates more than one omnibus, each must display a correlative number 376

Ch. 

T.27 § 72-126 to identify it, corresponding to the number of vehicles which are owned and operated. 

§ 72-120. 

Color, size, and style of letters The letters and numbers referred to in the foregoing section shall be of such color, size, and style as to make them readable under normal light conditions. 

§ 72-121. 

Unapproved signs

No omnibus shall display on its exterior signs or letters other than those required in this Division without the previous approval of the Commission. 

§ 72-122. Radios 

No omnibus shall be equipped with a radio receiving set. The use of a radio-telephone to communicate with the company's office is not forbidden. 

§ 72-123. Interior lighting 

Every omnibus occupied by the public shall be lighted in the interior while in service between sunset and sunrise. 

§ 72-124. - Display of route description 

Every regular omnibus shall display permanently on the top over the windshield or in the space specially used to display the routes and also on the top over the rear window or on the rear glass in capital letters readable at a reasonable distance and in a color in contrast with that of the omnibus, the description of the route by which it is authorized to operate. § 72-125. 

Display of timetable and rates Every regular omnibus authorized to operate over a route shall display in its interior in a visible place and in letters of readable size to all passengers and of a color in contrast with its interior paint the timetable approved by the Commission and the rates in force. In case the omnibus is authorized to operate continuously it shall be so stated in the afore-mentioned manner. 

§ 72-126. Colors 

Every omnibus shall be painted in a color or combination of colors distinctive of the company, which shall be previously approved by the Commission. 

377

T.§ 72-127 

Ch. 5

PUBLIC SERVICE 

§ 72-127. Distinguishing colors, insignia, and emblems

No omnibus shall have colors, insignia, or emblems that, in the opinion of the Commission, are not easily distinguishable from colors, insignia, or emblems already approved for other companies operating in part of the same area or route. 

§ 72-128. 

Specifications Every omnibus shall comply with the following specifications: 

(1) The height from the floor to the ceiling shall not be less than 72 inches. (2) The width of the aisle shall not be less than 20 inches. (3) The seats and their backs shall not be less than 32 inches long and 16 inches wide. (4) The vertical distance between seats in the same position shall not be less than 10 inches. (5) The seats shall be of springs or foam rubber covered for the public comfort. (6) It shall have two pipes running lengthwise along the ceiling or individual leather hangers for the standees. (7) It shall have a call bell or other adequate system so that the passengers, from their seats, may signal the operator their desire that the omnibus be stopped. 

§ 72-129. Extra seats 

No omnibus shall have seats in the aisle or in such a manner that they block the passengers. Every extra seat shall be previously approved by the Commission. 

§ 72-130. 

Emergency door

Every omnibus shall have in its left or rear part an emergency door opening toward the outside. The lock mechanism shall be of such type that it will not open accidentally, but should be easy for the passengers to operate. 

§ 72-131. Fire extinguisher; first-aid kit 

Every omnibus shall be equipped with a fire extinguisher and a first-aid kit. 

§ 72-132. Inspection 

The omnibuses shall be inspected every 120 days, it being compulsory for their operators or owners to bring them to the Commission or to the place designated for inspection. 378

§ 72-133. Inspection tag 

Every omnibus shall display on the inner side of the windshield, and where it does not affect the visibility of the operator, evidence that the vehicle has been inspected. 

§ 72-134. Cooperatives and associations 

Individual owners of one or more omnibuses in a specific area may organize as cooperatives or associations to operate under a common trade name, colors, combination of colors, and emblem or insignia.

§ 72-136. Operators-licensing 

No company shall consent or allow any person to drive or control an omnibus belonging to it unless such person is an operator duly authorized by the Commission and whose license is in force. § 72-137. -Discharged operators

No operator who has been discharged by any company on grounds that may cause the suspension or cancellation of his license shall be employed by any other company without the prior approval of the Commission. The company which discharges any operator shall notify the Commission within 48 hours stating the reasons for the discharge. 1969

§ 72-138. 

Operator's license

No person shall act as an operator unless he has applied for and obtained an authorization from the Commission. To obtain it he must comply with the following requirements: (1) Be a citizen of the United States and of the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico. (2) Be between 21 and 65 years of age. (3) Be a chauffeur of heavy motor vehicles duly authorized by the Secretary of Public Works and to have at least 2 years' experience as an operator of heavy motor vehicles in Puerto Rico or with heavy vehicles of the armed forces while in military service. (4) File: (A) His record as chauffeur of heavy motor vehicles from the Department of Public Works. 

(B) Certificate of conduct issued by the Police Department as of the date the application is filed. (C) Medical certificate from a public health unit or a private physician showing petitioner's good physical condition, specially of the following organs and limbs: eyes, ears, heart, lungs, condition of legs and arms (reflexes). (D) Three pictures, size 2" x 2". (E) Birth certificate. (F) Photostatic copy of discharge, if a veteran. (5) Pass an examination prescribed by the Commission which will include, among other things, knowledge of the provisions of this division. § 72-139. Renewal of license

The operator's license shall be renewed every 2 years, except the licenses which belong to the operators of the Metropolitan Bus Authority, which must be renewed every 4 years. To do so the requirements of paragraphs (A)-(D) of sec. 72-138 (4) of this title must again be complied with.

 T.27 § 72-149 § 72-142. 

Smoking No operator shall smoke while the omnibus he is operating is carrying passengers. 

§ 72-143. Drug addiction; alcoholism 

No operator shall be a drug addict or a habitual user of intoxicating beverages. 

§ 72-144. Surrender of omnibus 

No operator shall surrender the omnibus to a person who has not an operator's license in force and without the company's consent. 

§ 72-145. Funds for change

Every operator shall have at all time no less than $5 in change. 

§ 72-146. 

Stopping

Every operator shall stop the omnibus at the bus stops whenever ordered to do so by the passengers, or whenever the vehicle is not fully occupied and a stop signal is given to him by any person desiring to ride in the omnibus. Nothing herein contained shall be construed to compel the operator to stop in places prohibited by law or traffic regulation or municipal ordinance. 

Unnecessary delays 

Once the trip is started the operator shall not cause unnecessary delays. 

§ 72-148. Conduct of operator

Every operator shall observe a correct and respectful attitude toward the public and passengers. Any behavior showing disregard for the duties imposed upon him by this Division or any rude or disrespectful conduct or conduct at variance with moral and proper conduct, that should be observed by every person serving the public, shall be sufficient cause for the suspension or cancellation of the operator's license. 

§ 72-149. Possession of license; showing on request

Every operator shall always have with him his operator's license while driving an omnibus. It shall also be his duty to show his license to any person that justifiably and correctly requests it. 

381

T.§ 72-150 Ch. 5 

PUBLIC SERVICE 

§ 72-150. 

Higher or lower rate

No operator shall demand or receive a higher or lower rate than that approved by the Commission. 

§ 72-151. Place and number of passengers; conduct

No operator shall allow a passenger to travel in that part of the platform where he, the operator, sits, nor allow to travel more passengers than authorized, nor drunks or persons who in any other manner may disturb or offend the passengers. 

§ 72-152. Operation of omnibus; inspection 

Every omnibus shall be operated in accordance with the laws, municipal ordinances, and traffic regulations in force. Every operator shall stop and allow the inspection of the omnibus at the request of any inspector of the Commission. 

§ 72-153. Letting off, picking up passengers

No operator shall stop the omnibus to let off or pick up a passenger in a street or road intersection, nor in such manner as to block or interfere with traffic; he shall stop the vehicle to let off or pick up passengers as near to the curb as possible or close to the right side of the road if it does not have a sidewalk. In zones where there are fixed stops for the omnibus, the operator may not let off or pick up passengers outside of said stops. 

§ 72-154. Passing another omnibus

While driving an omnibus in an urban or populated zone, no operator shall pass another moving omnibus until it stops to let off or pick up passengers or for any other proper cause. 

§ 72-155. Invitation to public 

No operator or his agents shall request or invite the public to use the omnibus he is operating. 

§ 72-156. Health 

Every operator shall be in good health. If suffering a contagious, heart, or mental disease, the company shall separate him from service. 

§ 72-157. Parking 

No operator shall park the omnibus outside its terminal, approved by the Commission, or the place designated for such purposes by the municipal authorities. 382

Ch. 

 T.27 § 72-164 

§ 72-158. Recommendations of business places by operator 

Except at the request of a passenger, no operator shall recommend the patronage of restaurants, night clubs, dance halls, hotels, or other business of the same nature. Nor may he recommend any illegal business place. 

§ 72-159. Lost articles 

At the end of each trip the operator shall examine the omnibus to make sure that the passengers have not left any package or object. If after the passenger has left he discovers any package or object he shall attempt to return it to its owner within 30 minutes and, if unable to do so, he shall take it to the City Hall where the proceeding provided in the Civil Code will be followed. 

Text references. The Civil Code, referred to in text, is classified to title 31, L.P.R.A. 

§ 72-160.- - Revocation of operator's license 

The violation of any of the provisions of this Division, or the conviction for a crime involving moral turpitude, or for the violation of traffic laws or regulations, shall be deemed sufficient cause for the revocation of the operator's license, following the procedure provided in this Division. A license which has been revoked or cancelled shall be returned to the Commission by the operator. 

§ 72-161. 

Report of accident

Every operator shall render to the company for which he works a written report of any accident he may have had in which persons were killed or injured or damage to other persons' property was caused. Such report shall be rendered with 24 hours after the accident. 

§ 72-162. 

Trip records

Every operator shall keep a daily record of all trips made, stating the time and place of origin and destination of each trip and the amount charged for it. 

§ 72-163. Collectors Use of collectors 

The use of collectors is not allowed, except with the approval of the Commission in omnibuses operating long routes between towns. $ 72-164. Renewal of license

Every collector shall obtain a license from the Commission before acting as such. The license shall be renewed every 2 years. 

383

T.27 872 Ch. 5 

PUBLIC SERVICE 

§ 72-165. 

Health, general requirements

Authorized collectors shall be in good health and are subject to the requirements for operators of secs. 72-140 to 72-143, 72-145, 72-148 to 72-151, 72-155, 72-156 and 72-158 to 72-160 of this title. 

§ 72-166. Safety, comfort, and convenience Authorized capacity of omnibus

No omnibus shall carry passengers in excess of its authorized capacity. 

§ 72-167. 

Carrying annoying or dangerous animals or objects Passengers shall not take or carry in an omnibus any animal, or parcels, suitcases, packages, boxes, or other objects which by their size annoy other passengers. Nor may they carry acids, weapons, dynamite, explosives, or other dangerous substances. 

The prohibition with regard to animals is not applicable to trained dogs used by blind persons. 

§ 72-168. Smoking by passengers 

Smoking shall not be allowed in an omnibus except in the last two lines of seats. The omnibus shall display a sign stating where smoking is allowed. In omnibuses operating in intraurban zones smoking shall not be allowed and a sign so stating shall be displayed. 

§ 72-169. 

Conduct of passengers, cleanliness

No person shall be allowed to travel or remain in an omnibus while intoxicated or behaving in an immoral or disorderly manner, or who shows symptoms of a contagious disease or mental disturbance, or who for lack of cleanliness of body or clothes is an improper person to travel in the omnibus. 

§ 72-170. Conversation with operator 

No person shall unnecessarily divert the operator's attention with conversation or otherwise. The omnibus shall display a sign to this. respect. 

§ 72-171. Towing or pushing 

Omnibuses while in service shall not be used to tow or push other vehicles, except, in an emergency, to remove any vehicle blocking traffic. 384

Ch. 

 T.27 § 72-179 

= 

§ 72-172. Omnibus service 

Complete trips Omnibuses shall be operated in complete trips between terminals on the authorized route. 

§ 72-173. 

Compliance with timetable

Omnibuses shall comply with the timetable approved by the Commission although there are no passengers at the starting point. 

§ 72-174. Routes between towns, stopping 

Omnibuses operating on routes including several towns shall not stop in the towns unless required to let off or pick up a passenger. 

They shall follow a direct route without using streets of towns which are not necessary to cross. 

§ 72-175.- Causes for revocation of omnibus license 

Noncompletion of trips, noncompliance with the timetable, deviation from the route between terminals, and charging or intending to charge a rate different from that approved by the Commission, shall be sufficient cause for the revocation of the omnibus license. 

§ 72-176. 

Special trips 

The Commission may authorize special trips outside the routes when in its judgment such authorization does not impair service to the public along the route served by the omnibus. 

§ 72-177. Interruptions of service 

No company shall interrupt the authorized service without notifying the Commission, at least 5 days in advance, stating the reasons for the interruption of the service. In case of unforeseen interruption of the service, the company and the operator shall notify the Commission, within 24 hours of the interruption, stating its causes and its probable duration. The resumption of service shall be reported in writing to the Commission, stating the date and hour in which the service was resumed. 

§ 72-178. 

Suspension of service

Suspension of service without the Commission's approval shall be sufficient cause for revocation of the licenses of the omnibuses operated by the company. 

§ 72-179. Complaints - Writing 

Every natural or artificial person who wishes to complain against 385

T.§ 72-179 Ch. 5 

PUBLIC SERVICE 

an operator or collector shall write to the Commission stating the acts performed by the operator or collector and the date, time, and place they occurred, the description of the omnibus, plate number, the company to which it belongs, and any other pertinent information. In the letter the complainant shall also state his name and address, as well as the name and address of his witnesses, if any. 

§ 72-180. 

Referral of complaint

Every complaint received in accordance with the previous section shall be referred by the Chairman to the office of legal services of the Commission, who shall study it to determine if the facts stated therein constitute a violation of this Division. § 72-181. Complaint not involving violation

Should the office of legal services determine that the facts stated in the complaint do not constitute a violation, it shall thus report to the Chairman, who shall inform the complainant and the Commission. Unless the Commission disagrees with the report it shall order that the complaint be filed. § 72-182. Complaint involving violation

Should the office of legal services determine that an operator or collector has violated this Division, it shall thus report with recommendations to the Chairman, who shall notify the Commission and the complainant, if any, of the action taken. If the recommendation is to the effect that the operator's or collector's license be suspended or cancelled, the Commission through the Chairman or one of the members of the Commission, shall notify the operator or collector of the facts reported and shall order him to appear before the designated official at a specified date, time, and place. to hear him in regard to the reported facts. The notice to the operator or collector shall be made by registered mail to his lastknown address in the Commission's records. Should the operator or collector waive hearing or fail to appear at the hearing, the Commission may suspend or revoke his license without further summons or hearing. 

§ 72-183. 

Disciplinary action 

The official appointed to preside at the hearing, once the appearing party or parties are heard, shall render a report with his recommendations to the Commission and the Commission shall take 386

Ch. 

T.27 72-186 כי whatever action it deems pertinent. Within 15 days after notice of the disciplinary action is served, the operator or collector concerned may petition for reconsideration and rehearing, which shall be held before the Commission or one of the commissioners. Until the case is finally decided, the disciplinary action taken shall remain in full force. § 72-184. Temporary suspension The Commission may, in the manner specified in sec. 72-185, temporarily suspend the license issued to an operator or collector. 

This authority shall be exercised when in its opinion the operators or collectors are incompetent or unable to exercise their functions or when the facts charged to them constitute a menace to public safety. 

§ 72-185. Suspension or cancellation of omnibus licenses

If the Commission learns that in any part of Puerto Rico any motor vehicle subject to this Division is operated without having complied with the requirements herein stated, or, after having complied with these requirements, said vehicle is being operated under conditions that constitute a menace to public safety or if there is reason to believe that its owner or operator is not competent to own or operate such type of vehicle, or is violating this Division, the Commission may issue an order, without previous notice, temporarily suspending the operation of said vehicle for a period not to exceed 15 days. Orders so issued shall be considered final orders. Immediately after suspending the operation of a vehicle in the manner described above, the Commission shall summon its owner to appear before the official designated by the Commission to preside at the hearing within a period not to exceed 

15 days from the date of suspension to show cause, if any, why a longer period of suspension or the definite cancellation of the omnibus license should not be ordered. If the hearing is postponed at the request of the party involved, the vehicle license shall remain suspended until the case is finally decided by the Commission, even though the 15 days of temporary suspension have elapsed. 

§ 72-186. Reports and accounting system Name and address 

Every company shall report to the Commission its name and address and any change in name or address shall be reported to the Commission within 48 hours of such change. 

387

T.§ 72-187 Ch. 5 

PUBLIC SERVICE § 72-187. - Preservation of daily record 

The daily record referred to in sec. 72-162 of this title shall be kept by the company for at least 1 year from the date, for examination by the Commission. 

§ 72-188. Shifts of work, license numbers, vehicles operated 

Every company shall keep a record of the operators working on the various shifts, with their license numbers and vehicles operated by them. This information shall be available at all times to the Commission, and shall be immediately forwarded at the request of the Commission, the Director of the Bureau of Inspection or the secretary of the Commission. 

§ 72-189. Accident report 

Every company shall render a written report to the Commission of every accident occurring to its vehicle in which persons are killed or injured or damages to their property are caused; said report shall be rendered within 24 hours after the company receives the report of the accident from the operator. In case the operator does not render his report to the company, said company shall render its report within 24 hours after it has knowledge of the accident. § 72-190. 

Insurance company report

The report required by sec. 72-189 of this title shall be rendered to the Commission by the insurance company, covering the vehicle, within 48 hours after the accident has been reported to them by the company. The insurance company is subject in this regard to the requirement of sec. 72-109 of this title. 

§ 72-191. 

Report as evidence 

No report rendered in accordance with this section shall be used as evidence in any criminal or civil action for damages arising from the matters mentioned in the report. 

§ 72-192. Labor contracts 

Every individual or collective contract or agreement which affects the worker-employer relations between the operators or collectors. and companies shall be filed with the Commission within 5 days after it has been made. Any change in said contract or agreement shall also be reported to the Commission within the same period. 388

Ch. 

 T.27 § 72-199 § 72-193. Biannual statements 

Every company shall keep the accounting system prescribed by the Commission and shall render biannual statements. 

§ 72-194. General powers of Commission 

None of the provisions contained in this Division shall be understood in any way as limiting or restricting the general powers of the Commission, which retains the power to approve any pertinent orders to regulate omnibus service in Puerto Rico and to grant special or temporary permits to operate omnibuses on designated routes which by any circumstances are convenient and necessary to the public welfare. 

§ 72-195. Exemptions 

Notwithstanding the provisions of this Division the Commission retains the power, through orders to that effect, to grant exemptions from compliance with any of said provisions when such exemptions are considered justified and convenient. 

§ 72-196. Liability of companies 

The companies shall be liable for violations of this Division committed by their operators or collectors. 

§ 72-197. Persons to enforce compliance 

Policemen, public service inspectors, and the employees of the Department of Public Works in charge of policing and maintenance of roads shall require compliance with this Division and in case of violations thereof, shall notify the Commission and file complaints in court. § 72-198. Enforcement by citizens; complaint

Every citizen shall have the right to demand from operators compliance with this Division. In case of noncompliance he shall have the right to file a complaint before the Commission, as provided in sec. 72-179 of this title, or before the courts. 

§ 72-199. Penalties 

The violation of any of the preceding rules shall constitute a misdemeanor and shall be subject to the penal sanction established by the Public Service Act of Puerto Rico [27 L.P.R.A. §§ 1-255]. 

However, the Commission, in case of violation of any of the preceding rules, may, after hearing, suspend or cancel the omnibus license, or the license of the operator or collector concerned. 389

§ 72-301. Definitions 

(a) It shall be understood that the words or terms used in this Subdivision in the singular shall be deemed to have a plural meaning or vice versa, as the case may be. (b) The following terms, whenever used or referred to in this Subdivision, shall have the meaning hereinafter expressed, unless the context clearly indicates otherwise: (1) "Commission" shall mean the Public Service Commission of Puerto Rico. 

(2) "Vehicle" shall include any vehicle propelled by power 390

. Ch. 

T.27 § 72-302  

other than muscular, with capacity for not more than 10 passengers, engaged in the transportation of passengers for hire. (3) "Routes in the metropolitan area" shall mean the routes between the city of San Juan and its barrios, and the routes between the city of San Juan and the city of Río Piedras and intermediate points, including Caparra Heights and Puerto Nuevo settlements. (4) "Operation" shall mean the transportation or offering to transport passengers for pay. (5) "Common carrier" shall include any person, association, partnership, company, corporation or organization of any nature, who as owner, manager, or lessee, operates, or applies for authorization to operate, a vehicle subject to this Subdivision. (6) "Agent" shall include any person to whom a common carrier voluntarily renders his vehicle. (7) "Operator" shall mean the driver of a vehicle.

§ 72-302. Authorization to operate 

After July 1, 1949, no common carrier, either personally or through agents, shall operate any vehicle on the routes of the metropolitan area without having first obtained a certificate of convenience and necessity to operate, issued by the Commission and approved by the Governor of Puerto Rico, besides having complied with all other requirements of this Subdivision or with the orders and resolutions of the Commission. 391

"ORDER "WHEREAS, the Honorable Governor of Puerto Rico on 

May 14, 1949, approved Act No. 360 amending Section 19-(a) 

of the [Act to regulate the use of motor vehicles] * * * approved April 5, 1946, as amended by Act No. 1, of Febru ary 20, 1947 and for other purposes. 

"WHEREAS, Section 19-(a) of the above-mentioned Act approved April 5, 1946, amended by Act No. 1 of February 10, 1947, as amended further by Act No. 360 approved May 14, 1949 [9 L.P.R.A. § 190], provides as follows: 

'Public service automobiles with a ten (10) passenger capacity or less, once their owners have paid the amount hereby fixed as fees, may circulate on all public roads of the Island, without limitations of any kind regarding routes, except as to the routes comprised within the metropolitan area, in which case it shall be necessary to obtain on and after July 1, 1949, a certificate of convenience and necessity issued by the Public Service Commission of Puerto Rico; provided, that by metropolitan area routes shall be understood such as are comprised between the city of San Juan and its barrios, and between the city of San Juan and the city of Río Piedras and intermediate points, including Caparra Heights and Puerto Nuevo settlements...' "WHEREAS, said Act being of an urgent and necessary character took effect immediately after its approval, that is on May 14, 1949. "WHEREAS, for the purpose of protecting the common carriers authorized to operate in the metropolitan area, and also for the purpose of solving traffic problems on the route between San Juan and Río Piedras and intermediate points including Caparra Heights and Puerto Nuevo settlements.

Therefore, the Public Service Commission of Puerto Rico hereby decides and orders: "It is hereby definitely forbidden by this order, that any owner of motor vehicles, with a capacity of ten (10) passengers or less, to transport, personally or through an agent, passengers for pay between different points within the metropolitan area, that is, between the city of San Juan and its barrios and between the city of San Juan and the City of Río Piedras and intermediate points including Caparra Heights and Puerto Nuevo settlements without first having obtained a certificate of convenience and necessity issued by the Public Service Commission of Puerto Rico. 

"The Insular Police and the Inspector of this Commission shall be in charge of the enforcement of this order. "Any violation of this order shall be considered as a viola tion of Act No. 70, approved December 6, 1917 [27 L.P.R.A. 

§ 1 et seq.], as subsequently amended, and shall be punished according to the provisions of sec. 95 of said Act [27 L.P.R.A. § 244], provided, that for purposes of enforcement both the owner and the chauffeur or driver of the vehicle operating in the metropolitan area, violating the provisions of this order, shall be deemed violators. "This order shall go into effect on July 1st, 1949. 392

§ 72-303. Application for certificate 

The applications for certificates of convenience and necessity required by this Division shall be filed under oath by the petitioner with the Public Service Commission of Puerto Rico, and shall contain the following: (1) Name and post-office address of the applicant. (2) Description of the vehicle for which the certificate of convenience and necessity is applied, including make, model, motor number, passenger capacity, license number, and date on which it was issued by the Secretary of Public Works. (3) Description of all other vehicles owned by the applicant including their make, license number, and capacity. (4) Specification of the intermediate points between which the vehicle is to operate and a description of the terminals and the specific route over which the vehicle is to operate. (5) Detailed statement of the facts upon which the applicant relies to demonstrate that the privilege he requests is of public convenience and necessity. (6) All applications shall be accompanied by a certificate of the

Secretary of Public Works indicating all the vehicles registered in the name of the applicant in the records of his Department, and which also shows the address of the applicant and the date the public service license was originally issued to the vehicle for which the application is filed, in case the vehicle has such public service license. 

§ 72-304. Consideration of applications 

Applications for certificates of convenience and necessity to operate a vehicle subject to the provisions of this Subdivision shall be considered under the procedure provided by the Rules of Procedure of the Public Service Commission. 393

§ 72-305. Licenses and insignia 

Every vehicle subject to this Subdivision shall display over the windshield and over the back window, in letters not less than 3 inches high and permanently painted in a color contrasting with that of the vehicle, a description of its authorized route. 

§ 72-306. Painting 

Every vehicle subject to this Subdivision shall be painted in the colors and manner prescribed by the Commission. 

§ 72-307. Exterior signs 

No vehicle subject to this Subdivision shall have any exterior signs except those herein provided for without the previous approval of the Commission. 

§ 72-308. Display of annual license 

Every vehicle subject to the provisions of this Subdivision shall display in a conspicuous place inside the vehicle an annual license issued by the Commission after said vehicle has been inspected by the mechanical inspector of the Commission and a favorable report is rendered. 

§ 72-309. Number plate 

Every vehicle subject to the provisions of this Subdivision shall be provided with a plate or any other device, as determined by the Commission, which shall be supplied by the secretary of the Commission upon the payment of a fee of $1. This plate shall be firmly affixed on the front of the vehicle with the numbers perpendicularly located in such a way that it is clearly visible at a distance of 50 feet ahead. 

§ 72-310. Operators 

No common carrier shall permit or authorize any person to operate or drive any vehicle subject to this Subdivision, unless the said person is a driver or chauffeur duly authorized by the 

Secretary of Public Works to drive public service vehicles. 

§ 72-311. Operator's license 

No person shall conduct, drive, or operate a vehicle subject to this Subdivision unless he is a driver duly authorized by the 394

Ch. 

T.27 § 72-319 

Department of Public Works of Puerto Rico to drive public service vehicles. 

§ 72-312. Vehicle license 

No operator shall drive a vehicle subject to this Subdivision unless said vehicle is duly licensed by the Commission and it displays the insignia and license required under this Subdivision. 

§ 72-313. Cleanliness of operator 

Every operator shall be clean in dress and in person.

§ 72-314. Conduct of operator 

Operators shall observe a correct and respectful conduct towards the public and passengers riding in their vehicles. 

§ 72-315. Charging rates 

Operators shall not charge rates different from those approved by the Commission. 

§ 72-316. Rate fixing 

The Commission by order or resolution shall fix the rates to be charged by the vehicles subject to this Subdivision on those routes and in such cases where circumstances require. 

§ 72-317. Routes 

Every vehicle subject to this Subdivision shall be operated exclusively on trips between the terminals of its authorized route. 

Not completing the entire trip, without cause, when transporting passengers, or going beyond the terminal with passengers, or abandoning the authorized route while transporting passengers shall be deemed cause for revocation or cancellation of the certificate of convenience and necessity authorizing the service. 

§ 72-318. Transfer and substitutions 

The certificates granted under this Subdisivion shall be considered nontransferable, except in cases of force majeure or extraordinary circumstances, with the previous approval and consent of the Commission; provided, that, noncompliance with this section shall be considered sufficient cause for the cancellation of the corresponding certificate. § 72-319. Approval for transfer, sale, or assignment

No certificate of convenience and necessity issued by the Com- 395

T.§ 72-319 

PUBLIC SERVICE 

Ch. 5 mission shall be transferred, sold, or in any way assigned to third persons without first requesting under oath and obtaining the approval of the Commission for such transfer, sale, or assignment. 

§ 72-320. Substitution of vehicle 

Substitution of vehicle shall be permitted only in cases where the substituted vehicle is destroyed or goes into private service. 

§ 72-321. Violations 

(a) The violation on the part of a common carrier, personally or through an agent, of any of the provisions of this Subdivision or orders issued by the Commission or the traffic laws and regulations, or the operation of vehicles under such conditions that they constitute a menace to public safety, or if there is reason to believe that the owner of the vehicle is not qualified or competent to operate such type of vehicle, shall be sufficient cause for the suspension, cancellation, or revocation of the certificate of convenience and necessity authorizing the service. (b) With the approval of the Chairman of the Commission, the chief inspector of the Traffic Division shall have the authority to suspend, without previous notice, for a term not to exceed 15 days, the operation of a vehicle for the reasons stated in the previous paragraph. (c) Once a suspension is ordered by the chief inspector of the Traffic Division the common carrier shall be summoned to appear before the official of the Commission designated in said order within a term not to exceed 15 days from the date of suspension, to show cause and reasons, if he has any, why a longer period of suspension or the definite cancellation of the certificate of convenience and necessity should not be ordered; provided, that, if the hearing is postponed at the request of the common carrier operation of the vehicle shall remain suspended until the case is finally decided by the Commission, even though the term of 15 days of temporary suspension has elapsed. (d) The official designated to preside at the hearing shall render a report to the Commission, after hearing the parties, with his recommendations, and the Commission shall decide what it deems fit; provided, that, within the term of 15 days after notice is served of disciplinary action taken, the person affected by said action may file a motion for reconsideration and rehearing to be held before the Commission or any of the commissioners; provided 396

Ch. 

T.27 § 72-326 further, that, until the case is finally decided, the disciplinary action taken shall remain in force. (e) In the case of the cancellation of a certificate, the Secretary of Public Works shall cancel the public service license of the vehicle. 

§ 72-322. Name and address of carrier 

Every common carrier shall give the Commission his full name and address. Any change in name or address shall be reported in writing to the Commission within 48 hours after the change occurs. 

§ 72-323. Powers of Commission 

Nothing herein provided shall be understood as limiting the general powers of the Commission, which retains the power to approve any pertinent orders to regulate the vehicles under its jurisdiction and also to grant special or provisional permits for the operation of vehicles on certain routes when deemed convenient. 

§ 72-324. Exemptions 

Notwithstanding the provisions of this Subdivision, the Secretary retains the power, through order to said effect, to exempt any common carrier from compliance with any of said provisions when considered justified and convenient. 

§ 72-325. Penalties 

The violation of any of the preceding rules or provisions shall be subject to the penal sanction established by the "Public Service 

Law of Puerto Rico", Act No. 70 approved Dec. 6, 1917, as amended [27 L.P.R.A. §§ 1-255]; nevertheless, the Commission, in any case of violation of the preceding rules or provisions may, after a public hearing, suspend or cancel, temporarily or permanently, any permit or certificate of convenience and necessity. 

§ 72-326. Effectiveness 

This Subdivision shall go into effect immediately after its approval by the Governor of Puerto Rico. 

Approval date. Regulation File No. 94, set out in this

Subdivision, was approved by the Governor June 24, 1949.

No. 70 of December 6, 1917, as amended [27 L.P.R.A. § 72].

Separability. Sec. 77 of Regulation File No. 88, set out in this Division, provided: "Should any provision of these Regulations be declared illegal or unconstitutional by a court, such decree or judgment shall not apply to the other provisions of these Regulations, and to said effect these shall be considered separate and as if adopted independently of any provision declared illegal or unconstitutional."
