"These Regulations repeal any provisions, regulation, order, resolution or determination in regard to this matter adopted prior to this date, with the exception of the provisions in connection with insurance and rates contained in the Resolution issued by the Commission on August 9, 1955." 

§ 72-402. Definitions 

The following terms, whenever used or referred to in this Division, shall have the meaning hereinafter set forth, except where the context clearly indicates otherwise, and the singular number 402

Ch. T.27 § 72-403 

shall be construed to include the plural, and vice versa, as the case may be: (1) "Commission" means the Public Service Commission of 

Puerto Rico. 

(2) "Taxi" means any 4-door motor vehicle with permanent top of steel and with not over 7-passenger capacity, engaged in the transportation of passengers for hire between points within an urban zone and adjacent areas without fixed routes and time schedule. "Adjacent areas" means the territory comprised within 

8 miles from the limits of an urban zone. (3) "For hire" means the exclusive use of a taxi by one or more persons, with the consent of the one who hires, and includes the fare registered by the meter or the fare per hour in accordance with the rates in force approved by the Commission applicable to taxicab service. Only one charge should be made for the trip. irrespective of the number of passengers carried. (4) "Company" means any person, association, partnership, corporation, cooperative, or any organization of any kind which engages or intends to engage in taxicab service. (5) "Operator" means the person who drives or controls a motor vehicle engaged in taxicab service. (6) "Taximeter" means the instrument approved by the Commission which registers the distance travelled and the time the taxicab is used, as well as the fare to be paid by the passenger in accordance with the rates in force approved by the Commission. (7) "Cooperative" means any association or group of persons organized in accordance with the General Cooperatives Association 

Act of Puerto Rico, No. 291, approved on April 9, 1946 [5 L.P.R.A. 

§§ 881-909], for the purpose of engaging in taxicab service. (8) "Association" means a group of taxicab owners organized for the purpose of using common facilities, a business name, colors, insignia, or emblems. (9) "License" means franchise, certificate, permit, right, privilege, or authorization granted by the Commission to engage in taxicab service, irrespective of the number of taxicabs owned, or to act as an operator. 

§ 72-403. Taxicab license 

From the date this Division is in force, no company shall engage any motor vehicle in taxicab service unless the vehicle has a valid taxicab license issued by the Commission and has complied with 403

T.§ 72-403 

PUBLIC SERVICE Ch. 5 

the requirements established by this Division with regard to insurance, equipment, colors, and insignia. The license must be renewed every year. Once a taxicab license is granted, the taxicab must be operated within 30 days and its operation may not be suspended for more than 5 days unless the Commission authorizes such suspension. 

§ 72-404. Requirements for license 

The following requirements shall be complied with to obtain a taxicab license: 

(1) To file with the Commission a sworn statement stating the following facts: Name and address of the applicant; his financial status; description of the vehicle, including make, motor number, model, and license number issued by the Secretary of Public Works; the exact address from which the vehicle is to be operated and the telephone number, if any; the name under which the business will be conducted; the design or identification emblem; and the color or combination of colors to be used. (2) If the applicant is a natural person, he must file a certificate of conduct issued by the Police Department. The Commission may require when it deems convenient such certificate from the owners, partners, shareholders, or directors of artificial persons. 

§ 72-405. Transfers 

The transfers of licensed taxicabs shall not be authorized by the Commission unless 3 or more years have elapsed since the license was granted and special circumstances concur to justify it. 

§ 72-406. Accident insurance 

(a) Every company shall furnish a guaranty by means of a real mortgage or insurance policy through an insurance company duly authorized to do business in Puerto Rico to cover such a minimum amount as the Commission may determine for each vehicle as a guaranty for the payment of compensation to any person who suffers injuries or damages in any accident caused by the careless or negligent operation of the taxicab or defects in it. The insurance companies shall notify the Commission of all cancellations of insurance policies for default in payment. Said insurance companies shall not cancel any insurance policy for any cause other than default in payment without the previous approval of the Commis- 404

Ch. 

 T.27 § 72-411 

sion, or without having notified the Commission of its intention to cancel said policy, at least 15 days before the date of such cancellation. This provision shall be a condition of the insurance policy. 

When this Division is in effect, no taxicab shall operate until its surety is approved by the Commission. (b) The Commission shall not approve any bond consisting of an insurance policy with an insurance company which has not complied with the provision relative to the insurance contract required by this section. (c) In event that the Commission cancels a taxicab license, the insurance contract shall remain in effect until all claims commenced, due to acts or omissions which occurred before the cancellation, have been decided by the courts. 

§ 72-407. Rates 

Fixing, posting

Rates to be charged by taxicabs shall be those which, after legal proceedings, have been or are approved by the Commission and they shall be posted as provided in secs. 72-411 and 72-416 

of this title. 

§ 72-408. 

Payment of fare

No person who expressly or implicitly hires a taxicab shall refuse to pay the lawful charge, according to the rates in force and in accordance with sec. 72-443 of this title. 

§ 72-409. Discount 

No coupons or service cards that can result in a discount or reduction of the rates in force or any other method which may cause a change in the rates shall be used. 

§ 72-410. Equipment, colors, and insignia 

Generally Every taxicab in service shall be kept clean and in good mechanical and safe condition with seats, brakes, tires, body, windshield wipers, lights, and ignition system in good condition and shall always be supplied with fuel and oil. The tires shall be of the size proper for the vehicle and their air pressure shall be in accordance to their size. 

§ 72-411. 

Posting of material within taxicab

Every authorized taxicab shall have posted on the back of the front seat, visible to the passengers, the taxicab license, its opera- 

405

T.27 72 Ch. 5 

PUBLIC SERVICE 

tor's license with his picture, the amount of the insurance, the insurance company, if any, the rates in force and the conditions under which the taxicab is authorized to operate. The operator must look' in the picture as he does when he is driving the taxicab. 

§ 72-412. Taximeter 

Every taxicab shall be equipped with a taximeter duly inspected, sealed, and stamped by the Commission and adjusted in accordance with the rates in force. No taxicab thus equipped may travel or operate with passengers when the taximeter is not functioning or is defective unless the passenger has chartered it on the basis of the per hour rate. It shall be unlawful for any person to change the taximeter or allow it to be changed, or to remove its seal or allow it to be removed after it has been inspected and sealed by the Commission. 

§ 72-413. Curtains, passengers in front

No taxicab may be equipped with curtains which can be operated in such a way as to conceal the passengers or the operator, nor carry more than 3 persons, the operator included, in the front seat. 

§ 72-414. Radios 

The radio set installed in any taxicab may not be tuned in unless the passenger expressly approves. This provision should not be construed as prohibiting the use of a radio-telephone to communicate with the central office of the company. 

§ 72-415. Information posted on outside of taxicab

Every taxicab shall display on both front doors a design or emblem to identify it or its trade name and the name of the company which operates the taxicab. It shall also display on both sides of the vehicle the word "taxi", unless it is included in the emblem or design or in the trade name. The word "taxi" may be used only by companies authorized by the Commission to operate taxicabs. 

No other vehicle may use such word or any other term which may give the impression that it is engaged in taxicab service. When a company operates more than one taxicab, each of them shall display a correlative number which identifies it, corresponding to the number of taxicabs owned and operated by it. 

§ 72-416. 

Posting of rates on outside of taxicab

Every taxicab shall display permanently on the exterior of the 406

Ch. 

T.27 § 72-423 rear doors, legible at a reasonable distance, the rates in force, except the charges for baggage and waiting time. § 72-417. Approval of emblem or trade name

No company shall use an emblem or trade name without previously obtaining the Commission's aproval. § 72-418. Color, style, and size of letters, numbers, and emblems 

The letters, numbers, and emblems or designs shall be of a color, style, and size legible under normal light conditions. 

§ 72-419. Top light

Every taxicab shall be equipped with a top light on the front part of the top with the word "taxi", the trade name or the name of the company legible at a reasonable distance. The top light shall be off when the taximeter is working and on when not in use. The taximeter shall be working at all times whenever the taxicab is carrying a passenger, except when the taxicab has been hired on a per hour basis in accordance with the rates in force. 

§ 72-420. 

Top light on other vehicles

No vehicle which is not authorized by the Commission to operate as a taxicab shall have a top light or any other apparatus used for the same purpose, with or without light or label. The Commission, however, may authorize the use of a top light on public service vehicles operating between cities. 

§ 72-421. Other labels 

No taxicab shall display other labels than those authorized by these rules without the previous approval of the Commission. 

§ 72-422. Colors 

Every taxicab shall be painted with a color or combination of colors identifying the company to which it belongs, and said color or combination of colors shall be previously approved by the Commission. 

§ 72-423. 

Colors, insignia, and emblems to be distinctive

No taxicab shall have colors, insignia, or emblems which in the opinion of the Commission are not readily distinguishable from the colors, insignia, or emblems previously approved for other companies. 

407

T.§ 72-424 Ch. 5 

PUBLIC SERVICE § 72-424. Inspection 

Taxicabs shall be inspected every 120 days, it being compulsory for the operator and owner to bring it to the Commission or to the place designated for inspection. 

§ 72-425. Inspection tag 

Every taxicab shall display on the inner side of the windshield, and where it does not affect the visibility of the operator, evidence that the vehicle has been inspected. 

§ 72-426. Cooperatives and associations 

Individual owners of one or more taxicabs in a specific area may organize themselves as cooperatives or associations to operate not less than five taxicabs under a common trade name, colors, combination of colors, and emblem or insigne. § 72-427. Information filed by association (a) Every cooperative or association shall file with the Commission the following information: (1) A copy of its certificate of incorporation, if incorporated, or the bylaws of the cooperative or association. (2) The conditions and rules in regard to its organization and operation. (3) Name and address of each member and the make, motor number, license plate number, taxicab license number, and the number given to each car. (4) Evidence that its members have complied with the requirements of sec. 72-430 of this title. (b) All changes made in the information required by this section shall be filed with the Commission within 24 hours after the change. 

§ 72-428. Operators -License requirement 

No company shall consent or allow any person to drive or control a taxicab belonging to it unless such person is an operator duly authorized by the Commission and whose license is in force. 

§ 72-429. Discharged operator

No operator who has been discharged by any company on grounds that may cause the suspension or cancellation of his license shall be employed by another company without the previous ap- 100 408

Ch. 

T.27 § 72-431 proval of the Commission. The company who discharges any operator shall notify the Commission within 48 hours of his discharge stating the reasons for the discharge. § 72-430. 

Requirements for license

No person shall act as a taxicab operator unless he has applied for and obtained an authorization from the Commission. To obtain it he must comply with the following requirements: (1) Be a citizen of the United States and of the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico. 

(2) Be between 21 and 65 years of age. (3) Be a chauffeur duly authorized by the Secretary of Public Works and have at least 2 years' experience as an operator of public vehicles or with heavy vehicles of the armed forces while in military service. 

(4) Read and write Spanish and make himself understood in English. (5) File: (A) His record as chauffeur or chauffeur of heavy motor vehicles from the Department of Public Works. The applicant may request that this record and the one required by clause (5) (B) of this section be obtained by the Commission. (B) Certificate of conduct issued by the Police Department as of the date the application is filed. (C) Medical certificate of a public health unit or a private physician stating that petitioner is in good physical condition, especially of the following organs and limbs: eyes, ears, heart, lungs, condition of legs and arms (reflexes). (D) Three pictures, size 2" x 2". (E) Birth certificate. (F) Photostatic copy of discharge, if a veteran. (6) Pass an examination prescribed by the Commission which shall include, among other things, knowledge of the streets and places of the zone of operations. 

§ 72-431. Renewal 

The operator's license shall be renewed every 2 years. To do so the requirements expressed in sec. 72-430 (5) (A), (B), (C), and (D) must again be complied with. The knowledge of English is not applicable to operators previously authorized. 

409

T.§ 72-432 Ch. 5 

PUBLIC SERVICE § 72-432. Name and address, change 

Every operator shall give his name and address, and change of address shall be reported to the Commission within 48 hours of the change.

By 

§ 72-433. Cleanliness 

Every operator shall be clean in his clothing and body.

§ 72-434. 

Drug addiction; alcoholism

No operator shall be a drug addict or a habitual or excessive user of intoxicating beverages. 

§ 72-435. Smoking No operator shall smoke while the taxi he is operating is carrying passengers. 

§ 72-436. 

Starting taximeter

At the beginning of each trip the taximeter shall not have any amount registered and it is the operator's duty to start it when the taxicab is occupied by a passenger, except when it is hired by the hour in accordance with the rate in force. 

§ 72-437. 

Tampering with taximeter

If a taximeter is altered or its seal removed it shall be considered prima facie evidence that the operator altered it or allowed its alteration, or removed its seal or allowed its removal. 

§ 72-438. 

Stopping at request of passenger

It shall be the duty of every operator to stop the taxicab at the request of a passenger. Nothing herein contained shall be construed to compel the operator to stop in places prohibited by municipal ordinance, traffic law, or regulations. 

§ 72-439. 

Route, delays, end of trip 

Once the trip is started the operator shall not cause unnecessary delays. The trip shall be made by the shortest route, except when the passenger states the route. The trip shall be considered ended when the passenger alights from the vehicle and the operator's duty in regard to the passenger's baggage ends when he unloads it. 

§ 72-440. Lost articles 

At the end of each trip the operator shall examine the taxicab 410

Ch. 5

 T.27 § 72-446 

to make sure that the passenger has not left any package or object. 

If after the passenger has left he discovers any package or object he shall attempt to return it to its owner within 30 minutes and, if unable to do so, he shall take it to the City Hall where the pro ceedings provided in the Civil Code [31 L.P.R.A. § 1 et seq.] will be followed. 

§ 72-441. Conduct 

Every operator shall observe correct and respectful conduct toward the public and passengers. Any behavior showing disregard of the duties imposed upon him by this Division or any rude or disrespectful conduct or behavior at variance with moral and proper conduct, that should be observed by every person serving the public, shall be sufficient cause for the suspension or cancellation of the operator's license. 

§ 72-442. 

Request to use taxicab

The operator shall honor any proper and legal request to use the taxicab. To ignore or refuse such request shall be prima facie evidence of voluntary violation of this section. 

§ 72-443. Additional charges 

No operator may collect or demand a charge or amount higher than that resulting from the rates in force irrespective of the number of passengers carried, except the additional charges authorized for baggage, etc. 

§ 72-444. Recommendation of business places

Except at the request of a passenger, no operator may recommend the patronage of restaurants, night clubs, dance halls, hotels, or other businesses of the same nature. Nor may he recommend any illegal business places. 

§ 72-445. 

Compliance with laws and regulations; inspection 

Every taxicab shall be operated in accordance with the laws, ordinances, and traffic regulations in force. Every operator shall stop and allow the inspection of the taxicab at the request of any inspector of the Commission. 

§ 72-446. 

Letting off, picking up passengers

No operator shall stop the taxicab to let off or pick up passengers in a street or road intersection, or in such a manner as to 

411

T.§ 72-446 Ch. 5 

PUBLIC SERVICE 

block or interfere with the traffic. He shall stop the vehicle to let off or pick up passengers as near to the curb as possible or close to the right side of the road if it does not have a sidewalk. 

§ 72-447. Parking near another company's stand

No operator shall park the taxicab in the vicinity of another company's stand. 

§ 72-448. 

Improper use of taxicab

No operator shall use or allow the use of the taxicab for illegal or immoral purposes. Nor may he turn over the operation of the taxicab to an unauthorized person, without the company's consent. 

§ 72-449. 

Money for change

Every operator shall have at all times not less than $5 in change. 

§ 72-450. Receipt to passenger 

Every operator shall furnish at a passenger's request a receipt stating his name, his operator's license number, the time and place of origin and destination of the trip and the amount collected. To comply with this requirement he shall have at all times a receipt book in the taxicab. 

§ 72-451. Area covered 

Except with a special permit from the Commission, no operator shall travel from 6:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. with the taxicab beyond the adjacent areas, as they are defined in sec. 72-402 (2) of this title, of the urban zone in which it is authorized to operate. 

§ 72-452. Revocation of license 

The violation of any of the provisions of this Division, or the conviction for a crime involving moral turpitude, or for the violation of traffic laws or regulations, shall be deemed sufficient cause for the revocation of the operator's license, following the procedure provided in this Division. A license which has been revoked or cancelled shall be returned to the Commission by the operator. 

§ 72-453. 

Daily record

Every operator shall keep a daily record of all trips made, stating the time and place of origin and destination of each trip and the amount charged for it. 412

Ch. 

 T.27 § 72-458 § 72-454. Accident report 

Every operator shall render to the company for which he works a written report of any accident he may have had in which persons were killed or injured or damages to other persons' property were caused. This report shall be rendered within 24 hours after the accident. 

§ 72-455. Complaint against operator

Every natural or artificial person who wishes to complain against an operator shall write to the Commission stating the acts performed by the operator and the date, time, and place they occurred, the description of the taxicab, plate number, the company to which it belongs, etc. In the letter the complainant shall also state his name and address, as well as the name and address of his witnesses, if any. 

§ 72-456. Office of Legal Services 

Every complaint received in accordance with the previous section shall be referred by the Chairman to the office of legal services of the Commission, who shall study it to determine if the facts stated therein constitute a violation of this Division. § 72-457. Complaint not stating a violation 

Should the office of legal services determine that the facts stated in the complaint do not constitute a violation, it shall thus report to the Chairman, who shall inform the complainant and the Commission. Unless the Commission disagrees with the report it shall order that the complaint be filed. § 72-458. Complaint stating violation

Should the office of legal service determine that an operator has violated this Division, it shall thus report with recommendations to the Chairman, who shall notify the Commission and the complainant, if any, of the action taken. If the recommendation is to the effect that the operator's license be suspended or cancelled, the Commission, through the Chairman or one of the members of the Commission, shall notify the operator of the facts reported and shall order him to appear at a specific time and place before the official designated to hear him in regard to the reported facts. The notice to the operator shall be made by registered mail to his last known address according to the Commission's records. Should the 413

T.§ 72-458 Ch. 5 

PUBLIC SERVICE 

operator waive hearing or fail to appear at the hearing, the Commission may suspend or revoke the license without further summons or hearing. § 72-459. Hearing, rehearing, action 

The official appointed to preside at the hearing, once the appearing party or parties are heard, shall render a report with his recommendations to the Commission and the Commission shall take whatever action it deems pertinent. Within 15 days after notice of the disciplinary action is served, the operator concerned may petition for reconsideration and rehearing, the rehearing to be held before the Commission or one of the commissioners. Until the case is finally decided, the disciplinary action taken shall remain in full force. 

§ 72-460. Suspension 

The Commission may, in the manner specified in sec. 72-470 of this title, temporarily suspend the license issued to an operator. 

This authority shall be exercised when in its opinion the operator is incompetent or unable to drive or when the facts charged against him constitute a menace to public safety. 

§ 72-461. Reports and accounting system Name, address of company 

Every company shall give the Commission its name and address and any change in name or address shall be reported to the Commission within 48 hours of the change. 

§ 72-462. Preservation of daily record 

The daily record referred to in sec. 72-453 of this title shall be kept by the company for at least 1 year from its date for examination by the Commission. 

§ 72-463. Records relating to operators 

Every company shall keep a record of the operators working on the various shifts, with their license numbers and vehicles operated by them. This information shall be at all times available to the 

Commission, and shall be immediately forwarded at the request of the Commission, the Director of the Bureau of Inspection, or the secretary of the Commission. 414

Ch. 

 T.27 § 72-470 

= 

Company's accident report

Every company shall render a written report to the Commission of every accident occurring to its vehicle in which persons are killed or injured or damages to other persons' property are caused; said report to be rendered within 24 hours after the company receives the report of the accident from the operator. In case the operator does not render his report to the company, said company shall render its report within 24 hours after it has knowledge of the accident. 

§ 72-465. Insurance company's report

The report required by sec. 72-464 of this title shall be rendered to the Commission by the insurance company covering the vehicle within 48 hours after the accident has been reported to them by the company. The insurance company is subject in this regard to the requirements of sec. 72-406 of this title. 

$ 72-466. 

Reports as evidence 

No report rendered in accordance with this section shall be used in evidence in any criminal or civil action for damages arising from the matters mentioned in the report. 

§ 72-467. Labor contracts 

Every individual or collective contract or agreement which affects the worker-employer relations between the companies and operators shall be filed with the Commission within 5 days after it has been made. Any change in said contract or agreement shall also be reported to the Commission within the same period. 

§ 72-468. 

Accounting system; biannual statements 

Every company shall keep the accounting system prescribed by the Commission and, when it has in operation 5 or more taxicabs, it shall render biannual financial statements. 

§ 72-469. 

Chartering 

No company shall charter the use of two or more taxicabs permanently or for long periods without the previous approval of the Commission. 

§ 72-470. Suspension of taxicab license

If the Commission learns that in any part of Puerto Rico any motor vehicle subject to this Division is operated without having 415

T.§ 72-470 

PUBLIC SERVICE 

Ch. 5 complied with the requirements herein stated, or after having complied with these requirements said vehicle is being operated under conditions that constitute a menace to public safety or if there is reason to believe that the owner or operator of the taxicab is not competent to own or operate such type of vehicle, or is violating this Division, the Commission may issue an order, without previous notice, temporarily suspending the operation of said vehicle for a period not to exceed 15 days. Immediately after suspending the operation of a vehicle in the manner described above, the Commission shall summon its owner to appear before the official designated by the Commission to preside at the hearing within a period not to exceed 15 days from the date of suspension to show cause, if any there be, why a longer period of suspension or the definite cancellation of the taxicab license should not be ordered. If the hearing is postponed at the request of the party involved, the license shall remain suspended until the case is finally decided by the Commission, even though the 15 days of temporary suspension have elapsed. 

§ 72-471. Powers of Commission 

None of the provisions contained in this Division shall be construed in any way as limiting or restricting the general powers of the Commission, which retains the power to approve any pertinent orders to regulate taxicab service in Puerto Rico. 

§ 72-472. Exemptions 

Notwithstanding the provisions of this Division the Commission. retains the power, through order to said effect, to grant exemptions from compliance with any of said provisions when considered justified and convenient. 

§ 72-473. Liability of companies 

The companies shall be liable for violations of this Division committed by their operators. § 72-474. Licenses in force

The licenses in force at the time this Division takes effect shall remain in force, but they are subject to the provisions relative to their renewal. 

§ 72-475. Persons to enforce compliance 

(a) Policemen, public service inspectors, and the employees of 416

Ch. 

T.27 § 72-601 the Department of Public Works in charge of policing and maintenance of roads shall require compliance with this Division and, in case of violations thereof, shall notify the Commission and file complaints in court. (b) Every citizen shall have the right to demand from operators compliance with this Division. In case of noncompliance, he shall have the right to file a complaint before the Commission, as provided in sec. 72-455 of this title, or before the courts. 

§ 72-476. Penal clause 

The violation of any of the preceding rules shall constitute a misdemeanor and shall be subject to the penal sanction established by the Public Service Act of Puerto Rico [27 L.P.R.A. § 1 et seq.]. 

However, the Commission, in case of violation of any of the preceding rules, may, after hearing, suspend or cancel the taxicab license or operator's license involved. § 72-477. Effectiveness

This Division shall take effect immediately after its approval by the Governor. 

Approval date. Regulation File No. 88, set out in this Division, was approved by the Governor Feb. 14, 1957.

§ 72-601. Definitions 

(a) It shall be understood that the words or terms used in this 417

T.§ 72-601 Ch. 5 

PUBLIC SERVICE 

Division in the singular shall have a plural meaning, or vice versa, as the case may be. (b) The following terms, whenever used or referred to in this Division, shall have the meaning hereinafter expressed, except where the context clearly indicates otherwise: (1) "Commission" shall mean the Public Service Commission of Puerto Rico. (2) "Ticket agent" shall include any natural or artificial person engaged in the sale or offer for sale of air or marine passage to third persons so that the latter are transported from any point in Puerto Rico to another point within Puerto Rico, or outside of Puerto Rico, using air or marine routes; provided, that, for the purpose of this Division, every sub-agent and every representative of nonscheduled air lines engaged in the sale of air passage, directly or through agents, shall be considered as a ticket agent; provided further, that, nothing hereinbefore provided shall apply to the sale of air or marine passage directly by air or shipping enterprises duly certified or authorized to operate regularly or on schedule on the routes of Puerto Rico under the federal laws governing the matter.

Separability. Sec. 20 of Regulation File No. 90, set out in this Division, provided: "Should any section, clause, provision, article, paragraph, or part of these regulations be declared null, illegal, or unconstitutional by final decree of a court of competent jurisdiction, such decree or judgment shall not apply to the other clauses, sections, provisions, articles, paragraphs, or parts of these regulations, and for said purposes it is hereby declared that the same are separable and as though adopted independently from any declared void, illegal, or unconstitutional." 

§ 72-602. Licenses 

Thirty days subsequent to the approval of this Division by the Governor of Puerto Rico, no artificial or natural person shall engage in business as a ticket agent, or advertise himself in any way as such ticket agent, without having a ticket agent license issued by the Commission; provided, that every person who seeks transportation for persons who have bought their tickets outside of Puerto 418

Ch. T.27 72-606 

Rico shall be considered a ticket agent subject to the provisions of this Division. 

§ 72-603. Application for license 

Every application to obtain a ticket agent license, filed with the Commission, shall be duly verified under oath by the petitioner, and shall contain, as part of the same, the following: (1) Name and post-office address of the applicant. In the case of a corporation, it shall include also the name and post-office addresses of its directors, and shall be accompanied by a copy of the articles of incorporation, a certificate of incorporation, and a certificate of the treasurer of the corporation showing the paid-in capital of said applicant.

In the case of a partnership, the application shall state also the names and post-office addresses of the partners and shall be accompanied by a certified copy of the articles of partnership. (2) Description and location of the place to be used in the business. (3) The financial condition of the applicant, stating in detail the properties owned and their location and value. The total debts and obligations of the applicant shall also be stated. (4) In the case of a natural person, the application shall be accompanied by a certificate issued by the Chief of the Police of Puerto Rico regarding the personal record of the petitioner. In the case of a corporation or partnership, a similar certificate of the personal record of directors or partners shall be included. 

§ 72-604. Notice, hearings 

The Commission, when in its judgment the public interest and convenience so require, or at the request of an interested party, may order the publication of notices and the holding of a public hearing in regard to any application filed with the Commission, in conformity with the provisions of this Division. 

§ 72-605. Denial of application 

The Commission shall have the power to deny any application for a ticket agent license when in its judgment the petitioner is not economically or morally qualified to engage in this type of business in Puerto Rico. 

§ 72-606. Records and reports 

(a) Every ticket agent shall keep a daily record or manifest on which the following data shall appear: 419

T.§ 72-606 Ch. 5 

PUBLIC SERVICE (1) Name of the purchaser of the ticket. 

(2) Price of the ticket. (3) City in which the trip is to start and city of destination. (4) Name of the air or shipping line to furnish the transportation when it is a certified or regular line. If the passage is to be made by a ship or plane to be chartered by the agent, it shall be so specified, together with the name of the owner of the ship or plane, if possible. (b) This record or manifest shall be kept by the ticket agent in his files for a period of not less than a year, and it shall be completed in conformity with the form or model that may be prescribed by order of the Commission.

PUBLIC SERVICE § 72-607. Form regarding sale of passage 

(a) It shall be unlawful to complete a sale of air or marine passage without filling out a form to be signed by the ticket agent or his representative and by the purchaser of the ticket, which shall contain the following information: 

(1) Name and license number of the ticket agent. 

(2) Name of the purchaser of the ticket, specifying his address in Puerto Rico and the address at his destination outside of Puerto 

Rico. 

(3) Age, sex, weight, marital status, and occupation of the purchaser of the ticket. (4) Purpose of the trip. If the purpose is to leave Puerto Rico to work, it shall specify if he is going under contract and the name of the contracting person or entity. (5) Date on which the trip is to be made. (6) Name of the line which is to furnish the transportation. (7) Price of the ticket. (8) If an air ticket, the number of motors of the plane and type of seat. (9) Time and place where the sale is made. (b) The original of this form shall be delivered by the agent to the purchaser of the ticket and said original copy shall not be taken from the passenger until he boards the plane or ship; two copies shall be sent to the Commission within 24 hours after the sale; and a fourth copy shall be kept by the agent in his files for a period of not less than 1 year from the date of the trip. (c) The Commission shall prescribe, by order to said effect, the form or model to be used in the sales; and likewise, the Commission, in the case of sale of tickets by a scheduled line, which is made by telephone, may exempt from compliance with the requirement the signature of the purchaser or the delivery of the original to him.

PUBLIC SERVICE § 72-608. Charter trips 

(a) Every ticket agent who charters ships or planes for the transportation of passengers from any point in Puerto Rico to another point within or outside of Puerto Rico, or any ticket agent who as representative of a nonscheduled airline dispatches a plane with passengers to whom he has sold tickets directly or through agents, shall file with the Commission within 

24 hours after the start of the trip, a report on which the following information shall appear: (1) Name and license number of the agent. (2) Name and address of the owner of the ship or plane and number of certificate or license of the same. (3) Time and place in which the trip started. (4) Detailed list of the names of the passengers with their addresses in Puerto Rico and addresses at their destination. (b) Copies of this report shall be kept by the ticket agent in his files for a period of not less than 1 year from the date on which the trip is started. The Commission shall prescribe, by order to said effect, the form or model to be used for this report.

§ 72-609. Additional reports 

Every ticket agent shall file with the Commission such additional reports as the Commission may require. 

§ 72-610. Bond 

Every ticket agent shall submit a bond by a mortgage through an insurance company duly authorized to operate as such in Puerto Rico, for an amount whose minimum shall be fixed by the Commission after a hearing, to cover any damages caused for breach of contract to any persons to whom the agent sells tickets. 

§ 72-611. Inspections and examinations 

Every ticket agent shall allow any agent or official of the Commission, as well as the agents of the Department of Labor, to enter, inspect, and examine, on any working day and hour, the books, records, and documents of the agency; and said ticket agent shall give the officials of the Commission the necessary help to make the inspection and examination. § 72-612. Posting of license, rates

Every ticket agent shall display in his office in a place visible to the public the license issued by the Commission. Likewise, in every ticket agent's office there shall be displayed, visible to the public, copies of the rates in force of the different air or steamship lines for which the agent sells tickets; provided, that, in case a ticket agent does not represent an air or steamship line and his business consists of selling tickets for a second ticket agency, the former shall display in a visible place in his office the rates in force of the air or steamship lines represented by the second ticket agent, and when filling out the form required by sec. 72-607 he shall state the specific airline for which the ticket is sold. 

§ 72-613. Advertising 

In every sign or advertisement displayed or published by a ticket agent, the license number issued by the Commission shall be stated. 

§ 72-614. Selling methods 

It is definitely prohibited that the ticket agents make offers of employment or of garments or any kind of presents as propaganda for the sale of tickets. Advertisements that in any way may cause confusion in the minds of the public, regarding the price or type of transportation advertised, are likewise definitely prohibited. 425

T.§ 72-615 

PUBLIC SERVICE 

Ch. 5 § 72-615. Prices; changes; cancellations; intoxication; selling; speculation over- (a) It shall be unlawful for a ticket agent who charters or dispatches a ship or plane, to charge different prices to passengers to whom the same services or facilities between the same points is provided. Likewise, it shall be unlawful for a ticket agent who charters or dispatches a ship or plane, to charge the same prices. to passengers to whom different services or facilities are provided. 

Likewise, it shall be unlawful for a ticket agent to furnish a passenger with facilities different from those agreed upon; provided, that, in case a ticket agent sells a ticket for a certain type of plane or seat thereon, and because of causes beyond his control it is impossible to furnish such type of transportation to the passenger, he cannot furnish the passenger with transportation in a different type of plane or seat without the previous consent of said passenger and reimbursement of the difference between the price of the agreed type of transportation and that furnished, based on the rates in force of the air or steamship line furnishing the transportation. In such cases, furnishing the passengers with better facilities than those agreed upon shall not constitute a violation of this section. In case the passenger does not accept the substitute transportation offered, the ticket agent shall reimburse him the price of the ticket plus the transportation and hotel expenses incurred by the passenger. (b) It shall be the duty of every ticket agent to return the total amount paid for a ticket when the passenger notifies the ticket agent at least 24 hours before the date of the trip that he has cancelled the trip. In all other cases, the ticket agent may retain 

25% of the price paid. (c) No ticket agent shall allow a plane chartered or dispatched by him to be boarded by an intoxicated person. In case a passenger arrives in a state of intoxication to board a plane, the ticket agent is authorized to retain 25% of the price paid for the ticket, returning the balance to the passenger and notifying the Commission of such action within 24 hours after its occurrence. (d) It is definitely prohibited for a ticket agent who charters. or dispatches a plane to convene for a specific flight a greater number of passengers than the authorized capacity of the plane; provided, that, in case this rule is violated through error or oversight, said ticket agent shall pay the passengers who cannot board 426

Ch. 

 T.27 § 72-619 

the plane the transportation and hotel expenses which they have incurred. (e) It is definitely prohibited for a ticket agent to resell for purposes of speculation tickets already reserved or contracted for with a specific airline. 

§ 72-616. Violations of contract 

Every violation of the terms of the contract between the ticket agent and the buyer of the ticket shall be deemed a violation of this Division. 

§ 72-617. Powers of Commission 

None of the provisions of this Division shall be understood to restrict or limit the general or inherent powers of the Commission, which retains the power to approve any orders deemed pertinent to regulate the business of selling or offering for sale air or marine passage. $ 72-618. Penalties

The violation of any of the preceding rules or provisions shall be subject to the penalty established by the Public Service Law of 

Puerto Rico [27 L.P.R.A. § 1 et seq.]; however, the Commission may, in all cases of violation of any of the preceding rules or provisions, after a public hearing is held, suspend or cancel temporarily or permanently the corresponding ticket agent's license. § 72-619. Effectiveness

This Division shall take effect immediately after its approval by the Public Service Commission and by the Governor of Puerto Rico. 

Approval dates. Regulation File No. 90, set out in this

Division, was approved by the Public Service Commission 

Aug. 5, 1948, and by the Governor Nov. 26, 1948.

Separability. Sec. 53 of Regulation File No. 89, set out in this Division, provided: "Should any provision of these Regulations be declared illegal or unconstitutional by a court, such decree or judgment shall not apply to the other provisions of these Regulations, and to that effect shall be considered separate and as if adopted apart from any provision declared illegal or unconstitutional."

Repeal. Sec. 54 of Regulation File No. 89, set out in this 

Division, provided: 

"These Regulations repeal any provisions, regulations, orders, resolutions or determinations in regard to this matter issued by the Commission." 1 

§ 72-702. Definitions 

The following terms, whenever used or referred to in this Division, shall have the meaning hereinafter set forth, except where the context clearly indicates otherwise, and when used in singular number shall be construed in plural, or vice versa, as the case may be: (1) "Commission" means the Public Service Commission of 

Puerto Rico. (2) "Company" means any person, association, partnership, company, corporation, cooperative, or organization of any kind engaging or intending to engage in the sight-seeing business. (3) "Sight-seeing company" means any person who as a common carrier owns, controls, operates, or manages any kind of motor vehicle used exclusively to carry passengers and baggage incidental to the transportation of passengers, by water or air between points in Puerto Rico or over any public road, for the purpose of visiting interesting, picturesque, or historical places, irrespective of whether or not the transportation is rendered between fixed terminals, and through regular or irregular routes, as long as the trip originates and ends in the same place. (4) "Operator" means the person who drives or controls a motor vehicle engaged in sight-seeing. (5) "Authorization" means franchise, certificate, permit, right, or privilege granted by the Commission to engage in the sightseeing business or to act as an operator. (6) "Cooperative" means any association or group of persons organized in accordance with the General Cooperative Associations 

Act of Puerto Rico No. 291 approved on April 9, 1946 [5 L.P.R.A. 

§§ 881-909], for the purpose of engaging in the sight-seeing business. 429

T.§ 72-702 Ch. 5 

PUBLIC SERVICE 

(7) "Association" means a group of owners of vehicles engaged in the sight-seeing business organized for the purpose of using common facilities, business name, colors, emblems, or insignia. § 72-703. Authorization for sight-seeing car

From the date this Division is in force, no company shall engage any motor vehicle in sight-seeing unless the vehicle has a valid authorization issued by the Commission and complies with the requirements established by this Division with regard to surety and equipment. The authorization shall be renewed annually. § 72-704. Requirements for license

The following requirements shall be complied with to obtain a sight-seeing license: (1) To file with the Commission a sworn application stating the name and address of the applicant; his financial status; number of vehicles offered for operation and their passenger capacity. (2) If the applicant is a natural person, he must file a certificate of conduct issued by the Police Department. The Commission may require, when it deems convenient, such certificate from the owners, partners, or shareholders of artificial persons. 

§ 72-705. Special authorization 

Public Service vehicles may render sight-seeing services by obtaining a special authorization from the Commission and by complying with the requirements of this Division. 

§ 72-706. Accident insurance 

(a) Every company shall furnish a guaranty either by mortgage, insurance policy through an insurance company duly authorized to do business in Puerto Rico, or in cash to cover such minimum amount as the Commission may determine for each vehicle as a guaranty for the payment of any compensation to any person who suffers injuries or damages in any accident caused by the careless or negligent operation of the motor vehicle. Every insurance policy issued under this section shall contain a clause imposing upon the insurance company the duty to notify the Commission of the cancellation of a policy for any cause at least 15 days before the effective date of the cancellation. From the date this Division takes effect, no vehicle used in the sight-seeing business shall operate until its guaranty has been approved by the Commission. 430

Ch. 

 T.27 § 72-712 

(b) The Commission shall not approve any guaranty consisting of an insurance policy with an insurance company which does not comply with the provisions of the contract required by this section. (c) In the event the Commission cancels the authorization of a vehicle for sight-seeing tours, the guaranty shall remain in effect until all claims commenced due to acts which occurred before the cancellation have been decided by the courts. 

§ 72-707. Rates 

Every company shall file with the Commission its rates to be approved. Once the approval is obtained, the rates shall not be altered by the company, its employees, or agents, without the approval of the Commission. § 72-708. Payment of charges

No person who expressly or implicitly hires a vehicle for sightseeing shall refuse to pay the lawful charge in accordance with the rates in force. 

§ 72-709. Discounts 

No coupons or service cards that can produce a discount or reduction of the rates in force nor any other method which may cause a change in the rates shall be used. 

§ 72-710. Equipment 

Every vehicle engaged in sight-seeing shall be kept clean and in good mechanical and safe condition. A land vehicle shall have its seats, brakes, tires, windshield wipers, steering gear, horn, rearview mirror, ignition system, lights and stoplight in good condition and shall always be supplied with spare fuses, sufficient fuel and oil, spare tire, and tools. 

§ 72-711. Material posted inside vehicle 

Every vehicle authorized to engage in sight-seeing shall have posted in a place visible to the passenger its authorization, the operator's license with his picture, the amount of insurance, the insurance company, if any, the rates in force, and the conditions under which the vehicle is authorized to operate. The operator must look in the picture as he does when driving the vehicle. 

§ 72-712. Colors 

Every vehicle used in sight-seeing may be painted with a color 431

T.§ 72-712 

PUBLIC SERVICE 

Ch. 5 or combination of colors identifying the company to which it belongs, and said color or combination of colors shall be previously approved by the Commission. § 72-713. Distinctive colors, insignia, or emblems

No vehicle engaged in sight-seeing shall have colors, insignia, or emblems which in the opinion of the Commission are not readily distinguishable from the colors, insignia, or emblems previously approved for other companies. 

§ 72-714. Emblems and trade names 

No company shall use an emblem or trade name without having previously obtained the approval of the Commission. 

§ 72-715. Safety equipment 

When the sight-seeing vehicle has a capacity of more than 10 passengers, it shall comply with the requirements relative to equipment safety applicable to omnibuses. 

§ 72-716. Inspection 

Vehicles used in sight-seeing shall be inspected every 120 days, it being compulsory for the operator and the company to bring it to the Commission or to the place designated for inspection. 

§ 72-717. Inspection tag 

Every vehicle used in sight-seeing shall display on the inner side. of the windshield, and where it does not affect the visibility of the operator, evidence that the vehicle has been inspected. 

§ 72-718. Cooperatives and associations 

Individual owners of one or more vehicles engaged in sight-seeing in a specific area may organize as cooperatives or associations to operate not less than five vehicles under a common trade name, color, combination of colors, emblem, or insignia. § 72-719. Information required from association (a) Every cooperative or association shall file with the Commission the following information: (1) A copy of its certificate of incorporation, if incorporated. (2) The conditions and rules in regard to the organization and operation of the cooperative or association. (3) Name and address of each member and the make, motor 432

Ch. 

 T.27 § 72-722 

number, the license number issued by the Secretary of Public Works, and the authorizations granted by the Commission for the vehicles and the number corresponding to each vehicle. (4) Evidence that its members have complied with the requirements of sec. 72-722. (b) All changes made in the information required by this section shall be filed with the Commission within 24 hours after its occurrence. § 72-720. Operators; license

No company shall consent or allow any person to drive or control any vehicle engaged in sight-seeing unless such person is an operator duly authorized by the Commission and whose license is in force. § 72-721. Discharged operators

No operator who has been discharged by any company, on grounds that may cause the suspension of his license, shall be employed by any other company without the previous approval of the Commission. The company who discharges any operator shall notify the Commission within 48 hours of his discharge stating the reasons for the discharge. 

§ 72-722. Requirements for operator's license 

No person shall act as operator unless he has applied and obtained an authorization from the Commission. To obtain it he must comply with the following requirements: (1) Be a citizen of the United States and of the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico. 

(2) Be between 21 and 65 years of age. (3) Be a chauffeur duly authorized by the Secretary of Public Works and have at least 2 years of experience as such, or with heavy vehicles of the armed services while in military service. In case of aircraft or watercraft he must have a license from an agency recognized by the Commission. (4) Read and write Spanish and make himself understood in English. (5) File: (A) His record as chauffeur or chauffeur of heavy motor vehicles. 

(B) Certificate of conduct issued by the Department of Police as of the date the application is filed.

433

T.§ 72-722 Ch. 5 

PUBLIC SERVICE 

(C) Medical certificate of a public health unit or a private physician stating that petitioner is in good physical condition, especially of the following organs and limbs: eyes, ears, heart, lungs, condition of legs, and arms (reflexes). (D) Three pictures, size 2" x 2". (E) Birth certificate. (F) Photostatic copy of discharge, if a veteran. (6) Pass an examination prescribed by the Commission. § 72-723. Renewal of license

The operator's authorization shall be renewed every two years. 

To do so the requirements expressed in sec. 72-722 (5) (A), (B), (C), and (D) must again be complied with. An expired, revoked, or suspended authorization shall be returned to the Commission by the operator. § 72-724. Name, address of operator

Every operator shall report his correct name and address, and in case of change of address, it shall be reported in writing to the Commission within 48 hours of the change. § 72-725. Cleanliness

Every operator shall be clean in his body and clothing. 

§ 72-726. Smoking 

No operator shall smoke while the vehicle he is operating is carrying passengers. § 72-727. Drug addiction; alcoholism

No operator shall be a drug addict or a habitual or excessive user of intoxicating beverages. 

§ 72-728. Lost articles 

At the end of each trip the operator shall examine the vehicle. to ascertain that the passengers have not left any package or object. If after the passengers have left he discovers any package or object, he shall attempt to return it to its owner within half an hour and, if unable to do so, he shall take it to the City Hall where the proceeding provided in the Civil Code [31 L.P.R.A. § 1 et seq.] shall be followed. § 72-729. Conduct of operator 

Every operator shall observe a correct and respectful conduct toward the public and passengers. Any behavior showing disregard 434

Ch. 

 T.27 § 72-735 

for the duties imposed upon him by this Division or any rude or disrespectful conduct or behavior at variance with moral and proper conduct, that should be observed by every person serving the public, shall be sufficient cause for the suspension or cancellation of the operator's authorization. 

§ 72-730. Additional passengers 

After a trip is started no other passengers shall be accepted.

§ 72-731. Operation of vehicle; inspection 

Every vehicle used in sight-seeing shall be operated in accordance with the laws, ordinances, and traffic regulations in force. 

Every operator shall stop and allow the inspection of the vehicle at the request of any policeman or inspector of the Commission. § 72-732. Receipt to passenger

Every operator shall furnish at a passenger's request a receipt stating his name, license number, the time and place of origin and destination of the trip, and the amount collected. To comply with this requirement he shall have, at all times, a receipt book in the vehicle. § 72-733. Revocation of operator's license

The violation of any of the provisions of this Division, or conviction of any crime involving moral turpitude or violation of traffic laws or regulations, shall be deemed sufficient cause for the revocation of the operator's license, in accordance with the procedure provided in this Division. 

§ 72-734. Complaints against operator 

Every natural or legal person who wishes to complain against an operator shall write to the Commission stating the acts performed by the operator and the date, time, and place they occurred; the description of the vehicle, its plate number, the company to which it belongs, etc. In the letter the complainant shall also state his name and address, as well as the name and address of his witnesses, if any. 

§ 72-735. Office of legal services 

Every complaint received in accordance with the previous section shall be referred by the Chairman to the office of legal services 435

T.§ 72-735 

PUBLIC SERVICE 

Ch. 5 of the Commission, who shall study it to determine if the facts stated therein constitute a violation of this Division. 

§ 72-736. Facts not stating violation 

Should the office of legal services determine that the facts stated in the complaint do not constitute a violation, it shall thus report to the Chairman, who shall notify the complainant and the Commission. Unless the Commission disagrees with the report, it shall order the complaint filed. 

§ 72-737. Facts stating violation 

Should the office of legal services determine that an operator has violated this Division, it shall thus report with recommendations to the Chairman, who shall notify the Commission and the complainant, if any, of the action taken. If the recommendation is to the effect that the operator's authorization be suspended or revoked, the Commission, through the Chairman or one of the members of the Commission, shall notify the operator of the facts reported and shall order him to appear at a specified date, time, and place before the official designated to hear him in regard to the reported facts. The notice to the operator shall be made by registered mail to his last known address according to the Commission's records. Should the operator waive the hearing or fail to appear at the hearing, the Commission may suspend or revoke his authorization without further summons or hearing. 

§ 72-738. Disciplinary action; rehearing 

The official appointed to preside at the hearing, once the appearing party or parties are heard, shall render a report with his recommendations to the Commission and the Commission shall take whatever action it deems pertinent. Within 15 days after notice of disciplinary action is served, the operator concerned may petition for reconsideration and rehearing before the Commission or one of its commissioners. Until the case is finally decided, the disciplinary action taken shall remain in full force. 

§ 72-739. Suspension of operator's license 

The Commission may, in the manner specified in sec. 72-747, temporarily suspend the authorization granted to an operator. This authority shall be exercised when in its opinion the operators are incompetent or unable to drive or when the facts charged to an operator constitute a menace to public safety. 436

Ch. 

 T.27 § 72-745 § 72-740. Reports and accounting system 

Every company shall notify the Commission of its name and address and any change in name or address shall be reported to the Commission within 48 hours of occurring. 

§ 72-741. Records concerning operators 

Every company shall keep a record of its operators working on the various shifts, their authorization numbers, and the license numbers of the vehicles. This information shall be available at all times to the Commission and the Director of the Bureau of Inspection or the secretary of the Commission. § 72-742. Accident report

Every company shall render a written report to the Commission of every accident occurring to its vehicles in which persons are killed or injured or damages to other person's property are caused; said report to be rendered within 24 hours after the company receives the report of the accident from the operator. In case the operator does not render his report to the company, said company shall render its report within 24 hours after it has knowledge of the accident. § 72-743. Insurance company's accident report

The same report required by sec. 72-742 shall be rendered to the Commission by the insurance company covering the vehicle within 48 hours after the accident has been reported to them by the company. The insurance company is subject in this regard to the requirement of sec. 72-706 of this title. § 72-744. Accident report as evidence

No report rendered in accordance with this section shall be used as evidence in any criminal or civil action for damages arising from the matters mentioned in the report. § 72-745. Labor contract, report

Every individual or collective contract or agreement which affects the worker-employer relations between the companies and operators shall be filed with the Commission within 5 days after it has been made. Any change in said contract or agreement shall also be reported to the Commission within the same period. 437

T.§ 72-746 

PUBLIC SERVICE 

Ch. 5 

§ 72-746. Accounting system; biannual statements 

Every company shall keep the accounting system prescribed by the Commission and shall render biannual financial statements. 

§ 72-747. Suspension and cancellation of vehicle authorization 

If the Commission learns that in any part of Puerto Rico any motor vehicle subject to this Division is operated without having complied with the requirements herein stated, or after having complied with these requirements said vehicle is being operated under conditions that constitute a menace to public safety or if there is reason to believe that the owner or operator is not competent to own or operate such type of vehicle, or is violating this Division, the Commission may issue an order, without previous notice, temporarily suspending the operation of said vehicle for a period not to exceed 15 days. Immediately after suspending the operation of a vehicle in the manner described above, the Chairman of the Commission shall summon its owner to appear before the official designated by the Commission to preside at the hearing, within a period not to exceed 15 days from the date of suspension, to show cause, if any there be, why a longer period of suspension or the definite cancellation of the authorization should not be ordered. If the hearing is postponed at the request of the party involved, the license of the vehicle shall remain suspended until the case is finally decided by the Commission, even though the 15 days of temporary suspension have elapsed. 

§ 72-748. Powers of Commission 

None of the provisions contained in this Division shall be construed in any way as limiting or restricting the general or inherent powers of the Commission, which retains the power to approve any pertinent orders to regulate the sight-seeing service in Puerto Rico. $ 72-749. Exemptions

Notwithstanding the provisions of this Division, the Commission retains the power, through orders to that effect, to grant exemptions from compliance with any of said provisions when considered justified and convenient. 

§ 72-750. Liability of companies 

The companies shall be liable for violations of this Division committed by the operators of their sight-seeing vehicles. 438

Ch. 

 T.27 § 72-753 

§ 72-751. Persons to enforce compliance with these regulations (a) Policemen, public service inspectors, the Department of 

Tourism of the Economic Development Administration, and em ployees of the Department of Public Works in charge of policing and maintenance of roads shall require compliance with this Division and in case of violations thereof, shall notify the Commission and file complaints in court. (b) Every citizen shall have the right to demand from operators of sight-seeing vehicles compliance with this Division. In case of noncompliance, he shall have the right to file a complaint before the Commission as provided in sec. 72-734 or before the courts. 

§ 72-752. Penalties 

The violation of any of the preceding sections shall constitute a misdemeanor and shall be subject to the penal sanction estab lished by the Public Service Act of Puerto Rico [27 L.P.R.A. § 1 

et seq.). However, the Commission, in case of violation of any of the preceding sections, may, after hearing, suspend or cancel the authorization of the vehicle or operator involved. § 72-753. Effectiveness

This Division shall take effect immediately after approval by the Governor.

§ 1123-1. Short title 

This division may be cited as "Regulations for Rental Cars" and are approved pursuant to Act No. 109 of June 28, 1962 (Puerto 

Rico Public Service Act) [27 L.P.R.A. § 1001 et seq.]. 

Source. §§ 1123-1 to 1123-16: Regulation Applicable to Car-

Separability. Sec. 16 of Regulation File No. 981, set out in this division, provided: "If any provision hereof is declared unlawful or unconstitutional by a Court decree, said declaration or decree shall not apply to the rest of the provisions hereof, and to that effect it is hereby declared that the provisions hereof are severable as if they had been adopted independently of any one declared unlawful or unconstitutional." 

§ 1123-2. Definitions 

The following terms shall, for the purposes hereof and unless a different meaning clearly appears from the context, have the following meanings: (1) "Commission" means the Public Service Commission of 

Puerto Rico. (2) "Rental car" means any motor vehicle, of a capacity not over 10 passengers, to be leased and driven by the lessee or the person he may designate. (3) "Person" includes any individual, partnership, enterprise, association or corporation. It includes, likewise, lessees, trustees and judicial administrators or receivers of any person. (4) "Car-rental enterprise" includes any person who owns, controls, operates or manages motor vehicles for rent of a capacity not over 10 passengers, to be leased and driven by the lessees themselves or by those whom they may designate. (5) "Authorization" means the permit issued by the Commission to any person to operate as a car-rental enterprise. (6) "License" that which is issued by the Commission to any duly authorized rental car.

§ 1123-3. Petition for authorization 

Every petition for authorization shall be filed on the forms to be provided therefor by the Commission, or on any similar ones prepared and drafted by the petitioner himself. 

§ 1123-4. Authorization 

No person may dedicate himself to operating a car-rental enterprise unless he is previously authorized by the Commission and has complied with such requirements as this division establishes or may hereinafter establish. 

§ 1123-5. License 

The Commission shall, after granting an authorization, issue a license to every vehicle described in said authorization, which license shall be renewed annually at the petition of the grantee. 

Every application for renewal shall be filed not later than 30 days prior to its expiration date. Original and renewed licenses shall be issued only after the vehicle has been inspected and approved by this agency and after the grantee has filed, and this agency has approved, the insurance policy referred to in sec. 1123-7 hereof. 

§ 1123-6. Registration at the Public Works Department 

The Department of Public Works shall not register any motor vehicle as a rental car unless said vehicle is previously authorized by the Commission. 

§ 1123-7. Insurance policy 

Every car-rental enterprise shall submit to the Commission an insurance policy issued by a company legally authorized to do business in Puerto Rico, and the Commission shall fix the minimum amount of each vehicle's policy. Said amount shall warrant the claim to which any person suffering injury, harm or damage at any accident, due to reckless or careless driving or mechanical defects, may be entitled. The Commission shall approve said policy before issuing the corresponding license to authorized vehicles. (1) Every insurance policy submitted to the Commission shall contain a provision whereby the insurance company binds itself to notify the Commission of any expiration of the policy not less than 

30 days before said expiration date. (2) In the event of cancellation for non-payment the Commission shall be notified beforehand at least 10 days before the effective

date of such cancellation. Formal notice to the Commission shall issue on the same date as that of the insured when said cancellation takes place for any other reason besides non-payment. (3) If the Commission cancels the license of any rental car, the policy shall continue in full force and effect until the courts shall resolve on the claims arising from events occurring before said cancellation. 

§ 1123-8. Inspection 

Every motor vehicle operated as a rental car shall be inspected before a license is granted thereto, and once it has been licensed, it shall, every 180 days, be brought for inspection at the Commission or at any other place the Commission may designate. § 1123-9. Inspection and rental car evidence 

Every rental car shall display, inside the windshield and at a place where the driver's visibility is not impaired, the official evidence issued by this agency showing that the vehicle has been inspected. It shall also display on the rear glass the official evidence of this agency identifying it as a rental car. § 1123-10. Transfers; substitutions; additions; barters (a) No grantee authorized to operate a car-rental enterprise may, without the Commission's previous approval, transfer, substitute, add or barter any authorized vehicle. (b) The grantee shall comply with the following requirements before he receives the Commission's approval: (1) To fill out and file the forms to be provided by the Commission for each case, or such similar forms as the grantee himself may prepare. (2) To pay the filing and inspection fees prescribed by the 

Commission wherein required. (c) No transfer, substitution, addition or barter of vehicles shall be final until it has been approved by the Commission and the grantee has complied with the requirements contained in the Commission's resolution and order approving said transfer, substitution, addition or barter. 

§ 1123-11. Retirement from service 

No grantee may retire from service any duly authorized rental car if said vehicle is going to be used as a private vehicle (thus reducing the number of authorized units) without previously June 30, 1965 452.A3

PUBLIC SERVICE 

notifying the Commission, giving the description of such vehicle or vehicles to be retired from service. The grantee shall, furthermore, advise the Department of Public Works of the retirement from service of such vehicle. § 1123-12. Actions against car-rental enterprises 

If a complaint is filed or if the Commission finds out that there is a rental car operating in any part of Puerto Rico without having met any of the requirements prescribed hereby, or if after having met such requirements, the said vehicle is operating in such condition that it constitutes a health menace or public hazard, or is operating in violation of any order from the Commission concerning this service, the Commission shall request said car-rental enterprise to appear at a public hearing showing reason or cause, if any, for which the Commission should not proceed to impose an administrative fine thereon, suspend or cancel its authorization, as the case may be; provided that, when the vehicle is in such a condition that its operation constitutes a danger to public health or safety the Commission may, without previous notice, take or order possession of the license issued by the Public Works Department and plates issued to said vehicle for a period not to exceed 60 days. § 1123-13. Drivers; lessees

No car-rental enterprise may permit or allow any person to drive or operate any rental car belonging to said enterprise, unless said person is a motor vehicle driver duly authorized by the Department of Public Works of Puerto Rico, and whose license is in effect, excepting the provisions of sec. 3-102, clauses (b) and (c), of Act 

No. 141 of July 20, 1960 (Vehicles and Traffic Law of Puerto Rico) [9 L.P.R.A. § 652 (b), (c)]. 

§ 1123-14. General provisions 

None of the provisions contained herein shall be construed as restricting or limiting the general powers of the Commission, or those inherent thereto. The Commission reserves the right to issue any order it may deem convenient for the regulation of service of rental cars in Puerto Rico, as provided by law, and for the benefit of the public interest.

 § 1123-15. Penalties 

Every person violating any provision of the preceding sections shall be guilty of a misdemeanor and subject to the penalty estab lished by Act No. 109 of June 28, 1962 (Puerto Rico Public Service Act) [27 L.P.R.A. § 1001 et seq.]. However, the Commission may, in every case of violation of any provision hereof, and after holding a public hearing, impose an administrative fine or suspend or cancel the license issued to the rental car or authorization issued to the corresponding enterprise by the Commission.

SUBDIVISION 2. APPLICATIONS SECTIONS 

1123-71. Petition for granting of authorization 1123-72. Requirements of notice 

§ 1123-71. Petition for granting of authorization 

Applications for the grant of an authorization, or the amendment of any authorization already granted, shall be filed with the Public Service Commission of Puerto Rico. Said application shall be personally verified by the applicant, his attorney or legal representative and shall state and set forth the following: (1) Name and post-office and residential address of the petitioner. If a corporation, the name and post-office address of its directors. A copy of the charter of organization, a certificate of incorporation, and a paid-in capital certificate from the petitioner's treasurer shall also be forwarded therewith. If a partnership, name and post-office address of every partner and a certified copy of the partnership deed. Said documents may be attached by reference, if copy thereof is on file with the Commission, and they have not been substituted or amended. (2) Financial statement of the petitioner, indicating the value of the properties owned, liabilities and capital. (In the case of a previously granted authorization, the last statement of income and expenditures shall be submitted.) (3) Nature and character of the authorization sought, stating the specific locality where it is to be exercised. (4) A detailed statement of the facts upon which the applicant relies to show that the authorization requested, or its modification, is necessary or adequate for the public service, comfort, convenience or safety. (5) If the petitioner appears by counsel, the latter's name and post-office address.

1123-112. Answer and complaint; amendments § 1123-111. Filing complaint (a) Any person, governmental agency or instrumentality complaining of any act or omission which a public service company, contract carrier, or grantee, has carried out or intends to carry out, in violation of its tariff provisions or of any requirement or provision of the Public Service Act of Puerto Rico [27 L.P.R.A.

If any or all of the pleadings of the complaint are denied, the answer shall set forth all the facts upon which respondent relies for such a denial. § 1123-112. § 1123-151. Order of designation 

Once a motion requesting that a case be set for hearing is filed by the petitioner, the corresponding designation shall be made. specifying the place, date and hour for the hearing. 

§ 1123-152. Preliminary statement 

In every public hearing held, the petitioner or complainant may open the hearing, stating in general terms what he proposes to establish or indicating the type of evidence he shall offer and the documents he shall introduce to prove his case, without going into any detail regarding the evidence. The adverse party may make a similar statement. 

§ 1123-153. Order of evidence 

The petitioners or complainants shall introduce their evidence first; the intervenors who favor the petition or sustain the complaint shall then introduce theirs, thereafter the respondents and 

Jan. 31, 1967

Vol. 6, No. 1 

452.A10

Ch. 53

T.27 § 1123-156 

opposing intervenors shall introduce their evidence. Persons who, though not qualifying as intervenors, wish to testify in regard to the question involved in the case may then be heard. 

§ 1123-154. Examination and cross-examination 

Only one attorney for each party shall be allowed to examine and cross-examine the same witness. 

§ 1123-155. Arguments following evidence 

After the parties to the case have introduced all the evidence, attesting and documentary, counsel thereof may offer oral argument before the Commission or presiding examiner clearly explaining all the leading facts and conclusions which they might deem in order to support their pleadings. 

§ 1123-156. Court stenographer 

(a) The testimony received in every public hearing will be recorded by a reporter, or by adequate and reliable mechanical means when a reporter is not available. At the request of any of the parties and after payment of its cost, a copy of the record will be supplied. In these cases and in those in which judicial review of a Commission's decision is sought, the party requesting a copy of the record, or the Petitioner in review, will pay for the cost of typing, preparing and certifying the administrative record, through the Secretary of the Commission. (b) Except when for just cause the Commission directs otherwise, the Secretary will compensate the reporter on the basis of one dollar ($1.00) for each double-spaced, legal size page, including 

2 copies. Payment to the reporter will be made from the funds received by the Commission from the petitioner in review or from the party who has requested a copy of the record, as the case may be. The Secretary of the Commission will determine the order in which requests for transcripts of records will be honored, considering the dates in which said requests are made, and he will require a reasonable amount of money as a deposit before ordering the preparation of any transcript.
