PUBLIC SERVICE § 1123-157. Postponements and continuances 

The Chairman or any member of the Commission may in their discretion grant postponements and continuances at the request of any interested party. Postponements and continuances may be granted also upon the Commission's own initiative. Requests for postponements shall be filed, in writing, at least 3 days prior to the date for which the hearing is set. § 1123-158. Agreement upon facts; additional evidence

The parties to any hearing, investigation or any other proceeding pending before the Commission may, by stipulation in writing filed with the Commission, agree upon the facts or any portion thereof involved in the controversy, which stipulation may be regarded and used as evidence in said hearing, investigation or proceeding. The Commission may, however, request from the parties such additional evidence or reports as it deems necessary. 

§ 1123-159. Investigations 

The Commission may, at any time, at its own initiative or upon motion of any interested party, carry out investigations and order hearings to be held with reference to any act performed or to be performed by any public service company, contract carrier or grantee, which the Commission deems in violation of any legal provision or of any order or ruling of the Commission or in violation of the rules and regulations adopted by the public service company.

SECTIONS § 1123-160. Deposition 

The testimony of any person may be taken by deposition, at the request of any interested party, or upon petition of the Commission in any proceeding pending before it.

Every motion to reconsider any decision, determination, resolution or order of the Commission shall state the grounds upon which the party or parties rely and shall be filed within 15 days following the date when said decision, determination, resolution or order was notified. Proof or evidence of such service shall be filed with the Secretary of the Commission, after which the Commission, in case a rehearing is granted, shall set the date and place for the hearing, giving notice thereof to all interested parties. Notwithstanding the preceding the Commission may deny any petition for reconsideration without holding a public hearing, whenever from the context thereof facts are not adduced which justify the revocation, change or modification of the decision, determination, resolution or order entered in the case.

SECTIONS DIVISION 3. LIQUEFIED PETROLEUM GAS SUBDIVISION 1. DEFINITIONS 

1123-301. Definitions 

§ 1123-301. Definitions 

The following terms or phrases, as used in this division, shall have the meaning and/or scope stated below: (1) "Liquefied petroleum gas" shall mean and include any material which is composed of any of the following hydrocarbons, or mixtures of them: propane, propylene, natural butane, isobutane, and butylenes. (2) "Container" all vessels used for the transportation and storage of liquefied petroleum gases, such as tanks, bottles, cylinders or drums, and other similar vessels. (3) "Container installation" means the mounting which consists essentially of the structure of the container and other accessories, including shutoff valves, excess flow valves, level gaging devices, safety devices, and protective housing. (4) "System" refers to the installation of the equipment, which essentially consists of the container and primary devices, such as safety valves, excess flow valves, regulators, and piping connecting said parts. (5) "Fillers or loading points" means the equipment prepared for the delivery of liquefied gas to tank-trucks or trailers, and applies specifically to the accessory equipment needed, which includes valves, pipes, hoses, odorizing equipment, meters, charging platforms and its covers, if any. (6) "Building" includes any structure, frame or public or private housing. 

(7) The initials NFPA correspond to National Fire Prevention 

Association. (8) The initials ASME correspond to American Society of 

Mechanical Engineers. 

(9) The initials API correspond to American Petroleum Institute. 

(10) The initials NEC correspond to National Electrical Code. 

(11) The initials ICC correspond to U.S. Interstate Commerce 

Commission. 1971 

 452.A14.1

T.§ 1123-301 

PUBLIC SERVICE 

Ch. 53 (12) "Underground containers" means installations in which the superior part of the container is below ground level with the inspection opening uncovered. (13) "Partially buried or in mounts" refers to installations in which the superior part of the container is above ground level and the inferior part is covered with earth. (14) "Cylinder" includes any container used for the purpose of containing liquefied petroleum gas with a water capacity up to 

1,000 pounds, including commercial weight. (15) "Filling density" means the proportional rate between the weight of the gas in a container and the weight of water which the container may contain at a temperature of 60 degrees Fahrenheit. (16) "Tank" includes any portable or stationary container used to deposit liquefied petroleum gas with over 1,000 pounds water capacity, commercial weight. (17) "Commission" means the Commonwealth Public Service Commission. (18) "Liquefied petroleum gas enterprise" includes any person who may own, control, exploit, or manage as a public service company, a plant or business in Puerto Rico for the production, generation, transportation, delivery, supply, or distribution of liquefied petroleum gas. (19) "Public service company" includes any public carrier, pipe conduction enterprise, gas company, electric power company, telephone company, telegraph company, drydock enterprise, travel agency, transportation broker, dock operator, person or entity engaged in warehousing, toll bridge enterprise, and nuclear power enterprise, who offers to render or render their services, or offers to deliver or deliver products for pay, to the public in general, or to a part thereof, in Puerto Rico. It does not include persons who render services for their exclusive use or for that of their tenants. "Public carrier" includes any: (A) railroad enterprise, (B) omnibus enterprise, (C) taxi enterprise, (D) public automobile service enterprise, (E) truck loading enterprise, (F) water transportation enterprise, (G) air transportation enterprise, 1971 

 452.A14.2

Ch. T.27 § 1123-311 

(H) tours enterprise, (I) car rental enterprise, who offers to render or renders, in Puerto Rico, paid passenger or loading transportation service, to the public in general, or to a part thereof. The term shall not be applicable to carriers by contract. (20) "Distributor of liquefied petroleum gas" includes any person who shall own, control, exploit, or manage, as a public service enterprise, any plant or business of transportation, delivery, supply, or distribution, of liquefied petroleum gas in Puerto Rico.

Ch. 53 § 1123-311. Requirements for the commencement and maintenance of operations 

(a) Authorization. 

(1) No person shall start operations as a gas enterprise, nor shall continue operating if already in operation, unless he is granted a written authorization from the Commission. (2) The authorization of the Commission shall express the enterprise's specific activity or activities, and the terms and conditions under which it is granted. (3) The authorization shall be granted for a maximum period of 5 years. A renewal application shall be filed before the Commission 45 days prior to the authorization expiration date. 

(b) Public liability policy. 

(1) The Commission shall not grant any license until the interested party shall subscribe to and file with the Commission a public liability policy which guarantees compensation for any damage caused to a person or property as a result of the negligent or faulty actions or omissions of the company or of the carrier. 

The policy shall contain the following terms: (A) $100,000 for damages to a person. (B) $200,000 for accident. (C) $100,000 for damages to another's property, including the ultimate consumer. (2) As a condition to the insurance contract, the required insurance policy shall contain a clause by virtue of which its cancellation shall be prohibited without previous written notice to the Commission. Any intention to cancel the policy for default in payment shall be made known to the Commission at least 10 days in advance of the date of cancellation or at least 15 days when there is any other reason involved. (3) The terms indicated in the preceding clause (2) shall begin to run from the hour and date in which said notice is filed with the Commission. (4) The policy shall cover the obligations arising as a result of the negligent or faulty actions or omissions of the enterprise in the storage, sale or handling of liquefied petroleum gases, including any claim of the ultimate consumer or injured citizen. Any endorsement of the policy which shall be made by the insurer company or any of its authorized representatives to protect the activities of the ultimate consumer or injured citizen shall be, in its pertinent parts, similar to the original policy. 1971 452.A14.4

Ch. 53

T.27 § 1123-312 (5) The policy shall further cover any damages caused by the negligent or faulty actions or omissions of the gas company, when the cause of action arises within a term of 6 months subsequent to the closing operations of the company. (c) License. (1) Any enterprise to which the Commission grants a license shall, before beginning its operations, apply and obtain from the Commission a license which it shall renew annually. The enterprise shall pay for this license, as well as for its annual renewal, the fee fixed by the Commission. (2) Any enterprise having a license from the Commission prior to the approval and effectiveness of this division shall, within 90 days from its effective date, apply and obtain from the Commission a license in order to be able to continue operating the specific activities in which it was engaged. This license shall be renewed annually upon payment of the proper fees. (3) Said license shall specify the activity or activities which the enterprise is authorized to operate, the address of the place authorized to operate, the license expiration date, license number, and any other proper information. (4) The enterprise shall post said license in a place visible to the public within the premises in which its operations are executed. (5) The enterprise shall request and obtain a license for each authorized place where the enterprise offers its services to the public. (6) To supply gas, or in any other manner aid another person to distribute gas, without the proper authorization from the Commission, shall be sufficient cause for the license cancellation. (d) Personnel. Any person who in any manner handles gas containers or tanks, who operates filling or charging plants, who operates a vehicle engaged in the distribution of gas, or who is engaged in the installation of gas cylinders, shall have a certificate granted by the Commission for such purpose. In order to obtain this certificate, the interested party shall approve a training or the examination that the Commission determines. 

§ 1123-312. Duties 

(a) Accidents. The enterprise shall notify the Commission of any accident or event, such as fire, explosion, asphyxia, or any other of a similar nature which might happen and in which a container or equipment of a gas company is involved. The notice shall be made 1971 452.A14.5

T.§ 1123-312 

PUBLIC SERVICE 

Ch. 53 at any of the offices of the Commission, within a period of not more than 4 hours after the enterprise has knowledge of the accident. When the accident or event takes place outside working hours of the Commission, the enterprise shall notify it not later than 10 o'clock in the morning of the next working day. (b) Accounting system. Every enterprise shall comply with the accounting requirements which shall be prescribed by the Commission by an order to that effect, and shall submit every year financial statements duly certified. (c) Odorizing gases. No licensee shall distribute or supply liquefied petroleum gases without distinct odor so as to indicate positively the presence of gas to a concentration in air of not over 1/5 the lower limit of flammability. Odorization shall be obtained by using one pound of ethyl mercaptan, one pound of thiophane, or 1.4 pounds of amyl mercaptan per 10,000 gallons of liquefied petroleum gas. With any of the above-mentioned odorants, the desired odor may be obtained. 

(d) Equipment. 

(1) Every liquefied petroleum gas enterprise shall keep a permanent inventory of its own containers or of those of which it has legal possession. (2) Every authorized liquefied petroleum gas enterprise shall only employ in the supply, sale, or distribution of said gas, its own equipment or that of which it has legal possession or enjoyment of its use by express authorization of its owner. In any contract by virtue of which a person leases, assigns, transfers, sells, or exchanges to an authorized gas company in Puerto Rico, equipment covered by these subdivisions shall clearly and unequivocally specify the quantities, trademarks, symbols, and serial numbers of all the equipment object of the contract. (3) Any person who, as a public service company, is engaged in the distribution and supply of liquefied petroleum gas in containers shall make the necessary installation to connect the cylinders furnished to the consumer's appliances for which service it may charge a reasonable fee. The enterprise shall not distribute liquefied petroleum gas if the cylinder is not correctly installed. (4) Every enterprise engaged in supplying liquefied petroleum-gas containers to domiciles, shall furnish the necessary regulators for the installation of said containers which shall remain the property of the enterprise. In the installations made prior to the effectiveness of this division in which the regulator belongs to the 1971 452.A14.6

Ch. 53

T.27 § 1123-312 consumer, the latter shall have the option to withdraw the regulator from the installation or to transfer ownership of the regulator to the company furnishing the containers, upon payment of a reasonable sum of money which shall not be less than $1.75. The client shall exercise said option at the first opportunity in which liquefied petroleum gas cylinders are installed after the effectiveness of this division. (5) Every distributor who, in order to install a liquefied petroleum gas cylinder to a client, must remove a cylinder not belonging to him or over which he does not have legal possession should take the cylinder and regulator immediately to his warehouse and deliver both to the owner within a term of 48 hours, if the latter has his offices in the same municipality of the distributor, or in the municipality where the cylinder is installed. If the offices of the cylinder owner are not in the same municipality, the distributor shall indicate to him by mail the place where the equipment is stored. (6) Every liquefied petroleum gas bottling plant shall, upon filling the containers thereof, require the person who brings said cylinders to the plant to show the license number authorizing him or his representative to operate as a gas enterprise in the sale and distribution thereof, and said bottling plant shall likewise specify in the invoice issued, the number of the license and serial number of the cylinder. (7) Every vehicle in which liquefied petroleum gas cylinders are regularly transported shall permanently exhibit on the outside of both front doors, with letters not less than 3 inches high and 1½ inches wide, the name of the company for which such service is rendered and the number of the license authorized by the Commission. (8) Every vehicle used regularly for the transportation of liquefied petroleum gas containers shall be provided with: (A) Tires, including the spare tire, in good traction condition. (B) Two (2) back mirrors installed on the sides of the vehicle and in good operating condition. 

(C) Regulation lights as established by the Motor Vehicles 

Act. (D) High and intermediate steel rails at 42 and 21 inches high, respectively, which will allow the fastening of the gas cylinders at a safe height. 1971

Said cart shall have rubber tires and a chain to fasten the cylinder to the cart. (H) A chock block 4 inches wide, 4 inches high, and 12 inches long (4″ × 4″ × 12″) as appropriate. § 1123-313. Improper practices 

(a) Every person or liquefied petroleum gas enterprise, authorized by the Commission to operate, is prohibited to mar, erase, strike, cover, remove, or in any manner hide the markings, symbols and serial numbers stamped or printed on the equipment by the manufacturer. (b) It is hereby prohibited to every authorized person or liquefied petroleum gas enterprise to fill or cause or allow to be filled, cylinders, containers or tanks, without the express consent of its legitimate owner or of the person having legal possession or enjoyment, thereof. (c) It is hereby prohibited to any authorized person or liquefied petroleum gas enterprise authorized to fill or allow to be filled, cylinders, containers or tanks, the marks, symbols, or serial numbers of which have been erased, stricken, or altered in any manner, whatsoever, or which are not clearly legible. (d) It is hereby prohibited to any authorized person or liquefied petroleum gas enterprise to use, sell, transport, negotiate, install, destroy or hide any equipment used for the transfer, delivery, supply, sale or distribution of liquefied petroleum gas without the consent of its legitimate owner or of the person having legal possession or enjoyment, thereof. 1971 

 452.A14.8

Ch. 

 T.27 § 1123-321 

(e) Any authorized person or liquefied petroleum gas enterprise is prohibited to fill or cause to be filled, cylinders or containers, the capacity of which does not exceed 100 pounds, in places not authorized by the Commission to carry out said activities. (f) Any authorized person of a liquefied petroleum gas enterprise is prohibited to transport equipment or material easily inflammable, such as paper, cardboard, padding, wood, etc., together with gas cylinders. 

§ 1123-314. Safety standards 

(a) Every authorized gas distributor shall deliver to each new customer, at the time of installing a gas container, a printed copy of the following safety standards: (1) At the time of turning on the gas: first light the match and keep it half an inch away from the burner; turn the gas on. 

Never allow the gas to come out before the lighted match is near the burner. (2) If the gas is finished, shut the burners of all the appliances connected to the gas system. Do not tamper with said appliances, nor with the gas pipes. (3) If you suspect any gas leak, do not light matches or other objects producing flames of any kind. Do not connect or disconnect any electrical appliance, nor turn on or off any lights. Open doors and windows so as to let out the gas. Check that all burners of the appliances are shut off. If the leak persists, shut off completely the cylinder valve. Do not move the tank nor attempt to remove it to another place. Get in touch with your distributor, so that he may locate any defect or breakage in your gas installation. (4) Once the gas in the cylinder is consumed, do not allow any person to move it, except the licensed distributor or supplier with whom you made your service contract or a Public Service Commission Employee. (5) If you wish to contract with a new distributor, be sure he is duly authorized by the Public Service Commission. (6) Get in touch with your distributor in case you are moving or for any other reason which might make it necessary for removing the cylinders.

SUBDIVISION 3. SPECIAL AND GENERAL PROVISIONS SECTIONS 

1123-321. Special provisions 

1123-322. General provisions 1971 

 452.A14.9

T.§ 1123-321 Ch. 53 

PUBLIC SERVICE § 1123-321. Special provisions 

(a) Scope. (1) This division covers the minimum requirements for the design, construction, transportation, handling, location, operation, inspection, testing, certification, and marking of liquefied petroleum gas containers and equipment. (2) General requirements shall apply to all containers and equipment. (3) Special requirements shall apply to containers indicated in each subdivision in addition to the general requirements. (b) Interpretation and application. (1) It is not the intention of this division that its provisions be applied to oil pipelines, marine terminals, natural gasoline plants, refineries, chemical plants, or utility gas plants. (2) In cases of practical difficulty or unnecessary deprivations, the Commission shall, upon a showing thereof, dispense with the requirements established in this division or shall permit the use of other means or similar or equivalent devices, provided it is established in a clear and evident manner that reasonable safety shall be obtained. (3) In cases of accidents putting a container out of service, the owner or licensee shall immediately notify the Commission and submit an accurate report of said accident, properly identifying the container. (4) In cases of serious accidents, such as explosions, the licensee shall immediately notify the Commission by telephone, telegraph, or messenger, and he shall not remove or alter any part of the container, except to safeguard the public health and safety, until the Commission carries out an inspection and investigation of the accident. Within the shortest time possible, the inspector in charge of the investigation shall report to the Commission the results of his investigation.

Gases, NFPA, No. 58, which were in effect at the time of the construction of the container. (6) Tanks, cylinders and devices used in the storage, handling and use of liquefied petroleum gases shall be of the type and construction suitable for said purposes, in accordance, insofar as possible, with the standards established by the recognized authorities in this division. (7) Valves, fittings and accessories connected directly to the container, including primary shutoff valves, shall be of material and design suitable for liquefied petroleum gas service. They shall be designed to stand a working pressure not less than the working pressure of the tank for the gas in question. Cast iron shall not be used for container valves, fittings, and accessories; however, container valves made of malleable or nodular iron may be used. (8) Connectors and accessories shall be suitable for the particular use provided in the gas systems covered by this division. 

The design and material used in the connectors and accessories shall provide sufficient resistance to avoid breakage to the maximum pressure to which they may be submitted in normal operation. (9) Safety devices shall be installed and maintained in good operating condition. (10) Every person, with the exception of the owner of the enterprise or his authorized representative, is forbidden to fill any liquefied petroleum gas tank or cylinder. 1971 

 452.A14.12

Ch. T.27 § 1123-322 

(11) No person shall fill or refill any tank or cylinder for liquefied petroleum gas, unless said container has been designed and constructed for said purpose in accordance with this division and with the authorization of the owner. (12) The tanks and cylinders shall be filled solely in the open or in buildings specifically constructed for that purpose. (13) The maximum pressure of liquefied gas vapor which may be transferred to the tanks or cylinders shall be in accordance with the accepted standards in the industry for each type of gas, or as provided by regulation. (14) The maximum permitted filling density for tanks and cylinders shall not be greater than that established by this division. (15) Filling connections on the tanks and cylinders charged in the company shall be provided with automatic shutoff valves. (16) Pressure-reducing regulators shall be attached directly to the shutoff valves or by means of flexible connectors. In both cases the regulators shall be firmly supported. (17) The tanks and cylinders having a 2,000 gallon water capacity or less, shall not have more than 2 openings or plugged openings. (18) Every tank and cylinder shall stand on firm bases or otherwise be firmly secured. Every container shall have flexible connections for piping or special devices where the settling of the earth may affect the safety of the connections. (19) Welding to the shell, head, or any other part of the container subject to internal pressure, shall be done in compliance with the Code under which said container was manufactured. 

Other welding will be permitted solely on saddle plates, lugs or brackets attached to the container by the tank manufacturer. (20) Where repair or modification involving welding of ICC container is required, said container shall be sent to one of the qualified manufacturers making containers of the same type or to a shop duly qualified by the Commission to make the repair or modification in compliance with ICC specifications. (21) Weldings on tanks and cylinders shall not be made until they have been duly washed and drained. (22) Weldings shall be done only by a qualified welder authorized by the Commission. (23) Tanks and cylinders shall be maintained by painting or otherwise treating, providing an adequate protection against the effects of inclemency. 1971 

452.A14.13

T.§ 1123-322 

PUBLIC SERVICE 

Ch. 53 (24) Smoking is strictly prohibited to any person performing the transfer of liquefied gas to any tank or cylinder during any of the stages of connecting, transferring or disconnecting the tank. (25) Readily ignitable material, such as weeds and dry grass, shall be removed from the surrounding area near the tanks and cylinders. Said area shall always be maintained clear. (26) Only persons authorized by the Commission or personnel authorized by the governmental agencies with jurisdiction shall perform the connection or disconnection. (27) When the conditions of a container covered by this division constitute a risk to the life and safety of the persons, the owner or distributor shall remove said container from any establishment within a period of 10 days after having been notified. 

When the risk is imminent, the removal shall be immediate. (28) Pipe, except as otherwise provided in this division, shall be wrought iron or steel, black or galvanized, brass, copper or aluminum alloy. Aluminum alloy pipe shall be in accordance with the United States of America Standard Specifications for Alumi num Alloy Pipe, H. 38.7 (ASTM B-241), except that the use of alloy 5456 is prohibited and shall be suitably marked at each end of each length indicating compliance with said specifications. (29) Aluminum alloy pipe shall be protected against external corrosion when it is in contact with dissimilar metals other than galvanized steel, or its location is subject to repeated wetting by such liquids as water (except rain water), detergents, sewage or leaking from other piping, or it passes through masonry, plaster, or insulation. Galvanized sheet steel pipe, galvanized inside and out, may be considered suitable protection. (30) The maximum nominal pipe size for aluminum pipe shall be 3/4 inch and shall not be used for pressures exceeding 20 pounds per square inch gauge (20 p.s.i.g.). (31) Aluminum alloy pipe and tubing shall not be installed within 6 inches of the ground. (32) Tubing shall be seamless and of copper, brass, steel, or aluminum alloy. Copper tubing shall be of type (K) or (L) or equivalent, as provided in the United States of America Standard 

Specifications for Seamless Copper Water Tube, H-23.1 (ASTM 

B-88). Aluminum allow tubing shall be of type A or B or equivalent as covered in ASTM B-307 and shall be marked every 18 inches, in compliance with said specifications. 1971 

 452.A14.14

Ch. T.27 § 1123-322 

(33) All tubing shall have sufficient resistance to withstand the mechanical handling to the required working pressure, but under no circumstances shall it be less than 125 pounds per square inch for gases and 250 per square inch for liquids. (34) The fittings and accessories for operating pressure of 125 pounds per square inch or less shall be designed for a minimum pressure of 125 pounds per square inch gauge (125 p.s.i.g.), except when used in transportation by trucks. For operating pressures above 125 pounds per square inch gauge (125 p.s.i.g.), the fittings and accessories shall be designed for a minimum pressure of 250 pounds per square inch gauge (250 p.s.i.g.). (35) Hoses shall be fabricated of materials that are resistant to the action of gas in the liquid and vapor phases. If wire braid is used for reinforcing the hose, it shall be of corrosion-resistant material, such as stainless steel. (36) Hoses subject to container pressure shall be designed for a bursting pressure of not less than 1,250 pounds per square inch gauge (1,250 p.s.i.g.). (37) Hoses subject to container pressure shall have its correctness as to design, construction, and performance determined by: or

(38) Hose connections subject to container pressure shall be capable of withstanding, without leakage, a test pressure of not less than 500 pounds per square inch gauge (500 p.s.i.g.). (39) Hose and hose connections on the low pressure side of the regulator or reducing valve shall be designed for a bursting pressure of not less than 125 pounds per square inch gauge, or 5 times the set pressure of the relief devices protecting that portion of the system, or whichever is higher. (40) Flexible hoses may be used on the low pressure side of the system, provided its construction is resistant and that the connectors are designed for said purpose. The markings indicating the various liquid levels from empty to full shall be on the system nameplate or gauging device or part may be on the system nameplate and part on the gauging device.  452.A14.17

PUBLIC SERVICE 

Ch. 53 (50) Gauging devices that require bleeding of the product to the atmosphere, such as the rotary tube, fixed tube and slip tube, shall be designed so that the bleed valve maximum opening is not larger than a No. 54 drill size, unless provided with excess flow valve. (51) Gauging devices shall have a designed working pressure of at least 250 pounds per square inch (250 p.s.i.g.). (52) The length or position of the tube in the fixed liquid level gauge shall be designed to indicate the maximum level to which the container may be filled for the product contained. This level shall be based on the volume of the product at 40°F. and at its maximum permitted filling density for aboveground containers and at 50°F. for underground containers. (53) Fixed liquid level gauges used on containers other than ICC shall be stamped on the exterior of the gauge with letters "DT" followed by the vertical distance (expressed in inches and carried out to one decimal place) from the top of the container to the end of the dip tube or to the centerline of the gauge when it is located at the maximum permitted filling level. For ICC containers the stamping shall be placed both on the exterior of the gauge and on the container. On aboveground or cargo containers where the gauges are positioned at specific levels, the marking may be specified in percent of total tank contents and shall be stamped on the container. (54) Gauge glasses of the columnar type shall be restricted to charging plants where the fuel is withdrawn in the liquid phase only. They shall be equipped with valves having metallic handwheels, excess flow valves, and with extra heavy glass adequately protected with a metal housing. They shall also be shielded against the direct rays of the sun. Level gauges of this kind shall not be installed on motor fuel tanks and on containers used in domestic, commercial and industrial installations. (55) Gauging devices of the float, or equivalent type, which do not require flow for their operation and having connections extending to a point outside the container do not have to be equipped with excess flow valves provided the piping and fittings are adequately designed to withstand the container pressure and are properly protected against physical damage and breakage.

(1) Tanks or containers installed aboveground shall meet the following requirements: (A) In order to avoid excessive concentration of loads, every tank shall be mounted on the portion supporting the metal structure of the shell or head of the container. (B) Container foundations shall be of solid masonry, concrete or steel, with the exception of tanks mounted on skids. 

Structural metal supports may be employed when the tanks are protected against fire with a material whose fire resistance capacity is at least 2 hours. Likewise, as to the steel saddles with a single opening but they shall only be protected with fireresistant material on its exterior. (C) Horizontal containers shall be mounted on saddles in such a manner as to permit expansion and contraction of both the container and the connecting tubing. Only 2 saddles shall be used. (D) Suitable means of preventing corrosion shall be provided on that portion of the container in contact with the saddles or foundations. (E) Tanks of 2,000 gallons of water capacity or less may be installed with ferrous metal supports, if mounted on concrete pads or footings and if the distance from the outside bottom of the container to the ground does not exceed 24 inches. (F) Tanks with foundations attached, semi-fixed, or portable with steel runners or skids, popularly known in the industry as "skid tanks", shall have supports designed, installed and used in accordance with standards approved by the industry and the rules by the Commission. (G) Skids or lugs for attachment of skids shall be firmly secured to containers. However, skid tanks shall not be used in place of tank-trucks, trailers, or semitrailers for regular deliveries. (H) Tanks shall be properly painted or otherwise protected against the weather. (I) The location of every liquefied gas storage tank shall require the written approval of the Commission before being installed. The Commission shall be given a "sketch" of the proposed location before the tank is installed. After it is installed 1971 

 452.A14.19

PUBLIC SERVICE 

Ch. 53 and before it is put to use, the installation must be inspected and approved before the tank is operated. (J) Every tank to be reinstalled and which has been out of service for more than one year shall not be reinstalled unless it satisfactorily supports, without distortion, a hydrostatic test at the same pressure as the original hydrostatic test required by the Code under which the tank was constructed. Said tank should have no evidence of serious corrosion. (2) Underground tanks or containers shall be installed as follows: 

(A) Tanks buried underground shall be placed so that the top of the tank is not less than 6 inches under the surrounding ground level. Tanks partially buried or on an artificial mount shall have 12 inches of earth cover, sufficient to provide drainage on the surface without causing erosion or any other damage. (B) Inspection meters of tanks shall not be covered with fill or surface. In case conditions require that the cover of the inspection meter be below ground level, then there shall be a passage sufficiently accessible. No other part of the container shall be exposed. (C) Containers shall be set on a firm foundation or firm earth and surrounded with soft earth firmly tamped in place. 

Measures shall be submitted taking into account the seat and rotation of container. (D) Containers should be properly protected against corrosion. (E) Connections at the bottom of the tank are prohibited. 

All connections shall be at the inspection meter or at the openings along the superior surface of the container. (3) For installation of storage containers for liquefied petroleum gas employing 2,000 gallon (water) capacity, tank plans shall be submitted in triplicate to the Commission for its approval before commencing the installation. These plans shall indicate, in detail, the proposed location of the storage tank or tanks, filling density for the storage tank or tanks, filling platform, facilities for loading and unloading vaporizers, pumps, compressors, and any other pertinent facility. These plans shall be approved by an authorized engineer in Puerto Rico. (4) Containers installed for use shall not be stacked one above the other. 1971

When the surface area is not stamped on the nameplate or when the marking is not legible, the area can be calculated by using any of the following formulas: (i) Cylindrical containers with hemispherical heads. 

Area Over-all length x outside diameter x 3.1416. (ii) Cylindrical containers with other than hemispherical heads. Area (Over-all length + 0.3 outside diameter) x outside diameter x 3.1416. 

(iii) Spherical containers. Area Outside diameter squared x 3.1416.

The minimum setting on relief valves installed on piping connected to other than ICC containers shall not be lower than 140 percent of the containers relief valve setting and on piping connected to ICC containers not lower than 400 pounds per square inch gauge. Hydrostatic valves shall not be installed on the pump discharge piping, if the same protection can be provided by installing the relief valve on the suction piping. The start-to-discharge pressure setting of such a relief valve, if installed on the discharge side of a pump, shall be greater than the maximum pressure permitted by the recirculation device in the system. (21) The inspection shall meet the following requirements: 

(A) Aboveground tanks shall be inspected in accordance with the regular inspection standards for pressure containers of the Labor Accident Prevention Bureau.

(A) In cases of bulk storage, special care shall be taken to establish restrictions of individual tank capacity of the tank, total storage and the adequate distances from the buildings and other areas. (C) The distances indicated in Table III, clause (9) of this section, may be reduced in cases of buildings exclusively devoted to the charging distribution of gases, provided the safety of employees and public is taken into consideration. 

SUBDIVISION 5. CONTAINERS SECTIONS 

1123-341. Liquefied petroleum gas cylinders or bottles § 1123-341. Liquefied petroleum gas cylinders or bottles 

Liquefied Petroleum gas cylinders or bottles shall conform, insofar as pertinent, to the requirements provided in sections 1123321 and 1123-322 of this title and to the following: 

(1) Construction and installation. 

(A) All cylinders, with the exception of those devoted particularly to be used and transported horizontally, shall be provided 1971 

 452.A14.29 5

T.1123-341 Ch. 53 

PUBLIC SERVICE 

with a device to protect the bottom of the container unless its base is made of special construction. (B) Every gas cylinder shall be provided with a protective hood or other equivalent protection for the valve. (C) The protective hood shall have a vent of adequate size in order to avoid accumulation of gas within the hood. (D) The material used for the different elements of the valves and other fittings shall be of such nature as not to be affected by contents of the cylinder. (E) Liquefied petroleum gas cylinders, its accessories and fittings, shall meet the following requirements: (i) Shall be designed in such a manner as to be suitable to the particular circumstances of its use. (ii) Shall have sufficient resistance to support internal pressures to which they are normally subject. (F) Liquefied petroleum gas cylinders shall conform to the specifications established by the Commission, and particularly shall be of good quality material, free of defects and with sufficient thickness. 

(G) Liquefied petroleum gas cylinders shall not be buried underground. However, this shall not prohibit the installation in a compartment or recess below ground level, such as a niche in a wall or terrace or slope which is used for no other purpose, provided that the container and regulating equipment are not in contact with the ground. The compartment or terrace shall be dry and ventilated horizontally to the exterior from the ground and with an outlet not less than 3 feet from any building opening which is below the level of such outlet. The discharge from said safety relief devices shall be located not less than 3 feet horizontally, away from any building opening which is below the level of such discharge, and shall not terminate beneath any building, unless such space is well ventilated to the outside and is not closed on more than 2 sides. (H) The cylinders shall be set upon firm foundations. Flexible connections or special fittings shall be used to avoid the possible effect on the outlet piping due to the installation. (I) When the use and location of portable cylinders and equipment outside the buildings or structures become impracticable due to the exigencies of the operation, the containers and equipment may be used within said buildings or structures in accordance with, and only for the purposes included in clause (2) of this section. 1971 452.A14.30

This shall not prohibit the use of heaters specifically designed for attachment to the container or to a supporting standard, provided they are designed and installed so as to prevent direct or radiant heat application from the heater onto the container. Blower and radiant type heaters shall not be directed toward any liquefied petroleum gas container within 20 feet. (S) Liquefied petroleum gas containers are permitted to be used in industrial occupancies for processing, research or experimental purposes as follows: (i) The maximum water capacity of each container shall be not greater than 245 pounds (nominal 100 pounds liquefied petroleum gas capacity). (ii) Containers connected to a manifold shall have a total water capacity not greater than 735 pounds (nominal 300 pounds liquefied petroleum gas capacity) and not more than one such manifold may be located in the same room unless separated at least 20 feet from a similar unit. (iii) The amount of liquefied petroleum gas in containers for research and experimental use shall be limited to the smallest practical quantity. (T) Liquefied petroleum gas containers are permitted to be used in educational and institutional laboratory occupancies for research or experimental purposes, but not in classrooms. SECTIONS SUBDIVISION 6. FILLING OF GAS CONTAINERS 

1123–351. Filling of gas containers 

§ 1123-351. Filling of gas containers 

(a) Liquefied petroleum gas containers shall not be filled so that the proportion between the cubic capacity of the cylinder and the 1971 

452.A14.35

T.§ 1123-351 

PUBLIC SERVICE 

Ch. 53 weight of the load be less than that approved by the Commission for the gas in question. (b) Before filling, cylinders shall be: (1) Carefully examined in the filling station to determine whether they are in accordance with the specifications established in this section. (2) Completely emptied. (c) Liquefied petroleum gas containers which have a critical temperature exceeding the regular atmosphere temperature shall not be fully filled in order to avoid the generation of dangerous pressure when they are used at temperatures exceeding the critical temperature. (d) Liquefied petroleum gas cylinders shall be weighed while being filled. In order to determine whether there is any overload, said containers shall be submitted to a subsequent periodic weighing. (e) Cylinders shall be filled in accordance with the filling density indicated in section 1123-322 (a) (46) of this title.

SUBDIVISION 7. HANDLING AND STORAGE SECTIONS 

1123-361. Handling and storage 

§ 1123-361. Handling and storage 

(a) Cylinders shall be conveniently protected against excessive variations of temperature, against direct sunrays, and continuous humidity. (b) The storage of filled cylinders within warehouse shall conform to the following requisites: (1) Storage of cylinders in buildings not constructed for said. purposes is prohibited. (2) Cylinders shall be stored in places with floors and walls of fire-resistant material and away from sources of ignition. (3) Cylinders shall be conveniently placed and secured in order to avoid rolling. (c) Containers, whether empty or filled, shall have protective caps for the valves while in storage. (d) The outlet valves of containers in storage shall be closed. (e) Containers used in liquefied petroleum gas service shall be preferably stored in the open. When stored inside they shall be 1971 452.A14.36

Ch. T.27 § 1123-361 

considered as full containers for the purpose of determining the maximum quantity of permitted gas. (f) Containers when stored inside shall not be located near exits, stairways or in areas normally used or intended for the safe exit of people. (g) Places used for storing charged cylinders shall be marked on the outside with adequate and legible danger signals. (h) Cylinders shall be stored separately according to the type of gas and away from empty containers. (i) Cylinders used within the establishment shall be handled with extreme care and special attention shall be taken to avoid striking, letting them fall or roll, and they shall not be left near sources of heat. (j) The storage area of containers shall be fenced or otherwise protected whenever necessary. The fence shall be provided with at least 2 entrances. 

(k) Storage places shall meet the following conditions: 

(1) Adequate ventilation facilities to the outside. (2) Convenient number of exits (2 at least) according to the quantity and nature of the stored gases. (3) Shall be constructed of noncombustible material. (4) The platform where the cylinders are stored shall be of such a height as to facilitate the loading and unloading of distribution trucks without danger of throwing the cylinders. (5) They shall keep a distance of at least 50 feet from the storage point (platform, tank, container, etc.) to the nearest building or line of adjoining property which may be built upon. (6) They shall not be near meeting places such as schools, churches, etc. (7) They shall be fenced with a cyclone fence 6 feet high and at a minimum distance of 50 feet on each side. When the total capacity of the stored containers is 2,000 gallons or less (water capacity), the above-mentioned distance of 50 feet may be reduced to 25 feet. (8) The whole area within the fenced perimeter shall be free of readily ignitable material such as grass, paper, wood, etc. (9) The installation and electrical equipment shall conform to the provisions of the National Electrical Code (No. 70) or in accordance with the requirements of the Commission. 1971 452.A14.37

T.§ 1123-361 

PUBLIC SERVICE 

Ch. 53 (10) They shall be provided with chemical extinguishers and any other equipment or facility to extinguish or combat fire as required by the Commission. (11) Where the amount of stored gas is 2,000 gallons (water capacity) or more, they shall be provided with appropriate accesses for fire extinguishing equipment, such as the fire engines from the 

Fire Department, or others. (12) Where the quantity of stored gas is 2,000 gallons (water capacity) or more, and there exists a regular watchman service on the premises, this service shall be extended to the installations of liquefied petroleum gas. The personnel thus employed shall be trained as to the safety measures to be used on the premises. (13) Cylinder bottling plants shall be equipped with automatic scales for the filling of cylinders. (1) Smoking is prohibited on the premises of stored cylinders. (m) The cylinders together with their valves and other fittings and markings shall be maintained in good condition. (n) The decantation and emptying of cylinders containing liquefied gases shall not be accelerated by heating the cylinder applying directly open fire or flame; but it may be accelerated by means of a hot water jacket. (0) Cylinder valves shall be immediately closed after the cylinders have been emptied. (p) Cylinders shall be transported so that they do not extend beyond sides, rear or front of the vehicle. (q) Adequate precautions shall be taken to prevent the cylinders from being subject to rough movement, excessive commotion or stress on a particular point. (r) Cylinders shall not be moved by magnetic cranes. (s) When cylinders are moved by means of lifting appliances a float frame properly designed shall be used with adequate slings. (t) Valves, regulators and other accessory equipment of the container shall be protected against physical damage while in transportation. (u) Hoisting ears in stationary containers shall not be used as exclusive means to lift said containers. (v) The protective cap of the valve shall not be used to raise or hoist cylinders from a vertical position to another. (w) No bars shall be placed under the valves or its protectors to lift the cylinder from the ground. 1971

(x) Before lifting a cylinder which is provided with protective valve cap from a horizontal position to a vertical position, the cap should be duly located in its place. The cap shall be moved circularly towards the right in order to make certain that it is taut by hand and then the cylinder shall be lifted by the cap. (y) Cylinders shall not be used as rollers or supports whether filled or empty.

SECTIONS 

1123-371. Inspection and tests 

§ 1123-371. Inspection and tests 

(a) The useful life of the cylinders shall be established by means of tests following the rules of the United States Interstate Commerce Commission (ICC) and of the Department of Transportation (DOT), as applied. (b) Gas cylinders shall be submitted to inspection and tests by qualified inspectors authorized by the Commission, in the following stages:

SUBDIVISION 8. INSPECTION AND TESTS 

(1) Before being put to service for the first time. (2) Before being put to service after repairs other than changing the ring on the collar on which the new cap is screwed or changing the ring of the base. (3) Periodically, at the intervals determined by the Commission and not later than 5 years. (c) It shall be the duty of the owner to submit the cylinder to inspection and tests whenever proper. (d) The tests to which the cylinders are submitted in accordance with subsection (b) of this section shall consist of hydrostatic pressure test and internal and external inspection. 

SUBDIVISION 9. LABELS SECTIONS 

1123-381. Markings and colors 

§ 1123-381. Markings and colors 

(a) Every gas cylinder shall be marked in accordance with the 

United States Interstate Commerce Commission Regulations. Addi tional markings not in conflict with the United States Interstate 

Commerce Commission may be used. 1971 452.A14.39

T.1123-381 

PUBLIC SERVICE 

Ch. 53 (b) Cylinders shall be marked with its water capacity in pounds or other identified unit of weight. (c) When cylinders are filled and maintained only by the owner or his representative and if the water capacity of each cylinder is identified by a code, compliance with the requirements of the preceding subsection (b) is not required. (d) Each cylinder shall be marked with its tare weight in pounds or any other identified unit of weight including all permanently attached fittings but not the cap. (e) Every gas cylinder shall be marked so that it be readily visible and lasting, with the following details: (1) Name of owner. (2) Registry number. (3) Exact identification of the gas contained. (4) Date of tests made. (5) Maximum pressure permitted. (6) Date of construction. (f) When liquefied petroleum gas cylinders are stored or used in the same area, the containers shall be marked to identify their contents in compliance with the United States of America Standard, Z 48.1-1954, "Method of Marking Portable Compressed Gas Con tainers to Identify the Material Contained".

Explanatory note. The English version of this section has no subsection (g). The text in Spanish of said subsection is as follows: "(g) Cuando se empleen colores para identificar el contenido no se permitirán marcas de color que sirvan para distinguir cilindros para otros fines." 

SUBDIVISION 10. TRANSPORTATION 

1123-391. Truck transportation 

§ 1123-391. Truck transportation 

(a) Cargo tanks or tank motor vehicles. (1) Cargo tanks and pertinent equipment for tank vehicles for the transportation of liquefied petroleum gas, in addition to complying with the requirements of this section, should also comply with the regulations of the United States Interstate Commerce Commission and those of any other regulatory body which may apply. (2) Shell or head thickness of every cargo tank shall be at least 3/16 of an inch. 1971 

 452.A14.40

+ 

Ch. 53

(3) Longitudinal shell welds or seams shall be located in the upper half of the container. (4) Tank motor vehicles with frames not made integral with the tank, as by welding, shall be provided with turnbuckles or similar positive devices for drawing the tank down tight on the frame. In addition, suitable stops or anchors shall be attached to the frame and/or the tank to prevent relative motion between them due to starting, stopping and turning. The stops and anchors shall be so installed as to be readily accessible for inspection and maintenance. (5) Any tank motor vehicle designed and constructed so that the cargo tank constitutes in whole or in part the stress member used in lieu of a frame shall be supported by external cradles subtending at least 120 degrees of the shell circumference. The design calculations shall include beam stress, shear stress, torsion stress, bending moment and acceleration stress for the cargo tank as a whole using a factor of safety of 4, based on the ultimate tensible strength of the material. Maximum concentrated stresses which might be created at pads and cradles due to shear, bending and torsion shall also be calculated in accordance with Appendix G of the ASME, 1962 edition. Fully loaded vehicles shall be assumed to be operating under highway conditions equal to twice normal loading. The effects of fatigue shall be taken into consideration. 

Cargo tanks mounted on frames may be supported by longitudinal members attached to pads providing the above-stated factors are taken into account. (6) When any tank support is attached to any part of the bottom of the tank, the stresses imposed upon the bottom of the tank shall be provided for. (7) Tank supports, bumpers, stops and anchors shall not be welded directly to the tank but shall be attached by means of pads of the same material as the tank. The pad thickness shall be not less than 1/4 inch, or the thickness of the shell material if less, and no greater than the shell material. Each pad shall extend at least 4 times its thickness, in each direction, beyond the weld attaching the support, bumper, stop or anchor. Each pad shall be preformed to an inside radius not greater than the outside radius of the tank at the place of attachment. Each pad corner shall be rounded to a radius at least 1/4 the width of the pad. Weepholes and telltale holes, if used, shall be drilled or punched before the pads are attached to the tank. Each pad shall be attached to the 1971 452.A14.41

PUBLIC SERVICE 

Ch. 53 tank by continuous, straight angle welding using filler material having properties conforming to the recommendations of the maker of the shell and the bottom of the tank. (8) Nonrecessed container fittings and appurtenances shall be protected against damage by the following factors: (A) Their location, (B) the vehicle frame or bumper, or (C) a protective housing. (9) The protective housing, if used, shall comply with the requirements under which the tanks are fabricated with respect to design and construction and shall be designed to withstand static loadings in any direction equal to twice the weight of the tank and attachments when filled with the lading using a safety factor of not less than 4, based on the ultimate strength of the material to be used. (10) The protective housing shall be provided with a weather cover if necessary to insure proper operation of valves and safety devices. (11) Filling connections shall be provided with approved automatic back pressure check valves, excess flow check valves or quick closing internal valves to prevent excessive escape of gas in case the filling connection is broken. Where the filling and discharge connect on a common opening in the container shell, and that opening is fitted with a quick-closing internal valve as specified in the following clause, the automatic valve shall not be required. In addition, every inlet and outlet connection shall be equipped with a manually or automatically operated shutoff valve. (12) Liquid discharge openings, except those for engine fuel lines, on tanks built after September 1, 1965, shall be fitted with a remotely controlled internal shutoff valve. Such valve shall conform to the following requirements: (A) The seat of each valve shall be inside the tank, or in the opening nozzle or flange or in a companion flange bolted to the nozzle or flange. (B) All parts of the valve inside the tank, nozzle, or companion flange shall be made of material not subject to corrosion or other deterioration in presence of the loading. (C) The arrangement of parts shall be such that damage to parts exterior to the tank will not prevent effective seating of the valve. 1971 

 452.A14.42

Ch. 53

 2 (D) The valve may be operated normally by mechanical means, by hydraulic means, or by air, or gas pressure. (E) The valves shall be provided with remote means of automatic closure, both mechanical and thermal, in at least 2 places for tanks over 3,500 gallon water capacity. These remote control stations shall be located at each end of the tank and diagonally opposite each other. The thermal control mechanism shall have a fusible element with a melting point not over 220 degrees Fahrenheit or less than 208 degrees Fahrenheit. At least one remote control station shall be provided for tanks of 3,500 gallon water capacity or less, and such actuating means may be mechanical. (13) All other connections to containers, except those used for gauging devices, thermometer wells, safety relief devices and plugged openings, shall be provided with suitable automatic excess flow valves, or in lieu thereof may be fitted with quick-closing internal valves. The control mechanism for the internal valve shall be provided with a secondary control, remote from the fill or discharge connections, for use in the event of accidents or fire during delivery operations, and such control mechanism shall have a fusible element of melting point not over 220°F., or less than 208°F., permitting the valve to close automatically in case of fire. (14) Manually operated shutoff valves, except as covered in this division, or self-closing internal valves shall be closed except during transfer operations. (15) Excess flow valves shall close automatically at the rated flow of vapor or liquid as specified by the valve manufacturer. The flow rating of the piping beyond the excess flow valve shall be. greater than that of the excess flow valve and such rating shall include valves, fittings and hose, except, when branching or necessary. restrictions are incorporated in such a piping system so that flow. ratings are less than that of the excess flow valve at the tank. Then additional excess flow valves shall be installed in the piping where such flow rate is reduced. (16) An opening shall be provided in each cargo tank to afford complete drainage. (17) Container inlets and outlets, except those used for safety relief valves, liquid level gauging devices, and pressure gauges, shall be labeled to designate whether they communicate with vapor or liquid space when the container is filled to maximum permitted filling density. 1971

Ch. 53 (18) Each cargo tank shall be equipped with a suitable pressure gauge. (19) Any gauging device used to determine the maximum allowable filling limit of a cargo tank of a trailer or semi-trailer shall be located as near the mid-point (front-to-rear) of the cargo tank as practical. If a gauging device, such as a rotary gauge or a slip tube gauge, is used for the above purpose, a fixed tube gauge set in the range of 85-90 percent of the water capacity of the tank shall be provided, in addition, as a means of checking the accuracy of the variable gauge. The capacity indicated by this fixed gauge shall be marked on or adjacent to this gauge which shall be secured to prevent tampering with the setting. (20) The discharge from safety relief valves shall be vented away from the container upward and unobstructed to the open air in such a manner as to prevent any impingement of escaping gas upon the container. Size of discharge lines from safety relief valves shall not be smaller than the nominal size of the relief valve outlet connection. Suitable provision shall be made for draining condensation which may accumulate in the discharge pipe. (21) Each discharge outlet from a safety relief valve shall be provided with a rain cap or other protector to keep water and dirt from collecting in the valve. The protector shall be in place except when the valve operates. The rain cap or other protector shall not reduce the flow through the valve. (22) When a safety relief valve is installed in a well in the top of a container, the well shall be painted or otherwise protected to reduce corrosion, shall be checked frequently and kept free of water and dirt. (23) Any portion of piping between tank and pump inlet or any wet hose which at any time may be closed at each end should be provided with relief valve to prevent excessive pressure developing. (24) Pipe, tubing and fittings shall be suitable for a minimum pressure of 250 pounds per square inch gauge. Pipe shall be at least schedule 80 if joints are threaded, or welded, and at least schedule 40 when the joints are welded, or welded and flanged. (25) The use of aluminum alloy pipe tubing or fittings is prohibited in tank trucks. (b) Trailers. (1) Trailers shall be firmly and securely attached to the vehi- 1971 452.A14.44

(2) Every trailer shall be equipped with a reliable system of brakes, and adequate provision shall be made for its efficient operation from the driver's seat of the vehicle drawing the trailer. (3) Every trailer shall be provided with sidelights and a taillight. (4) Trailers with drawbars shall be of a type of construction which will prevent the towed vehicle from whipping or swerving from side to side dangerously and will cause it to follow substantially in the path of the towing vehicle. (5) When a fifth wheel is employed, it shall be ruggedly designed, securely fastened to both units, and equipped with a positive locking mechanism which will prevent separation of the 2 units, except by manual release. (6) Every trailer when parked shall be so positioned that the safety relief valve shall communicate with the vapor space of the container. (7) Cargo tank, chassis, axles and springs shall be metallically connected. (8) Lighting in trucks, trailers and semitrailers shall be electrical. Lighting circuit shall have fuses or automatic circuit breakers for overcurrent protection. Lighting shall have sufficient carrying capacity and mechanical strength and shall be suitably secured, insulated, and protected against physical damages. (9) The exhaust system of motor gases, including muffler and exhaust line of trucks, trailers, or semitrailers, shall have ample clearance from the fuel system and combustible materials. Truck exhaust discharge shall be directed away from any tank and appurtenances and to the outside of the frame and any skirting. (10) Protection against collision of trucks, trailers, and semitrailers, shall meet the following conditions: (A) Each truck and trailer shall be provided with properly attached steel bumpers or chassis extension which shall be so arranged as to protect any tank, piping, valves, and fittings in case of collision. (B) Each tank truck and trailer shall carry chock blocks which shall be used to prevent rolling of the vehicle whenever it is parked, including when loading and unloading. (11) Protection against fire in trucks, trailers, and semitrailers, shall meet the following: 1971 

 452.A14.45

PUBLIC SERVICE 

Ch. 53 (A) Truck drivers and their helpers shall not smoke or allow smoking in or around the truck on the road, while making deliveries, filling the tank, or when making any repairs to truck or trailer. (B) Each tank truck or tractor shall be provided with at least one approved portable fire extinguisher having at least a 12-B, C rating, or when more than one is provided, each extinguisher shall have at least a 6-B, C rating. Each truck transporting gas cylinders shall have at least one extinguisher having an 8-B, C rating. Ratings shall be in accordance with the Standard for Installation of Portable Fire Extinguishers, NFPA No. 10. 

(12) Markings and colors of cargo vehicles shall meet the following: (A) Every truck or tank truck vehicle used for the transportation of gases shall be marked on each side and rear, thereof, on a sharply contrasting background, with FLAMMABLE GAS in block letters at least 5 inches high, and in block letters at least 3 inches high, LIQUEFIED PETROLEUM GAS, or BU- 

TANE or PROPANE, as appropriate. (B) At least the upper 2/3 of cargo tanks shall be painted with a light reflecting paint for the finish coat except for lettering. (13) Garages and parking places for trucks, trailers, and semitrailers, shall meet the following conditions: (A) Tank vehicles or trailers containing vapors or liquefied petroleum gases (except in an emergency and except as provided in par. B), shall not be left unattended on any street, highway, avenue or alley. This shall not prevent a driver from the necessary absence from the vehicle in connection with a delivery, nor shall it prevent stops for meals or rest. (B) Unattended tank trucks or trailers shall not be parked in congested areas. Such vehicles may be parked off the street in uncongested areas and at least 50 feet from any building used for assembly, institutional or multiple residential occupancy. (C) Tank vehicles or trailers containing liquefied petroleum gas shall not be stored, parked or garaged in any building unless the building is specifically approved for such use by the Commission, or is designed for such use. (14) The following essential precautions shall be followed when it is necessary to garage liquefied petroleum gas tank vehicles for service on the chassis or engine: 1971 452.A14.46

Ch. 53 53  

OW Or 1 (A) All primary shutoff valves shall be closed and liquid and vapor in the hose and piping vented to a safe location prior to moving the vehicle into the building. (B) The system shall be checked for any leaks and any found shall be repaired before the vehicle is moved inside of the building. (C) The cargo container shall be gauged to determine that it is not filled beyond maximum filling capacity according to section 1123–322(a) (46) of this title. If overfilled, it shall be corrected before the vehicle is moved inside of the building. (D) The vehicle shall not be parked near a source of heat or similar sources of ignition. (E) The driver shall instruct the responsible people in the garage of the nature of the cargo contents and instruct them not to tamper with the tank valves or fittings. (F) Repair work shall not be done on the cargo container or primary shutoff valves if the cargo container contains product. (15) Any truck tank or trailer which has suffered damage as a result of an accident which might have caused unsafe conditions, or when the damage is of such magnitude as to give rise to suspect the existence of such conditions, the tank shall be tested as follows: (A) The tank without its accessories shall be submitted to a hydrostatic pressure of 12 times the design pressure or maximum permitted working pressure. (B) The tank shall be inspected during the hydrostatic test in order to determine whether there are any leaks, corroded areas, dents and other conditions affecting its resistance and which may render the tank unsafe for transportation service. 

The tank shall be withdrawn from service when there is evidence of such unsafe conditions. (C) It shall not be necessary to remove the coating, if any, nor the isolation jacket of the coated tanks, unless it is determined that it is impossible to reach the test pressure and maintain a stable pressure once the test pressure is reached while testing the tank. (16) Loading and unloading siding for trucks, tanks, trailers and semitrailers, shall meet the following requirements: (A) Shall be relatively level. (B) A "Tank Car Connected" sign, as covered by the Interstate Commerce Commission rules, shall be installed at each 1971 452.A14.47

PUBLIC SERVICE 

Ch. 53 active end of the siding while the tank car is connected for loading or unloading. (C) A man shall be in attendance at all times while the tank car, cars or trucks are being loaded or unloaded. (D) The pipeline to which unloading hoses are connected shall be equipped with a backflow check valve in order to prevent discharge of the gas from the receiving container and pipeline in case of hose and accessories rupture. (17) The truck unloading point should be located with due consideration to the following: (A) Proximity to highway traffic. (B) The distance of such unloading point from adjacent property. (C) Distance with respect to buildings on installer's property. (D) Nature of occupancy. (E) Topography. (F) Type of construction of buildings. (G) Number of tank cars or transport trucks that may be safely unloaded at one time. (H) Frequency of unloading. (I) Where practical, the distance of the unloading point should conform to the distances in Table III of section 1123-331 (a) (9), of this title, except that lesser distances may be used, keeping in mind the above items and upon approval of the Commission. (18) Liquid transfer between containers shall conform to the following: (A) The determination of the maximum permitted filling when loading cargo tanks or trucks, trailers or semi-trailers shall be by the use of suitable liquid level gauge or by weighing, whether or not a meter is used. (B) Pumps or compressors shall be designed for use with gas and shall be properly protected against damage and breakage caused by collision and shall be maintained in good operating condition. Such pumps or compressors may be mounted upon tank trucks, trailers or semitrailers and may be driven by the truck motor power take-off or internal combustion engine, hand or mechanical, hydraulic or electrical means. When a meter is used, the automatic device shall be installed between the meter outlet and the hose connection. An excess flow valve may also be used but shall not be used as the exclusive means to accomplish the requirements of this section. (19) In case of accident, the truck or trailer driver shall take the following steps: (A) Park the vehicle outside the road, whenever possible, and disconnect the interruptor and place chock blocks. (B) Place the fire extinguisher in position to be used and turn off any flame in the area. (C) Examine the vehicle and cargo tank to determine the damage. In case of fire in the tank or pipelines, stop the traffic and keep the public away. (D) Place caution signs on the highway. (E) Notify the highway patrol, local police and employer before moving vehicles from scene of accident. (F) Give first aid, if necessary. (20) In case of accident where the cargo tank receives such serious damages that it is not safe to continue driving, the contents of such tank shall be transferred to another tank or tanks before moving away. (21) In case of fire in a tank truck or trailer, the driver shall take the following steps: (A) Try to extinguish the fire with the equipment at hand, provided the gas leak can be closed or obstructed immediately. (B) If the fire cannot be extinguished, notify all persons within the area. If on open highway, post caution signs at a reasonable safe distance from the tank truck. 1971

SUBDIVISION 11. MOTOR FUEL CONTAINERS SECTIONS
