§ 1123-3101. General 

(a) Fuel may be used from the cargo tank of a truck vehicle while in transit, but not from cargo tanks on trailers. (b) Fuel from the cargo tanks to operate stationary engines is permitted providing wheels of cargo tank are securely blocked. (c) All inlet and outlet connections on the tanks and containers used to supply fuel direct to an internal combustion engine shall be labeled to designate whether they communicate with vapor or liquid space. 

§ 1123-3102. Construction 

(a) Fuel containers for use on industrial trucks, including lift trucks, shall be constructed according to the Interstate Commerce Commission rules, authorized for liquefied petroleum gas service and should have a minimum service pressure of 240 pounds per square inch gauge or minimum container type 250. Containers under 1950 and later ASME Codes shall have a 312.5 pounds per square inch gauge design pressure. (b) All container inlets and outlets except safety relief valves and gauging devices shall be labeled to designate whether they communicate with vapor or liquid space. Labels may be on valves. 

§ 1123-3103. Installation 

(a) Containers shall be located in a safe place and in a manner to minimize the possibility of damage to the container. Containers located in the rear of trucks and buses, when protected by substantial bumpers, will be considered in conformance with this requirement. 1971 

452.A14.50

Ch. 

 T.27 § 1123-3104 

(b) Fuel containers on passenger-carrying vehicles shall be installed as far from the engine as is practicable, and the passenger space and the space near the container compartment shall be vented to the outside. (c) In case the fuel container is mounted near the engine or the exhaust system, the container shall be shielded against direct heat radiation. (d) Containers shall be installed with as much clearance as practicable but never less than the minimum road clearance of the vehicle under maximum spring deflection. This minimum clearance shall be to the bottom of the container or to the lowest fitting on the container or housing, whichever is lower. (e) Permanent or removable containers shall be securely mounted to prevent jarring loose, slipping or overturning. (f) Fuel containers on buses shall be permanently installed. (g) Fuel containers shall be mounted to the vehicle and the fastenings shall be designed and constructed with a safety factor of not less than 4 to withstand loading in any direction equal to 4 times the weight of the tank when filled. Field welding, when necessary, shall be made only on saddle plates, lugs, or brackets, originally attached to the container by the tank manufacturer. (h) Containers from which vapor only is to be withdrawn shall be installed and equipped with suitable connections to minimize the accidental withdrawal of liquid. 

§ 1123-3104. Valves and accessories 

(a) Container valves and accessories shall have a rated working pressure of at least 250 pounds per square inch gauge and shall be of a type suitable for liquefied petroleum gas service. (b) Filling connections shall be fitted with an approved double back-pressure check valve, or a positive shut-off in conjunction with an internal back-pressure valve. On a removable container the filler valve may be a hand operated shutoff valve with an internal excess flow valve. Main shutoff valves on the container on liquid and vapor lines must be readily accessible. (c) With the exception of the provisions of section 1123–3103 (f) of this title, filling connections equipped with approved automatic back-pressure check valves, and safety relief valves, all connections to containers having openings for the flow of gas in excess of a No. 54 drill size of established specification shall be equipped with excess flow valves to prevent discharge of content in case connec- 1971 452.A14.51

T.§ 1123-3104 

PUBLIC SERVICE 

Ch. 53 tions are broken. This requirement may be waived by the Commission when such exception is recognized. (d) Variable liquid level gauges which require the venting of fuel to the atmosphere shall not be used on fuel containers of industrial trucks and lifting cars. (e) Permanently mounted fuel containers shall be equipped with a fixed length dip tube gauge to measure the volume of gas content. (f) In the case of containers used solely in farm tractor service, and charged at a point at least 50 feet from any important building, the fixed liquid level gauging device may be so constructed that the outward flow of container content exceeds that passed by a No. 54 drill size opening, but in no case shall the flow exceed that passed by a No. 31 drill size opening. An excess flow valve is not required. Fittings equipped with such restricted drill size opening and container on which they are used shall be marked to indicate the size of the opening. (g) All valves and connections on containers shall be adequately protected to prevent damage due to accidental contact with stationary objects or from loose objects thrown up from the road. All valves shall be safeguarded against physical damage due to collision, overturning or other accident. For farm tractors where parts of the vehicle provide such protection to valves and fittings, the fore-going requirements shall be considered fulfilled. However, on removable type containers, the protection for the fittings shall be permanently attached to the container. (h) Exchange of removable fuel containers preferably should be done outdoors, but may be done indoors. When removable fuel containers are used, means shall be provided in the fuel system to minimize the escape of fuel when the containers are exchanged. 

This may be accomplished by either of the following methods: (1) Using an approved automatic quick-closing coupling which type closes in both directions. (2) Closing the valve at the fuel container and allowing the engine to run until the fuel in the line is consumed. § 1123-3105. Piping and fittings (a) Pipe from fuel container to first stage regulator shall be not less than Schedule 80 wrought iron or steel, black or galvanized, brass or copper; or seamless copper, brass or steel tubing. Steel tubing shall have a minimum wall thickness of 0.049 inches, and 1971 452.A14.52

Ch. 

 T.27 § 1123-3107 

shall be adequately protected against exterior corrosion. Copper tubing shall be type K or L or equivalent having a minimum wall thickness of 0.032 inches. Approved flexible connections may be used between container and regulator or between regulator and gas-air mixer within the limits of approval by the Commission. The use of aluminum pipe or tubing is prohibited. In the case of removable containers an approved flexible connection shall be used between the container and the fuel line. (b) All piping shall be installed, braced, and supported so as to reduce to a minimum the possibility of vibrations, strains or wear. 

§ 1123-3106. Safety devices 

(a) Spring-loaded internal type safety relief valves shall be used on all motor fuel containers. (b) The discharge outlet from safety relief valves shall be located on the outside of enclosed spaces and as far as practicable from possible sources of ignition. They shall be vented upward in such a manner as to prevent impingement of escaping gas upon containers, or parts of vehicle, or on vehicles adjacent in traffic. A rain cap, or other protector, shall be used to keep water and dirt from collecting in the valve. (c) When a discharge line from the container safety relief valve is used, the line shall be metallic, other than aluminum, and shall be sized, located, and maintained so as not to restrict the required flow of gas from the safety relief valve. Such discharge line shall be able to withstand the pressure resulting from the discharge of vapor when the safety relief valve is in the full open position. When flexibility is necessary, flexible metal hose or tubing shall be used. § 1123-3107. Regulating equipment (a) Approved automatic pressure reducing equipment shall be installed. The installation shall be in a secure manner between the fuel supply container and gas-air mixer for the purpose of reducing the pressure of the fuel delivered to the gas-air mixer. (b) An approved automatic shutoff valve shall be provided in the fuel system at some point ahead of the inlet of the gas-air mixer. 

The valve shall be designed to prevent flow of fuel to the mixer when the ignition is off and the engine is not running. In the case of industrial trucks and engines operating in buildings other than those used exclusively to house engines, the automatic shutoff valve shall be designed to operate if the engine should stop. Ch. 53 nors of atmospheric type regulators shall be considered adequate as an automatic shutoff valve only in cases of outdoor operation such as farm tractors, construction equipment, irrigation pump engines, and other outdoor stationary engine installations. (c) The source of the air for combustion shall be completely isolated from the passenger compartment, ventilating system or air conditioning system. 

§ 1123-3108. Capacity 

No single fuel container used on passenger carrying vehicles shall exceed 200 gallon water capacity. No single fuel container on other vehicles normally operating on the highway shall exceed 300 gallon water capacity.

SECTIONS SUBDIVISION 12. INDOOR OPERATIONS 

1123-3111. Garaging liquefied petroleum gas fueled vehicles and tank vehicles indoors § 1123-3111. Garaging liquefied petroleum gas fueled vehicles and tank vehicles indoors (a) Vehicles in garages. (1) Liquefied petroleum gas fueled vehicles may be stored or serviced inside garages provided there are no leaks in the fuel system and the fuel tanks are not filled beyond the maximum filling capacity provided in this division. (2) Liquefied petroleum gas vehicles being repaired in garages shall have the container shutoff valve closed except when fuel is required for engine operation. (3) Such vehicles shall not be parked near sources of heat, open flames or similar sources of ignition or near open pits unless such pits are adequately ventilated. (b) Stationary or portable engines. (1) All engine rooms shall be adequately ventilated at floor level. (2) Whenever engines are installed underground, ventilation by adequate mechanical aspiration shall be provided at floor level. 

Ventilation system shall operate continuously or adequate means shall be provided to purify the room before starting engine. In any event, the mechanical ventilation shall be in operation when the 1971 452.A14.54

Ch. 

 T.27 § 1123-3121 

engine is working. The rooms shall be ventilated before and after any engine repair. (3) Automatic firewalls shall be provided in open spaces inside the engine room which communicate with other sections of the building. (4) Exhaust gas shall be discharged outside the building in such a way as not to cause fire or any other hazard. (5) Regulators and pressure relief valves installed in buildings and engine rooms shall be ventilated to the outside and discharged at not less than 5 feet from any opening in the building. This ventilation shall not be required for engine gas mixtures, fuel reducing, and gauging devices, provided the automatic shutoff valve required in section 1123-3107(b) of this title is installed immediately before said devices. (6) A flexible hose shall be connected at the terminal of the fuel line leading to the motor. This hose shall be of an approved type and shall not exceed the length of 3 feet and shall be connected in such a manner as to eliminate the possibility of damage by vibration. (c) Industrial trucks. (1) Liquefied petroleum gas fueled industrial trucks are permitted to be used in buildings and structures. (2) No more than 2 liquefied petroleum gas containers shall be used on an industrial truck for motor fuel purpose. (3) Subject to approval by the Commission, liquefied petroleum gas fueled industrial trucks are permitted to be used in buildings frequented by the public, when occupied by the public. The total water capacity of containers on each industrial truck shall not exceed 105 pounds, a nominal 45 pounds of liquefied petroleum gas. (4) Industrial trucks shall not be left unattended in areas occupied by the public.

§ 1123-3121. Penalty 

(a) Any violation of any of the preceding provisions of this division shall constitute a misdemeanor and shall be subject to the 1971 

 452.A14.55

T.§ 1123-3121

[27 L.P.R.A. § 1273]. 

(b) The Commission may also, in the case of a violation of any of the provisions of this division and after a public hearing, suspend or revoke the license of the gas company in question. 

§ 1123-3122. Separability clause 

If any provision of this division should be declared illegal or unconstitutional by judgment of a court, said declaration or judgment shall not apply to the other provisions of this division and for that reason it is hereby declared that they have been adopted independently of any one provision that should be declared illegal or unconstitutional. § 1123-3123. (b) Approved by the Public Service Commission of Puerto Rico, with the unanimous vote of its members, in its September 28, 1970, executive session, after having received proof, arguments and the views of the interested persons during the public hearings held for that purpose.
